Heading: Chief secy announces compensation for kin of Belpahari victims - Indian Express
Content:
Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya took the Chief Medical Health Officer (CMHO), Debdwaipayan Chattopadhaya, to task on Thursday for not revealing the actual figures of those affected by vector-borne diseases in the city.

After being grilled by Bhattacharya, the CMHO disclosed a chart of revised figures, according to which, 72 people have been affected by dengue. The earlier figure was 55. There have been 14,053 cases of falciparum malaria. The earlier figure was 650-800. Two deaths from malaria and four from dengue have been reported as well.

Bhattacharya, however, said the confusion was not created deliberately.

Earlier, the health department did not get any data from private laboratories. Now, some data have been collected from private laboratories and added to the revised report.

Also, two NGOs — the Kolkata Nagarik Samanaya Samity and the People's Health — have submitted a memorandum to health minister Surjya Kanta Mishra with the present status of the diseases in the city.

Also, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) slapped a notice on the premier state-run SSKM hospital, asking it to remove all existing and potential breeding grounds of vectors. Bhattacharya, along with the CMHO and the local councillor, took part in an awareness campaign on vector-borne diseases in ward number 30.

Another malaria death
One more person succumbed to malaria in the city on Thursday. Kashinath Saha (45), a resident of 1, Taltala Library Row, died at the Saviour Clinic on Dr Suresh Sarkar Road in Entally. He had been admitted to the clinic on October 20 and was diagnosed with malignant malaria. According to doctors, his condition had been improving. But since Thursday morning, he suffered a relapse.

"Towards the afternoon, he experienced multiple organ failure," said Dr Sunando Haldar, a doctor attached to Saviour.

Heading: ‘Dawood Ibrahim of Hooghly’ arrested by CID - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Secretary Amit Kiran Deb announced on Thursday that the government has decided to give a compensation of Rs 2 lakh to the families of those killed by the landmine blast at Belpahari on Wednesday.

Other than Dr Dhoni Ram Mandi and nurse Bharati Maji, both employees of the state health department, the family of the driver of the hired vehicle will also get a compensation of Rs 2 lakh.

Deb said two persons were arrested on Thursday from a village in Belpahari in connection with the landmine blast. Investigation conducted by the West Midnapore district police revealed that the duo had given shelter to Maoist activists in their house. The police have seized posters and leaflets of Maoists from their house. Deb, however, did not disclose the name of the arrested persons.

Heading: Coal shortage: Kolkata faces blackout threat - Indian Express
Content:
Notorious criminal Shyamal Das alias "Hubba", wanted by the state Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for jumping bail last year, was arrested in Uttarpara area of Hooghly on Thursday. Known as the "Dawood Ibrahim" of Hooghly, Das has several cases against him including murder, extortion and drug smuggling.

A CID officer said, "We received a tip-off that Das was still running a crime ring in the industrial belt of Hooghly and would visit Konnagar. A police team intercepted him on GT Road Thursday afternoon."

Das was arrested with his associate Benarasi Bapi in 2005 by the CID from Baguiati area in North 24 Parganas in connection with a 2002 murder case in Uttarpara. He fled from Hooghly soon after being released on bail.

"An arrest warrant was issued against him since he repeatedly failed to appear before the court that had granted him bail," said the officer.

Das, a resident of Dharmadanga near Konnagar in Hooghly, entered the crime world in 1991.

In 1995, Das extended operations up to Uttar Pradesh and began dealing in arms and ammunition. He had managed to elude the police till he was caught in 2005.

"He also got involved in iron scrap smuggling across the eastern region. He returned to Konnagar in 1998 after his gang in Hooghly was divided and joined hands with another criminal, Bholanath Das," said a police officer.

The duo had also invested several crores of rupees in real estate in the district.

Heading: Illegal tanneries gutted in Tiljala, 6 firemen injured - Indian Express
Content:
Thermal power plants of West Bengal are running short of coal reserves and the state might be heading towards a blackout. "On Thursday, power plants of the state had a coal reserve of 1,60,000 tonnes. This is just enough to run the plants for four days," said S Mahapatra, Managing Director of West Bengal Power Development Corporation (WBPDCL).

"While the WBPDCL receives nearly 31,000 tonnes of coal daily, we require nearly 41,000 tonnes of coal a day to run the power plants and 50,000 tonnes are required to run these plants at full capacity," he said. Mahapatra added, "A daily gap of 10,000 tonnes is eating into the coal reserves that the WBPDCL has right now."

WBPDCL sources said the situation at several power plants was critical. "Three days ago, Bakreshwar Thermal Power Plant had just four hours of coal reserves and was on the verge of a shutdown. On Thursday, the plant had just 20 hours of coal reserves."

The state power department is alarmed at the development. Senior officials say that a power plant is expected to have coal stocks to maintain its operations for nearly 21 days. Officials are apprehensive that if the situation does not improve, the state may witness a complete blackout.

"No one can predict what would happen. It is not possible for me to predict that the coal supply would improve or deteriorate," said Mahapatra.

The department has blamed the coal-supplying companies for the situation. "Despite promises the companies made to us, they are supplying insufficient coal," said Power Secretary Sunil Mitra. Further, in spite of a promise to supply extra coal for generating additional 1570 mw this year, the coal companies are reluctant to increase the supply, said an official.

The coal companies, however, blame the state government for the crisis. "We are supplying the amount of coal that we had promised to the government. This year we would supply 292.93 metric tonnes of coal, which is 12.8 metric tonnes more than last year," said Partha Bhattacharjee, chairman of Coal India Limited.

He alleged that the state government has not imported sufficient quantity of coal this year, which has caused the crisis. The state government has also not developed the coal blocks that the coal company handed over to the power department, Bhattacharjee said.

Mitra, however, said: "Imported coal is more than three times costlier than indigenous coal. We want to reduce the burden on the power department."

The CPM has taken up the matter to the top level in Delhi. Talking from Delhi, party MP Bangsagopal Choudhury threatened that they will prevent coal transportation from West Bengal, if the coal companies do not increase the state's share in the coal produced in the state.

"We discussed the issue with Union Coal Ministry officials. If the situation does not improve, we will stop loading and transportation of coal from Bengal," said Choudhury.

Heading: Govt to change nomenclature of PTTIs, degrees to be called DEd - Indian Express
Content:
In a rerun of two incidents in March and June, two illegal tanneries were destroyed in a fire in Tiljala near Chinatown, leaving six firefighters severely injured.

Seepching Tannery and Flu Leathers on Matheswatola Road were completely destroyed after the fire broke out at 7.45 am. Initially, 10 fire engines were rushed to the spot but considering the severity of the flames, 10 more were dispatched. The fire was brought under control to some extent after 3 pm.

Around 4 pm, when firefighters were dousing the flames inside the premises, a portion of the floor collapsed and six firefighters were trapped under the debris. They were rescued and taken to the National Medical College. Two of them were admitted in the hospital with 20 per cent burns.

Fire Minister Pratim Chatterjee said the tanneries, set up in residential areas, neither had fire licences nor any fire-safety arrangement. He asked the police to arrest the tannery owners under the West Bengal Fire and Emergency Services Act. One of the owners, A C Lee, fled the place after the incident.

Chatterjee said the fire department will file an FIR against the owner and ask for a forensic report. Chatterjee and Manab Mukherjee, small-scale and cottage industry minister, will conduct a joint survey of the area soon.

Director Fire and Emergency Services Gopal Bhattacharya said: "If the fire had broken out at night, it would have destroyed the entire locality, claiming several lives as lots of leather pieces and chemicals are dumped inside the tanneries. Preliminary investigation reveals that the fire was caused by a short-circuit."

Frequent fires and loss of property have become common in the area, where leather cutting units and illegal tanneries are thriving. In March 2008, a leather factory in Tangra was gutted and five persons had sustained serious burns. In June 2008, a fire had broken out in an illegal leather-cutting unit in a Tiljala building, leaving four persons injured.

Official records reveal that nearly 532 tanneries were initially operating in Tiljala, Topsia and Tangra. Nearly 350 sites in the Calcutta Leather Complex (CTC) at Bantala were allotted to the tanneries for shifting their establishments from the city area. Of these, nearly 250 units have already shifted to the CTC, while the remaining are operating in the city area with the apparent indifference of the administration. No raids are conducted at the illegal units.

The police, however, denied this. "We often carry out raids in the area and seize leather products and chemicals. We will launch an investigation, if any tannery is found illegally operating," said Police Commissioner Gautam Mohan Chakraborty.

Heading: BESU student’s body fished out of Hooghly - Indian Express
Content:
With the future of around 75,000 students hanging in balance after the Calcutta High Court declared the Primary Teachers Training Institutes in the state as illegal on October 1, the state government is keen to change the nomenclature of these institutes.

According to Secretary of the Primary Education Board, West Bengal Debarshi Roy, the degree will be called a Diploma in Education (DEd).

On Wednesday, 58 PTTIs in the state signed a letter of commitment stating that they are under the National Council of Teachers Education (NCTE). Another 80 self-financing PTTIs followed suit on Thursday.

It is not just the name of the institute that is changing. Earlier, a candidate who had cleared the Madhyamik examination was eligible for the course. From now onwards, candidates seeking admission will have to clear higher secondary examination.

The duration of the course will also be increased from the existing one year to two years.

As per the norms of the NCTE, not more than 50 students can be inducted in one institute. However, the state government sought permission for induction of 100-150 students. A delegation of representatives from the state government had visited the NCTE office in Bhubaneswar to discuss these issues.

Sources in the school education department, however, said the NCTE office at Bhubaneswar can only give and collect admission forms. Any policy decision on the issue will be taken by the NCTE office in Delhi and the Ministry of Human Resource and Development.

Meanwhile, students of these institutes demonstrated in front of School Education Minister Partha De in north Bengal.

They threatened the school education department will not be allowed to employ a single teacher unless the government resolves the deadlock.

"We will go to court if necessary. We will also sit in protest in front of the Bikash Bhavan and protest against the education minister wherever he goes," said Pintu Parui, a student leader.

Heading: Dredgers dispatched to Haldia port - Indian Express
Content:
The body of a student of the Bengal Engineering and Science University who had fallen into the Hooghly on Wednesday was fished out on Thursday evening. Subhajit Saha was a second year student of computer science, who accidentally fell into the river at 6 pm. Saha, 19, was a resident of Chinsura in Hooghly district.

Saha, along with five of his friends from the institute, had gone to BE Garden Ghat on Wednesday evening. He tried to jump over to a steamer from the jetty and fell into the river. Neither Saha nor any of his friends could swim.

Police reached the spot at 7.15 pm and launched a search. Two teams of the district traffic police and the disaster management wing of the Kolkata Police tried to trace the teenager till late Wednesday night.

A pall of gloom descended on the institute when his body was brought there on Thursday evening. "He always took part in extra-curricular activities. Hooghly was his favourite hangout," said a student.

"His parents had arrived on Wednesday night. He used to stay in the university hostel," said Biman Bandopadhay, registrar of the university. Many teachers, along with Bandopadhay, had gone to the ghat on Wednesday after hearing about the incident. The university officials said Saha was a bright student.

According to the police, initial investigations revealed it was an accident.

Heading: Trains cancelled over MNS violence - Indian Express
Content:
After remaining worried over the decreasing navigable depth of the Haldia Port, relief is around the corner for the Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT).

Two dredgers are on their way to Haldia after the Centre agreed to dispatch them for the port. The CPM parliamentarian from Haldia, Lakshman Seth, and senior CPM leader Shyamal Chakrabarty had taken up the matter with the Union Minister for Shipping, Road Transport and Highways T R Baalu on Wednesday.

"The minister has also asked the Dredging Corporation of India (DCI) to hire technologically-advanced dredgers from abroad," said Seth.

"One dredger left Paradeep around 5.30 pm, while another left Vizag around 3.30 pm. We expect them to reach Haldia by late tonight," said Rajeev Dube, Deputy Chairman, Haldia Dock Complex, KoPT. The two dredgers will be put to use by Friday.

The Centre has also committed two dredgers from Sethusamudram. One of these needs minor repairs and is likely to be pressed into service in a week. The deployment of the other one is likely to be delayed, as there are some contractual issues involved with the Russian firm from which the DCI had hired it.

The KoPT authorities are also planning to float global tenders to hire dredgers from abroad. This is usually done through the DCI but the Centre has made an exception considering the urgent requirement for Haldia Port. A special arrangement has been worked out to allow the KoPT to directly hire dredgers from abroad. Normally, five dredgers suffice for the port, with one dredger kept on stand by.

"The KoPT authorities are not willing to take any chance and are keen on hiring more dredgers as stand by to meet any emergency," added Dube.

Heading: Tiger strays into Sunderban village - Indian Express
Content:
Eastern Railways cancelled trains on the Patna and Gaya routes on Thursday after violence was reported in certain areas of Bihar.

Violence against north Indian students by Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) in Mumbai had trigerred the protests, during which a compartment of the Danapur Express was set on fire.

Bhagalpur-New Delhi-Vikramshila Express, Howrah-Patna-Janshatabdi Express, Howrah-Haridwar-Puja Special, Howrah Raxual-Mithila Express were cancelled earlier in the day. On Wednesday, the Eastern Railways had cancelled 14 trains running via Gaya and Patna in Bihar.

In the evening, however, the services resumed and the trains from Howrah via Patna and Gaya were on their way. Since then the trains have been running normally, an Eastern Railway official said.

Heading: Farmers to get agriculture info through SMS - Indian Express
Content:
Panic spread in Gosaba area of the Sunderbans in South 24 Parganas after a tiger strayed into a human habitat on Wednesday night.

Locals saw the predator dragging away a cow from a cowshed of the Purba Sonargoaon village on Thursday night, said forest officials. Villagers chased away the tiger, which had swum across the Bidyadhari river to enter the area.

This is the third instance of tiger straying in Gosaba. In September, a tiger had strayed into Jameshpur village of Gosaba and remained elusive for two days until it was captured by the forest department. In June, a Royal Bengal tiger had entered Kumirmari village in the Sunderbans and killed a calf.

On October 22, villagers of Sunderbans submitted a deputation to Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, demanding that they be allowed an entry into the forest area for fishing and catching crabs. Every year, several fishermen fall prey to big cats while making unauthorised entry into the core area of Sunderbans forests.

Heading: On track after a year, aerobridge shuts down again - Indian Express
Content:
A national farmers' network was launched during a Confederation of Indian Industry conference in Kolkata to inform farmers about various developments in field of agriculture like weather forecast, agriculture prices and soil consultation through SMS. Under the network, nearly 20,000 farmers throughout the country across 325 districts will get the SMS services. In West Bengal, 750 registered farmers will avail the services.

During the event, representatives of the state government expressed concerned over increasing the availability of credit for farmers in the state. "Credit requirement of farmers in the state is about 15,000 crores, but the credit availability is only Rs 3000 crore to Rs 4000 crore, " said Sanjeev Chopra, an official of Agriculture department.

He said the Kisan Credit Cards are available to nearly 15 lakhs farmers in the state and the government plans to double it in the 11th Plan period.

Heading: Cleaning fund in pocket, KMC overlooks drains - Indian Express
Content:
The only aerobridge at the international terminus of the Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Airport had to be shut down on Wednesday, hours after it was made operational after a period of over one year. Nearly a year ago, the parking area at the aerobridge had become unusable due to erosion caused by heavy aircrafts. Subsequently, it was shut down for repairs.

"The area beneath the aerobridge had to be repaired layer by layer and thus took a long time," said Airport Authority of India (AAI) officials.

On Wednesday, AAI officials announced that the repair work had been completed and the aerobridge could be used. Just as the bridge was about to be used for a Biman Bangladesh aircraft, it was noticed that the visual docking system of the bridge was not working. The system guides aircrafts towards the bridge with the help of lights. The Biman Bangladesh flight was then guided manually to the bridge. Soon after, the aerobridge was shut down for repairs.

Heading: Chirag win heart, fail to score - Indian Express
Content:
The Solid Waste Management Department (SWMD) of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) remains indifferent towards clearing up heaps of garbage and stagnant water in its several wards.

The department, which plays an important role in controlling the outbreak of vector-borne diseases by destroying potential breeding zones in the city, has been allocated Rs 247.54 crore during this financial year.

According to a health official, there is no coordination between the health department and the SWMD.

"Not only the vector-borne diseases, this year my ward has become enteric-prone due to dirty drains and roads. Water is stagnant in each and every drain. The KMC workers hardly bother to clean the drains," said Javed Ahmed Khan, councillor of ward 65, one of the worst affected by the department's negligence.

The other wards that are in equally pitiable condition are 24, 65, 66 and 40. For past several days, heaps of garbage has not been removed from G J Khan Road (ward 66), Topsia Road (ward 65), Pathuria Road (ward 24).

Officials of the SWMD department, however, claim at least 80 to 110 sweepers have been deployed in every ward for cleaning two times a. The civic body spends around Rs 4 to 6 lakh per month for paying the sweepers in every ward.

"Our ward is short of 40 workers. I had repeatedly asked the SWMD department to deploy more sweepers, but to no avail. Besides, the remaining workers are not fit to do work. Most of them are ill and cannot clean the ward regularly," Khan added.

The chief municipal engineer of the SWMD, Arun Sarkar, does not agree with the situation. "It is impossible that drains and streets remain unclean for several days. The sweepers are sent to every ward twice a day. Even then we will look into the matter," Sarkar said.

The building department of the civic body is also negligent about the disease outbreak.

"At several construction sites, stagnant water is found. We have asked the building department several times to take penal action but nothing has happened," said a senior official.

Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya too washed of his hands saying the civic body has issued a circular to remove stagnant water from construction sites and garages but it will take time for implementation.

Heading: Three points on agenda, Mahindra take on Md Sporting - Indian Express
Content:
Subrata outwits Sukhwinder in battle of coaches

Subrata Bhattacharya did it once again. With seven front-line players missing, he had an uphill task to contain JCT in the I-League match today. He was successful as it ended in a goalless draw at Yuba Bharati Krirangan (YBK).

The match had been billed as a battle of wits between two experienced coaches. Subrata outwitted JCT's Sukhwinder Singh.

The Chirag coach, however, was far from satisfied. The hosts would have won this match hands down had their strikers been right on the money. A penalty miss didn't help their cause either.

Striker Ayan Chowdhury, who came in for S Raleng after the latter had to leave the field following a collision with Anwar Ali in the 17th minute, was the man to be blamed. He wasted three golden opportunities. Dulal Biswas missed the penalty that was awarded after Dawit Singh handled the ball inside the box in the 39th minute.

JCT custodian Karanjit Singh had a very good game and was an aberration in an otherwise insipid show by the visitors. Actually, Sukhwinder didn't have an answer to Subrata's 4-5-1 formation that saw Basudeb Mondal and Mrinmoy Chakrabary do the coordination job in the midfield and Snehashis Chakrabarty operates through the flanks during the counters. At times, the JCT defence was at sixes and sevens.

The visitors, on the other hand, failed to create a single goal-scoring opportunity. Brazilian Eduardo was kept on a tight leash that took the sting out of the Punjab outfit.

Chirag now have five points from as many matches, while JCT move to eight.

Heading: Prose Painting - Indian Express
Content:
Mahindra United coach Derrick Pereira is confident that his team will bounce back in the I-League and the process has started from the last match in which they defeated JCT 1-0 at Ludhiana. He wants to keep the momentum going as his side gears up for the next challenge — Mohammedan Sporting here tomorrow.

All's not well in the hut though. NP Pradeep is yet to recover fully from illness, while Steven Dias is nursing an ankle injury. Both, however, will play as the coach wants to go all out for three points.

"We made a slow start, but it's a long tournament and there's enough scope to come back. Yes, we have to be consistent. Last match was good for us. It showed some improvements. Things will get better from here on," Pereira said after team's practice at Howrah Stadium today.

The Mumbai outfit is languishing in the ninth spot with just three points from four matches, while Md Sporting are placed 11th with two points.

"They (Md Sporting) have good foreigners. But if we can play to our potential, we should win," Pereira said.

Md Sporting, on the other hand, are working overtime to get Theodore Sunday fit for this tie. The Liberian striker appears to be a doubtful starter with an injured knee. Coach Sabbir Ali kept his fingers crossed. "It's a marathon league and Theo is one of our main players. We shouldn't be taking any undue risks at this stage," he said on the match eve.

"Mahindra have India players. But with some luck, we can overpower them. We have to win because we would be playing five away matches after this. So, the onus is on the strikers to convert the chances into goals," Ali observed.

The club management yesterday issued a show cause notice to goalkeeper Naseem Akhtar for allegedly breaching disciplinary codes. "It won't make any impact (to our preparations)," Ali asserted.

Heading: Down Memory Lane - Indian Express
Content:
His contemporaries and his fans, remember Paritosh Sen's magical talent in wielding the pen

A mighty Arjuna tree stands tall in the middle of his village. It alsocolours a young Paritosh Sen's imagination. So much so that it becomes almost an allegory — a symbol of village life. It's branches, where different birds nestle separately, represent the hierarchy of caste and class in his village. In his autobiographical book Jindabahar Lane , Paritosh Sen creates a potent world of imagination and reality, where his reaction to his surroundings is recorded with heartbreaking tenderness, but not soppy sentimentality. "Paritosh Sen had the amazing ability to talk about past without romaticising it. That I believe, is a mark of a great writer," says painter Jogen Chowdhury, who cites Jindabahar Lane as one of his favourite books.

Indeed, for a number of his admirers, the death of Sen is not only a loss of a great painter, but also of "an important Bengali writer of the century". "When it comes to writing, Sen had the advantage of having a painter's eye. He was perceptive of the size and shape, the colour and the texture of the things he described," says artist Suvaprasanna. And he possessed the power to record that vividly too. In Jindabahar Lane and also in his prose collection, Fire and other Images, his evocative style, shines through.

"Sen was equally adept with the pen as the brush, if not more. My father, who was a Urdu poet, is a great admirer of his writing. He considers his work in great esteem," says painter Wasim Kapoor.

Even Satyajit Ray considered Sen to be a great writing talent. "Ray was a great admirer of Sen's writing. And why shouldn't he be? The vivid imagery that his writings evoked would appeal to all filmmakers," says painter Ganesh Haloi, a self-confessed fan of Sen's writings.

His essays on art and his contemporaries make for essential reading for any art aficionado. "Recollections of past and attempts to comprehend the present, is the hallmark of Sen's works, be it his paintings or books. His critiques reflect his beliefs," says Chowdhury. Suvaprasanna treasures the essay that Sen wrote on him in the Bengali publication Desh. "I consider that write up to be one of the most important critique of my works," says the painter.

Moreover, his preoccupation with art history of India made him a unique writer. "His writing on the Kishangarh Radha paintings and Aamsundari are seminal stuff," asserts Haloi. Yet, he rues the fact that very little has been done to promote his work beyond the art circles. "His writings aren't only meant for art students. They make for great literature," says Haloi.

All his admirers agree that what makes Sen one of the most important artists of our times is his conviction that creativity can only exist in correlation with artistic freedom. "His writings endorse freedom as central to the human experience. In this age of hooliganism, that is an important statement," sums up Chowdhury.

Heading: Pretty in Pink - Indian Express
Content:
Market mania and smart publicity mechanisms have rung the knell for old-school art groups

It's not everyday that time finds a match in the human mind. However, when ideas do come from the grey cells of the likes of Paritosh Sen, time is mostly likely to bow out. Exactly what happened after Sen formed the Calcutta Group in 1943 in a bid to get modernism its due in the Indian art milieu steeped in traditional, tried and tested methods of expression. Standing beside him in his endeavour were sculptor Pradosh Das Gupta, painters Gopal Ghose, Nirode Mazumder and Zainul Abedin. The rest, to use a cliché, is history. However, half a century later, art groups, which once used to top the list of priorities of artists like Sen, seem to have fallen out of favour with most contemporary artists.

Art galleries, online art clubs, virtual auctions – with business, visibility and feedback just a click of the mouse away, the brainstorming of art groups evidently have fallen out of step with time. "Things are managed with such clinical precision by public relations firms and art galleries these days. The sort of elaborate planning and debating we used to have might seem outmoded in comparison," says artist Jogen Chowdhury who is still a member of the nearly 40-year-old Calcutta Painters. The likes of Chowdhury misses the discussions and debates which used to be the life force of such groups, but artists today don't share the extreme enthusiasm.

The growing number of artists wanting a slice of the art boom probably find it more sensible to market their works individually with results. "It has now become easy to break into the scene with galleries mushrooming across the country and the city. Therefore there's too much competition around," says painter Wasim Kapoor. Kapoor continues to be a part of the Calcutta Painters like Ganesh Haloi who is a member of the Society of Contemporary Artists. "There is a group unity that still holds us together," says Haloi. Not a case with young painters who would prefer to make statements individually, than establish emerging trends and styles like their predecessors.

While the groups in past was a platform for idea exchange, it also grew in size as artists found it difficult to find a toe-hold in the then restricted market for art all by themselves. "We joined hands because it was important to create a market for what we did as a passion. In contrast, art is almost a sophisticated industry in the country now," says Haloi. Galleries, exhibits, publicity, reviews and purchase – all professionally managed like for most other commodities – have therefore reduced art groups to just their intellectual relevance.

Thought too, seems to have run out of food, as artists say veterans have alienated themselves increasingly. "Previously most fields of culture – art, films, music, literature – used to admit to a symbiotic relationship because their business value was still in a nascent stage unlike today," says artist Suvaprasanna. So, growth needed association and that's how the groups worked. "Experimentation, which often is reduced to gimmicks by amateurs, sells today. In the past, breaking out of a mould needed a concerted effort," says artist Isha Mohammad.

"I wouldn't say people today don't feel for art, as an entity and not a commodity, like they used to before," says Haloi. But it is evident that limelight, which finds its way to the boy-next-door even through reality shows, is addictive. "Art has turned into a giant market now. You can't blame people, if they run after fame and profits by themselves," says Kapoor.

Heading: Former director of health services dies of dengue - Indian Express
Content:
Elizabeth Hurley, who is the spokes-model for Estée Lauder and The Estée Lauder Companies' Breast Cancer Awareness Campaign, is scheduled to be in Mumbai today for the campaign's Global Landmarks Illumination Initiative, where a historic landmark is symbolically covered in pink lights. This year the Taj Palace Hotel & Tower will be illuminated by Hurley in a pink glow. The event will also travel to London where the Tower of London will be covered in the same pink tones.

Fashion magazine L'Officiel's October issue also features the lissome Hurley on the cover. Sporting clothes from Dior's Autumn-Winter and Cruise collections, Hurley can be seen in various hues of pink and purple in support of Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

Heading: Small-scale industries hit hard by global slump - Indian Express
Content:
Former director of Health Services, Punjab, Prithipal Singh died in the early hours of Thursday after developing complications related with dengue. Singh (75) was admitted to the DMCH over a month ago after being tested positive for the mosquito-borne disease.

Talking to Newsline, Dr Harpal Singh, Orthopedecian, DMCH, and his son, said: "He was admitted on September 18 and later developed several complications. He was already suffering from liver and heart-related problems. These problems aggravated after the fever."

He had intestinal bleeding following dengue, doctors said. With this, the death toll of dengue patients has risen to 21.

Prithipal was the first Medical Superintendent of the ESI Hospital, Ludhiana, and is the man behind the establishment of the hospital in 1969. He had also served as Civil Surgeon, Ludhiana, Director Research and Medical Education, Punjab, Director Health and Family Welfare, Punjab among several other key posts.

He is survived by wife Dr Jagjit Kaur, sons Dr Jaspal Singh and Dr Harpal Singh, and daughter Dr Baljit Kaur.

Meanwhile, with 59 fresh cases of dengue being reported from various city hospitals, the total number of confirmed dengue patients has swelled to 1,458 this season. There are 351 suspected cases getting treatment at clinics and hospitals.

According to the Health department officials, 664 dengue patients from other cities and towns are getting treatment at city hospitals and clinics.

Heading: PAU engg students go on strike: V-C summons police - Indian Express
Content:
banks stopping financial help makes Industries see red and cry foul

Although the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Union Finance Ministry are taking measures to prevent a liquidity crisis in industry, it seems that the small-scale industries (SSI) and small and medium enterprises (SME) sectors are still not happy with these measures. The industries are crying foul that banks have stopped financial help and are even reluctant to enhance further the bank limits.

Avtar Singh, General Secretary of the Chamber of Industrial and Commercial Undertakings (CICU), said, "Some sops should be given to the SME sector to keep the industry on rails, which is already reeling under financial crisis." Joint Secretary Upkar Singh endorsed his words.

K.K Seth, spokesperson of United Cycles Parts and Manufacturers' Association, said: "Banks don't want to take risk, especially in the case of SME sector, as a number of them are reeling under crisis due to global meltdown, steel prices and many other issues and hence their credit rating has gone down. Earlier, despite the credit rating, banks were ready to co-operate. But now, they have become strict."

Avtar added, "Money should be released to the banks for paying some subsidy to the SSI units to ease the financial crisis being faced by the industry. The measures being taken are not enough."

The engineering industry representatives say that China has reduced the steel prices by 22,000 dollars, but such a relief is not being given by the Indian industry. Also, the local scrap prices have come down by over 1,000 per tonne due to which the units selling scrap are facing further losses.

Heading: Health Dept officials seize 4.25 quintal of ‘spurious’ khoa - Indian Express
Content:
It seems that the strike called by the students of College of Agricultural Engineering at PAU did not go down well with Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang. This was evident from the fact that the V-C, who otherwise enjoys a soft and liberal image, ordered the police to be called into the campus to remove the striking students without even listening to them.

The students had declared their strike, which was in its second day on Thursday, by staging a dharna outside the V-C office. The agitating students insisted that despite orders by the V-C, they were not consulted while the date sheets were decided. Moreover, the attitude of Dr P K Gupta, Dean, College of Agricultural Engineering, was rather rude towards the students.

Officiating dean of the college Dr V K Sehgal said the allegations were "totally false". He said in any university, the students are never consulted while the date sheets are made and neither are they changed on the whims of the students. "Basically, it is one students who are ruining the future of all other students," he said.

On his attitude towards the students Dr Gupta commented, "It is now easy to please to every one." The summoning of the police was an unusual development, as previously, the campus had witnessed even bigger and more vociferous agitation by students. Besides, the university also enjoys a track record of not allowing the police to interfere especially where the students are concerned. Last month, students from all the colleges of the university, led by the College of Agriculture, had boycotted classes for almost three days. They had also held rallies and raised slogans against the V-C, yet no police was called in. But today, only 100 students sat silently outside the V-C office, when the police was called in to handle the issue.

Incidentally, Dr Kang, who was waiting outside his office when the students came marching towards the Thapar Hall, asked the students very curtly to "stop the nonsense and go back." The agitating students were clearly taken aback and while they were working out their strategy, the V-C ordered his subordinates to inform the police.

The students, however, refused to step back and instead sat on a dharna which ended at the noon. Around two dozens policemen armed with canes appeared in minutes, without any female personnel, to handle the girls who too were sitting there, in case such a condition arose.

But the situation did not take an ugly turn as the students hesitate to indulge in any sloganeering that could provoke the police into action. In the absence of any other potential leader, Amir Hameed Wani, already at logger heads with the authorities, emerged as the leader.

As per PAU officials, Wani had thrice been granted mercy plea but he had not been able to clear his courses. After the strike on October 22, the university officials had terminated his provisional admission to the university and had asked him to leave the campus. "Out of the total 160 credit hours 40 that I had cleared at my previous university have not been added up in my Overall Credit Point Average," said Wani.

Protesting against what they termed an 'Unfriendly examination schedule' the students had skipped many of their exams. The students had strategically bunked the examination in which they felt that ample time for preparation was not provided.

The students of third-year engineering had dropped four examinations, while those of the second-year had dropped two. If the strike continued, the students of first- year will skip their third consecutive exam on October 24.

Heading: Garbage piles up near Baba Bhan Singh’s memorial - Indian Express
Content:
A team of doctors led by Dr Yashpal Mehta, Assistant Civil Surgeon, conducted a raid at the railway station and seized 4.25 quintals of khoa suspected to be spurious. The raid was conducted at the behest of Dr Satpal Sharma, District Civil Surgeon. The team also included Dr G P Mangla (District Epidemiologist) and Harjot Singh (Food Inspector).

"We received information that some sweet makers have been procuring spurious khoa from cities of Uttar Pradesh. Acting on it, we reached the railway station at 9 pm yesterday. At 12.30 am, 4.25 quintals of khoa were unloaded at the platform number 2 by Hemkund Express and Shalimar Express. The consignment was in nine big packs. Six of them were on the name of Keshar Sweets while three were on the name of S Kumar. Around 5 am, a young man named Raju arrived and loaded the khoa in an auto rickshaw. Our team started following him and seized the material when he unloaded it at the Lovely Sweets workshop. We have sent three samples for testing, as we suspect it to be spurious," said Dr Yashpal Mehta.

The khoa came from Muzaffar Nagar. Dr Mehta said, "In the past, we had seized spurious khoa sent from cities in UP. This one is from Muzaffar Nagar. We have kept the khoa in police custody."

Charanjit Singh, the owner of Lovely Sweets and president of Ludhiana Halwai Association, said: "The khoa is totally pure. We haven't committed any mistake. To fulfil the increasing demand of sweets during festival days, we have to arrange for it from other cities. The sweets which we make are also consumed by our own family. We always sell pure products."

Heading: Train cancellations leave many in lurch - Indian Express
Content:
Even after a protest by the members of Maha Sabha, the municipal corporation authorities have not cleared the garbage lying near the memorial of kalapani martyr Baba Bhan Singh near Sunet village.

Maha Sabha members had staged the protest against the authorities on October 11, but not much has changed since then. Jaswant Jheerakh, general secretary of Maha Sabha, said, "After the media highlighted the issue, some garbage was lifted. But it stopped after a few days and now again a big heap is lying near the memorial site."

He added: "This shows a lack of concern of the MC towards a great martyr who laid down his life for the country. We had given complaints in writing also to the commissioner of zone D. But now it seems that we will have to lodge our protest at the MC office itself."

Area councillor K L Chabra, meanwhile, passed the buck to the officers, saying he had been asking them to clean this site again and again, but to no avail.

Members of Maha Sabha had raised this memorial with voluntary donations in 2005 and had even cleared the garbage lying at the site. However, its surroundings are still stinking.

Heading: Artmosphere to host photo exhibition - Indian Express
Content:
Gurcharan Singh Dhamija, a resident of Muradabad, who had come to the city to meet his relatives, is now finding it difficult to reach back home. Despite train reservation, Dhamija who has been making rounds of the railway station, does not know whether his train — 2318 Akal Takht Express — is still running or has been cancelled.

Dhamija is not alone. Hundreds of such people can be seen frantically making inquiries at the railway station. The cancellation of Bihar-bound trains has created a lot of problems for the passengers which is being aggravated by the fact that no clear-cut information on the details of the train is available at the station. And while passengers are at loss, so are the railway authorities who have had to refund tickets worth Rs 2 lakh over the last two days.

Ram Sikander, one such harried passenger, complained, "I wanted to be home for Diwali and had made my booking well in advance. My village is near Patna, but now I do not know whether my train is on time or not." Sikander further complained, "The passengers are not getting the full information from the enquiry counters, as they themselves have no information yet. The authorities should inform the general public so that they could have an alternative arrangement if something like this happens."

Another Bihar-bound passenger, Rakesh Kumar, and his group say that the that the railway authorities were not providing any correct information to the passengers. "The worst is when the officials announce the cancellation in the evening leaving no option for the passengers to cancel their tickets. The queue for cancellation of tickets is much longer than for buying it."

The passengers even got troubled with the ill-treatment of the clerks while claiming refund of their reserved tickets. One of the employees at the station said that there is nobody to guide the general public in a right way and the clerks were passing the passengers from one counter to another, which troubled the passengers even more. It is true that the counters were opened for the benefit of the general public, but there also they get nothing more than harassment and trouble.

A.S. Salaria, Station superintendent, said that they have no information regarding the cancellation of the trains till now as there was no message from the headquarters. "So it is very difficult to comment on the position of the trains but Sealdah Express 2317 from Sealdah to Amritsar has been cancelled," he said, and added, "Route for some trains like Punjab Mail, Howraha Express, Dhanbad Express and Himgiri Express have been changed. They will not go through Patna but Gaya."

Heading: Sacred Heart students enthral audience - Indian Express
Content:
In first-of-its-kind photo exhibition in city, Artmosphere, the contemporary art gallery here, is hosting works of photojournalists working in Punjab.

The two-week exhibition opens on Friday with the collected works of Gurpreet Singh, a senior photojournalist working with The Hindustan Times in Ludhiana.

Giving this information, Sukhvir Singh, the curator of the gallery, said the solo-exhibition to run for a week will be followed by collected work of others in the next week. With no fixed theme, the photographs were selected just on the basis of their having been clicked in Punjab, he said.

These are the photographs depicting the state with all its hues and shades, as seen by the photojournalists gathering images for the newspapers during the course of their work. What lends these photographs a unique bent with being present at the right place and at the right moment than the technicalities and mere aesthetics as these images have meaning in particular contexts, said Sukhvir Singh.

Taking a viewer on a journey of the state with a perspective of someone else's eye, the exhibition will be a visual treat at the same time, he said.

Heading: CAPE makes a case for pollution free Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
Students of Sacred Heart Convent Senior Secondary School, Sarabha Nagar, on Thursday enthralled the audience on the second day of the school's four-day annual function. Brig P.R. Deshpande, army station commander, was the chief guest in the morning function.

The students of class IV performed different cultural items and displayed their talent. They thanked their parents through a melody. The youngsters enacted an English play "Bold and the beautiful" conveying the message to the masses that humility went a long way and it was one's conduct that was responsible for one's destiny. The synchronised action song "Synergy" was addressed to the parents to let their children grow and bloom.

Jose Paul, an educational consultant, advised the parents to identify their child's potential and motivate him or her to aim high on life. The youngsters displayed their acrobatic ability in "Skills and drills," a performance in gymnastics.

Brig P.R. Deshpande said, "Children are more energetic and better visionaries than parents. Listen to them and prize their words." He congratulated the meritorious students of class X and awarded them with trophies and certificates. The programme ended with an appreciation of the Indian culture even as a colourful folk dance "Dandiya" was presented by the students.

The evening show was hosted by the students of class VIII. Priyank Bharti, additional deputy commissioner, was the chief guest. Dressed up in colourful costumes, the children entertained parents as well as guests. A play "Mother's Day" very aptly depicted the role that a mother plays in every family but is not shown any gratitude. It was a straight message for the family members to recognize the efforts of a mother, who builds a family with her love and care.

While "Unity in diversity" showcased the fusion of Indian folk dances — Haryanvi, Rajasthani, Punjabi and Gujarati dances — in a perfect blend, vibrant costumes and synchronized steps made it a breath-taking performance. A dance drama, "Sarvdharm Sukham," was also appreciated by all.

Heading: Sri Aurobindo College holds biz quiz contest - Indian Express
Content:
Care for Animals and Protection for Environment (CAPE), India, has urged the city residents to celebrate a pollution-free Diwali.

"The sound and smoke emitted from the crackers not only pollute the atmosphere and pose a threat to the lives of asthmatics and heart patients but are also stressful for animals like dogs, cats, donkeys, cows and birds etc. These do not understand that the deafening noise and fireworks are a part of celebration," said a release issued by CAPE India.

Futher the NGO said that by buying crackers, the fireworks industry is encouraged which employs millions of children in their factories, exposing them to harmful chemicals used in its manufacturing under deplorable conditions, said the release.

The NGO also wants that animals should be kept indoors on Diwali day. "Please ensure that your companion animal is wearing a collar with identity tag, as there are chances that it may try to escape from home and get lost," added the release.

The NGO urged the residents to not to burst crackers, especially with loud sound and spread fire on roadsides and narrow lanes. "And completely stop bursting crackers after 10.30 p.m," said a release.

Heading: Foreign students to take PU’s own language test - Indian Express
Content:
The B.Com-I students of Sri Aurobindo College of Commerce and Management organised College Quiz - 2008. Harman Bajaj, Mridul Jain, Amanjot Singh, Keshav, Geeshu Sikka, Ekta Madaan, Supreet Kaur and Avneet Kaur, students of B. Com (Ist year), organised the quiz contest.

The students of the first year participated in the quiz competition. Four teams participated in the quiz consisting of six rounds. Different areas covered in the quiz are business knowledge, general awareness, quantitative aptitude, science, geography, national and international affairs and economic issues.

Team A was declared winner, Team B stood second, Team D came third while Team C bagged the fourth position. Dr Prem Kumar, principal of the college, and all the faculty members were also present on the occasion.

Dr Prem Kumar congratulated the organising team and all participating students and urged them to make this a routine affair in college activities.

Heading: Plea for stepping up security outside temples - Indian Express
Content:
Indian students applying to foreign universities are usually made to take English proficiency tests, mainly International English Language Testing System (IELTS) and Test For English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL).

The Panjab University has now decided to return the favour. Foreign students enrolling themselves here would now have to pass the university's own English proficiency test. The test would be compulsory and if a student fails, the degree would not be given.

This is probably one of the first instances where an Indian university has introduced a mandatory English proficiency test.

Professor Shelley Walia, Dean Foreign Students, explained the purpose: "We often find that foreign students, who have completed their degrees, have no clue of the language. The mode of instruction here is primarily English so it is appropriate that the student has a basic understanding and skill in the language."

Whether the test would have minimum passing marks or a grading system of evaluation is yet to be determined. All students, who are not the citizens of India and are studying in the Panjab University, would have to take this test whether they come from English-speaking countries or not.

Every year, around 300 foreign students apply to the Panjab University. Several of them are from the Middle East, Bhutan and Africa. Of late, a lot of students have come from Afghanistan. This is mainly attributed to reinstation of a liberal government in Kabul and the Centre's proactive policies to foster friendly ties with the Hamid Karzai Government.

The university has, meanwhile, made entry into the Ph d. course strictly on the basis of merit. An exemption, however, has been allowed to the foreign teaching professionals seeking admission in higher education.

Prof Walia said: "The teaching professionals, in a way, are mature enough and have experience. We have, therefore, exempted them from the entrance exam. They can directly enroll with us on the basis of their experience and educational qualifications."

Heading: Arya College shines at youth festival - Indian Express
Content:
Dinesh Goel, a resident of BRS Nagar, filed a writ petition in Punjab and Haryana High Court, in which he has made a case for deploying police security outside the temples of BRS Nagar.

The court has directed the deputy commissioner, Ludhiana, to look into the matter. Goel meanwhile said that BRS Nagar was having three temples such as Durga Mata Mandir, Prachin Sitla Mandir and Shri Luxmi Naryana Mandir.

Goel said after the incidents of bomb blasts, police security near temples was a must. He also stated in his writ that no bicycle should be allowed to be parked within 100m radius of temple.

Heading: Rosebys starts retail operations - Indian Express
Content:
Students of Arya College here once again proved their mettle at the Panjab University Zonal youth and heritage festival held at GNN College, Doraha by bagging 24 prizes in various categories.

The college principal S M Sharma and incharge, women's section, Prof Paramjit Kaur Pannu told press reporters that the college had participated in 35 events and had won 24 prizes. Sharma congratulated the winners and the professors in charge of various events and exhorted them to bring home more such laurels in future too.

Reflecting an enthusiastic team spirit, the college excelled in group events too. In the prestigious one-act play competition, the college won third position with Deepika Rautela (M.Com-I) winning second prize in the individual best-actor category.

Similarly, students brought alive the cultural heritage of Punjab through their prize-winning performance of Malwai Gidda. Second positions were won in Group Dance, Group Song and Quiz.

Sharma congratulated Dr V.B. Sudhir, Dean, Co-curricular Activities, Dr S.P. Singh, Joint Dean, CCA, Sukshan Walia, Incharge CCA (women section), Prof Surinder Khanna and other professors in charge for their inspiring efforts in bringing out their hidden talent in the students.

Heading: Factions clash at PU, once again - Indian Express
Content:
Rosebys Interiors India Ltd today started its Indian retail operations by launching its stores in the state of Punjab. The company simultaneously opened four stores in Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula and two in city of Ludhiana on Thursday.

The store is having home decor and life-style products. Speaking on the occasion, Nikhil Sen, Director, Rosebys India Interior Ltd, said: "With organised retailing growing at more than 30% annually, there is a huge untapped market for the home décor and life-style stores in India, which is pegged around Rs 10,000 crores. We are targeting this space across the country to deliver world-class products and shopping experience to consumers. We are in the process of building a powerful brand and are poised to have a dominant presence in the country's retail arena".

Heading: After long wait, PU gets Sports Director - Indian Express
Content:
An old animosity between factions of Student Organisation of Panjab University (SOPU) and Haryana Student Association (HSA) turned ugly right outside the Botany department at the Panjab University campus today.

Two persons reportedly sustained injuries in the group clash and were identified as Sanjay Kumar and Surinder, former students of GSSD College in Sector 32 and HSA supporters. Police arrested former SOPU president, Uday Bhan, and Ankush, a student of Law department, from the spot.

Sources said Sanjay and one Sumit were involved in a tiff with SOPU supporters during the college elections last month. University Police Post in-charge Uday Pal Singh said Sanjay had come to the university on Wednesday to seek admission in the Physical Education department. "The members of SOPU saw him and decided to take revenge," he added.

Sources, however, said the groups had prefixed the clash and designated a time and venue for it. "About 30 HSA supporters reached the students' centre at 3 pm armed with swords and other weapons. When SOPU supporters reached the spot, the HSA supporters attacked them. The SOPU supporters ran towards the Botany department where their other members were waiting," sources added.

Eyewitnesses said the clash lasted 15 minutes until the police intervened. The gates of the university were immediately closed.

The members, however, managed to flee after scaling the wall of the campus opposite PGI. The police immediately rushed the two injured to Government Multi-Specialty Hospital in Sector 16. Doctors attending to them stated their condition was stable.

Prof Naval Kishore, Dean Students Welfare, said: "The students who are involved in the incident are outsiders and I am still to enquire about the matter and get details."

Police have registered a case against SOPU party president Barinder Singh Dhillon, president of campus from SOPU Sahil Nanda, Uday Bhan and Ankush, under Sections 147,148,149,323 and 506 of the IPC. Besides the two arrested, the others are still at large.

Heading: 'Gilchrist remarks on Sachin a marketing strategy' - Indian Express
Content:
Finally, after a wait of eight years, the 'headless' Sports Department of Panjab University has found a suitable candidate in the form of Dr Charanjit Singh Grewal. After Dr Ajmer Singh, PU Sports had been functioning without a proper Director of Sports due to lack of qualified and suitable candidate as earlier told by Vice Chancellor, V C Sobti. Now, the long wait is over and today he was sworn as the Director of Sports, Physical Education.

Talking to Newsline, Dr Charanjit Singh said that his main agenda is to bring up PU sports up to the level of other universities in India. He also added that scientific sports back-up is a must for any sportsperson to excel in his field. "We will try to procure good equipments and provide it to the sportspersons so that the level of PU sports is at par with other universities. I would make sure that the sportspersons get their due. And we will provide incentive money to motivate sportspersons to do well. We would also request respective principals of schools and colleges to provide ample facilities and funds so that atleast one players can atleast excel in one sports in that institution," said Charanjit, who had earlier worked as the assistant professor in physical education and sports at Panjab Engineering College, Chandigarh for 20 years. He also rued the lack of qualified coaches in PU. "Yes, it is a big problem and to overcome that we will try to recruit the best coaches. We will try to rope in atleast 10 coaches for 15 different games," said the newly appointed Director of Sports who has done his Masters in Physical Education from Panjab University.

Heading: Golf legend Ballesteros serious before third brain surgery - Indian Express
Content:
Former Indian Chief Selector Dilip Vengsarkar on Friday described Australian vice-captain Adam Gilchrist's remarks on Sachin Tendulkar's honesty in his autobiography as just a "marketing strategy".

"You have to write something sensational to sell a book," Vengsarkar said.

"I think it's a marketing strategy that Adam Gilchrist has adopted. Very unfortunate, but a fact," the former Indian captain told a private TV Channel.

Gilchrist in his autobiography 'True Colours', scheduled to be released next week, questioned Tendulkar's honesty in the 'Monkeygate' controversy during the Sydney Test.

The former wicket-keeper said Tendulkar had initially told the hearing that he could not hear what was said, he was "certain he was telling the truth" because he was "a fair way away".

But during the appeal which followed, Tendulkar said that Harbhajan used a Hindi term that sounded like "monkey" to Australian ears.

"In the Australian mentality, we play it hard and are then quick to shake hands and leave it all on the field. Some of our opponents don't do it that way. Sachin Tendulkar, for instance, can be hard to find for a changing room handshake after we have beaten India. Harbhajan can also be hard to find," Gilchrist added.

Heading: Aussies were very defensive, says Pak coach Lawson - Indian Express
Content:
Golf legend Seve Ballesteros is in a serious condition and is to undergo a third round of brain surgery.

The Madrid hospital where the Spanish golf star is being treated confirmed that the operation would go ahead to try to remove the rest of his brain tumour, the Sky News reported.

A spokesman for La Paz Hospital said: "Ballesteros remains in a serious and stable condition and will undergo a new operation."

He said the tumour was in a particularly difficult area for surgeons to reach, adding: "It is located in an area that requires a very thorough approach of great complexity."

Doctors said the 51-year-old is suffering from an oligoastrocytoma - a tumour that affects two types of brain cell and spreads diffusely inside the brain cavity. Dr Geoff Pilkington, a tumour expert at the UK's University of Portsmouth, said the tumour was very difficult to eradicate but survival time could be improved by radiotherapy followed by chemotherapy.

He said it was difficult to say how long he might survive without knowing more about the tumour, which will have been classified from one to four on a grade of seriousness.

The hospital declined to reveal the tumour's grade. "I think it's going to be at least a three because the mixed tumours usually are," he added.

"They generally develop into a high grade tumour from which a patient will eventually die. This is not good. The likelihood is that he will die from the tumour at some stage."

The star, who collected 87 titles before knee and back problems forced him to retire last year, underwent major brain surgery earlier this month.

He was admitted to hospital and the brain tumour diagnosed on October 6, after he collapsed and briefly lost consciousness at Madrid airport.

The first operation was followed by a second round of surgery to ease a build-up of fluid on his brain after he took a turn for the worse.

Ballesteros won the British Open in 1979, 1984 and 1988 and became the first European to win the Augusta Masters in 1980, a title he repeated in 1983.

Heading: 'I always admired Sachin, never called him a liar' - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistan cricket coach Geoff Lawson is amazed at the lack of aggression displayed by the Australian pace attack, and said Brett Lee did not have the height to trouble Indian batsmen on their own pitches.

The Pakistan coach said he could not understand why the Australian quicks, with the exception of Peter Siddle with the first ball of his Test career, did not try to intimidate the Indian batsmen with short-pitched bowling.

"It was a different game when India was bowling, a different ball and a different pitch," the 'Sydney Morning Herald' quoted Lawson, as saying.

"The Australians were very defensive. They need to be more aggressive with the ball. I was amazed in the second innings that they didn't seem to bowl a bouncer in the first five overs," he said.

"If someone didn't bowl me a bouncer in the first five overs I would be pretty sure I wasn't going to get one. Gautam Gambhir was charging down the wicket at the pacemen. He hooks and cuts in the air, that is how you get him out in one-day cricket and I don't see why Test cricket would be any different," Lawson added.

Lawson, a former NSW bowling coach, believes Lee needs to find other ways to succeed on India's unresponsive pitches because he does not deliver the ball from a high trajectory, unlike the steepling 20-year-old Ishant Sharma.

Asked what Lee needed to do to improve, Lawson said: "He needs to be a foot taller. They are flat wickets, he slides on, and he is not doing anything much with it."

Lawson said he intended to complete his contract with Pakistan, who by next January's landmark series against arch rivals India will not have played a Test for 13 months because of a succession of terrorist bombings in the country.

Heading: Sachin might play in Australian T20 league - Indian Express
Content:
Stung by a barrage of criticism, retired Australian wicketkeeper Adam Gilchrist denied calling Sachin Tendulkar a 'bad sport' and a 'liar' in his upcoming autobiography, claiming that he was misinterpreted by the media.

Gilchrist said all is well between him and Tendulkar after he rang up the Indian batting maestro to explain how excerpts from his autobiography had been quoted out of context by newspapers. He said the conversation with Tendulkar has left him a relieved man.

"There were headlines around the cricketing globe on Friday suggesting that I had accused Indian batting great Sachin Tendulkar of being a bad sport and also that he had lied when giving evidence in the Harbhajan Singh racial vilification hearing earlier this year.

"Neither of these accusations are true and I felt strongly enough on this to immediately ring Sachin once it was brought to my attention, to explain to him. I am pleased to say that at the conclusion of our chat, the same respect Sachin and I have always had for each other continues to exist," Gilchrist said.

Rattled by the furore that has virtually turned into a backlash in India ever since the controversial excerpts came out, Gilchrist said a couple of sentences from an entire chapter were used to script a sensational story.

"The headlines arose from the manner in which some journalists interpreted a couple of points I have made in an about-to-be released autobiography," he said in a column for and Indian English daily.

"In the book I mention that a cultural difference between our team and that of the Indians was the importance of shaking hands with the opposition after a loss. From my experience it seemed this routine wasn't as important to some oppositions as it was in Australia, where it is drilled into us from an early age," Gilchrist explained.

The former stumper said he stood by his comments on Tendulkar and Harbhajan Singh being hard to find for a handshake after a match, but this did not imply that he considered them a bad sport.

He clarified that his comments were only aimed at highlighting the cultural differences between the two sides. "I made the comment that Sachin and Harbhajan were sometimes not around to shake hands. Whether that is right or wrong is not my point. It was more the cultural differences I was trying to highlight, which it's fair to say, have been integral in most disputes or flare-ups between these two proud nations."

"Nowhere do I accuse Sachin of being bad sport," he said. He is drawing flak for reopening the 'monkey-gate' saga which has been set aside as a closed chapter by both the teams but Gilchrist insisted that he merely "stated the facts" and never called Tendulkar a liar as has been reported.

"...I obviously had to address it in the book as it was a huge issue last summer and too big to ignore. That said, my only reference to it was recall the way the events unfolded from the initial hearing, the night the match finished, through to the final judicial hearing a few weeks later," wrote Gilchrist.

"All I stated are the facts that everyone knows, that initially Sachin had mentioned he wasn't sure what Harbhajan had said, then later confirmed his support when Harbhajan said he'd used a Hindi word in the heated exchange with Symonds. Nowhere do I accuse Sachin of lying," said Gilchrist.

The celebrated keeper said he had the utmost respect for Tendulkar. "To have spoken directly with Sachin about there matters was a great relief for me. I have always admired his amazing cricketing ability and have spoken regularly about how I believe he has set the finest example of how to handle fame and the extraordinary public profile that comes with being an Indian cricketing superstar."

Gilchrist hoped that his clarification on the matter would put an end to the furore. "I have always enjoyed touring here, and most importantly have many strong friendships in India. For those reasons and for my personal friendship with Sachin, I was most concerned that a few off-the-mark headlines and interpretations of my book could possibly sour these friendships. Thankfully that hasn't occurred and I look forward to visiting these shores both as a cricketer and personally for many years to come," he said.

Heading: It’s not all over for Australia: Chappell - Indian Express
Content:
Cricket Australia (CA) will invite international stars such as Sachin Tendulkar to compete in the domestic Twenty20 competition from 2009.

Australia, South Africa and New Zealand have also put their heads together in a bid to establish a T20 competition for the southern hemisphere, to be launched by 2011, the Daily Telegraph reported.

"CA (is) ... encouraging international stars from overseas to play in each side and increasing promotional support in a move to make the tournament a bigger bash," the game's national ruling body said on Friday in a statement.

"Cricket Australia's Board, meeting in Melbourne this week for two days of Board and Annual General Meeting discussions, has approved that CA's management work with counterparts in South Africa and New Zealand to develop a regional T20 contest built on city-based, franchise-owned teams."

CA Chief executive James Sutherland said the southern hemisphere concept had been developed over the past 18 months.

"Regional-level T20 cricket played at the level immediately below international cricket has shown it can capture the public imagination and create new audiences for cricket," he said.

"But as we have seen in India, it needs critical mass to generate major public excitement and the regional concept we have been charged with developing provides that critical mass."

India's hugely successful Indian Premier League domestic competition featured Australian and other international guest players earlier this year.

The southern hemisphere T20 competition is still at a concept stage. It is based on having a yet-to-be determined number of franchises in an Africa-centred eastern conference and a similar western conference with an Australasian focus".

The top teams from each conference would contest finals. "Timing would complement IPL timing, creating opportunity for Indian players to participate," CA said.

Heading: Draw leaves Anand on the threshold - Indian Express
Content:
Banging on the doors of badminton's world top-10 and playing her first world-level event in India, Saina Nehwal is expected to do what Paes-Bhupathi do for tennis in the Davis Cup — start a tie assuring a 1-0 lead — with which India can push oppositions into tight psychological corners.

Nehwal starts off on her latest assignment at the BWF World Junior Championship here in Pune in the mixed team event. The more important of the four group ties of the team event scheduled for October 24-27 will see the 18-year-old take on singles specialists from Hong Kong and Singapore; Russia and Sri Lanka are the relative minnows.

"With Saina playing, you can start one match up. She can even chip in for the mixed doubles and women's doubles," says Guru Sai Dutt, India's top singles player, who himself is in good form after his title at the recent Commonwealth Youth Games.

Ranked eighth in the team event, India will look to better their previous showing of quarter-final appearances, and Nehwal, who's had a tremendous run in the seniors, looks likely to blunt rivals with the crowds rooting for her. They surprised her by packing the stadium for three days of the CYG, and Nehwal insists they'll mean more motivation, less pressure.

The drift, caused by the stadium A/C, has rendered stroke-making unpredictable. Nehwal admits she was caught unawares in her final against Sikki Reddy a week ago. "But it's the same for everyone, so it won't matter much."

She's been on the road since August now, and the sheer hectic nature of the event could make her task difficult. "I don't want to remember the previous tournaments as just thinking will make me mentally tired. This is a new event, and I'm ready," she maintains.

Nehwal's journey into the top flight started with the World Juniors at Incheon two years ago (that was also her last junior tourney), when she unexpectedly stormed into the final before losing to Chinese Wang Yihan. "It might be a junior event, while I've moved onto seniors. But I'd lost that final in the individual category, remember," she stresses.

The Chinese, as secretive as ever about which bunch they have brought, remain formidable opponents. Saina Nehwal, though, will be the name to beat for any junior from any part of the world at this competition.

Heading: Pakistan dismiss Lawson as coach - Indian Express
Content:
Viswanathan Anand inched closer to the World Chess Championship title after playing out a draw in the seventh game against Vladimir Kramnik of Russia on Thursday.

Having won three games and drawn four game, the Indian leads 5-2 and needs only three more draws in the remaining five games to take the title yet again.

The seventh round was not high on adrenaline as Kramnik resorted to the Slav defence, an opening that has served Anand well.

This did not yield any advantage for Anand as Kramnik went for regulation exchanges. By the 16th move, two minor pieces and a pawn was off the board and Kramnik, was never in real danger.

Anand took a pawn on the 36th move and reached a king pawn endgame where the extra pawn of white was not of much consequence. The peace was signed immediately.

Heading: Chandrayaan-1 shifted to 2nd orbit, condition healthy: ISRO - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to nail Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray, the Mumbai Police appear to have more than his slogans that indicate his involvement in the violence on October 19 and later. Stating that the police have "enough substantial evidence to establish Raj's involvement in mobilising supporters well in advance", the remand copy moved before the Kalyan Magistrate's court on Wednesday cites text messages and phone calls that "could have originated from" Raj's phone to various MNS leaders.

While seeking his custody, the argument of the state's prosecution was that Raj and his party workers were, for the past few months, actively "conspiring" against a section of society. The messages ask MNS leaders and shakha pramukhs to unite against "outsiders," the remand copy states.

Special Public Prosecutor Rohini Salian, confirming that the state sought to probe into his role in a "conspiracy", said there was a pattern to these text messages. "They are all inducing the Maharashtrians to unite and fight for their rights. A few messages also spoke about a clean-up drive," Salian said.

MNS sources said they were aware that the Government was trying to charge Raj for criminal conspiracy. "We will maintain before the court that Raj had not made any call for violence as he had not spoken till late on Sunday evening, hours after the applicants for the Railway Board Exams were assaulted at railway stations," said advocate Santosh Sawant from Raj's legal team.

On Wednesday, the prosecution had argued that Raj was creating law and order problems. On its part, the defence counsel had held that there was no direct evidence to prove that it was at Raj's instance that MNS activists went on the rampage. Raj has been booked under various sections of the Indian Penal Code and Bombay Police Act for rioting, inciting communal tensions and unlawful assembly.

On Wednesday, an hour after Raj got bail, prominent MNS leader Shirish Parkar and 13 other leaders were arrested by the Kherwadi police in a case related to rioting and instigating a mob at Bandra court where Raj was to be produced after his arrest at Ratnagiri. "But these leaders were not even present on the spot at the time of Raj's presentation," said advocate Prashant Pansare, representing Parkar and others. Parkar and six others were released on bail on Thursday.

With inputs from Swatee Kher

Heading: To cover 15 kms in Delhi, Patil uses a chopper - Indian Express
Content:
In its movement towards the moon, India's first moon mission spacecraft Chandrayaan-1, launched on Wednesday from Sriharikota, aboard the PSLV-XL, was on Thursday morning lifted to its second orbit.

The spacecraft is scheduled to lock in on the moon's orbit - 386,000 km from the earth - on November 8 after further orbit changing maneuvers, including a crucial mid-course correction and a transfer into the lunar orbit trajectory.

"The first orbit-raising maneuvers of Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft was performed at 09:00 hrs IST on October 23, 2008 when the spacecraft's 440 Newton Liquid Engine was fired for about 18 minutes," said ISRO officials on Thursday.

The commands for the orbit raising maneuvers were sent to the spacecraft from the Spacecraft Control Centre at ISRO Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network center at Peenya in Bangalore.

"With this engine firing, Chandrayaan-1's apogee (furthest point from earth) has been raised to 37,900 km, while its perigee (nearest point) has been raised a little, to 305 km," an ISRO statement said.

In its current orbit, the spacecraft will take about 11 hours to go once around the earth. When launched on Wednesday PSLV-XL put the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft in an elliptical orbit with a perigee of 255 km and an apogee of 22,860 km - orbiting the earth once in about six and a half hours.

Both the Space Control Centre and the Deep Space Network (DSN) at Bylalu outside Bangalore have tracked the spacecraft, received signals and sent commands to the spacecraft which is in a healthy condition, ISRO said.

The spacecraft will lock in on the moon's orbit on November 8 at the point of intersection with Chandrayaan-1's orbit after further intermediate orbit changing moves.

"The major maneuver of the mission, called lunar orbit insertion leading to lunar capture is carried out at the peri-selene (nearest point to the moon) part of the spacecraft's trajectory," ISRO has stated.

Heading: Rae Bareli land row: Bureaucrat suspended - Indian Express
Content:
On a day when various non-BJP parties demanded action against the Hindu Jagran Manch and other Hindutva organisations alleged to have a hand in the Malegaon blasts, the BJP slammed the "non-BJP forces" for "dragging the name of nationalist organisations in the terror attack" while the RSS smelt a "political conspiracy" in the whole episode.

BJP general secretary Vinay Katiyar alleged that politics was behind the allegations and demanded a CBI inquiry into the episode. "This is an old case. It's only due to the approaching elections that such allegations are being levelled. Let the accused be arrested, and let there be a CBI inquiry into the whole episode," said Katiyar.

The RSS, on the other hand, said there was a "conspiracy to malign Hindu organisations". "The charges against Hindu organstions are utterly false and malicious. Violence and blasts must be condemned. But we also condemn the project to malign various Hindu organisations," said former RSS spokesperson Ram Madhav.
