Heading: Six dud firms to transfer money to Virbhadra, family - Indian Express
Content:
The first of Arvind Kejriwal's planned daily janta durbars collapsed an hour after it started Saturday, after a heaving crowd of over 20,000 people threatened to physically swamp the chief minister and his cabinet colleagues, and the meeting teetered on the edge of disintegrating into complete chaos.

Kejriwal and Urban Development Minister Manish Sisodia were forced to retreat into the secretariat building about an hour after the durbar started at 9 am, leaving the other ministers attempting to hear the people's complaints.

The chief minister said he was in danger of being crushed by the crowd, and announced that the durbar was being suspended until the government was able to plan better and put proper arrangements in place.

Standing on the roof of the reception wing of the secretariat, Kejriwal told the crowd behind police barricades: "I accept that there were problems with the arrangements. I am deeply sorry that we could not listen to all your problems. People climbed on to the chair and table at which I was seated, and I could have been crushed if I had not left... We will come back to you with full arrangements and have another janta durbar in four to five days."

"When the crowd became unmanageable, there were two options before me, either to resort to a lathicharge or to talk to the people. I chose the second option. Next time we will have the janta durbar at a stadium," he said.

The chief minister had announced that the entire cabinet would sit outside the Delhi secretariat every Saturday to listen to the people's grievances, and would attempt to solve the urgent problems on the spot. Every weekday, a minister would receive grievances from the public.

A large proportion of the people who thronged the road outside the Delhi government headquarters were contract workers seeking permanent jobs.

Kejriwal said: "I realise that the maximum grievances are among contractual workers from BSES, Asha workers, teachers. I assure you that we have taken note of your complaints.

"On Monday I will ask all departments for data on the number of contractual staff, and why they cannot be made permanent. They will submit a report in a week, and I will try to take a decision in a month. You have waited for so many years, give me this much time."

He also requested them not to come back at the next janta durbar, so that other complaints could be heard.

The chief minister and six cabinet ministers sat in the open outside the secretariat along with senior officials, as people began handing in their complaints. Health Minister Satyendra Jain, whose mother passed away on Saturday morning, was not present.

Each person was given a slip to confirm the receipt of his complaint. Officials at the help desk said those who had supplied their mobile phone numbers would receive a confirmation SMS. \"All written complaints will be put up on our web site and the status of action taken on the complaint will be constantly updated," an official said.

Barely 15 minutes into the durbar, however, the crowd — Kejriwal said there were 5,000 people against an expected 500, while police sources said at least 20,000 people had turned up — turned unruly. Delhi Police and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel struggled to manage the crowd, which broke the barricades at some places. The entire stretch of road from ITO to Rajghat was closed, and barricades were erected on the divider so that people could occupy one carriageway.

Some 300-400 police personnel were present outside the secretariat. "There was seating arrangement for 1,000 people outside the secretariat, but a much larger crowd turned up, leading to the chaos," a police officer said.

Several people returned disappointed. "I had come here in the hope of getting relief from my problems. But I was pushed around, and I am leaving after having waited for five hours. I wanted to meet the CM to seek a job for my physically handicapped son. There is no one to look after his needs after I retire," said M S Kaushik.

The BJP accused the AAP of promoting anarchy. "This is definitely promoting anarchy. It is a sign of bad governance," senior BJP leader Harshvardhan said.

Heading: After telling Delhi to sting, AAP wants Lokpal to snoop - Indian Express
Content:
The web of financial transactions between Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, members of his family and controversial businessman Vakamulla Chandrashekhar involve money transfers from him to the CM and his family via at least five companies that ceased to exist. And, in one case, money moved back and forth between the two sides.

This is revealed in an investigation by The Indian Express based on Registrar of Companies records and bank statements, including the one made public by Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Arun Jaitley.

As per that statement, on January 10, 2012, Chandrashekhar received Rs 49.99 lakh in his personal account from Maple Destinations, a company owned by the CM's son and daughter, Vikramaditya Singh and Aprajita Kumari, respectively. The very next day, this amount was transferred to Tarini International, a company of Chandrashekhar's Tarini group. As per RoC records, in the financial year 2011-12, Maple received Rs 49.99 lakh from Tarini Sugar and Distillaries Ltd, another company of the Tarini group.

No one from the CM's family responded to questions from The Indian Express on this transaction and others and involving companies that didn't exist. Chandrashekhar denied any wrongdoing and said he was "open for any investigation at any levels".

Between November 4 and November 21, 2011, Chandrashekhar, as per his bank statement, received inflows into his personal account amounting to Rs 1.6 crore from six companies. During the same period — November 4 to November 29 — a total of Rs 1.75 crore was transferred to the accounts of Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, wife Pratibha Singh and son Vikramaditya Singh.

Consider the nature of these transactions:

* One of these six companies is Punjab Foods Private Ltd. On November 21, 2011, Punjab Foods deposited Rs 45.5 lakh into Chandrashekhar's account and four days later, Rs 40 lakh from here was transferred to Vikramaditya Singh's account.

Incidentally, six months earlier, on April 18, 2011, Punjab Foods had filed an application before RoC, Chandigarh, to wind up its operations.

That application stated, "Pritpal Singh (director of the company), informed the members the company is not having any business activity for the last 10 years. Further company is having neither any assets nor any liabilities, therefore Easy Exit Scheme 2011 is opted for the closure of the company".

The company was officially wound up on April 20, 2011. Yet, Chandrashekhar's account showed a deposit of Rs 21.50 lakh from Punjab Foods as late as July 24, 2012.

Speaking to The Indian Express on January 2, Chandrashekhar had said he received money from Punjab Foods against agricultural produce he sold.

* On November 4, 2011, Chandrashekhar had a balance of Rs 4.05 lakh in his account. Over the next five days, Rs 92.90 lakh came into it from Kesari Nandan and Co (Rs 17.99 lakh), Shiva Stores (Rs 15.01 lakh), Jai Durga Impex (Rs 12.25 lakh), Laxmi Enterprises (Rs 7.65 lakh), Siddharth International (Rs 26 lakh) and one Suraj Singh (Rs 14 lakh). On November 11, Chandrashekhar transferred Rs 65 lakh, in two transactions, to Virbhadhra Singh's account.

According to the RoC records, Jai Durga Impex, Shiva Stores, Kesari Nandan and Co and Siddharth International all had ceased to exist before any of these transactions.

From Chandrashekhar's account, a transaction of unknown value failed on November 15, due to "insufficient funds".

* Between November 17 and November 21, Chandrashekhar's account received Rs 45.5 lakh from Punjab Foods and Rs 53 lakh from from one "V Chandra Shekhar". Four days later, Rs 71.80 lakh in two instalments of Rs 40 lakh and Rs 31.8 lakh was transferred to CM's son Vikramaditya Singh from Chandrashekhar's account.

Subsequent to this transfer — and some minor transfers not related to the CM's family — Chandrashekhar's account balance became Rs 55.05 lakh on November 25, 2011. On November 29, 2011 two instalments of Rs 25 lakh each were transferred to Pratibha Singh and Virbhadhra Singh.

His balance after these transactions was Rs 4.73 lakh, marginally higher than what it was when the transactions began.

When asked about the transactions with the CM and his family, Chandrashekhar said: "These companies are vendor companies with whom we have had trade relationships. We have done all transactions legitimately through banks. Whether they are doing business still or not, I am not competent to answer as it is purely their business."

Despite telephone calls and text messages Vikramaditya Singh was not available for comment. Jaitley has accused Virbhadra of granting an extension to Venture Energy and Technology, promoted by Chandrashekhar, for executing a hydel project.

Asked about the money received from Maple, Chandrashekhar said: "I and VVikramaditya Singh together wanted to do a construction project in 2010-11. Accordingly, my part contribution of Rs 2 crore was made to Vikram. Since the project did not take off, he returned the money through Maple. Where is the illegality?" He added: "Shri Virbhadraji is a very noble person and worthy of friendship...I am open for any investigation at any levels."

Heading: Delhi businessman overtakes Vadra’s car, booked for rash driving - Indian Express
Content:
After urging citizens to sting corrupt government officials, the AAP government is pushing hard to pass its version of the Jan Lokpal Bill in Delhi. While the process to draft the bill is already underway, Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal has announced that the Bill will be passed in a special Assembly session by February.

"A committee has been formed to draft the law. The committee under the chief secretary will include secretaries of the departments of home, urban development, law, finance and advocate Rahul Mehra," Kejriwal said on Thursday.

"We will all meet at Ramlila Maidan either in the last week of January or first week of February," he said.

The Bill, he said, would be discussed with the "people of Delhi" at Ramlila Maidan for consent.

A Lokayukta will head the new body to combat graft with powers to conduct its own investigations, surveillance and even tap phones.

"As in the AAP's model Jan Lokpal Bill, the head of the body, in this case the Lokayukta, will have powers to tap phones, conduct independent investigations and surveillance against those who face corruption charges," Urban Development Minister Manish Sisodia said.

According to Kejriwal, the Lokayukta would function as an independent body. "Today if I am accused of corruption, there is no independent body which can investigate me but this will happen once the law is drafted," he said.

Heading: Does AP mean Ahmed Patel, asks prosecutor in Italy court; middleman says don’t know - Indian Express
Content:
A Delhi businessman was penalised by traffic police for "rash driving" after his car overtook the cavalcade of Robert Vadra, son-in-law of Congress president Sonia Gandhi.

A police officer, who did not wish to be named, said the car of Saurabh Rastogi, a businessman who lives in Paschim Vihar, was chased and intercepted by police after Vadra's securityman called the police control room and complained that a car had driven past "dangerously".

The officer said Rastogi was headed towards Lajpat Nagar from the Modi Mill flyover in Okhla at the time of the incident.

"Rastogi was in a Maruti Ritz and Vadra's cavalcade was ahead of him. We were told he had been honking continuously. In a bid to overtake the cavalcade, he accelerated and sped past Vadra's car. It was then that a securityman travelling with Vadra made a PCR call. The traffic police were also informed," the officer said.

Rastogi's car was chased by traffic policemen and intercepted near Amar Colony in south-east Delhi. "He was issued a challan for dangerous driving under Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act and let off," the officer said.

Heading: Tata Group’s security up after threats from Maoists - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: In Taltala, locals learn to fear hospitals - Indian Express
Content:
The police have decided to upgrade security at the offices of Tata Group in the city after Maoist leaflets urging stepped-up agitation against the land acquisition for Tata projects have been recovered.

The leaflets were received on October 17, after some English and vernacular dailies carried an open letter from Ratan Tata detailing his reasons for shifting the Nano project from Singur.

Though senior police officers preferred to deny the issue, sources in the Special Branch said the police apprehend sudden and possibly violent demonstrations at Tata business establishments by Maoist sympathisers.

The leaflets in Bengali and English, signed by a CPI-ML spokesperson for eastern India, who identified himself as Comrade Surya, state: "We shall expose and smash all conspiracies being hatched by the Tata-Buddhadeb gang. Tata has justified land acquisition, lied about transparency in the acquisition of land in Singur, made false charges of theft of goods from the Tata Motors factory and shed crocodile tears for the people of Singur. However, he skipped important issues like the merciless repression in Singur, forcing people to part with their plots".

Tata, it said, has come out in the open most vocally in defence of the CPM's development policy.

"Ratan Tata, alongwith Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, Benoy Konar, Prakash Karat & Co have steamrolled over the lives of thousands of Singur peasants and nearly 1,000 acres of highly fertile land," the leaflet said. "Tata wants to be a self-proclaimed teacher of the people, sermonising them not to struggle but to fall in the CPM's policy of destructive development."

When contacted, Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch) Parthasarathi Ghosh refused to comment on the issue.

Inspector General (Law & Order) Raj Kanojia said the Maoist leaflet has not been brought to his notice as yet. "We will take adequate steps as and when the need arises. Outside Kolkata, the Tatas have so many establishments. Probably the leaflet was intended for Kolkata Police."

Heading: Pro-Nano outfits meet Buddha, demand return of project - Indian Express
Content:
The death of 45-year-old Kasi Saha has shocked the residents of Taltala Library Row.

That he should have contracted malaria has not surprised anyone ¿ the residents claim the area is prone to the vector-borne disease. But medical negligence has scared people off admitting others in hospital.

Mira Sahani (40) has been suffering from high fever for the past three days and was diagnosed with falciparum malaria on Thursday. But her relatives refused to get her admitted to a hospital.

"We all know that Saha died due to medical negligence. He was recovering, but he was given the wrong injection and we heard that he died soon after," said Sahani's daughter. The family has been treating her at home, administering round-the-clock care. "The doctor said today that I am much better and should recover in a few days," said Mira.

Other residents of the neighbourhood too claim they would prefer to keep patients at home. Four others had been diagnosed with malaria in the same lane but residents claim that the KMC is yet to take action.

"The surrounding areas have stagnant water and accumulated garbage but no one takes any action. We have given a number of petitions but no one is bothered. Even the KMC turns up once in nine months to spray," said another resident.

The residents now collect money and buy their own bleaching powder and try to disinfect their lane, but they admit that it does not help much.

Heading: Bengal has a new problem: greenfield airport will block a coalfield - Indian Express
Content:
Members of the Singur Nano Bachao Committee and Singur Shilpa Bikash O Unnayan Committee — the forums campaigning for the Tata small car factory — on Friday appealed to Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee to take all possible initiatives to bring back the car project to West Bengal.

The committees, which claim to represent the people of Singur, submitted a memorandum to Bhattacharjee.

"After hearing the harsh decision of Ratan Tata about the transfer of Nano project from Singur to Gujarat, most people are disappointed, especially the 11,500 families who have already given up their land for the project. People, including small traders and trainees, who were working inside and outside the project have also lost their livelihood and are facing tremendous problem," said Udayan Das, president of the two committees.

Das said the chief minister has assured them that he will convey their request to the Tata Motors on their behalf.

The memorandum stated: "Eighty-five per cent of the total project has already been completed, including 27 ancillary units, and the trial run of the car was also started." It further stated, "Now, most of the remaining farmers, who are yet to receive their cheques, have agreed to give their land for the project on the terms of the final package declared by the state government."

The forums urged the chief minister to take initiatives for the development of the infrastructure of the surrounding areas adjacent to the project area. They also demanded that locals, especially those who had given up their land be provided with suitable jobs.

CPM leader Binoy Konar, meanwhile, said if the Tatas are not interested to set up any industry at Singur, the state government will write to Tata Motors to return the land allotted to them. "There is no concrete proposal for any other industry at Singur, but the state government is confident to set up industry at that site," said Konar.

Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee also demanded that the government should allot the Singur land through a global tender.

Heading: Mob on rampage after truck mows down woman - Indian Express
Content:
The West Bengal government and the Centre face a tough choice: a greenfield air port in Durgapur-Asansol belt or a coal reserve worth Rs 2,40,000 crore.

The greenfield airport in Burdwan's Andal, the work for which was to start by the year-end, has now been deferred as the state government will have to enter a dialogue with the Coal India Limited (CIL), which has raised objections to the project.

"We will have to hold dialogues with the CIL. The deliberations will be based on the actual ground data about presence and extractability of underground coal, which the CIL claims, lies below the proposed greenfield airport," said Sabyasachi Sen, secretary for Commerce and Industries, West Bengal.

He added that coal can be found below the Durgapur Steel Plant and IISCO, situated in the same area, but still the projects had come up.

"We will have to find out a solution that enables the project to come up but will not affect the coal reserve's extractability," Sen said.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation had already given the go-ahead for the airport and the process of acquiring of about 3500 acres was to begin shortly.

The CIL has raised the objection that if the project comes up, 2 billion tons of coal will become unextractable. It has submitted their objections to the civil aviation ministry on October 12.

The CIL, however, claimed that it had not, technically speaking, raised any objection.

"We have merely stated facts about how the coal reserves will be affected if the project were to come up. Now it is upto the state and Centre to decide whether they want coal or airport," said Partha Bhattacharjee, chairman, CIL. "We have plans to use advanced machinery for the extraction of coal from the area.

But if the airport comes up, we will have to stop our plans," Bhattacharjee said.

The present impasse will delay the project, admitted Sen. He, however, added that the state government was not sure what would delay the project, CIL's objection or land acquisition.

The CPM and the state government, however, seem determined to go ahead with the project, to be developed by Bengal Pragati Aerotropolis Limited (BAPL).

A pact with Changi Airports of Singapore for foreign equity participation in the project is to be signed next month.

Member of Parliament from Asansol, Bangsogopal Choudhury said he had held talks with the civil aviation minister Praful Patel in Delhi last week after complications about the project emerged.

"He has assured that the ministry will not pay heed to the report filed by the CIL," Choudhury said from Delhi.

Squarely blaming the bureaucrats for being too pro-active, Choudhury alleged that they were acting under instructions from politicians. He however did not specify the name of any political party. "The area where the project is to come up is not within the lease area of CIL. How can the CIL object? How can a few bureaucrats be so bold without any political patronage," he asked.

Heading: New CNG station opens in Asansol, long wait for Kolkata - Indian Express
Content:
At least eight buses were damaged by a mob near Rajabazar after a woman was run down by a truck early on Friday morning. The Rapid Action Force (RAF) had to be called in to bring the situation under control.

The police said the victim, whose identity could not be confirmed, was around 35. She was mowed down by the truck while trying to cross the road.

Local residents first tried to stop the police from taking away the body, but when they tried to use force, the mob went berserk and started damaging buses caught in a traffic jam at the accident site. Three belonged to the state transport department.

The irate mob also blocked the road demanding construction of a divider.

Senior police officials and local MLA Anadi Shau rushed to the spot and the blockade was lifted only after they assured the protesters that the administration would look into their demand.

Heading: TMC team meets minister over schemes of zilla parishad - Indian Express
Content:
The Great Eastern Energy Corporation Limited (GEECL), the first commercial producer of coal bed methane (CBM) in India, has opened its seventh CBM-based compressed natural gas (CNG) station at Neamatpur in Asansol on Friday.

The company has already signed a franchisee agreement for supply and retail of CNG through Indian Oil Corporation's (IOC) petrol pumps in Asansol, Durgapur, Raniganj and other cities across the state. Overall there are seven CNG stations in the area, of which, four are the "mother stations" and three are the "daughter stations".

Coal bed methane is considered to be of better quality than the CNG available in the market. It has 96 per cent methane, contains no sulphur and has very little carbon dioxide, while the natural gas contains about seven per cent carbon dioxide.

While automobile users will have access to clean fuel in the region, for users in Kolkata, there seems to be a long wait ahead. The company has spoken to the state government about extending CNG supply to Kolkata, which will be implemented gradually. It estimates a CNG demand exceeding 40 to 50 million cubic feet per day in Kolkata alone.

"We have begun with Asansol and Raniganj. Later, we will gradually extend it to Durgapur, Burdwan and Dankuni. It will take at least six months to extend the supply to Durgapur. Kolkata might take longer and as of now, opening a supply station in the immediate future is ruled out," said Prashant Modi, president and chief operating officer of GEECL. Given the huge market for CNG in Kolkata, it is difficult to match supply with demand. Moreover, supply to Kolkata requires pipelines to be laid which could take some time. "Supply by truck-mounted cascades is not feasible for Kolkata, as trucks are not allowed into the city. Pipelines are the only option," added Modi.

State Transport minister Subhas Chakraborty on Thursday had said that all autorickshaws, running on petrol or diesel, will be off the roads after December 31. Only autos fuelled by LPG will be allowed in Kolkata and other parts of the state.

Heading: State hopes for a ‘powerful’ Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
A Trinamool Congress team met Panchayat Minister Surjyakanta Mishra at Writers' Buildings on Friday to complain about the non-cooperative attitude of the state government in implementing the schemes introduced by the Trinamool-led zilla parishads.

"The state government is delaying funds for all rural development schemes introduced by the Trinamool-led zilla parishads," alleged Trinamool leader Partha Chatterjee. Apart from Chatterjee, the other members of the team were — Trinamool leader Sisir Adhikary, East Midnapore Zilla Parishad Sabhadhipati Ranjit Mondal and South 24 Parganas Zilla Parishad Sabhadhipati Shamima Sheikh. Incidentally, Trinamool had snatched these two districts from the CPM in panchayat elections this year.

"The state government is blocking even health schemes in these two zilla parishads," alleged Chatterjee.

He added the district magistrates, who are also ex-officio executive officers of zilla parishads, are not attending the meetings called by the Trinamool sabhadhipatis.

"We believe the district magistrates are taking instructions from the CPM. We will not tolerate this attitude," Chatterjee said. He added, "The people will think that the Trinamool-run boards are doing nothing about development, but we are helpless if funds are not approved by the state government."

Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, meanwhile, wanted the Centre to convene an all-party meet to resolve the crisis arising out of the attacks against Hindi-speaking job aspirants in Maharashtra.

Heading: JNNURM projects: ‘Patta’ to remove hurdles - Indian Express
Content:
Though the power situation in the state continues to remain poor, officials of the state power department are confident that they will not face any major problems in Diwali. This, in spite of the fact that thermal power stations have received only half the amount of coal required to run the plants in the recent past.

A fifth unit of the Santhaldih power plant began production on Friday. The new unit, constructed and commissioner by Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited will produce up to 130 mw of electricity in a couple of days. On the first day, the generation was about 80 mw. "This additional power will improve the situation to some extent. We hope that very soon, the unit will generate up to 130 mw every day," said S Mahapatra, Chairman of West Bengal Power Development Corporation Limited (WBPDCL).

The Santhaldih unit, with a capacity to generate 250 mw, was to be commissioned by December 2007. Due to technical problems, the project was delayed for over a year.

During festivals like Diwali, the daily power requirement increases by about 100 mw. "This is not much of a problem as we can easily meet the demand from imports," Mahapatra said. As most offices remain closed during this period, the burden is reduced. "We did well during the Durga Puja," he added.

The coal stock situation for the thermal power stations, meanwhile, remained critical even on Friday. "On Thursday, the Coal India Limited had given us nine rakes of coal. Today we have received only about seven-and-half rakes," said Mahapatra. The plants require about 12 rakes of coal daily to function, he added.

Heading: An early solution needed on Darjeeling: Governor - Indian Express
Content:
After the projects of Basic Services for Urban Poor (BSUP) under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) faced resistance from locals at Hatgachia and Anandapur on the issue of land acquisition, the state government has introduced the "Right to Land" or "Patta" system for the urban poor.

"The state government will prepare the land deeds and hand it over to the urban poor. If a land encroached by the poor is a government-vested one then it will be directly handed over to the family who lives there. In case the land belongs to the railways or the Kolkata Port Trust, the state will acquire the land or buy it for preparing the land deed and give it to the poor," said Asok Bhattacharya, state Urban Development and Municipal Affairs minister.

The state, however, is lagging behind other states in executing the BSUP projects resulting in a huge escalation of the cost that has to be borne by the state.

"We have repeatedly asked for viability gap funding from the Centre, which bears 20 per cent of the project cost, but did not manage to get it. So, we have to deal with not just the local resistance and land acquisition problems but are also affected by scarcity of funds," Bhattacharya added.

Besides, the state has also been asked to ensure that there is a 24-hour uninterrupted water supply.

"For helping the poor and creating a healthy environment, two very important factors need to be implemented. One is uninterrupted water supply that can arrest the water contamination technically. Another one is creating an open defecation free-environment by successfully executing the national sanitation policy," said Srinivas Chary Vedala, Director, Centre for Energy, Environment, Urban Governance and Infrastructure Development of the Administrative Staff College of India. Bhattacharya said he had asked civic bodies to take preventive measures before the outbreak of vector-borne diseases.

Heading: CITU: Govt ignoring workers’ problems - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi — who met a Gorkha Janmukti Morcha delegation on Wednesday during his trip to Darjeeling, broke his silence on the subject on Friday.

Following Wednesday's meeting with the GJM, Gandhi had not issued any statement. Sources in Raj Bhavan said the Governor's response that day was "let the GJM do the talking".

But during his return journey to Kolkata, Gandhi told the media in Siliguri that he hoped that the tripartite talks would "move forward smoothly".

"The main thing is that a solution should be reached at the earliest possible. The state government, the Centre and the GJM are engaged in the talks. Everyone should wish the talks are successful and that peace prevails," Gandhi said.

In Kolkata, the Siliguri-based Minister for Urban Development Ashok Bhattacharya said the only way forward is through talks.

"The tripartite discussion alone can solve the problem. We want them (the GJM) to withdraw the agitation. Until and unless they do so, the problem will not be solved," Bhattacharya said.

Heading: Price of festive season: CU teachers on vacation, decision on course delayed - Indian Express
Content:
Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) — the trade union wing of the CPM — has blamed the state government for ignoring the problems of workers in the state. On Friday, CITU leaders handed over a complaint to the state Finance Minister Asim Dasgupta citing their dissatisfaction over implementation of labour laws.

CITU claimed that the government is employing casual workers in areas where it is mandatory to employ permanent ones. In its complaint, the trade union alleged that various government departments —panchayats, municipalities and educational institutions — are violating the labour laws of 1970.

CITU said that if an organisation employs casual workers then it has to be registered as a contractor. But most of the organisations employing casual employees do not follow the law, it added.

The trade union in its complaint demanded that the state government should regularise all casual employees who have been working for more than 240 days in state government departments or other allied organisations.

CITU leaders sought an answer from the government on whether or not it has any plans to secure the future of para-teachers who sometimes work in place of regular teachers but receive much less remuneration.

In its complaint, the trade union alleged that the government has not taken steps to resolve provident fund, bonus and other related disputes of casual employees.

"The state government departments that employ casual workers claim that they are acting on instructions of the Finance Department. The finance minister should clarify," demanded a CITU leader.

The trade union has also pointed out that despite writing several letters and repeated deliberations with the state Finance Department the issue of dearness allowance has not been resolved.

Heading: Trains back on track, but passengers still stranded - Indian Express
Content:
Though the 2008-09 academic session of the Calcutta University has reached its halfway mark, the authorities have yet to decide on two critical issues — the number of unit tests that a college has to conduct and the total marks of the environmental science paper.

The university will hold another round of meetings before it can decide on these twin issues.

"We have sought opinions of teachers and principals on both the issues. The undergraduate council of the university will meet on November 14 to discuss the matter after which the syndicate will deliberate on it. The decision will be taken after these steps," said Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Academics) of CU Dhrubojyoti Chattopadhyay.

The university has taken some initiatives to discuss the matter with the academic faculties of various colleges but the Puja holidays halted the process.

Earlier, the University Grants Commission (UGC) had sent a letter to the university threatening to cut its grants if it fails to increase the marks of the environmental science paper to 100 at the undergraduate level.

This made it imperative for the Calcutta University to do so since the marks allotted in the paper was 50. There is, however, confusion over who will conduct the examination. While a section of university officials feel that colleges should conduct the examination, the rest feel there will be a dilution of the academic standards if this happens.

Presently, the students have to qualify for environmental science and the marks obtained by them in the paper are not added to the total marks secured by the candidate. The university is deliberating on having a multiple choice question paper that can be checked through an optical mark reader (OMR) sheet. No decision has yet been taken on the issue.

On the issue of reduction of number of unit tests, the university is again indecisive. Earlier, its syndicate had decided to reduce the number of unit tests from four to one, as most of the colleges do not have adequate infrastructure to conduct the examination.

The matter was later referred to the university, which decided to consult the staff of the affiliating colleges. University officials said a unit test is scheduled for November-end. If the final decision is on conducting one unit test, this test will be valid, they added.

Heading: Behala shopowner shot dead - Indian Express
Content:
For passengers stuck at the city's railway stations, the nightmare seems unending. On Friday, news of resumption of train services came as a relief to many, but the respite proved to be short-lived.

Stranded passengers found that inspite of the resumption of services, getting a ticket was a tough job.

Bhudev Yadav, 45, scheduled to board a Patna-bound train, found it cancelled on Thursday after violence erupted in Bihar.

With a family of five, Yadav is still not sure when he will be able to return home as he waits for reservation.

"We were supposed to travel by the Howrah-Patna Janshatabdi Express. But when we came to the station on Thursday, we found that our train cancelled. Though train services have resumed now, we do not have tickets as the train for today was already packed to capacity," said Bhudev, whose ailing mother stays alone in Patna.

The Eastern Railway cancelled 25 trains on Wednesday and 10 trains of the Patna-Gaya routes on Thursday after students set fire the compartments of Danapur Express, Ujjain Express and Danapur-Saharsa Inter-city to protest against the attack on north Indians by Maharashtra Navnirman Sena in Maharashtra.

On Friday, the trains were back on the track with the Eastern Railway running all their scheduled trains, except 3005 Up Punjab Mail and 2323 Up Howrah-New Delhi Special which were running late.

"Unlike the last two days, when we had to cancel a number of trains, today we have been able to run all our long distance trains as per schedule except for two which ran late. There were no disturbances in Bihar and so we went ahead with our regular train schedules," said Binod Sharma, PRO, Eastern Railway.

But for many like A Kumar, who was supposed to be traveling on Thursday, the relief was of no help.

Like Bhudev, Kumar and many others, did not get a full refund. They also failed to get fresh reservation.

"The trains were cancelled on Wednesday and Thursday keeping in mind passenger safety. Though we provide full refund for the cancelled tickets within 72 hours from the scheduled time of departure, it is not possible to get additional coaches for the passengers to accommodate them," Sharma said.

Heading: BA/BSc students await results of exams held in June-July - Indian Express
Content:
A 42-year-old shopowner was shot dead in broad daylight in Behala's Parnasree area on Friday afternoon.

The police said Dilip Naskar, a resident of Maharani Indira Debi Road in Behala, was alone at his stationary shop near Parnasree bus stand when three youths carrying a pipegun came on a motorbike and fired three rounds at him.

Naskar sustained bullet injuries on his chest and neck and died at the spot, police said.

Additional Superintendent of Police (Industrial), South 24 Parganas, Sunil Cowdhury said the motive behind the murder was not clear. "We have come to know that Naskar used to supply building materials earlier. We are probing whether the murder was a result of an old enmity," he added.

No arrests have been made so far, police said. Police sources said that since there are no eye witnesses and no one has seen the killers or the motorbike, it would not be easy to track down the culprits.

Heading: Fire dept blames KMC for Tangra tannery fire - Indian Express
Content:
The largest university of the state, Calcutta University, has now become synonymous to unprecedented delays when it comes to publication of results.

The results of 1.7 lakh students, who wrote their examination in June and July this year, have not been declared yet and the university is not in a position to declare the final date for the publication of the results.

While the students who appeared in the BA/BSc (Hons and General) part I and part II examinations under (1+1+1) system and BA/BSc (Hons and General) part I under (2+1) system are awaiting the results, the examiners are enjoying their vacation.

"We can declare the final date only after the teachers return from vacation and the colleges reopens on November 4," said Pro Vice-Chancellor (Academic) Dhrubojyoti Chattopadhyay.

According to sources in the university, many examiners have not submitted the corrected answersheets and the examination department is trying to contact them.

According to the general practice, an examiner has to return the corrected answerscripts within 21 days from their date of issue. In many cases, however, teachers take more than the stipulated time.

It took more than a year to publish the results of the Mass Communication and Journalism examination and the university had to ask for a declaration signed by the teachers that the answersheets would be submitted in a fixed period of time.

"The delay in submission of answerscripts is not the only reason for the delay in declaration of results. There is a huge gap between the number of examiners and the answersheets that they have to check," said an official of the examination department.

Heading: What is the diameter of the Earth? Measure it yourself - Indian Express
Content:
A day after two tanneries were destroyed in a fire in Tangra, the Fire and Emergency Services department on Friday blamed the Kolkata Municipal Corporation for illegal tanneries thriving in the area.

"Most of the tanneries here are illegal and do not have any licence. The fire department cannot be held responsible for them," said Gopal Bhattacharjee, Director, Fire and Emergency Services. All tanneries were supposed to shift to Bantala three years ago but lack of facilities there prompted some to stay back and continue work in an illegal manner.

In June this year, the civic body had made it mandatory for certain establishments to obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the fire department before conducting trade or other operations from their premises.

"No tannery in the Tangra area has ever approached us for an NOC. Since most of them do not have a trade licence, we cannot enforce fire-safety norms on them," Bhattacharjee said.

Fire department officials said that the tanneries that were gutted on Thursday did not possess any firefighting equipment.

"They were dealing with highly inflammable materials but did not care to have wet risers, fire alarms or any in-built system. They had just a few fire extinguishers, most of which had never been serviced," said a divisional officer.

The fire that broke out at 8:30 am on Thursday required 41 fire tenders and six hours to douse the flames. The cause of the fire is still not known.

Heading: Fit Baichung gives Bagan edge in I-League derby - Indian Express
Content:
To mark the International Year of Planet Earth, a travelling exhibition — "Measuring Our Planet" — took off at the Birla Industrial and Technological Museum (BITM) in Kolkata on Friday.

"This is the first-of-its-kind initiative taken by the National Council of Science Museums (NCSM) where visitors can use scientific methods to measure the earth," said Ingit Mukherjee, director-general, NCSM. The exhibition will be held at eight Science centres across the country for the next two years.

"The earth exploration exhibit will teach visitors a number of techniques to explore various aspect of our planet. One can measure the diameter of the earth through scientific methods. For an instance, practical applications show that India's population of 1,100 million can encircle the earth 50 times," said Jayanta Sthanapati, director of BITM.

The exhibition also highlights modern techniques used in measuring the speed of rotation and revolution of the earth, studying the continental drift and earthquakes.

The exhibition, spread over an area of 1,500 square feet, showcasing 25 exhibits with interactive and multimedia applications, expects a heavy rush.

The purpose of the exhibition is to highlight simple methods to calculate various features of the earth, something that the lay person can understand easily.

According to museum officials, there is no separate entry fee for the exhibition. The exhibition, which incurred an investment of Rs 45 lakh, will continue till November 30 from 10 am to 5.30 pm every day.

Heading: Okoro does it for Md Sporting - Indian Express
Content:
Mohun Bagan coach Karim Bencherifa has almost made up his mind. If his team loses tomorrow he will chuck it in.

So, the onus is on Baichung Bhutia & Co to ensure Karim stays. The Moroccan has ushered in freshness and modern methods in an otherwise insipid Kolkata football. It will be sad if his stint comes to a premature end.

Going into this I-League match against East Bengal, the green-maroons have a psychological advantage. Yuba Bharati Krirangan (YBK) has been their happy hunting ground of late where they have six wins and one draw against their arch-rivals in last seven matches.

That Baichung is fit is a definite shot in the arm. Right back Habibur Rahaman too has recovered from the injury, and Bagan now have Brazilian Marcos Pereira to do the holding job in the midfield. Rakesh Masih's place is likely to be taken by Lalkamal Bhowmick. So, after a long time, Bagan are back to full strength.

They so far have managed only two points from four outings. Still, Bencherifa feels they are under no extra pressure. "Every match is important, and there's pressure everytime. You can't single out a particular contest at this level. I have told the boys to play their natural game. Let's hope things fall in place," Bencherifa told The Indian Express.

East Bengal, on the other hand, are banking on their striking duo of Sunil Chhetri and Yusif Yakubu. The two gelled very well in the last match against Vasco.

"Mohun Bagan would be a different proposition altogether. A team that has the likes of Baichung and Barreto upfront needs to be given special attention. But we have the resources to win. If they have Baichung and Barreto, we have Yakubu and Chhetri. The defence has to be tight," East Bengal coach Stanley Rozario preferred to keep a low profile.

Indeed, defence has been a problem area for the red-and-golds. M Suresh is too slow to offer assurance.

His partners, Nirmal Chhetri, Khelemba Singh or Suley Mussah too don't inspire confidence.

Mehrajuddin Wadoo and Renedy Singh appear doubtful starters. So, the onus is completely on the men upfront to do it for their team.

"In Goa, I have played a number of derby matches. So I am not worried about it. I will try to live up to the expectation," Yakubu said.

East Bengal are currently placed sixth in the league standings with six points from four matches. A win tomorrow will see them move into top five.

Heading: Male-o-drama - Indian Express
Content:
Mike Okoro's outstanding performance helped Mohammedan Sporting record their first win in the ongoing I-League as they edged past Mahindra United 1-0 at the Yuba Bharati Krirangan (YBK) today.

Okoro netted the winner in the 74th minute outsmarting his marker NP Pradeep with a brilliant off the ball play.

He timed his run perfectly to meet a Jyothi Kumar lob inside the box and then chipped the ball over the head of an advancing Mahindra custodian Subhashis Roy Chowdhury. The goal has class written all over it.

The win gives the black-and-white brigade some breathing space ahead of their next five away ties.

They moved to five points from as many outings, while Mahindra stay on three.

The visitors began on an aggressive note and came very close to scoring in the seventh minute. But Steven Dias missed a sitter as his shot, off a Douhou Pierre floater went wide.

Edeh Chidi wasted another in the 20th minute. This time Dias set it up for the Nigerian but his header from inside the box was off the mark.

Md Sporting were struggling to find their footing. But they clawed their way back in last 20 minutes, thanks to a super show by Okoro. Without his partner Theodore Sunday, the onus was on him to make things happen. He rose to the occasion. His deft touches, splendid close control and incisive passing proved to be too much for the Mumbai outfit that has some top national team players like Pradeep and Dias.

Md Sporting's young goalkeeper from Mizoram, Tungshang Tharangachan also deserves special praise for an outstanding show under the bar. Adebayo Adewusi too had a good game in the midfield.

Heading: Saturday reviews - Indian Express
Content:
Most menswear designers want to keep it simple; so what's a fashion hack to do?

Show of the day
Moroccan-inspired weaves with bursts of cool mints, liquid azures and flaming oranges set apart Vineet Bahl's collection. It would be unfair to label him just consistent for his clothes get more beautiful with each show. Indulge your calves and knees in his dresses and stay cool in his feather-light georgettes. Let's hope summer's here soon enough.

Celeb of the day
The presence of some glittering faces in the front row for Dev R Nil's show added some glitter into the otherwise slow-paced proceedings. There was Shatrughan Sinha, Poonam Sinha, Arbaaz Khan, Rohit Roy and Kiron Juneja who came to cheer the sweet Sonakshi who sashayed down the ramp. But the applause was the loudest from a back bencher, a certain Jackie Shroff, who was the showstopper of the day, literally. Posing for photographs, joking around, talking in typical Bambaiyya Hindi and whistling for Sonakshi, Jaggu Dada was in a cheery mood. Indeed.

Trend of the day
Single-button jackets were probably the biggest sellout on the Menswear Day at LFW. They look utterly urbane, sophisticated and best suited for the hot season. From single-breasted cotton jackets presented by Zubair Kirmani to stylish printed bomber jackets and embroidered jackets by Dev R Nil, sequined denim jacket by Tarun Tahiliani and formal blazers by Troy Costa, these single-button jackets will definitely cool your torso on a mercilessly hot afternoon.

Goss of the day
It was a blink-and-miss appearance by ex-Australian skipper Steve Waugh. Seated in between Sabyasachi and Ravi Krishnan, nobody saw him enter or leave the venue. What happened to the forever intruding Indian paparazzi?

Ensemble of the day
Trust Narendra Kumar to breathe life into the dull; his menswear line had all the makings of a trendy toy-boy. A black silk jacket with flat sequins on it was teamed with cotton skinny pants—all the rage in the west—and a brown chiffon shirt. We like.

Heading: City meets new killer Meningoencephalitis - Indian Express
Content:
New York, New York
Film: Padre Nuestro
Director: Cristopher Zalla
Cast: Jesus Ochoa, Armando Hernandez, Eugenio Derbez, Jorge Adrian Espindola
Rating: *********
Running at: Fame (South City, Hiland Park)
Under the shadows of New York's spiraling high-rises, a subterranean world grows parasitically. It's a dog-eat-dog world where the first world ideals of one of the world's largest democracy are redundant. As one of the characters of director Christopher Zalla's brilliantly executed ode to love and ambition, Padre Nuestro, says to a freshly arrived illegal immigrant —"You need to know the importance of a 50 dollar bill to survive in this city". Yet, hope and dreams survive in this bleak, bleak world in the hearts of its brow-beaten and hardened denizens. Not because they are exceptional dreamers, but simply because they are human.

In a dusty Mexican village, Juan (Armando Hernandez) is fleeing a pack of goons who are obviously after his life. Negotiating his way through the bylanes, he hops into a truck which will transport him illegally to New York City. In a subhuman journey to freedom (men, women and children are packed into the back of truck like sardines), Juan befriends Pedro (Jesus Ochoa), a 17-year-old kid from central Mexico who is headed to New York to seek his rich restaurateur father, Diego. Pedro tells Juan about a sealed letter that his mother, now dead, has given him-an introduction to the father he never knew. The truck pulls into New York City. The glittering skyline, along with the Empire State Building, looms large behind. A disoriented Pedro wakes up to find both his belongings and his new friend gone without a trace. Penniless and lost in a strange city, Pedro stumbles around. At the other end of Brooklyn, Juan, shows up at Diego's door with the letter, claiming to be his long-lost son, Pedro.

Padre Nuestro is one of those films which rattle along at such a lick, that there's little time to ponder the plot holes – not that there are any. Yet, it is the director's use of actors, locations and energy, and its buried theme, that makes Padre Nuestro one of the most potent cinematic experiences of our time.

Also notable is the director's use of New York. It is a world where everybody has secrets, agendas, and a willingness to pull the trigger. And underneath their carefully composed disguises, all of them are hopelessly lonely beings pining for some human comfort.

And where is God, you may ask? Does the Almighty even care about the plight of the righteous man in this town anymore?

Roadside Ramblings
Film: Roadside Romeo
Director: Jugal Hansraj
Voice Cast: Saif Ali Khan, Kareena Kapoor, Javed Jaffrey, Tanaaz Irani
Rating: *****
Running at: Inox (Forum, City Centre, Swabhumi)
Roadside Romeo is not one of those melt-in-your-mouth animations that leave an aftertaste that figures among the few unapologetically sweet things in life. If a quirky Nemo, a bumbling Shrek or a robust Alex is your yardstick for an animation, Jugal Hansraj's spunky hairstylist is in trouble.

They make him super cool, give him groovy Bollywood numbers to jive too, and give him a voice that is Bollywood's stereotype for irreverent spunk. So Romeo is all set to rock. But then Bollywood takes over. And Romeo turns more into Saif Ali Khan's hundred and one similar-looking characters than himself, his cronies just canine versions of silly, bungling filmi chelas, his villain a caricature straight out of a David Dhawan flick. At times, it is not funny.

But yes, Kareena Kapoor's voiceover as a sultry seductress Laila does lend Hansraj's heroine her character, but it surprisingly doesn't get on to your nerves. So, with Laila and the film's superior animation, Roadside Romeo does give us hope. The humour at times, seems too bawdy for an animation, but it does have the rough edge of Bollywood slapstick.

However, the film seems so smitten with Romeo that somehow it forgets that there has to be a story. And so it's all up to Romeo, and yes Saif Ali Khan's vocal emotive abilities to see the film through. While Khan does a good job of living his screen image once over again, Javed Jaffrey as Charlie Anna outdoes himself.

So, just before the animated canine Bollywood drove you nuts, the film ends, but with a funny tribute to this generation's greatest romantic moment. If you have not already guessed the film in question, most of RR's humour would be lost on you.

P.S: Sit through the credits. For a change it's smart, funny and has a bit of the best thing about Roadside Romeo – it's title track.

Hero-less
Film: Heroes
Director: Samir Karnik
Cast: Mithun Chakraborty, Salman Khan, Preity Zinta, Sohail Khan, Vatsal Seth, Sunny Deol and Bobby Deol
Rating: ****
Running at: Inox (City Centre, Forum, Swabhumi)
You don't have to be a soldier to love our country, says director Samir Karnik. You can be a screaming, howling caricature of an Air Force pilot (Sunny Deol) or a brave widow of a soldier (Preity Zinta) who drives a tractor through lush fields of Punjab to support her family, as long as you are serving the country in some way, your contribution counts. A noble thought indeed, but who will buy it when it's peddled by a beefy Sohail Khan (who is very appropriately named Saand) and an insipid Vatsal Seth (now where have we seen him before) who try to pass off as fresh-off-the-oven film students?

Moreover, Heroes is as by-the-books formulaic as can be, and there's not a surprise around that the corner that isn't obvious immediately. Karnik tries to do a Rang De Basanti, but ends up making a watered down version of Border meets Friends instead (if you think that's a weird marriage of genres, so do we).

So these two are irresponsible film students, who would rather chase the professor's daughter around the trees than attend classes. Since one can't really get a degree for running around trees, the duo is assigned a project— a graduation film. Somehow, (don't ask us how) the Saand and his sidekick decide to make a film on why youngsters shouldn't join the Army. And they do so by delivering the last letters of three Army men to their respective families (yet again, don't ask us how the letters end up with these two).

A road trip is planned. Designer camps packed. And Ray Ban sunglasses worn. As they yoddle their way through picturesque Ladakh locales, you brace yourself for some high voltage jingoism. Instead, you are pleasantly surprised by a luminous Priety Zinta, who actually delivers a performance of a lifetime as a taciturn widow, struggling to keep her family together. No melodrama, no rona-dhona. Just simple heart tugging moments. So you sit up and look forward to the rest of the film. Thereon, much happens —some of it incomprehensible, most of it pointlessly preposterous and all of it slightly less involving than watching algae grow on a stagnant pond.

Apart from Priety Zinta and the likable child actor who plays her son, none of the actors impress. Seeing Sunny Deol huff and puff his way through his allotted 10 minutes of screen time you wonder exactly how stilted our idea of a good performance was in the 1980s. He actually is a two-time National Award winner. Seriously…

Heading: Award for Nilu Phule - Indian Express
Content:
This season, vector-borne diseases have killed eleven people in the city, though the Kolkata Municipal Corporation puts the figure at eight

After dengue, malignant malaria and Japanese Encephalitis panic, Kolkata is in the grip of a new killer disease — Meningoencephalitis.

Sailendra Kumar Chowdhury (28), a resident of 61/C Tollygunge Road (ward 53), died on Friday at the MR Bangur Hospital due to "cardiac respiratory failure in a case of Meningoencephalitis" as it is mentioned by MR Bangur hospital.

According to specialists, Meningoencephalitis is a medical condition caused by attacks of malaria, Japanese B Encephalitis, herpes and tuberculosis. The disease is associated with high rates of mortality and morbidity.

"The case should have been thoroughly investigated to detect the underlying reasons," said Amitava Nandi, former director, School of Tropical Medicine.

Chowdhury was admitted in the SSKM hospital with high fever and severe stomach cramp. But he had been referred to the MR Bangur hospital on Friday at 12.26 am and died at 2.50 am.

"We did not get time to conduct any test. The deceased had been admitted with mental disorientation, high fever and pain in the abdomen. Clinical diagnosis reveals it was a case of Meningoencephalitis," said Harikrishna Chanda, superintendent, MR Bangur hospital.

This season, vector-borne diseases have killed 11 people in the city, though the Kolkata Municipal Corporation puts the figure at eight. Nandi added that the cases are increasing by the day and north Kolkata is severely affected.

Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya admitted that there was confusion over the KMC figures. "I have asked the health department to check and re-check all the data. I have also asked them to include reports of private clinics as much as possible and coordinate with the hospitals," he added.

Medical Service Centre, a socio-medical voluntary national organisation, has submitted a deputation to the CMHO, demanding immediate action to regulate the outbreak of vector-borne disease.

Meningoencephalitis
Inflammation of the brain and its meninges (The surrounding membranes the brain and spinal cord) Most cases exhibit fever, pain and rigidity of meningitis with the tremor, convulsions and paralysis of encephalitis. Localising signs such as circling, falling to one side, unilateral facial paralysis and Jacksonian type seizures are more common than in a viral encephalitis.

Could be caused by
Attacks of malaria, Japanese B Encephalitis, herpes and tuberculosis

Symptoms
* High fever
* Stiffness in the neck
* Nausea
* Unconsciousness
* Stomach cramps

Precautions
* Maintain hygiene
* In case of fever, consult a physician immediately
* Get a blood test done and if need be, go for Cerebro-Spinal Fluid Test
