Content:
The Bharatiya Vidyarthi Sena (BVS) Pune city has sent a memorandum to University of Pune (UoP) to initiate inquiry against Indian Law Society's (ILS) Law College for various reasons. Ajay Shinde, president of BVS -Pune city issued a press note alleging that the college does not complete all the lectures in an academic year.

He also alleged that the college takes the same amount of fees from students from other Backward Classes (OBC), Schedule Caste (SC) and Schedule Tribes (ST) as it does from students in the open category. Shinde stated that college amenities like the tennis court, swimming pool and gymnasium are leased out to private persons, which are of no use for the college students.

Shinde along with Sachin Shingvi, Nilesh Naikwade, Kiran Sali, Prashant Rane, Hrushikesh Pawar and other volunteers met the Vice-Chancellor to submit the

memorandum.

The BVS had intervened last week when the college denied permission to some students from taking their semester exam citing attendance shortage.

Heading: Phoenix Mecano strengthens base in India - Indian Express
Content:
Guardian Holidays, one of the leading tourism companies in the city has launched its overseas operations by opening its branch office in Singapore. Guardian has thus become the first company from Western India to receive this distinction.

Rebeca Lim, Deputy Director, Singapore Tourism, Sanjay Vaze, Jet Airways, Anil Deshmukh, Regional Manager, Air India, Neela Lad, Assistant Director, Indian Tourism - Singapore were present during the inauguration function along with Sandeep Joshi, Manish Sabde and Yatin Datar Directors of Guardian Holidays.

While describing the scope of Singapore operations Sandeep Joshi, Director, Guardian Holidays said, "Primarily Singapore office will act as an inbound tour operator for the tourists coming to Singapore from all across the globe. It will also organize conducted tours for Singapore clientele, including tours to India and various other destinations in the world."

Guardian has been appointed as the 'authorized space camp ambassador' in Singapore by NASA's US Space and Rocket Center. This will enable Guardian Holidays to undertake special educational tours for school kids to the space center. Guardian has already been associated with US Space and Rocket Center and has been conducting such educational tours for school kids in India since the past one year.

While sharing the future plans of Guardian, Manish Sabde, director - Guardian said the Singapore office marks the first step of our ambitious oversean expansion plan. "We plan to our overseas network by staring offices in Thailand and USA in near future. "

Heading: Grin and beer it - Indian Express
Content:
Invests four million Euro for capacity expansion of Pune plant

Phoenix Mecano (India) Ltd. an Indo-Swiss joint venture, engaged in the manufacturing of enclosures, mechanical and electronic components has strengthened its manufacturing base in India by adding on to the existing capacities and by starting production activities for new segments.

The Phoenix Mecano Group has invested over 4 million Euros in the last couple of years to expand its manufacturing and distribution activities in India.

Benedikt Goldkamp, CEO Phoenix Mecano AG said, "Since inception we believed in the strengths of Indian engineers to deliver out of box solutions and we also believed in advantages of undertaking manufacturing activities in India. We started our global sourcing from India 12 years ago & to leverage the advantages of the Indian manufacturing platform we also set up capacities on our own."

"Today, we are very happy to share that India has emerged has a major manufacturing hub for us, from where we service Asian & European markets and to cater to their needs we have expanded our manufacturing base here," Goldkamp added.

Under the expansion drive an ultramodern aluminum die-casting unit to manufacture enclosures has been set up, which has not only increased the capacity by 3 folds but has also increased the number of types of enclosures being manufactured in India as compared to the capacity before.

Now the Pune unit is manufacturing 70 different types of enclosures as compared to 30 before. The current capacity of the plant is to manufacture over 2.5 million enclosures per annum & the sprawling facility is spread over 70000 square feet.

Saurabh Shukla, managing director, Phoenix Mecano (India) Ltd. stated that while the company was concentrating on making India as a production hub for their global business, equal importance was given to the Indigenization of many products, making them cost competitive in the domestic market. The domestic market has been growing rapidly. Currently 60% of the sales revenue of India operations is contributed by the domestic market.

Heading: Magical Mouthfuls - Indian Express
Content:
Malaka spice Oktobeerfest is must visit for beer lovers to bond

If you have been dreaming of long lazy afternoons of sipping beer and sampling exotic cuisine, then a trip to the Malaka Spice restaurant's, Oktobeerfest is a must.

The Oktoberfest, originally a 16-day German festival is held in late September and early October in Munich with over 6 million people attending. Beer plays the main role, with 30 per cent of the year's production of beer by Munich breweries, being consumed in just two weeks of the Oktoberfest! Dating back 200 years, the first 'Oktoberfest' commemorated a Royal wedding. In 1819, the town fathers of Munich decided to celebrate it every year thus giving birth to a tradition that delights beer lovers all over the world, as various cities host their own event.

Malaka Spice at Koregaon Park, Lane 6, has been hosting their version of it for the last four years. This year the festival spans from October 7 to 30, from 12 pm to 5 pm, with unlimited Carlsberg beer and a set menu of South East Asian cuisine. All for Rs 450 per head!

For those who do not believe in chugging beer, the one reason to be there is the sumptuous menu. Chef Cheeru offers a mouth-watering spread of dishes from Thailand, Philippines, Burma, Indonesia, and Korea. These exotic dishes are authentic in taste, the dominant flavours being coconut milk, lemon grass and Galangal or Thai ginger.

Attracting a loyal multi cultural crowd every year, the festival has become almost a tradition of sorts in Pune. "I always make it a point to attend one day of the fest, although I wish it would stop getting more expensive every year!" says Melissa Fernandes. Amitabh Sharan, student, on the other hand says, " For me the fest is a time to relax and bond with old friends! We sit and catch up for the whole five hours!"

Women can indulge in the Beer Goddess Contest, and vie to see who consumes the most number of pints in one day of the festival! All in all, a fun event to be part of. So round up your gang and kick off your day with an O'zapft is! (It's tapped) as they say in Germany, or just plain Cheers!

Heading: Return of the Gold Rush - Indian Express
Content:
Brugge comes to the city this festive season laden with the inimitable taste of Belgian chocolates

The sweet season of indulgence has arrived! For the discerning consumer chocolates have moved beyond the bar variety to more delicately conjured up specialties. A relatively new kid on the chocolate block is Brugge -La Chocolaterie that offers a delight of gourmet Belgian chocolates this Diwali. The city Brugge is situated in northwest Belgium, renowned for its rich heritage of chocolate. The chocolaterie at Dhole Patil road attempts to re create that atmosphere of sheer indulgence.

"All our ingredients are imported from Belgium, and machinery from Germany," says Usma Shaik, who runs Brugge. Each piece has a luscious ganache; a filling made by heating heavy cream, poured over chopped, dark chocolate. Each bite ensures an explosion of unique flavours. Some favourites are Hazelnut Embrace, a crunchy dark chocolate wrapped around a heart of smooth hazelnut, Caramella, milk chocolate with delicious caramel filling and Dark Seduction, rich dark chocolate. "Other manufacturers use a compound of cocoa mass and vegetable fat, we use cocoa mass with butter that gives an intense flavour and melt in your mouth experience!" says Shaikh.

The pièce de résistance is their collection of- Origine Chocolates-Tanzania: A rare dark chocolate with 73per cent cocoa and hint of vanilla; Madagascar: A delicate, pale dark chocolate with 66percent cocoa content; Ecuador: refined dark chocolate with 70percent cocoa yet mild enough to carry flavours and fruity aromas; Arriba: A Creamy milk chocolate with intense Arriba cocoa body and fruity flavours with 39percent cocoa and Ghana: A rare, dark chocolate with 60percent cocoa.

Getting into the spirit of things, Brugge offers special Diwali boxes too like the Dark Temptation Box, (Bitter ganache, crunchy, milk ganache) Classic Milk Box (apricot, strawberry silk, caramella and pista) and Continental Box (cappuccino, almond delight, gianduja and lemon.).These range from Rs 550 to Rs 3000 and are packaged in crystal jars from Walterglas Germany or brocade boxes. One can even pick single pieces for Rs 25 or a box of 12 assorted chocolates for Rs 100. So treat yourself to a sublime chocolate experience this Diwali at Brugge .

Heading: Musical treat - Indian Express
Content:
Gold prices have dipped and that along with the lure of the festive season is seeing sparkles back in market

Diwali is the season to add that dazzle and sparkle in your life, and very obligingly the markets seem to comply. The price of gold that was about Rs 13,800 just days back is now hovering around Rs 11,800. Doors have started swinging again at jewelry stores around town as happy families rush in to do what we Indians do the best; buy gold!

Surendra Oswal, treasurer of Pune Saraf Association says, "This is the right time to invest in gold, with the global economy in a turmoil it is a stroke of fortune that right now during Diwali, prices are low."

Jay Parshottam of Para Amar Jewellers also elaborates on the sudden gold rush "There is a day to day fluctuation in the price of gold, up to Rs 1000 sometimes, so people have started buying in order to invest quickly." This is a burgeoning trend that is catching up in stores across town and those who can are quickly stocking up on this magic metal. He further adds, "Most of my customers are buying pure gold coins or simple gold rings. We have not had that many orders for designing jewelry, it seems as if people want to buy gold purely for investment this time instead of buying as accessories also."

Shrikant Soni, floor manager at Tanishq showroom though observes that people are still playing it safe. "Now that the prices have fallen, people expect them to fall even more. So although sales have increased a bit, we still have not got that much of walk-in crowd. It is the festive season though so we have a lot of special offers for our customers and a Diwali collection called Aleya. On display will be real uncut diamonds set in 22 carat gold."

Women however seem to have a different set of reasons irrespective to the fluctuating rates because there are many who seem to prefer buying Gold to Silver or other coloured stones. "It looks classy and does not tarnish, but one has to wear it wisely or it looks gaudy," says housewife, Richa Gupta.

Meghna Nair, student, feels that there is a major change in jewelry fashion. " We youngsters usually wear silver, but simple gold jewelry with small pendants really looks sophisticated on certain formal parties and evenings. Gold stands alone. Offer gold to someone and they will take it."

You can buy exactly the same value with a gram of gold now than you could 50 years ago. Not something that could be said about currency. Gold will continue to be a favourite and considered valuable regardless of the times and economics of the day.

Heading: Sachin Ala Re... Dhoni TOO - Indian Express
Content: For all those who love music and theatre, here is a great opportunity! Three music videos named- Emil Gilels playing Mozart, Beethoven- a triple concerto for violin, piano and violoncello and Under the stars- Renee Fleming and Bryn Terfel will be showcased on October 26 at Mazda Hall, Dastur School, Opposite Ladies Club, Camp. Organised by Poona music society, the screening will begin at 6.30 pm. Entry is open to all.

Heading: Cong gets a Diwali gift, Mathkari finally ousted - Indian Express
Content:
The Master and the Prince get a warm reception, as fans jostle to get a closer look

Sachin Tendulkar and Mahendra Singh Dhoni thrill the crowds, on the field or off it. So when the people turned up in Pimpri-Chinchwad on Friday to felicitate the master blaster, who recently scored the highest Test runs and the captain-in-waiting Dhoni who, as the stand-in skipper, led India to victory over the Aussies in the Mohali Test, there was bound to be some fireworks.

Both were honoured with the traditional Maharashtrian pheta and a sword amid scenes of jubilation, as thousands turned up from every nook and corner of Pimpri-Chinchwad to give their heroes a standing ovation.

Tendulkar and Dhoni were in town for the inauguration of the Dilip Vengsarkar Cricket Academy set up in association with the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation at Thergaon.

There was one hitch though. The crowd was badly managed by the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) and the city police. Rather than managing the crowd, they played crazy fans.

Chaos reigned during the hour-long stay of the ace cricketers at the venue. The moment they arrived at the gates of the stadium, all hell broke loose. A stampede-like situation prevailed for minutes. Over 300 shutterbugs, both professionals and amateurs, went on a clicking spree blocking their entry into the stadium. Even as the two were being led on stage, the jostling lensmen and local fans tried to keep pace. Some tripped and some got hurt, others just fell down by the side and were left out.

The volunteers appointed to help the security made life miserable for mediapersons. It was perhaps sheer providence that the two cricketers escaped unscathed.

There was more tamasha on stage. Alongside speeches, the corporators, MLC, civic officers and local heavyweights present, many with their children in tow, vied with one another to get their pictures clicked with the cricket stars. There was a melee as autograph hunters too got on stage. After the show, the scene was replicated on the ground where the two went out to toss for the inaugural match between Maharashtra XI and Mumbai XI.

Thankfully, both Tendulkar and Dhoni kept their cool, smiling and signing autographs without any fuss. In fact, Tendulkar, who has Z-plus security cover, reportedly asked his security staff to remain in the vehicle.

And when it was their turn to speak, the two didn't let the crowd down.

"Namaskar," said Sachin as the crowd of youth waiting for him since early morning went delirious. "Mehanat kara, phal jaror milel. (work hard, it will yield fruit)," he said while thanking the residents for the honour bestowed on the two.

Tendulkar said he was sure the academy would produce outstanding cricketers. He didn't utter a word on the comment made by Adam Ghilchrist regarding the monkeygate incident.

With the colourful pheta in place, Dhoni, the Jharkhand boy, hoped the "academy will not only produce Ranji trophy cricketers, but also Test cricketers."

Municipal Commissioner Asheesh Sharma played down the chaos during the visit. "Such things do happen... But overall, the function was very good. I was sitting next to Sachin and he sounded very happy. He was enquiring about the city and how the academy will be developed."

Heading: Lift death: Police still clueless - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Friday revoked the appointment of Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Vikas Mathkari as Leader of the Opposition in the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), bringing an extra Diwali cheer to the Congress. The post is most likely to go to Ulhas Bagul, Congress leader in the PMC. After the success of the Commonwealth Youth Games, this is the second time the Congress has found reason to rejoice within a week.

As news of the decision trickled in, the Congress workers wasted no time celebrating. They distributed sweets, played loud music and danced outside the PMC headquarters in Shivajinagar. Shaken by the judgement, Mathkari vacated the opposition leader's office on the third floor of PMC headquarters in Shivajinagar. He also deposited his official vehicle with the PMC.

The dispute over the post had started a year-and-a-half ago when Bagul filed a petition in the High Court challenging Mathkari's appointment by Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale.

The Congress contended that since their party was the second largest in the PMC after the NCP, the post should go to them. While the Congress had won 42 seats in the municipal polls in February 2007, the BJP-Shiv Sena alliance bagged 46, with BJP's share of 25.

Interestingly, the Congress had then started the protest against the Mayor by adopting 'Gandhigiri' and sending her flowers daily.

The court, which had held a hearing on the issue in June, gave the judgment on Friday afternoon.

The judgment says the position of the opposition leader was to be held by a party that has greater numerical strength in the house.

Upbeat over the development, Bagul said the Congress had at last got justice. "This judgment has finally given justice and relief to the Congress. The ruling 'Pune Pattern' was confusing, since the BJP was at the helm of affairs as the opposition party at PMC. This confusion has been cleared now. This will stop the unruly regime," Bagul said.

However, Bagul was wary when he said, "I am hopeful that I get the post."

The court has directed the mayor to issue appropriate directives recognising the petitioner as the 'leader of the opposition' in the PMC within a week.

The judgment says: "If the petitioner is not at present a leader of Indian National Congress, then that party shall communicate within one week, the name of the leader of the party to the mayor, who should within a week issue a declaration in favour of such person, whose name has been communicated by the party."

Mathkari said, "As democratic ethics, I immediately vacated my office and stopped using the vehicle and other facilities given to me by PMC as opposition leader. The court has revoked my appointment and refused to take the BJP-Shiv Sena union, as an alliance, saying this alliance was not registered before the polls."

He said, "After close perusal of the judgment, I will hold talks with the party leaders and take any further decision. If there is a need, we might even approach the Supreme Court." The Congress was represented by a team which included advocates R D Soni and Chandrashekhar Pingale while the advocates S K Jain and Hitesh Jain argued on behalf of the BJP.

Heading: Prime suspect in BPO employee’s murder case sent to police custody - Indian Express
Content:
The director of a software firm, Wave Technology, died after getting caught in a moving lift at the Bhosale-Shinde Arcade at Deccan Gymkhana on Thursday. Police are investigating whether human error or technical fault was the cause of the death of 36-year-old Ajay Dhayatkar.

Police on Friday recorded statements of those involved in maintenance of the lift and some eyewitnesses. "Kumar Builders had given Icon Elevators the contract for annual maintenance of lifts in the arcade in April last," said police inspector Vijaykumar Palsule. Police said Dhayarkar, a resident of Swapna Apartment in Bhusari Colony, Kothrud, had pressed the button to go down, but the lift all of a sudden, went up. He was trapped for about 25 minutes. Murlidhar Borhade of Kumar Builders, said, "When I learnt a man was trapped, I switched off the power and rushed to the sixth floor. His face and upper body was inside and from chest down, he was outside the lift." Police said the liftmen and company staff rushed him to a private hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

"The postmortem report says Dhayatkar died of shock and haemorrhage due to multiple injuries," said Palsule. "The family members are not in a position to speak. The office staff were not speaking about the incident. We are trying to record statements of more eyewitnesses. An offence would be registered against those found guilty," he added.

Mahesh Shinde of Icon Elevators said, "Our company is ISO certified. We have been maintaining various private and government lifts for the last 10 years. Safety is our top priority. Dhayatkar's death was a shock for us."

Some persons at the arcade said there was a technical problem in the lift as sometimes it used to move up even though the button for a lower floor was pressed.

Heading: Pune racing season ends with the good, the bad and the unpredictable - Indian Express
Content:
The prime suspect in the murder of 22-year-old Khushboo Dinesh Mishra, Manu Mohinder Abrol, has been remanded to police custody till October 31. Khushboo had been found murdered at the flat where she was staying on October 20 and prime suspect in the case, Manu, was found absconding from that evening.

Manu was arrested from Bhopal and was produced in the district court in Shivajinagar on Friday. He had fled the city fearing prosecution by the police. However, according to his lawyer he had turned himself in to the police at Bhopal.

Both Khushboo and Manu were working with Cap Gemini's Nigdi BPO unit as engineers. They had completed their B.E. from Bhopal and had come to Pune for job. Khushboo was staying at Aditya Breeze Park in Balewadi, while Manu was residing at Nisarga Society in Wakad.

The defence lawyer argued that since the weapon used for the murder has been found and the clothes worn by the accused as well as the deceased had been identified Abrol should not be remanded to 14 days police custody.

The defence also said that he was not a hardened criminal and that the girl had not complained anywhere against Manu.

The prosecution, meanwhile, argued that since the crime was of a serious nature and also the fact that the two had previously been involved in a serious relationship, a deeper probe into the case was required.

Taking note of the argument, judge A K Mandavgade remanded him to seven days police custody. Manu will now be produced in the court on October 31.

Heading: Mother-son duo attempt suicide - Indian Express
Content:
The 29 days of the Pune racing calendar had its rounds of highs and lows. With the season offering the highest stakes offered so far — a record prize money of Rs 613.35 lakh — there were many expectations from it. While some in the forms of sponsored Sundays and a ten per cent incentive to owners scored points, there were disappointments too like the fewer number of runners in the field and the rainfall that struck off an entire racing day. As the Pune season concludes here's an overall view of the July to October sporting event.

The basic yardsticks of judging a season are the attendance, the betting and sponsorships and we did well in all three, said Vivek Jain, chairman marketing committee of the Royal Western India Turf Club (RWITC). According to Jain, while attendance went up by 10 per cent, betting increased by 20 per cent this season. Plus the committee managed to make every racing Sunday a sponsored one, an unprecedented achievement for the Pune races. "I would say the season went off very smoothly-there were no major glitches," added Behram Engineer, secretary RWITC, even as trainer Narendra Lagad called it his best season since he had a whopping 271 runners overall.

On the downside though rains played spoilsport right from the beginning and finally the September 20 race day was washed out completely. Many of the races also saw very few runners, due to horses being withdrawn because of the viral fever that dominated the season. On October 24 itself 12 horses were withdrawn belonging mainly to owner Khushroo Dhunjibhoy leading him to comment that though the season was okay, "it is ending on a disappointing note for him."

Even though the club registered a ten per cent increase in attendance according to race goers this was mainly due to the sponsored races on Sunday with the sponsors bringing in their guests. "The crowds have been very scarce on Saturdays giving the course a dull look," said Savita Kolhi, a regular race goer. Online instant replay of the races and the proliferation of Off Course Betting Centres (OCBC) were some of the reasons cited for low attendance by Colonel (retd) GS Gill, another racing aficionado. There was also an ongoing tussle between the RWITC and the PCB and army authorities over parking (tyres of many of the vehicles parked outside the race course were deflated on a certain day) that may have also kept away some of the crowd.

The races also saw a few upsets and controversial decisions. "We have undertaken three enquiries where we felt the jockey did not let the horse run to its potential and will take strict action against offenders if they are proved guilty," said Pradyuman Singh, senior stipendiary steward.

And while not directly affecting the racing season the Cyrus Poonawalla-Vivek Jain rift coming to the fore this season and the subsequent unpleasant exchanges between the two did dampen the spirits somewhat. "It does disturb everyone and cannot make for a happy environment," agreed Jain, as he added, "I do hope it doesn't snowball into a fight just as we go on to the Mumbai season now."

The racing authorities nevertheless plan to end the season on a high note. The 'O' awards instituted by the RWITC "on the lines of the Oscars'' but given only to the racing fraternity will be declared and given away on Saturday. A special jury had been constituted for the purpose. That coupled with the many dos that were hosted by the sponsors of the Sunday races did mange to keep the glamour tag firmly on the sport.

Now it's onto the Mumbai turf for further action.

Heading: Husband, in-laws burn woman - Indian Express
Content:
A mother and son attempted suicide on Friday by consuming a bottle of insecticide in the premises of the Shivajinagar district and sessions court.

They have been identified as Rahibai Haribhau Johri (55) and her son Laxman Haribhau Johri, 30. The incident occurred around 5 pm, outside court number four.

The duo has been fighting a land dispute case in the civil court for the last twenty years and was apparently stressed over the delay in reaching a verdict. Both of them were rushed to Sassoon General Hospital where they are undergoing treatment.

A case of attempted suicide has been lodged at the Shivajinagar police station. According to sources, Rahibai is recovering while her son is in a critical condition.

Heading: Three held for selling stolen vehicle parts - Indian Express
Content:
A woman, who was into the five months of her marriage, was allegedly set on fire by her husband and in laws on Wednesday morning. The incident occurred at Narayangaon Peth in Haveli taluka.

The victim Tejaswini Rahul Chaudari (19), is a resident of Naigaon Peth in Haveli taluka. Her parents live in Bhivdi in Purandar taluka.

The Loni Kalbhor police have arrested husband Rahul Haribhau Chaudary, his father Haribhau Maruti Chaudary, mother Subadhra Haribhau Chaudary, brother Ashok Haribhau Chaudary, and sister Rekha Ashok Chaudary on the basis of a complaint filed by the victim.

Rahul owns a farm in Naigaon. He also works with a vehicle showroom. Tejaswini's in-laws wanted to build a house and demanded that Tejaswini bring money from her parents.

At 9 am on Wednesday, her mother-in-law poured kerosene on Tejaswini and set her on fire. Hearing her cry for help, the neighbours came to her rescue and took her to Sassoon Hospital. According to police sub inspector Bhimrao Naik, Tejaswini has suffered 96 per cent burns.

Heading: ‘Retd armed forces personnel should use expertise in corporate world’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Hadapsar police raided a godown at Nana Peth and arrested three persons for their alleged involvement in selling spare parts of stolen vehicles. The accused have been identified as Mohammed Arif Yusuf Shaikh (49), owner of the godown, his son Sabir (23) of Nana Peth and employee Ayaz Yakub Shaikh (30) of Mundhwa.

Acting on a tip off, a police team raided the godown on Thursday afternoon. Senior police inspector V S Sonawane said, "We found that Ayaz Shaikh was dismantling a motorcycle. Owner Arid Shaikh said that he had a license to purchase the vehicles on auction and then sell the spare parts. We found some 42 number plates of motorcycles at the spot. Some vehicles were legally possessed. But there was a point of suspicion because a few numbers were of new motorcycles. The regional transport office and the court don't give permission for auctioning new vehicles."

"We arrested the owner, his son and the employee who was caught red-handed while dismantling a two-wheeler. The accused have been remanded to police custody till October 26. "A search is on for one more accomplice who was providing the vehicles to them," Sonwane said.

Police suspect that accused have nexus with vehicle thieves. "The accused have been charged with purchasing stolen motorcycles. We recovered 16 engines of different motorcycles, tyres, rims, tools, fuel tanks and other parts worth Rs 2.5 lakh," said investigation officer sub inspector Bhimrao Gajare.

Heading: MUHS to begin course in reproductive genetics - Indian Express
Content:
In order to keep the armed forces young, over 60,000 men and women aged 38 - 40 have to choose an alternative career, said Maj Gen S G Chaterji, director general, resettlement, here on Friday.

Chaterji was speaking during an interactive session between the defence forces and the industry organised by the Southern Command. "Those who opt out of or complete their tenure with the armed forces are skilled, motivated and experienced individuals with a sense of responsibility who are looking for continuity in their professional careers. These are the exact requirements the industry looks for in its workforce today," he said.

He said that retired defence forces personnel could use their experience and expertise in several areas within the corporate world, such as security, logistics, marketing and telecommunications. "If ex-service workforce and those in the industry come together on a common platform, it will be a win-win situation for both sides," Chaterji said.

The chief guest on the occasion, Southern Command General Officer Commanding-in-chief Lt Gen Noble Thamburaj urged the industry — particularly in and around Pune, which is home to a sizeable number of retired armed forces personnel — to take cognizance of the various qualities that they bring with them. "Cost control, safety measures and environmental protection are second nature to them," he said, adding that most of them were proven team leaders who have regard for authority.

Thamburaj also suggested that corporates visit the various Army Training Centres and observe first-hand how the armed forces personnel tackle the challenges they face and take quick decisions, often without any detailed instructions.

Senior executives from Tata Motors, Forbes Marshall, Finolex Cables, Godrej Industries and University of Pune vice chancellor Narendra Jadhav among others attended the function.

Heading: Thane-Borivali BEST buses soon - Indian Express
Content:
Genetic disorders account for three per cent of all births. Ten to 15 per cent of all conceptions end in loss of pregnancy during the first three months. At Sassoon General Hospital the incidence of spinal disorders among foetuses was as high as 7.5 per 1000 births.

This and the increasing trend of the rise in number of genetic disorders has led the Maharashtra University of Health Sciences (MUHS), Pune to introduce a course in reproductive genetics.

Dr Prakash Gambhir, director of Genetics, Immunology and Biochemistry unit at the MUHS, Pune centre said that the course will be conducted on weekends and will introduce the speciality to gynaecologists and medical postgraduates. A high-tech facility that will enable research in genetic disorders — conditions caused by abnormalities in genes and chromosomes — and provide diagnostic and prenatal facility .

According to Gambhir, the medical education has so far remained focussed on areas like infectious disorders, communicable diseases, nutrition and related disorders. We have antibiotics and immunisation modes to deal with these ailments. With this separate department specialising in genetics, immunology and biochemistry, research can also be done on the reasons behind genetic disorders.

The course will provide training and an overview of these issues including details about the new technologies for health care providers.

Heading: Pune-based advocate, husband arrested on charges of fraud - Indian Express
Content:
There is good news in store for residents of Ghodbunder road area. Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) will soon start its bus services between Mulund (West) station and Borivali via Ghodbunder. Commuters on this route had been having problems because of poor bus connectivity.

"We will soon be plying 20 buses on the route. We will increase the frequency and the number of buses after looking at the response," said BEST General Manager Uttam Khobragade. "We also plan to start more services on the (Thane) Bus Rapid Transport System (BRTS) route, but this would be non-AC buses." BEST at present operates the King Long buses from Thane (Cadbury junction) to Backbay Depot.

The road is an important link that connects the eastern and western suburbs besides Borivali and other satellite townships of Mira road and Vasai Virar.

Over the past five years, a township has come up on Ghodbunder road.

The bus service would be a welcome change for the residents of Ghodbunder as the area doesn't have enough transport facilities, though the Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) and TMT ply a few vehicles on the route.

The Thane Municipal Transport (TMT), part of the Thane Municipal Corporation (TMC), has some 250 buses in its fleet and a sizeable number is either more than 15 years old or non-functional. Thane commuters have been complaining for long against TMT's inefficient services.

Interestingly, BEST has sent a proposal to the state government to allow them to take over TMT. "We are waiting for the nod from the government. If there are any issues to be solved, we can sort them out," added Khobragade.

Both TMT and BEST buses ply on each other's routes, but both have denied permission to each other to ply on the Ghodbunder route. On the same route, the TMT takes passengers to Mira road and Bhayander.

The matter was sorted out last week after the Deputy Chairman of the Assembly, Vasant Davkhare, arranged a meeting among senior officials of BEST, TMC, TMT, RTO and officials from the state transport department.

Heading: Four sentenced to life for raping, murdering minor - Indian Express
Content:
Acting on a complaint filed in the magistrate's court at Borivali by a businessman, the Malvani police on Wednesday arrested a Pune-based advocate Jayshree Mahadi (39) and her husband Vishnu Mahadi (45), who works as an estate agent, for cheating the businessman to the tune of Rs 5 crore.

According to the Malvani police, Tuljitsingh Rajput, a businessman based at Malad had got in touch with the couple in 2007 through some other estate agents and property dealers. During their meeting, Uma and her husband told Rajput that they knew the owner of a plot of cultivable land in Madh Island which Rajput was eager to purchase.

The couple had claimed that the land measuring 9.30 acre was worth Rs 7.51 crore and accepted an initial amount of Rs. 3.75 crore from Rajput, the police said.

"However, after the payment was made and the duo promised to get the paperwork done, Rajput got suspicious of the duo beacuse of their general behaviour. Also, the paperworks they procured did not seemed to be genuine," said Senior Police Inspector Jaywant Hargude of the Malvani police station.

However, early this year Rajput informed the Mahadis that he wasn't interested in the deal and asked them to return him a sum of Rs. 5 crore, which had been agreed as the cancellation deal charges by both the parties.

"Consequently, the Mahadis gave him a cheque of Rs 5 crore which was dishonoured. Rajput also realised that the paperwork regarding the land ownership that the due had shown him was forged. Based on this, he approached the Borivali Metropolitan Court and filed a private complaint against the Mahadis for cheating and forgery," said Hargude.In June 2008, the magistrate directed the Malvani police to investigate the matter and after conducting due inquiry, a team of officials attached to the Malvani police station went to Pune and arrested the couple on Wednesday and brought them to Mumbai.

"The due were produced in the court and were remanded to court till October 27. During the investigation, we also discovered that the land in question which the Mahadis had claimed to be able to sell is owned by a joint family and there is a dispute in court relating to its ownership. The Mahadis are not even remotely connected to the family that owns the land. We're conducting further inquiries into the matter," added Hargude.

Heading: Fire in industrial estate, safety norms flouted - Indian Express
Content:
Convicts were denied a 'sedative' without doctor's prescription by victim's father who ran a drug store

Four daily wage earners were on Friday sentenced to life imprisonment for raping and murdering a minor girl after her father, a chemist shop owner, refused to give them a medicine, which can be used as a sedative, without a doctor's prescription in 2006.

Additional Sessions Judge S Ganediwal convicted the four accused — Parvez Ahmed (32), Mohammad Sarif (25), Hasib Manjum (25) and Mohammad Sameer (18)— who worked as labourers in Shivaji Nagar area.  

According to the police, the four accused had on April 7, 2006 visited the chemist shop of complainant Raju Shikhare asking for a medicine called Restil which has to be given only on doctors advise as it can be used as a sedative. Since the accused did not have a doctor's prescription, Shikhare refused to give them the medicine after which the four accused got into a verbal spat with him and threatened him of dire consequences within a short period. 

The next day Shikhare's three and a-half-year-old daughter, Minakshi went missing and after a thorough search when she couldn't be found Shikhare lodged a missing person complaint with the Shivaji Nagar police station. Accordingly on April 9, 2006, one person Kunnar informed the police, that foul smell was emanating from an under-construction septic tank in the area, following which the police searched and found a decomposed body. On personal identification by Shikhare, the body came to be identified to be of his daughter.    

During investigation, the police got vital leads after one Sayyaed Rehmatali informed them that he had seen the four accused taking the victim with them on the fateful day. The police a week later zeroed in on the four accused. One of the accused Sameer confessed to his crime before a magistrate, while the police carried out a narco-analysis test on the others in which they also confessed to the crime. n the test, all of them stated that their motive for committing such a ghastly act was that Shikhare had refused to give them the medicine.

During the trial, the prosecution examined 23 witnesses to build up its case. They told the court about the recovery of the girl's body while the father narrated his spat with the accused at his medical shop. Public Prosecutor D K Joshi demanded that the accused should be given death sentence as it falls under the category of rarest of rare. However, the court sentenced them to life imprisonment.

Heading: Pisavli murder: Sena corporator held - Indian Express
Content:
A major fire broke out at an industrial estate in Andheri on Friday afternoon. While no casualties were reported, the Mumbai Fire Brigade has said that the units clearly violated basic safety regulations.

The fire broke out at Laxmi Industrial Estate along New Link Road in Andheri around 3 pm. As the units were under renovation, there were no employees present.

The destruction was similar to that in the Retiwala Industrial Estate fire which took place in March this year. Those units had violated fire safety rules, to the extent of blocking emergency exit and entry points.

Although the fire department is still investigating the cause of Friday's fire, officials said it could be related to the renovation work. "The fire was major. However, we have prevented it from spreading," said Chief Fire Officer A V Sawant. The main unit where fire took place also has two garment units and a hotel next door. Right behind the spot where the fire gutted property worth several lakh rupees is a pre-primary school, L'Ecole Montesorri, which luckily suffered no damages.

Officials said the units in the industrial estate had flouted many fire safety rules. "The fire exits were blocked. It was fortunate there were no employees inside, or else we could have seen several people injured," said Divisional Fire Officer S A Mahdi. The interiors were gutted completely, owing to the garments and wooden furniture stored inside. Eight fire engines, five water tankers and an ambulance were used in the fire-fighting operations.

In March, a major fire had broken out at Byculla's Retiwala Industrial Estate, killing eight people who found themselves trapped inside the small and congested units due to suffocation. Following this incident, the fire department had surveyed 518 industrial estates in the city and had found that almost all of them flouted fire safety norms.

Heading: Five MNS men held for shopkeeper’s death - Indian Express
Content:
Meanwhile, the Manpada police on Friday sought custody of Shiv Sena corporator Kailash Shinde in connection with the murder of MNS activist Gurunath Bhoir who was allegedly murdered in Pisavli village of Kalyan earlier this week. Two North Indians had also been found murdered in Pisavli.

Gurunath Bhoir was the brother of Kalyan taluka chief of the MNS, Moreshwar Bhoir.

After the Bhoir family alleged that it was personal rivalry that had led to his murder and not the MNS- North Indian clashes, Manpada police arrested Kailash Shinde. Amidst huge protests by Sena supporters, Shinde was brought to the Kalyan metropolitan court.

The prosecution argued that a complaint was lodged against Shinde just eight days before the murder. Bhoir had apparently approached the Manpada police complaining that Shinde's men had tried to kill him, argued Prosecutor S V Kamble.

Magistrate S D Jadhav handed Shinde to police custody till October 28.

Heading: Raj’s bail extended till Nov 11 - Indian Express
Content:
Five Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) workers are in the dock in connection with the death of a shopkeeper. The shopkeeper, Lalji Krishna Yadav, collapsed after the MNS workers allegedly threatened him to roll down the shutters of his shop on Wednesday afternoon.

A group of MNS workers had reached the shop and ordered him and the owners of neighbouring shops to down shutters. According to eyewitnesses, they were brandishing bamboo sticks and had pushed and shoved Yadav. While closing his shop after the threat, Yadav collapsed. Post-mortem report reveals that his death was due to "natural causes".

The police on Thursday arrested Dinesh Gawli (20), Sachin More (18), Sunil Pandey (27), Sachin Salvi (22) and Abdul Choudhari (28) under Indian Penal Code sections 143, 149 and 304 (A) relating to unlawful assembly and causing death due to negligence.

Heading: HC orders Bigg Boss producers to give CDs to police - Indian Express
Content:
Court has asked GRP not to arrest the MNS leader till his anticipatory bail application comes up for hearing

Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray got a Diwali breather on Friday when a Sessions Court in Kalyan extended the interim relief granted to him till November 11. The Government Railway Police(GRP) on Wednesday had moved an application seeking his custody.

Sessions Judge K K Tantrapale has now asked the GRP not to arrest Raj till November 11, when his anticipatory bail application comes up for hearing.

On Wednesday, Thackeray's lawyer had moved an anticipatory bail application foreseeing arrest by the GRF before moving for interim relief. On Friday, however, the prosecution sought time to file a reply regarding the anticipatory bail plea of Thackeray.

The judge has also directed the MNS leader to abide by the conditions laid down on Wednesday while granting him interim relief and to present himself before the Kalyan railway police as and when required.

Special public prosecutor Rohini Salian also argued that Thackeray's presence was required when the court was hearing his bail application. The court asked if the state was prepared to tackle any situation or further violence. "Is your machinery prepared?" asked the judge. The court will on November 11 decide if Thackeray's presence is required during the hearing.

Heading: Slow death - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court has directed the producers of Bigg Boss: Season 2 to provide the CDs of the TV show to the police to help in their investigation into a complaint regarding charges of obscenity on the show.

President of Mumbai Pradesh Youth Congress Committee, Sunil Ahire, had lodged the complaint with the Andheri police station earlier this month, saying the show was propagating indecency and vulgarity through its participants. Later, Endemol India Private Limited, which is producing the reality show, had moved the court for quashing of the FIR.

The court on Friday asked the producers to submit all the 60 CDs to the police and adjourned the hearing till November 14.

According to additional public prosecutor Shahajirao Shinde, only five CDs have been handed over to the police so far. "Pursuant to the investigation, the matter will come up for hearing on November 14," Shinde said.The court had earlier directed the police not to take any coercive action against the petitioners till further orders.

The complainant has named the producer, director, channel and participants of the show — Rahul Mahajan, Payal Rohatgi and Sambhavana Set—for promoting obscenity. According to the petition, Ahire in his complaint states that the (Colours) channel was propagating indecency and vulgarity that was being "acted and represented" by the participants, which has the effect of vitiating the minds of the youth.

The producers, however, had contended that there is not a shred of evidence in the complaint to even remotely suspect that the petitioners are guilty of the offences. They point out that the complainant is president of city Youth Congress, which also includes Congress MP Sanjay Nirupam, who incidentally was a part of the reality show and was the first to get eliminated from it.

They further allege that it was a political game being played by the complainant as the show also features late BJP leader Pramod Mahajan's son Rahul Mahajan. The petition contends that the participants are not enacting a script and are merely living their lives within the confines of the house, cut off from the rest of the world.

Heading: Aglow - Indian Express
Content:
The last day of Lakme Fashion week draws to a never-ending close

Show of the day
On a day when bad designs reigned supreme, Anuj Sharma emerged a winner with his Knot for You collection. The collection revolved around strategically placed knots that bound, shaped, draped and constructed his carefully tailored outfits. Effortlessly chic, he only made use of crepe and georgette selecting just three muted colours: brown, nude and grey. For a Grecian effect, the designer knotted the fabric to create versions of flowers or a butterfly-like effect and held the garments at the shoulders with the help of slim black ribbons.

Ensemble of the day
ANEETH and Chinar of Gaba created some rustic magic with their khadi and handloom line. What we loved the most was a pair of loose pedal pushers in white teamed with a two-layered smock flowing green tunic with a white embroidered gamcha thrown around the bag. Nice.

Celeb of the day
WHEN your collection isn't doing the talking for you, bring on Shiamak Davar to shake his hips. An absolutely atrocious collection by Vikram Phadnis was overshadowed by a brilliant performance by Shiamak. After all, what are good friends for?

Goss of the day
SHOWSTOPPERS have become a joke lately. To begin with, Achla Sachdev was the 'show starter' for Babita M. We could have digested that. But then came the icing on the cake —a limping Chhaya Momaya sauntering down the ramp for Lina Tipnis. The photographers roared in protest.

Trend of the day
IF you want to get your wardrobe ready for summer, make sure you have lots of prints. Agnimitra Paul showcased saris with floral and leaf prints, while Babita Malkani's abstract prints were seen on gowns and knee length dresses. Lina Tipnis too showcased a few outfits that had a hint of geometrical prints on them.

Heading: The end of a beginning - Indian Express
Content:
A 24-year-old youth was allegedly kidnapped by some young men on Saturday. Amir Hamid Sheikh was allegedly picked up from his office in Pune Camp and taken away in a black Scorpio while some others followed them in a red Maruti Swift (MH-14 7175). Amir is an employee of Parmar Travel agency located in the basement of Parmar Classic, a building near Parmar Hospital in Pune Camp.

He was said to be in love with a Hindu girl from Thergaon. When her brother found out about their relationship, he went to Amir's office along with 10-12 youths and forcefully took him along with them, police said.

When Amir did not return home, his uncle lodged a complaint at Lashkar police station. The youths took Amir to Hinjewadi where they thrashed him in the car.

Amir later reached home, but the scared family decided to take him to the Hinjewadi police station.

Four youths were arrested by Hinjewadi police and they were produced in court on Sunday.

They have been remanded to police custody till October 29. The youths include Amit Waghmare (3) Sandip Shelke (24), Mayur Pawar (21), all staying at Pawar Nagar at Thergaon, and Sandip Jadhav (22) staying at Jay Mathur Society in Thergaon, said police. Police have booked the four youths and their accomplices under Sections 363, 365, 452, 427, and 34 of the IPC.

Heading: Talking point  with  Abhijeet Sawant - Indian Express
Content:
A British-Asian project gives 60 filmmakers, 60 seconds each to answer this question

Are we outsiders in our own homes?" asks Delhi-based filmmaker Khadeeja Arif in her film To Be Continued. The postscript of her film and 59 others is clear — there's no easy way to spell home. The films are part of a British-Asian project called 60x60. The brainchild of London-based arts organisation Motiroti, 60x60 comprises 60 films by 60 filmmakers — 20 each from Britain, Pakistan and India.

"The filmmakers present their perspective of what home is," says Ali Zaidi, creative director of 60x60, who wanted to "focus on creative exchange between Britain, India and Pakistan". The project began last year with calls for entries. "We received 55 proposals from India, 47 from Pakistan and 49 from Britain," he says.

Arif, 30, vents her anger through a story of a young model who is relentlessly questioned by the police after finding a picture of her against the Twin Towers. "Once, we were what we thought we were. Then 9/11 happened, and how we looked at ourselves became different from how others looked at us. Even in our own home ground, we're under constant surveillance," says Arif. The spectre of terror shadows another Delhi filmmaker. Ritu Datta's film We Do follows the drama of hatred through the moods of a Kathakali dancer. Twenty-somethings Neel Chaudhuri, Samar Grewal and Kartikey Shiva, meanwhile, confront a motorist's fear on the Capital roads. "In a city like Delhi, our fears and insecurities come alive when the road becomes a landscape of uncertainty," says Chaudhuri. The film, Man on the Road, is a photorama, a series of spliced photographs taken on winter nights at Connaught Place and near Khan Market.

But it is not just terror — or the absence of it — that defines home. British director Said Adrus's film Homebound shows his mother in her Swiss home, constantly surfing channels for Hindi films and soaps. Hers is a journey that began in a Gujarati village and the 80-year-old is still looking for a place called home. Screenings of the films are on at Islamabad and London. A special screening was held at Delhi colleges in September, but an official premiere is planned later this year in the Capital.

Heading: Stay Tuned - Indian Express
Content:
Tread with caution

Tanaaz Currim is one cautious lady. Apparently both Tanaaz and her husband Bakhtiyar Irani were approached to perform together on Zee TV's Diwali Hungama, but Tanaaz politely declined the offer citing prior commitments. But the fact of the matter is that she didn't want to do any act with Bakhtiyar because of his wild ways. She's had previous experience of Bakhtiyar's overexcited ways on reality shows when he'd throw her and kick her whenever she missed a step or could not get them right while rehearsing. We're sure Bakhtiyar will now tone down his enthusiasm in the future.

Jugal's surprise

Indian Idol 4 just got more interesting. The special guest on Thursday's episode was Jugal Hansraj, and accompanying him were none other than Romeo and Laila, the adorable leads of his directorial debut Roadside Romeo. The Indian Idol contestants were delighted to see their guests and put up an impromptu show of singing, dancing and mimicry and in between shots; they also sang songs from Jugal's films. The actor-director was touched by this gesture and in spite of a cold he happily posed and interacted with all the contestants.

He also promised to send everyone a music CD of his film as a token of appreciation. Talk about a mutual admiration club.

Honest Himesh

Himesh Reshammiya will be at his candid best on IBN7's Zindagi Live which will be telecast Sunday night at 8 pm. The singer tackles questions about his family, struggles and his perceived arrogance with great aplomb. Nobody can accuse Himesh of not being honest especially when he admits that in his infamous row with senior singer Asha Bhonsle, he was in the wrong. Now with this kind of honesty, no wonder the singer is such a hit with the masses. Maybe the real Himesh shines through the reel Himesh.

Fantastic four

On November 2, Jalwa Four 2 Ka 1 will air every Sunday at 9 pm on 9X. The show will bring together Mika, Rakhi Sawant, Shakti Kapoor and Shweta

Tiwari as four opposing captains. TV actors Ali Asgar and Divyanka Tripathi will play hosts. As its judge, Mahima Choudhry will be back in the reckoning after vanishing from the big screen. Director-actor Satish Kaushik is the other judge. The show as a novelty factor, has introduced bidding system.

Heading: Chatter box - Indian Express
Content:
As that titanic soap, Kyunki Saas bhi Kabhi bahu Thi, goes off air after eight politically-incorrect years, here's a list of other shows that need to follow suit

It's okay to cast a patronising glance when someone brings up the topic of the soap operas on Indian television, but if you say you don't know who Parvati and Tulsi are, you have to be lying through your teeth. Indian television changed forever when Balaji Television introduced to the audiences the ideal daughter-in-law through its twin shows: Kahani Ghar Ghar Kii and Kyunkii Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi. Mothers-in-law sang their praises for daughters-in-law who toiled hard to exceed expectations. As Kyunki, following in the tracks of Kahanii, prepares to go off air by the year-end, it takes with it the end of an era, for better or worse.

Says Rajesh Chadha, business head, BAG Films (known for another long-running show, Kumkum), "Kyunki and Kahanii paved way for others and in many ways opened the minds of the Indian audiences." The shows have seen their ups and downs in TRPs, and reinvented storylines by introducing elements of love, hatred, infidelity, vengeance and generation leaps into drawing rooms, coming close to the iconic Bold and the Beautiful. Kyunki is famously credited for the resurrecting characters. This was the result of the lead character on-screen Mihir's death, which was no less than a national tragedy. But over years, TRPs continued to dip and after having tried every trick, the shows are finally being pulled off air.

While there is no dearth of shows that started with a good story but eventually lost the plot, a handful that have tried every trick to survive, need to bow out gracefully.

Woh Rehne Wali Mehelon Ki (Sahara One) has been on air for over three years now and two generation leaps later, the producers, Rajshri Productions, refuse to give up. The TRPs have dipped but the producers still feel that it has a select audience. "Keeping with the values that Rajshri is associated with, our show has always been inspirational and steered clear from clichés like rape and kidnaps. Like our movies, this is a show that a family can watch together," justifies Kavita Barjatya.

Kumkum - Ek Pyaara Sa Bandhan on Star Plus has been on air for over six years now. But Chadha feels that their USP remains Hussain Kuwajerwala and Juhi Parmar's love story. He accepts that while the show is facing a rough patch a 'reincarnation' of the lead character may just save Kumkum.

In a country obsessed with fairness creams, Saat Phere on Zee TV, the longest-running show after Kyunki and Kumkum, struck a chord with millions by introducing a dusky girl as the protagonist Saloni, making Rajshree Thakur the next uncrowned queen of the industry after Smriti Irani and Sakshi Tanwar. But with Thakur's expected exit from the Saat Phere, many doubt the future of the show.

Meanwhile, shows like Balika Vadhu have paved way for a new trend. As scriptwriter Gautam Hegde points out, "The latest trend is to make the soap high on the emotional quotient. Balika Vadhu and Sapna Baabul Ka…and Bidaai — the current TRP chart toppers-are free of the zoom effects." Could these shows mark the end of the high drama? Erm, not yet.
