Heading: No end to canine nightmare in city - Indian Express
Content:
ROADSIDE ROMEO (animation)

Voices of Saif Ali Khan, Kareena Kapoor, Jaaved Jaaferi DIRECTOR: Jugal Hansraj

Indian animation has finally come of age. Roadside Romeo, the first Walt Disney-Yashraj rollout is a barrel of fun: "Bole toh, ekdum jhakaas, baap".

It combines the best aspects of both studies — Disney's expertise in creating animated figures which live and breathe, and Yashraj's forte in frothy romance: what better than getting Romeo and Laila voiced by real-life lovers Saif and Kareena?

Romeo is a one-time pampered pooch, now abandoned on the mean streets of Mumbai. Laila is a saucy, red-scarf-around-her-dainty-neck dancer, who only has to bat her impossibly large eyelashes for Romeo to start panting. Trouble looms in the shape of the pug-ugly Charlie Anna (Jaaved), who rules with a ruthless paw and a bunch of louts. He fancies Laila, and woe to any Tom, Dick, or Romeo who dares comes in between.

The alacrity with which the characters break into song-and-dance shows that Disney or no Disney, Bollywood rules. Whether style-bhai Romeo is kicking up his heels with his canine pals, or looking for a likely spot to pee ("Yahaan koi toilet nahin hai kya? Man, what a dump!") you can actually see Saif, who does cool like no else.

And when sexy Laila shakes her charming rump, breathily coming on to her besotted beau, you know that's Kareena. Both sizzle up the screen.

Where debutant director Jugal Hansraj falters is with the villainous Chaaaarrrlie Anna: Jaaved Jaaferi is made to growl incomprehensibly and break wind more often than getting a chance at being a riot.

He does make you guffaw, but only once in a while, and for someone of Jaaferi's goofy brilliance, that's not enough.

But we can live with this Charlie. In his words, he's our chappie, so he makes us happy. We can also handle the strong resemblance our Mumbai curs have to Disney-style American doggie-doos, because we know that given a chance, they will open their mouths to utter a desi "bhow bhow" rather than the westernised "bow wow".

Roadside Romeo is Hindi cinema's first stylish, slick animated feature, which pulls off the toughest fe— appealing to both adults and children.

That's, like, cool, dude.

HEROES

CAST: Salman Khan, Sunny Deol, Sohail Khan, Vatsal Sheth, Bobby Deol, Preity Zinta, Mithun Chakraborty, Dino Morea, Amrita Arora, Riya Sen; DIRECTOR: Samir Karnik

Two city slickers set out to deliver letters from dead servicemen to their far-flung families, and in the process, discover themselves.

The premise of Heroes is interesting. And in parts Samir Karnik's film does manage to say what it set out to: that pride ( the Hindi 'garv' is a better word) keeps the families of the deceased soldiers going, that we civilians sleep peacefully only because someone has given up his life for us, and that we have a country only because we have a brave 'fauji' guarding our borders. But the director falls for the easiest trick in the book: he wrings tears out of so many situations that everyth—ng ¿ even the supreme sacrifice that the soldiers —ake turns trite.

Heroes needed a radical change in treatment, but it falls through halfway between keeping things low-key and going full-tilt at melodrama. What can you do if pretty Preity is a war-widow, speaking flawless Punjabi, keeping it together for her old in-laws and a young son? And Salman her bluff Jat hearthrob who says : "Teri liye lakh jawani, par yeh jawani desh ke naam", or words to that effect. Sunny plays a rum-swilling disabled airman who loses younger brother Bobby who carried a torch for the Army. Mithun is an embittered father who hasn't forgiven son Dino for dying. And the two boys-who-turn-into-men on their road journey, armed with a camera and alarming naivete, are Sohail and Vatsal.

The subject deserved a better film.

shubhra.gupta@gmail.com

Heading: NHAI no to widen Pinjore-Kalka highway - Indian Express
Content:
The stray dog menace that has haunted the city for some time now does not appear to have a solution in hindsight.

The proposal of the Municipal Corporation to construct a dog pound has been hanging fire for over four years now even as over 5,000 stray dogs continue to wreak havoc regularly.

While a site in Dadumajra was initially identified for the construction of a dog pound, it met strong opposition from the residents, including area councillor Kamlesh. She rued that the garbage of the entire city was already being dumped at the area dumping site and therefore, the dog pound should be located at some other place.

Several suggestions followed suit: a dog pound in the dumping ground or at a site located in the outskirts of the city or even in Maloya or Hallomajra.

In 2007, the then UT Finance Secretary S K Sandhu had assured Municipal Commissioner P S Aujla that land required for the construction of the dog pound will be handed over to the corporation in a few days. The corporation identified half-an-acre of land at Dhanas for the purpose.

A proposal was also mooted to relocate the dog pound to Sector 25 at a site allocated to the People for Animals (PFA). A two-acre plot of land was given to the organisation to set up a centre.

The issue, meanwhile, finds a mention in the discussion of the coordination committee meetings of the UT Administration and Municipal Corporation with Mayor Pardeep Chhabra said to have shown urgency for a quick start to the project.

Mayor Pardeep Chhabra says, "The large number of stray dogs is a menace. Some steps will be taken at the earliest and we hope to finalise the site for the dog pound in the coming days."

The dogs, at present, are picked up, sterilised and then dropped back in the same sector. The agencies involved in the process include PFA as well as Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA).

Heading: Segregation at source: a step further towards garbage disposal - Indian Express
Content:
With the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) rejecting the Administration's request to widen the Pinjore-Kalka national highway, even the efforts of the district administration to seek the same have proved futile. The Panchkula Administration, recently, had gone ahead with the shifting of electricity poles and lines in the area to carry out the widening of the road.

After the Project Director of the NHAI claimed that there was never a proposal to widen the Pinjore-Kalka patch to decongest the traffic in the region, the Panchkula Administration had sent it a fresh proposal through the Haryana PWD (B and R). "Though a proposal was sent to the NHAI to widen the patch, it is not being entertained by them for the reason that the Pinjore-Parwanoo bypass is being constructed to take care of extra traffic," said KK Jalan, Commission and Secretary, PWD (B and R).

At present, as the Pinjore-Kalka highway is with the NHAI, the PWD cannot carry out the widening. Jalan said: "The widening by the PWD department will only be possible 2011 when the highway is handed over."

The Electricity department, however, rues the fact that a month after shifting lines and poles, its payment of Rs 19,65,620 is hanging fire. Panchkula DC Rajender Kataria refused to comment on the issue and said that the NHAI had agreed in principle to pay the Electricity department for the shifting.

Heading: ‘No change in strength of human rights panel’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Administration has taken many initiatives to develop an effective system of waste disposal in the city. From making the city bin-free to banning polythene bags and having sehaj safai kendras (SSKs), various kinds of efforts have been made.

There is a need, however, to improve the waste segregation system.

In the House Meet held last month, Union Minister of State for Finance, Pawan Kumar Bansal, said that the waste could be segregated at the source.

He stated that a start could be made from the markets. Different coloured bins should be marked for degradable waste, non-biodegradable waste and glass. This would ensure adequate disposal, he suggested.

At present, door-to-door collection of waste is being undertaken, which is then taken to the sehaj safai kendras where it is segregated.

There is also a proposal to have SSKs in every sector. The waste segregation system at the SSKs is, however, not very effective.

From here, the waste is then processed at the Solid Waste Management Plant in Dadumajra.

Professor R K Kohli, Director, Centre for Environmental Studies, Panjab University, says, "The best solution to the problem is to segregate waste at the source. The scrap dealers should also be made more aware. Also, pellets, which are the end products at the Solid Waste Management Plant, are presently being used in the cement industry. From a conservation point of view, this is not a very good option. The pellets are organic wastes which could be used as fertlizers."

Putting to rest speculation that more trees would be cut for making paper bags due to the polythene-ban, Prof Kohli says, "Fibres are used for making paper bags. The paper that is used is essentially made from various kinds of grass. Certain trees like eucalyptus and poplar are also used. It will not harm the environment in any way."

Heading: Revamped Tagore Theatre, lake at Sector 42 set for inauguration on October 29 - Indian Express
Content:
During the resumed hearing of a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by advocate H C Arora, seeking directions to the state government to fill up the three vacant posts of members in the Punjab State Human Rights Commission (PSHRC), the Advocate General today assured the Court that the strength of members in the PSHRC will remain the same, i.e. five members.

The Advocate General, H S Mattewal, stated that there is no proposal to reduce the strength of the panel from five members to three members. Explaining the 'incorrect information' given to the Bench during the previous hearing, Mattewal said that the previous statement was made due to some communication gap. He further assured the Bench that the process of appointment of one retired High Court judge and another retired judge of the level of a District and Sessions judge has been initiated and the file has been circulated to the Speaker of the Assembly and the leader of opposition, who are members of the statutory committee for the appointment of members of the Commission.

He also said that these two appointments would be finalised within fifteen days, and that would increase the present strength of the members of the Commission to four members. He further explained that the names for the appointment of the fifth member, who would be a non-judicial member, are under consideration and that a requisite process would be initiated soon. The Division Bench also directed the state government to finalise the appointment of the fifth member expeditiously. Home Secretary BC Gupta was also present during the hearing. In the previous hearing, the Bench, headed by Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur, had directed the Home Secretary to remain present in court today.

Heading: Admn amends land allotment scheme - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Administration is all set to launch the revamped Tagore Theatre with world-class facilities and the much-awaited lake in Sector 42. UT Administrator General SF Rodrigues (Retd) will inaugurate both on October 29.

The idea of revitalisation of the Tagore Theatre was generated by General Rodrigues during his visit on July 21, 2005. M/s Satnam Namita was appointed the consultant architect to carry out the internal renovation of the theatre without disturbing the outer façade to preserve the heritage status of the building. The internal structure was completely dismantled to reconstruct the basement, auditorium, foyer, backstage, toilets, AHU, seating steps, projection room boxes and stairs. The innovated modifications, in the form of the renovated plan, have been executed at a cost of Rs 536 lakh. The seating capacity of the auditorium will be around 850. Two transparent glass blocks with a height of 13 feet each at the entrances of the building will provide a modern look to the aesthetically designed structure.

The theatre will be open for use by artists and public after the inauguration and officials believe that it will help promote art in the UT and make Chandigarh an important cultural hub of the region.

Various cultural programmes by renowned artists and senior citizens will be organised to mark the inauguration of the new theatre.

Meanwhile, the new lake in Sector 42 will provide an ideal site for people to perform religious ceremonies like chhat and Ganesh puja. The lake has been constructed on the lines of the Sukhna for the residents of southern sectors. Besides serving as a recreational centre for the residents, it will decongest the Sukhna and Dhanas Lake. The lake will attract some crowd of Sukhana Lake, thereby reducing the heavy rush there, officials say.

To save the Sukhna Lake from dying due to silt, the Chandigarh Administration had put a blanket ban on observing festivals and rituals upon its bank. A delegation thus demanded a new water body or access to the existing ones in Dhanas and Dadu Majra to provide a way to the migrants from Poorvanchal to perform chhat puja. The Chandigarh Administration had chalked out a roadmap for the same and approved construction of the third lake in Chandigarh at Sector 42 near Sardar Beant Singh Memorial.

Pawan Kumar Bansal, minister of state for Finance and Parliamentary Affairs, had announced Rs 30 lakh for the construction of the lake. Facilities like toilets and changing rooms and campus lighting to facilitate the public will also be provided.

Heading: Foreigners play traditional Punjabi instruments to mark Guru Gaddi Diwas - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Administration has amended the 'allotment of land to various bodies or associations, trust or organisations of religious, charitable, cultural, social nature and governments or semi-government organisation and its autonomous bodies, on leasehold basis in Chandigarh, Scheme 2005'.

Under the new amendments, 'institutional purposes' will include any activity related to the field of art, culture, health, environment, sports, music and political among others. A 'political party' means any national political party, declared as such, by the Election Commission and will be eligible for allotment if it has at least one member of Parliament elected from the Chandigarh in the last 20 years, as on the date of application. The political party should also be duly registered and recognised as a national party by the Election Commission.

Under the new rules, land for residential purposes to the Central Government and the governments of Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh, including its autonomous bodies or semi-government organisations, boards and corporations owned and promoted by the respective governments, will be allotted at a price which is 48 per cent of the average auction price fetched in the last three years, held for the like category of land in the locality. Land for institutional purpose to the Central Government and the Governments of Punjab and Haryana will be allotted at a price which is 15 per cent of the average auction price fetched in last three auctions.

Also, land for institutional purposes to PSUs, boards and corporations of the central government and the governments of Punjab, Haryana will be allotted at a price 25 per cent of the average auction price fetched in the last three auctions of commercial properties.

Land for commercial purposes to wholly owned PSUs, boards and corporations of the central government and the government of Punjab and Haryana including CITCO will be allotted at a price 50 per cent of the average auction price fetched in the last three auctions. If the average auction rates of the same locality are not available, then the average auction price of like category of the last three auctions will be applicable.

Moreover, land for institutional purposes to political parties will be allotted at a price fetched in the auctions held in the last three years of residential properties.

Heading: HC disposes FIR against legislator - Indian Express
Content:
It was a heart-warming sight indeed in Sultanpur Lodhi, at a function organised on the banks of Kali Bein yesterday. About 30 foreigners, dressed in Punjabi attire, played on the traditional instruments of the state to mark the Guruta Gaddi Diwas.

What made the performance special was that these foreigners played instruments like the rebab, tanti saaj, saranda, jori, taus, sarangi, dilruba, which are forgotten in the land of their birth. The team includes men and women from UK, USA, France, Germany etc.

For the local residents, it was a touching sight to see that the musical instruments of which many Punjabis have no knowledge, were played with such ease and passion by these foreigners. The team performed at the site for about two hours.

The team had been invited by Ranjit Singh Rana, an NRI based at UK, to play the traditional instruments here. Rana stated that the came to Punjab with Professor Surinder Singh, another NRI who hails from Kapurthala district.

Rana stated that most of these foreigners have even adopted Sikhism. He added that Prof Surinder has opened an academy in UK, where he teaches people how to play traditional Punjabi instruments. Rana said the team will perform at various places in Punjab, including the Golden Temple.

Heading: Power pangs due to snag in Ropar thermal plant - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Friday quashed an FIR registered by the Punjab Police against Sukhpal Singh Khaira, an MLA and resident of Kapurthala.

An FIR was registered against Khaira on charges of wrongful confinement, causing damage to public property under Sections 341,294,427,382, 147 and 149 of the IPC.

A truck driver, Pal Singh, had alleged that Khaira and his supporters had surrounded and damaged his truck, besides abusing him.

Khaira had alleged that the FIR was a part of a political vendetta. An inquiry was marked in the episode which had found Khaira innocent.

Heading: Conman poses as SP, extracts money from cops - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of the state had to suffer power pangs once again, after a unit of Ropar thermal plant tripped early today morning, leading to shortage of power.

Sources say one of the units of the plant, producing 210 MW of power, tripped after short-circuiting. Reports said the unit is facing problems in its generator protection relay. As a result, Punjab faced shortage of power, as the demand was much more than the supply, from all sources put together. This resulted in power cuts for over two hours all over the state.

Sources say that while the demand for power stands at 1,050 lakh units daily, the power availability was only 900 lakh units on Friday, resulting in power cuts. PSEB officials said the cuts will continue tomorrow too, till the fault at the Ropar thermal unit is repaired. The plant contributes the maximum share of power to the state.

Sources said that a cash-strapped PSEB is not able to buy power from other sources to meet up with the demand for power. The state government continues to dither over the unbundling of PSEB.

Heading: PSEB fines minister’s son-in-law - Indian Express
Content:
The police force in the region is facing a strange challenge. An anonymous caller, who calls up SHOs and introduces himself as an SP with crime branches in metros like Delhi and Mumbai, has extracted money from a number of cops in Haryana, Rajasthan and Punjab in a well-calculated move.

With the police in these states failing to get any clues about him, the conman has started spreading his tentacles, and is started targeting police officials in other states, including Himachal Pradesh, say sources.

The modus operandi of the imposter, who introduces himself as Crime Branch SP Rajan Sharma, seems to be thoroughly planned. He telephones an SHO, ask him about any big theft case in his area, and claims that he has detained some burglars with money and valuables.

After convincing the SHO that the burglars were the ones wanted in that theft case, the conman demands money to help the SHO solve the theft case.

In most cases, he has even settled for a hefty recharge for his mobile phone. In Sirsa district alone, the conman has made such telephonic calls to four SHOs.

"He telephoned me on my mobile phone last Friday, and asked if there was any major theft in my area. When I said that I would check the record, he hit back saying what kind of SHO I was who did not know about thefts in his area," said Sirsa City SHO Ajay Sharma.

Sharma points out that on this, he got suspicious. "I gave him false information about a theft case. On this, the conman said that this was the case, and that the accused were with him, along with the money and valuables. He added that he wanted to talk to the complainant," Sharma recalled.

According to Sharma, police made a person pose as the complainant and talk to the conman. The imposter first asked him to deposit some money in the bank, but later settled for a mobile recharge of Rs 10,000, in lieu of getting him back his stolen amount of Rs 2 lakh. The conman wanted five phones to be recharged for Rs 2,000 each.

Sharma says the police did not get his phone recharged, as they suspected his moves. "I also spoke to Delhi crime branch. They told there is no SP by the name of Rajan Sharma," said Sharma.

Sources, however, reveal that the imposter has managed to get a number of recharges done from different places in the same manner. "He succeeded in conning some SHOs into doing his bidding," said Sharma.

Enquiries by The Indian Express reveal that the imposter had managed to get his phone recharged at the expense of a cop in Moga district. When contacted, Moga SSP Ashok Baath said, "The conman got his phone recharged from one of our cops in this fashion. We have contacted the intelligence agencies at Delhi, and efforts are on to nab the accused," Baath added.

According to Bathinda SSP Aashish Chaudhary, a similar case has come to light in his district too. "But the police got suspicious, so the man's phone was not recharged, and no monetary transaction took place either," Chaudhary added.

Police are now using the global positioning system (GPS) to trace the conman. His mobile phone seems to have been issued against the name of a person from Kotputli in Rajasthan, against fake documents. "We will nab him soon," said Sirsa SP Amitabh Singh Dhillon.

Heading: Sharma removed as Vigilance SSP - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) has served a notice and imposed a fine of Rs 38,000 on the son-in-law of Punjab Cabinet Minister Chaudhary Swarna Ram, for stealing electricity.

The PSEB team raided the house of Baljit Singh, the son-in-law of Punjab Technical Education Minister Chaudhary Swarana Ram, in village Tajpur near Lambra yesterday. The team found a 'kundi' taken from the electric pole close to the man's residence.

Yesterday, a team of the Board was threatened by a BJP leader, who fired in the air when the team went to check an electricity meter in the Lambra village. The PSEB team has filed a complaint regarding yesterday's incident to their senior official.

At another house, police found that the house owner had placed a magnet on the electric meter to tamper with the reading. The house owner called his brother, who is a BJP leader. The BJP leader opened fire in the air to threaten the PSEB team, and kept their identity cards.

The Junior Engineers of PSEB have given a complaint to Executive Engineer KPS Sekhon. They demanded the suitable action in the matter.

Heading: Sampark centres high on success, expand coverage to rural areas - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government today removed Patiala's SSP (Vigilance) Shiv Kumar Sharma from the post following the involvement of his son Mohit Sharma in the infamous diamond merchant robbery case.

The government has posted Sandeep Garg in his place. Garg, till now the SSP (Vigilance) in Ferozepur, has been replaced with Sukhdev Singh, who was SSP (Vigilance) in Amritsar.

Shiv Kumar Sharma, who has since proceeded on long leave, had been in the dock following the arrest of his son Mohit.

Sources say that Shiv Kumar Sharma had been investigating some important and sensitive cases, including corruption cases against former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh.

Sources add that Sharma was under tremendous pressure ever since the name of his son cropped up in the case and was accused of being a mastermind in the looting of a Surat-based diamond merchant.

Diamonds worth crores looted from the merchant had later been recovered from Mohit Sharma's residence in Ludhiana, where he ran a diamond shop. The Jalandhar police had later raided the official residence of Shiv Kumar Sharma in Patiala as well, from where some incriminating documents were recovered. Amandeep Singh, the gunman of Shiv Kumar Sharma, who was also involved in the diamond robbery, is absconding. He is also reported to be related to Sharma and was with Mohit Sharma most of the time.

They reportedly planned the robbery together.

Heading: Govt begins paddy payment to farmers - Indian Express
Content:
UT Administrator General SF Rodrigues (Retd) launched another Sampark centre at the Central Treasury in Sector 17 on Friday. The programme, with links to web portals of various departments of the UT Administration, provides 'one stop solutions' to multiple tasks, thus saving the time and energy of citizens, besides ensuring transparency in the delivery systems.

General Rodrigues, while interacting with IT Director Manjit Brar and other functionaries of the project, asked them to make the centre more 'people-friendly' through interactive computer processes and enhance its scope of service and coverage.

He further expressed happiness over the fact that since the launch of the Sampark centres in September 2004, over Rs 1,300 crore of government revenue has been collected by way of 55 lakh transactions through these centres. He called for giving special focus to the e-Gram Sampark centers, which provide various services to rural people besides providing information and internet services free of cost.

Manjit Singh Brar, Director IT, while briefing about the project, said 22 public utility services are being provided in the nine e-Sampark centers in different parts of the city. The various facilities offered by the centres include payment of electricity bills, water and sewerage bills, booking of open spaces and community halls, issuing senior citizen cards, disability identification cards, disbursement of pensions, tenant registration, domestic servant registration, passport application submission, sale and acceptance of CHB forms, payment of telephone bills and sale of stamp papers.

"Three more villages including Dadu Majra, Khuda Alisher and Daria have become operational from today under this facility," he said. IT deputy commissioner RK Rao, treasury officer Rajiv Tiwari, municipal councillors, elected representatives and senior officials from the Administration were also present on the occasion.

Heading: Immigration firm to pay Rs 1 lakh for shattering dollar dreams - Indian Express
Content:
Payment by the Union government yet to be made

Food and Civil Supply Minister Adesh Pratap Singh Kairon today said that Punjab, without waiting for payment from the Union government, has started making paddy payment to the farmers directly.

He told this to Union Food Secretary Alka Sirohi today while she reviewed the procurement of paddy in Punjab and Haryana during a high-level meeting.

Kairon urged the Union Food Secretary to make an amendment in the bonus payment notification so that payment of bonus could be made directly to farmers. He also requested that a decision regarding PAU 201 variety of paddy be made at an early date so that procurement of this variety does not suffer. He also requested to extend the milling season to December 31 for levy and CMR.

He said the traders' share in procurement has drastically reduced from 13 per cent to a meager 8 per cent, primarily due to ban on export of non-basmati rice.

Explaining the payment position to farmers for paddy, Kairon explained that Punjab is the only state that has set up electronic payment system in two districts to ensure payment to them within 48 hours of lifting of paddy.

He said that from the next procurement season, electronic payment season would be extended to all the 1,622 mandis of the state. Alka Sirohi appreciated the new initiative of the Punjab government of ensuring payment to them within 48 hours, a spokesperson said. She said that she would also visit electronic clearing houses set up in different mandis during her visit to mandis tomorrow.

Kairon urged that wheat should be immediately moved out of Punjab so that there is space to store rice.

She said the Jute Commissioner of India has assured to supply 80,000 additional gunny bags to Punjab keeping in view bumper crop in the state.

Heading: No Sankalp Diwas: ‘Decision unfortunate’ - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed an immigration company to pay Rs 1 lakh as compensation after they failed to send a Ludhiana resident to Canada. They have also been directed to pay Rs 5,000 as litigation cost.

The complainant, Lakhwinder Singh, a resident of Ludhiana, said that he and his family had planned to migrate to the province of British Columbia in Canada. For this, they contacted "Canadian 4UR Immigration Services" in Sector 9. They signed an agreement in November 2006. He was then told that he would get approval for immigration within three months and paid Rs 30,000 as retainer fee.

He was also asked to maintain a balance of Rs 6 lakh in his bank, which would be needed once all the formalities were complete.

The complainant, after noticing that there was no movement in his work, contacted the company and was told that they had to shift their office to Canada owing to some problems. The company later refunded Rs 30,000 by transferring the money in his account.

The complainant alleged that the company had deceived them, as they had not deposited the requisite fee with the firm in Canada.

In its reply, the company pleaded that after the complainant had qualified the interview and cleared the requisite norms as laid by the Canadian Embassy, he signed an agreement. An assurance was also given that he would maintain the required balance in his account.

His case was then forwarded to the overseas immigration branch of the company. The company pleaded that it was the complainant who abandoned the company and demanded for the refund of money, which was given to him. They pleaded that an agent in Canada was running their business under the name of Overseas Immigration Services. But their relations were severed after some friction between and hence the delay.

The forum said that the immigration company had retained the amount of Rs 30,000 for 14 months, for the purpose of procuring a job and visa for the complainant, which it failed to procure.

"The complainant waited for his interview call and visa for 14 months. It is argued by the complainant's counsel that his client could not work during this period. He procured the amount of Rs 6 lakh and deposited the same in the bank. The entire career of the complainant has been ruined. It was a cruel joke played by the immigration company," said Jagroop Singh Mahal, President, District Consumer Forum.

Heading: Students’ initiative to save St Bede’s - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Congress has condemned the Akali government's decision not to observe the death anniversary of Indira Gandhi as Sankalp Diwas.

Leader of opposition Rajinder Kaur Bhattal and Punjab Pradesh Congress chief Mohinder Singh Kaypee have termed the decision of the SAD-BJP government as "unfortunate". Kaypee said the decision amounted to insulting a great leader of the nation. Ahead of Indira Gandhi's death anniversary on

October 31, the state government had passed instructions a few days ago to observe the day as Sankalp Diwas.

After the government's move invited a reaction from its own ruling Akali Dal, the orders were withdrawn late last evening, fearing a political fallout at a time when elections are round the corner.

Talking to ENS, Kaypee said, "It's ironical that the government issues instructions and then withdraws it. I condemn the move." Incensed with the government move, Rajinder Kaur Bhattal said, "It is unfortunate and unfair that the SAD-BJP combine has taken this step. Remembering national leaders on their anniversaries is not a bad precedent." The state government's directions were in response to a letter this week from the Ministry of Home Affairs. The letter by Joint Secretary A.K. Yadav had desired that states should observe the day as National Sankalp Day.

Heading: $ 800 loan cleared for clean hydro power generation - Indian Express
Content:
Students of four college to take out rally on November 4

Four colleges in Shimla today announced to launch a joint action to save St Bede's College from closing down.

The college was faced with the problem of shortage of funds after the government decided to reduce the grant of all private colleges from 95 per cent to 50 per cent.

Shikha Chauhan, president of the Student

Central Association of the Himachal Pradesh University, today said a joint action forum of students from all colleges in Shimla would generate public opinion for government's support for the college.

St Bede's College has been an institution for girls' education in Himachal for over a century.

"A signature campaign urging the state government to restore grant-in-aid to the college would be carried

out by all students of

St Bede's College and it would be submitted to the

Chief Minister," she

said while talking to the mediapersons in Shimla.

Students of four colleges including Rajkiya Kanya Mahavidyalya, Rajiv

Gandhi Degree College, Chaura Maidan, Rajkiya Mahavidyalya, Sanjauli, and St Bede's would take out a joint rally in Shimla on

November 4 to support

the cause.

Though the government is taking support of the court's directions in slashing the grant-in-aid to private colleges, there is also an

option to give exemption in some cases, she said.

"The government should not hesitate in protecting the future of such institution," she urged.

The principal of the college Sister Molly Abraham has already said that due to shortage of funds it has

become tough to run the

institution effectively and they would finally be compelled to close it down.

The government had expressed its inability to bail-out one college and leave out the others.

Heading: Chaos rules on Purva Marg as road closed for construction - Indian Express
Content:
The Asian Development Bank has cleared a loan of US $800 million for investment in construction of run-of-river hydropower projects in Himachal Pradesh.

The state is expected to get a major boost in the hydro power sector, especially in harnessing at least 808 megawatts of hydropower, in the next eight years, during which the loan would be rolled out in a phased manner.

At the board meeting of ADB at its Manila headquarters, the bank cleared the loan investment for Himachal which would be repayable in 25 years, said Managing Director of Himachal Pradesh Power Corporation Tarun Kapoor.

"Though the bank had already given its approval in principle, the stage of board approval was remaining which was cleared in the meeting on October 23.

The first loan agreement for the two projects being executed by the Corporation is expected to be signed with the ADB in 15 days," said Kapoor.

Since the multi-tranche financing facility of the ADB in respect of this loan also allows the state government to take help from the bank in its clean energy policies, agreement with the bank would bring along strong prospects for the stateto earn carbon credits out of clean energy development mechanism in hydro power sector.

The loan is expected to come to the state in four installments. The first installment of US $150 million would be utilised in the construction of 111-megawatt Sawra Kuddu Hydro Power Project being constructed by the power corporation on Pabbar river.

The other project to be funded by the ADB would be 65-MW Kashang-I in Kinnaur district.

The next three installments would be allocated by the bank to the power corporation, through Government of India as and when new projects are taken up.

Power Secretary Ajay Mittal said, "The state would look to utilise bank's funding for other hydro projects like Shong-Thong, Kashang II, Karcham and Sainj that are next in line to be developed by the power corporation."

Heading: Hydro power generation - Indian Express
Content:
The construction of a road on the Purva Marg is leading to traffic chaos on the stretch. A part of the road has been closed for more than a week, thus escalating the problems. And with the traffic being diverted through the Industrial Area, long lines of vehicles can be seen waiting to find a way. Unruly scenes are also witnessed with people getting into tiffs with each other. The situation is especially chaotic in the evening.

While the traffic police personnel manage the traffic during the morning, there is no one to divert it during the night. Consequently, a single road becomes two-way. Also, with vehicles moving at a high speed, the chances of a mishap are quite high.

Rajiv Kumar, a resident of Sector 35 says: "I got stuck in a jam on the stretch for around half an hour. The road is in desperate need of repairs. The work should be completed at a faster pace."

Adding to the woes is that streetlights do not function properly. "The road witnesses heavy flow of traffic on all days. They can work on road construction at night," says Savita, a resident of Sector 47.

The officials, meanwhile, say the work will be completed within a few days.

Heading: UHBVN taken to task by HC - Indian Express
Content:
The MLA from Kaithal and president of All India Kisan Khet Mazdoor Congress, Shamsher Surjewala, today demanded Rs 1,000 as MSP for rice. Addressing a press conference here today, Surjewala said the Rs 50 bonus declared by the Central government was too little and it should have been at least Rs 100.

He said the inclement weather last month had adversely affected farmers' produce in north India. "The state governments must adequately compensate for the huge losses suffered by the farmers ranging from 10 to 40 per cent at different places," he said.

Welcoming Haryana government's decision to increase subsidy on pesticides to 35 per ent from the 25 per cent earlier, he said the policy should be continued in future as well.

Surjewala demanded strict action for people producing and selling spurious pesticides, seeds and agriculture equipments. Lamenting the recent ban on PUSA 1121 variety of basmati, he said the UPA government's decision had harmed the interest of the farmers. He also blamed the Union Agriculture Minister Sharad Pawar for not giving special package to the two major agriculture states — Haryana and Punjab.

Heading: State set to get 800 new doctors - Indian Express
Content:
Construction of flyover delayed as seven poles not removed

The authorities of Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (UHBVN), Haryana were taken to task today by the Punjab and Haryana High Court for allegedly causing delay in the construction of Samalkha flyover. The managing director of UHBVN was summoned by the Court after the contractor — IRCON Limited — said the nigam has not removed electric poles in the way of Chandigarh-Delhi highway, as a result of which the construction was delayed.

Taking serious note of this, the High Court summoned the MD, who reached the court within 15 minutes. The division bench, comprising Justice Uma Nath Singh and Justice Daya Chaudhary, questioned the MD over the reason behind the delay in removing the electric poles. Notably, only seven electric poles are to be removed in order to make the path free from all encumbrances. The Court took serious note of the fact that the UHBVN took more than 1 year and 10 months for removing only 10 electric poles. "We will mark a CBI enquiry into this to find out the reason behind the delay," said the Court.

The MD replied that the delay was on the account of National Highway Authorities (NHAI) as it had not deposited the funds for removing the electric poles.He assured that the remaining seven poles would be removed within two days. The Court has deferred the question of delay to the next date of hearing. Interestingly, the Court also objected to the dress which the MD was wearing.

After the Court's intervention, IRCON Limited, on its part, today gave an undertaking that one side of the Samalkha flyover will be opened to traffic by March 31 and the other side by June 30, 2009.

The counsel appearing on behalf of NHAI also submitted that some local residents of a village close to Panipat were causing hindrance in the construction of an underpass. The Deputy Commissioner and Senior Superintendent of Police, Panipat have been directed to ensure that no disturbance is caused.

Meanwhile, Valecha limited company has deposited an amount of Rs 25 lakh with the Registrar of the High Court, as penalty imposed by the High Court on the last date of hearing for causing delay in the construction of Murthal and Gannaur flyovers. Moreover, the land required for completion of the two flyovers has been handed over by the state government to the NHAI.

Heading: Students pitch in to ensure a cracker-free Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
In a major recruitment exercise, the Health Department is planning to recruit about 800 doctors within the next one-and-a-half month. The department has also decided to take steps to minimise expenses incurred on indoor treatment by patients and provide free education to all haemophilic children upto Class 10 in government schools, said Haryana Health Minister Kartar Devi.

Addressing a press conference here today, Kartar Devi said 200 doctors had already been recruited.

The government has approved in principal the hike in the pay scales of doctors, besides granting them 25 per cent of the basic pay as Non-Practising Allowance (NPA). The department also has a plan to give special incentives to doctors under the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM). Strength of the paramedical staff has also been increased. 2,306 posts of paramedical staff, that were abolished earlier, have been restored and 3,000 posts of staff nurses, 36 posts of dental surgeons, 60 of pharmacists and 66 radiographers have been sanctioned.

She further said the government had decided to provide free anti-haemophilic treatment to all severe cases of haemophilia on episode-basis, through registered haemophilia societies.

A project to tackle the menace of anaemia among women and children would also launched on November 14, in collaboration with the Department of Women and Child Development. It would cover one crore children between the age of six months and 18 years as well as pregnant and lactating mothers, she said.

Heading: RTI Act: 3 yrs on, system not on track yet in Mohali - Indian Express
Content:
In an effort to make Diwali smoke-free this year, Camphor, the eco-club of the Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 35D organised an anti-cracker rally and a painting competition in the school premises on Friday.

The students made placards with anti-cracker messages to protect the environment.

Dr S K Sharma, president of the Environment Society of India, flagged off the rally to spread awareness among the people. Principal Raviraj Kaur urged the students to act as agents of change and contribute towards a pollution-free environment.

Keeping with the festive spirit, Carmel Convent School celebrated Diwali in the school premises.

The celebrations started with a prayer, which was followed by a dance performance to mark the festival of lights.

Principal Sister Maria Christi gave out a message to the students to care for the environment and not burst crackers.

Heading: MC to pay up Rs 5,000 for wrong billing of water - Indian Express
Content:
Delays, denials galore, incomplete information another problem area

It has been over three years since the citizens of India were given the right to seek information from all public authorities. In Mohali, however, residents are denied this right, with most of the public authorities either denying and delaying information sought under the Right to Information Act of 2005, or providing incomplete and inappropriate information.  

This correspondent filed eight applications on the prescribed form and deposited the requisite fee under Section 6 of the RTI Act to seek certain information from different departments and authorities of the state and the Centre in the last two months. Only one public authority provided the desired information within the stipulated time of 30 days. Two departments not only delayed the supply of information, but also furnished incomplete and inappropriate information. In case of five applications, the public authorities concerned simply failed to respond even after two months.

The denial of information was reported to the Punjab State Information Commission under Sub-Section (c) of Section 18 of the RTI Act three weeks ago, but a response is still awaited.

Public information officers (PIOs) at the offices of the Mohali Deputy Commissioner, District Transport Officer, Airports Authority of India and the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority simply failed to provide the desired information.

The Punjab Infrastructure Development Board and the Punjab Health Systems Corporation provided incomplete and inappropriate information much after the expiry of the stipulated time. The Nayagaon Nagar Panchayat turned out to be the only such authority to provide complete information within the timeframe.

Though the District Revenue Officer (DRO), who is the Assistant Public Information Officer for the DC office in Mohali where two applications were filed, wrote to the sub-divisional magistrates (SDMs), tehsildars and other officials concerned to send him the desired information pertaining to their respective offices within a week, it has not reached him even after two months.

It is learnt that the Kharar SDM had forwarded the DRO's missive marked as "most urgent and time bound" to the Kharar tehsildar and the Majri naib tehsildar. The SDM even wrote to the officials that they would be penalised under Section 20 of the RTI Act if they failed to provide the information within the stipulated time.

To deny information under the RTI Act, the Kharar tehsildar cited the provisions of the Punjab Registration Manual, 1929, and the Indian Registration Act, 1908. "Deposit an additional fee of Rs 100 with the application fee of Rs 15 to get the copy of a single document," said the tehsildar. The RTI Act does not prescribe any such fee.

Information provided by the Majri naib tehsildar was incomplete and late.

In response to another application, the DTO, too, provided insufficient information, that too after the expiry of 30 days. He expressed his inability to provide complete information on the pretext of shortage of staff. "Providing information will take much time due to which public work will suffer," the DTO wrote.

What they say

"The Information Commission views seriously the appeals and complaints against public authorities for denying, delaying and supplying incomplete, inappropriate or misleading information. Such cases are taken up judicially and penalty up to Rs 25,000 is imposed as per the provisions of law. To make public information officers more accountable and responsive, the government imparts them training from time to time while the commission holds courts at district headquarters for delivery of justice at the people's doorsteps. Anybody aggrieved with public information officer or even the appellate authority's conduct can approach the commission."

S S Grewal, Secretary, Punjab State Information Commission

"In case of any lapse on the part of any public authority in providing information under the RTI Act, the applicant can file an appeal before the appellant authority. If the appellant authority, too, fails to take cognisance, the next remedy is to approach the State or Central Information Commission. If information is denied by the assistant public information officer at my office, you can file an appeal before me."

Rahul Bhandari, Deputy Commissioner, Mohali

Heading: Despite global meltdown, Chandigarh is still the most preferred place to buy a home - Indian Express
Content:
Forum finds civic body guilty of charging the complainant for the water consumed by his neighbour and vice versa for several years

The District Consumer Forum has directed the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for its "mistake" of interchanging the water bills of two neighbours.

The forum held the MC guilty of deficient services and restrained its officials from charging Rs 7,951 as arrears for water bills from the complainant. The MC has also been directed to pay Rs 500 as costs of litigation.

The forum said: "It is clear that for several years the MC had been billing the complainant for the water consumed by his neighbour and vice versa. When the fact came to light, without giving the complainant an opportunity to be heard, the MC slapped a bill, asking him to pay arrears of Rs 7,951."

The complainant, Ashok Kumar, a resident of Sector 29, said he received an inflated water bill, including Rs 7,951 as arrears, on October 17, 2007. He complained to the sub-divisional engineer (SDE), Water Supply Sub-Division, Sector 18, for testing of his water meter and an amount of Rs 65 was deposited for the purpose. The report, which was received two months later, said there was a minor fault in the meter. Kumar said the department then sent the next bill, adding Rs 66.50, for two months. It was alleged that despite a number of visits to the SDE for rectification of the bill, nothing was done. Further, the junior engineer who had checked the meter said the readings so far had been interchanged with his neighbour due to a mistake committed by an employee.

In its reply, the MC pleaded that the complaint was not maintainable against them as it had issued the bill according to the correct readings, which had earlier been interchanged. It was submitted that earlier the consumer of House No 1,652 was paying excess bill, with the meter reading of House No 1,653 (Kumar's house) being charged from him. As soon as the error came to their knowledge, the MC said, it was corrected and the due credit of the excess amount paid was given back to him. Thus, the complainant who was paying lesser amount up to March 2007 was told to pay the arrears, the MC added.

The forum said the reply filed by the MC demonstrated the carelessness and negligence of its officials and asked it to pay up for the deficiency in service.

Heading: 3-day youth festival concludes amid fun and frolic - Indian Express
Content:
AMID overall stagnation and recession in the real estate sector and the prevailing global meltdown, Chandigarh maintains its status as one of the most sought-after destinations for the buyers of residential property. Buyers, both locals and NRIs, have a strong preference for the city over Panchkula and Mohali.

The recent real estate auctions by the Estate Office in Chandigarh and the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) in Mohali clearly manifest Chandigarh as a hot destination when it comes to residential property. A comparison of the rates of the properties auctioned in Chandigarh and Mohali shows a wide difference. While a one-kanal plot in Chandigarh fetched Rs 4 crore against the reserve price of Rs 1.81 crore, a plot with similar area dimensions in Mohali was auctioned for Rs 2.8 crore against its reserve price of Rs 2.24 crore.

The prospective buyers as well as residents of the city strongly believe that Chandigarh scores better on infrastructure and maintenance parameters. "Infrastructure like roads, electricity and water supply in the city cannot be compared with that of Panchkula and Mohali where the situation is very bad. Also, the quality of education — both government and private — attracts a large number of students from other adjoining states in Chandigarh," says Neelam Vashisht, who has been living in Chandigarh for the last 17 years.

Chandigarh has been successful in maintaining a sustainable property price graph over the years despite stagnation and recession in the market. Though there has been no trade of properties in the city, the prices have not depreciated. The prevailing global recession, considered to be one of the worst, has failed to affect the demand for real estate and their prices in Chandigarh.

"The sustainable price graph of residential properties is due to the increasing influx of migrant population, which has resulted in an increased demand for houses while the supply is limited. The city is also catering to the residential needs of the workforce of IT professionals and the industrial town Baddi," says R P Malhotra, general secretary, Property Owners' Welfare Association, Chandigarh.

And now with the Chandigarh-Baddi rail link coming up, commuters will have an easier travel with reduced distance and time.  

"NRIs from all over Punjab want to own a house in Chandigarh. The city remains the first preference despite exorbitant property rates, compared to other cities," says Kamaljeet Singh, president, NRI Sabha.     

Real estate experts believe the city stands tall when it comes to residential real estate against all financial and global odds and this trend is ecpected to continue in the future.

Heading: Dowry and preference for male child still prevail in society: Minister - Indian Express
Content:

Heading: ‘Europe next dream destination for migration’ - Indian Express
Content:
"The state does not and never will endorse the one-child norm. We will not support any coercive policies that take away the rights of women," said Laxmi Kanta Chawla, Health minister of Punjab, while speaking at a conference on "Population Health and Social Development" on Friday.

The two-day conference was organised by the Population Foundation of India, New Delhi.

She said that dowry and son preference still prevail in the society and need to be stopped, if a positive change is to be brought.

The second day of the conference focussed on the issue of female foeticide in the states of Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh and upon the initiatives taken by the state governments.

Presenting the keynote address, Bijaylaxmi, a lecturer at the Delhi University, who has been associated with women's rights said the practice of sex selective abortion needs to be looked at in the larger context of the worth of women in society.

She further questioned the relevance of policies that offer incentives to parents to raise the girl child.

Ena Singh, assistant country representative, United Nations Population Fund, expressed her concern over the use of appropriate terminology and imagery, so that it does not impinge on the right to abortion.
