Heading: DDA puts red light on railway plan for New Delhi station makeover - Indian Express
Content:
Lyngdoh guidelines versus JNUSU elections: apex court puts conditional stay

The Supreme Court on Friday ordered a conditional stay on elections to the Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) students' union in keeping with its tough stand on universities failing to follow the Lyngdoh committee guidelines on students' union polls.

On Tuesday, the apex court had issued notice to JNU seeking guidelines governing the ensuing elections. Today, the Bench of Justices Arijit Pasayat and Mukundkam Sharma also issued contempt notices to the JNU vice-chancellor and the registrar for not ensuring that the election process is conducted in terms of the committee recommendations.

Elections for the JNU students' union were scheduled for November 3.

On Friday, the apex court Bench passed the directions on an application filed by amicus curiae Additional Solicitor General Gopal Subramanium. The application complained about violations of the Lyngdoh committee recommendations by the university. JNU, which follows its own constitution while conducting elections, has not been following the guidelines framed to keep criminalisation out and a check on 'money politics'.

The university's code of conduct for the elections clashes with the Lyngdoh committee guidelines on three grounds: age-limit set at 25 years, a qualifying criterion of 75-per cent attendance, and allowing candidates to contest for the same post again.

The Supreme Court-appointed Lyngdoh committee had in September 2006 come up with various guidelines and suggestions for smooth and orderly conduct of students' union elections in universities across the country. Among other things, the committee went into financial transparency and limits of expenditure for students' body polls, eligibility criteria for candidates, institution of a forum to address disputes arising from these elections as regards procedural fairness, and non-observance of norms during polls.

"It is a bad decision because the JNU students' union has been in existence for 36 years and is running well. There is no problem in its functioning. Such decisions will disrupt its functioning. I don't know why such matters have come under judicial purview. I don't think the judiciary should enter such matters."
Prakash Karat, CPI(M), JNUSU president (SFI) in 1972-73

"I don't think a lot of money is spent in the JNU students' union elections. When I was there, we collected Rs 10 from each student as campaigning 'fund'. Posters were handwritten throughout the night, and students themselves pasted them."
Digvijay Singh, JD(U), JNUSU general secretary (Students for Democratic Socialism) in 1979-80

Heading: Bubble gone ‘bust’, developers build on dream with free gifts - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) has sent back to the drawing board the Railway ministry's ambitious project to make New Delhi railway station a "world class" junction. The development agency has refused to prove certain salient features of the Rs 6,000-crore plan, Newsline has learnt.

The Railway ministry had submitted the plan to DDA a few weeks ago, since the Authority's go-ahead is crucial before launching any development work in the Capital. A railway official said project details, including plans to construct an 18-storey complex at the station as a "commercial component", were forwarded to DDA for approval. Detailed built-up area proposals were also forwarded, sources said.

Sources in DDA's planning department confirmed that the Railways' plans for commercial development were disapproved after much criticism. "The area where such development is being proposed cannot handle that kind of infrastructure pressure," a DDA official from the planning department said. "The proposal for commercial development needs to be revisited keeping in mind an area's constraints."

The DDA is of the opinion that Railways cannot develop the station in isolation. "They have to build approach roads leading up to various proposed structures; the area may not be able to handle such additions," the official said.

While many in DDA also found fault with the 18-storey commercial complex, it is still not clear whether the Authority has approved it. The planning department official simply said: "There are certain anomalies in the built-up area plans for that proposal."

The Railways had admitted in the past that plans for the commercial complex — including many retail outlets, restaurants, ATMs and so forth — are open to change. "The structure is not finalised," a Railway official said. "We have just circulated a basic design and hope to finalise other details later."

The project entails a complete conversion of 86 hectares. It was initially supposed to be completed by 2010, to coincide with the Commonwealth Games, but the ministry announced this January that it would not be able to complete the entire project by then.

A public-private partnership project, the airspace above the station and railway land around the station is slated to be used as commercial components. For now, though, the plans may have to be delayed yet again. For, the Railway ministry will need clear approvals from the DDA technical committee before it can begin development.

Heading: Man shot, another fired upon in separate incidents - Indian Express
Content:
With the Sensex taking one tumble after the other and amid a liquidity scare in the banking sector, the real estate industry is coming up with novel ways to attract a market that is slowing down.

Sources said the market has gone down, especially in the suburbs, to an extent that as opposed to 50 to 100 flats booked each day in Gurgaon this time last year, Thursday recorded not a single booking.

Therefore the freebies, say experts.

Jaypee Group has, for instance, offered a car for every flat booked at its housing projects in Noida and Greater Noida. In the Jaypee Greens project at Greater Noida, one can get a Maruti Swift, a BMW, a Mercedes or a Toyota Land Cruiser as gift, depending on the category of flats bought.

"If the value of a villa is Rs 4 crore and you get a Mercedes worth Rs 25 lakh, it is actually a discount being offered by the developer instead of reducing the price of the flat, or offering a cash discount," a real estate developer, who did not wish to be identified, said. "Developers are not giving actual cash discounts because they do not want the value of property to come down — they want the real estate bubble to exist."

A real estate expert in NCR said transactions have "literally stopped" due to primarily two reasons: the jacked-up prices on one hand, and home loan interests jumping from 7.2 per cent to 14 per cent in a matter of a couple of years. "While there is a genuine need for homes, they have become unaffordable," the expert said. "There is a requirement for 20 million homes in the country, annually."

But this potentially huge demand, he said, is being "killed" by the inflated prices and the interest rates showing no signs of driving down south.

Liquidity crunch hits home
Ashish Jindal, regional director at Knight Frank, a global real estate research firm, said: "One big reason for the slump in the market is the high interest rates. The kind of perks being given with flats nowadays is not just a discount but also a way to stimulate the market."

Experts said while demand has not slipped, banks have stopped lending and that has hit the realty market. "The main source of income in the property market is from speculators but these are the people who have lost money in stocks so this portfolio has been hit," an expert said. "The genuine customers comprise just a small fraction of the market."

What's worse, the expert said, banks have also stopped investing in real estate. Result: many developers, including big names, are unable to raise funds and have started cutting back on projects.

Developers also said the suburbs take the hit first, and harder, than the metropolises during slumps like these. "The problem with the market right now is developers are focussing on high-end consumers, whereas the demand is more in the middle segment," a realty expert said. "But this is not a sustainable strategy. We know big developers are looking at targeting budget consumers over the next year."

Tarun Mehrotra, chief operating officer, Pioneer Urban Land, said: "Most of the slowdown has appeared in projects under construction and even banks are limiting their exposure to real estate right now. So, while banks are no longer investing in housing projects they are also shy of second loans at the consumer level."

The market, he said, is "unlikely" to pick up anytime soon but "things aren't as dismal as they seem".

Mohatani Goswami of Jaypee Group said: "We have been selling consistently. The scheme for car was worked out eight months ago and is a coincidence that it was launched at a time when markets are down — the scheme was planned for Diwali in any case. Such offers take time to work out as we had to tie up with car manufacturers."

Housing for the poor
Earlier this week, Chief Minister Delhi Sheila Dikshit announced that 13,000 low-income group houses were already complete as part of the Rajiv Ratan Awas Yojana. "We have already received over 2 lakh applications for these 13,000 flats. They will be allotted within the next four or five months," Dikshit had said. "Our plan is to construct 4 lakh such houses over the next three or four years."

Heading: In Garcia land of intrigue, ‘Gabophobia’ plagues contemporary writers - Indian Express
Content:
One man died and another was sent to hospital in different firing incidents in the Capital in the past 24 hours.

In the first incident, reported around 5.30 pm Friday from Yamuna Vihar, two unidentified men on a motorcycle shot a 31-year-old man dead in Bhajanpura, Northeast Delhi.

The deceased has been identified as Maulana Mohammed Rehman, a resident of Sadar Bazaar. The incident reportedly occurred when he was on way back from Loni in Uttar Pradesh. According to the police, Rehman had gone to the UP town to scan a plot of land measuring some 500 acres. He was accompanied by two friends, Javed and Abdul Qazi. The police said the trio stopped on the road near Yamuna Vihar on their way back.

"At this point, two assailants arrived on a motorcycle and fired three rounds at the victims. One of the bullets hit Rehman on the chest," a senior officer said. Qazi and Javed, who escaped unscathed in the sudden attack, called the police and took Rehman to Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital.

He was declared dead on arrival at the hospital.

The assailants are absconding; police said it appears to be a case of personal enmity. A case of murder has been registered against unknown assailants.

In another incident reported late Thursday evening, a 24-year-old man was shot at in Palam Village, Southwest Delhi. Police officials said friends opened fire at Rajender following an altercation. The assailants are yet to be identified.

A bystander called the police, who admitted the victim in DDU Hospital. His condition is said to be stable. Rajender lives in Palam Village, the police said.

Heading: ‘Bar on elections attack on unique culture of JNU’ - Indian Express
Content:
It was once said of Colombian writer Gabriel Garcia Marquez that the long shadow cast by his magical realism does not let his sons be men in their entirety.

At a discussion — "Beyond The Influence of Gabriel Garcia Marquez on the Works of Contemporary Writers" — on Thursday at the Sahitya Kala Akademi, chaired by writer-journalist Santiago Gamboa, four Colombian writers marked their differences with "Gabo".

These writers — all under 50 — are not only products of a megapolis plagued by drug cartels and rampant corruption, but also believe the octogenarian writer's world of provincial towns and levitating grandmothers in One Hundred Years of Solitude never existed in the true sense. The discussion was part of the ongoing cultural week of Colombia, being held in India for the first time.

Why were the writers in such a hurry to abandon a survivor who made magical realism the main metaphor of Latin American literature? Writer-editor Héctor Abad Faciolince, 49, called it "Gabophobia". "The weapon of exaggeration exemplified in his books has been done to death. Now, he is more venerated than read. Besides, I did not grow up near the sea — the Caribbean land which is closer to Cuba. For me, going to the sea was like a pilgrimage," Faciolince said in his broken English. Faciolince is a post-boom writer feted for telling the history of Colombia through his father's life documented in The Oblivion We shall Be. His father was a human rights activist who was shot dead.

The slight Mario Mendoza, buttoned up in a blue shirt, had swooped on the writer's arena with the gritty tale Satanas (Satan), based on true life events. Mendoza, who grew up in Bogota, a city of elegant cafés and lonely clubs — where the smells of garbage and fresh bread co-exist — writes about the ghost city that is his home. "The literature of Garcia Marquez is drawn from rural environment, and we grew up in an environment where our references were urban," said Mendoza whose book was turned into a thriller last year. For Mendoza, the challenge lies in turning his works into a virtual reality machine. "In a virtual reality machine, you have to coerce the reader into action — looking around, discerning the smell and feeling the disorder of a metropolis," shared Mendoza.

The 42-year-old Gamboa said: "Not being a follower does not mean you are a killer. Each writer is like an island." It is a historical necessity to chart new directions, said writer Enrique Serrano Lopez, 47. He said: "The times demand new accents, new themes. Nobody wants to pursue that (magical realism) dream."

The group of writers, who have been in India for barely four days, find an eerie similarity between Delhi and Bogota, a city of 8 million. Gamboa said, "In Delhi, the beauty lies on the surface, while the horror is deep within. In Bogota, the horror is on the surface."

Heading: Security scare raises business for CCTV manufacturers in city - Indian Express
Content:
The student community of JNU on Friday came down heavily on the Supreme Court decision to put a stay order on the elections that were to be held on November 3. Calling the move "unjust" and a "political attack" on JNUSU, student leaders as well as past office bearers of JNU have decided to protest the order.

Sandeep Singh, former president and the AISA presidential candidate said the order is an attack on the unique culture of JNU. "We do not employ money or muscle power. Ever since elections were started in JNU, the process has been democratic. I would say it is unjust for the court to put a stay on it for not following Lyngdoh Committee guidelines."

On Friday afternoon, when the Election Commission held a meeting with students' representatives, it also invited former office bearers. Talking to Newsline, Kavita Krishnan, former joint secretary of JNUSU, 1995, said that it is time to take the protest all over the country. "JNU students are united in not accepting the guidelines at face value. We will be challenging the stay order and take the movement to other parts of the country," she said.

Students also considered the stay order "biased" as the Supreme Court failed to take cognizance of Lyngdoh Committee violations in other universities. "Several universities do not even have a system of elections. It is indeed sad that the SC has targeted JNU," said Virmani Ram, NSUI spokesperson.

Mohammed Hafeezur Rahman, contesting for the post of president for Student Voice, gave the example of Delhi University where despite Lyngdoh's guidelines being implemented on paper, they were openly flouted. "Several lakhs were spent in the elections, while Lyngdoh puts a limit of Rs 5000 for campaigning. They were never sent any notice against the violation," he said.

According to students, implementation of the Lyngdoh Committee guidelines will not be possible in JNU on three grounds. Firstly, the constitution of JNU allows students to contest in elections repeatedly, something that Lyngdoh does not allow.

Secondly, the age bar of 25 does not hold ground in a research institute where most students are above that age.

Finally, the criterion of 75 per cent attendance in class is not possible as JNU does not have an attendance system.

Effects that the implementation of Lyngdoh Committee's guidelines may have on JNU
* Serious political activism will be over: Over the years, JNU has given the country some of its finest leaders. Prakash Karat, Sitaram Yechury and Digvijay Singh are all ex-students of JNU. With the Lyngdoh Committee guidelines restricting re-contesting in elections, the careers of most student leaders will come to an abrupt end.
* The role of EC will be finished. Elections in JNU are fully managed by the students. With the Lyngdoh guidelines emphasizing on the participation by the administration, the Election Commission elected by students will lose value.
* Public meetings and campaigning will be affected: Public meetings where leaders from outside are invited and vigorous campaigning continues till midnight will face a serious setback. Lyngdoh's guidelines strictly prohibit campaigning after 6 pm.
* The 'unique' character of the elections will be undermined: For the last 37 years, JNU has had a unique system of conducting fair and peaceful elections. Student leaders are apprehensive that changes in the system will ruin the democratic system of the elections.

Heading: ‘Special’ athlete struggles to make ends meet as govt turns a blind eye - Indian Express
Content:
With Diwali festivities round the corner and people venturing out to shopping malls, markets, and various melas for festive shopping in the Capital, Delhi Police want to take no chances with security arrangements this year.

Companies manufacturing close circuit television (CCTV) cameras are now lining up for orders that the Delhi Police are expected to place soon to upgrade security facilities at various markets.

Police sources say they have been receiving numerous calls of late from various companies manufacturing CCTV cameras.

According to sources in the Delhi Police, plans are afoot to install CCTV cameras at 58 places, including markets and malls, in the near future. The police are expected to join hands with private security systems providers for the same. A city surveillance system on the lines of those being used in cities like London and New York could be setup in Delhi soon.

Zicom Limited, a company dealing in electronic surveillance systems, had recently bagged a contract to install CCTV cameras and the surveillance systems in the Supreme Court premises. They are now looking to cash in on the fresh need for such systems.

Pramod Rao, managing director of the company, said, "Delhi needs to build a central security surveillance system to monitor crime in the entire city. Awareness on the use of CCTV cameras and integration of the various security systems are important aspects," he said.

The way CCTVs are handled at present has resulted in the police failing to gather strong clues about terror suspects, as footage collected from the devices is either not stored, or the picture quality is blurred and unclear. "It becomes difficult to identify suspects using such footage, and it is not surprising that surveillance cameras have not helped the police bust cases in recent past," Rao said.

Police sources say they are now looking at installation of more than 400 cameras across the city with an integrated security system. Rajan Bhagat, PRO of the Delhi Police said, "We have initiated many programmes to beef up electronic surveillance in the city — decisions on the same are to be finalised soon."

The new systems, sources say, will have CCTV systems with video content analytics, public address systems, walkie talkies with law enforcement agencies, along with manpower trained in disaster management.

"No Indian city presently has such a system in place—Delhi will hopefully be the first," Rao said.

Police heighten security ahead of Diwali
Delhi Police have beefed up security arrangements throughout the Capital ahead of Diwali. Rajan Bhagat, PRO of the Delhi Police, said, "We have been holding meetings with members of all market associations and security agencies manning city malls." Police dog squads have been put on alert to respond within minutes to a possible bomb threat, officers said. Special officers have been posted at access points in malls and markets. Melas organisers across the city have been issued strict guidelines. "Our personnel in plainclothes have been posted at entry and exit points," Bhagat said.

Heading: Soumya case: yet another clue leads to dead end - Indian Express
Content:
Para-Olympian Bharat Kumar never let his disability dissuade him from pursuing his dream of becoming a professional athlete. Kumar, born without a left arm, realised that dream in 2006 when he clocked a throw of 10.82 m in shot-put to clinch a silver medal at the IWAS World Junior Athletics Championships in Dublin, Ireland. He also participated in the 200 m track event, but was disqualified due to a false start.

Kumar has no dearth of medals to prove his worth, his latest being a gold medal in the 400 m track event and a silver medal in the shot-put event at the National Para-Olympic Games in February this year.

With the 2010 Commonwealth Games approaching, however, a shadow of doubt looms over his hopes of improving on his past records.

With no help from the authorities, Kumar, 19, is struggling even for a decent daily meal, let alone having access to adequate sports equipment and training. His only pair of shoes have started tearing at the seams.

"I need money to maintain a proper diet needed to support my training schedule. There is no money to buy proper equipment either. If my funds are taken care of, I can focus on my training better," says Kumar, who trains for five hours daily at the Mayur Vihar Phase II ground close to his one-room accommodation, and survives on a thali worth Rs 12 from a local restaurant. Hailing from Najafgarh, Kumar left his ailing parents two months back, who work as bonded farmers, to live with friends in Mayur Vihar and train for competitions. "The ground is near my house and the local coach, Satpal Singh, coaches us there. I have been borrowing money from friends, relatives and whoever is willing to help, to pay the monthly rent of Rs 1,200. I do not want to pressurise my parents for money, since they can barely sustain themselves. Why can't the government finance athletes like us?" asks Kumar, who trains with 12 other para-athletes.

Six months ago, Kumar received help from the Delhi government in the form of a cash prize of Rs 75,000 for his performance at the 2006 games in Ireland. But that amount was quickly spent in paying off various debts.

"My parents had to repay loans taken for household expenditure and the land for our house in Najafgarh," says Kumar, who is yet to receive a cash reward for his silver medal-winning performance. According to the Para- Olympic Committee of India (PCI) there is no a clear policy laid down on the monetary compensation for players winning medals in international competitions. "We have submitted a policy draft for sports for the disabled to the Sports Ministry . The draft demands the provision of similar facilities for special sports in India, as enjoyed by other organisations. We are still waiting for a response from the ministry," says C V Raghunath, assistant secretary, PCI.

Kumar, meanwhile, prepares tirelessly to clinch gold in the 400 m track event at the 2010 Games. "My record stands at 54 seconds and I am working towards achieving the current world record of 49 seconds," he says.

Heading: Illegal building back in race after HC razed panel on MCD plea - Indian Express
Content:
South Delhi Police have negated the claims of a letter they received five days ago, in which the unidentified sender said he had seen two people on a motorcycle fighting with the deceased Soumya Vishwanathan on Nelson Mandela Marg on the day of her murder.

District Commissioner of Police (South) HGS Dhaliwal on Thursday said the claims of the sender were false as the said bike riders were nowhere close to the site at the time of the murder. The mobile phone records of the two men also corroborates the fact, police said.

According to Dhaliwal, the author of the letter said he had noted down the registration number of the bike, which had a Punjab number. He also claimed one of the two assailants was wearing a turban.

"The said registration number was traced to Pagwara and a team was sent. The owner of the bike said he had sold the vehicle to a Gurgaon resident. A team was then sent to Gurgaon for interrogating the men in question. They were released after their mobile phone records also revealed that they were not near the site of crime at the time," Dhaliwal said.

The police were also investigating the possibility of the involvement of a Scorpio car. DCP Dhaliwal said the owner was taken into custody and was released, after the police could not find anything against the owner and gave him a clean chit.

Working as a producer with a popular English news channel, Soumya Vishwanathan was found shot dead in her car in the early hours of September 30.

Police are yet to make a headway in the case. DCP Dhaliwal said, "We are working at getting hold of cell tower details to prepare a list of people who had taken the route that day. There are two angles that are being probed at present but it will not be appropriate to share details. We are very hopeful that the case will be solved very soon," he added.

Heading: Playing with fire: property dealer shoots self by accident in front of family - Indian Express
Content:
It seems encroachers are back on top barely a month after the MCD persuaded the High Court to do away with a committee for monitoring illegal construction in the Capital.

On Friday, a Bench led by Justice Mukul Mudgal sought a response from the civic body on a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) that said large-scale illegal building has gained speed after the court disbanded its panel and 10 court commissioners. The court had earlier wrapped up its panel and commissioners after MCD took offence to their "interference", and said there was no room for a parallel body to oversee the curb on unauthorised construction. A function, the MCD said, is exclusively within its own domain.

In return, the court was assured of a three-tier mechanism, starting right from the level of junior engineers in order to identify, demolish and monitor illegal buildings.

The MCD's plan included fixing of accountability on its personnel — from the level of junior engineers to additional commissioners.

The court had, however, cautioned MCD that it would reinstate the panel and court commissioners if evidence cropped up that the civic body's mechanism was unable to contain the encroachers.

But if the petition filed by advocate R P Sharma is to be believed, unauthorised construction is going on in full swing in areas such as Dwarka and Karol Bagh.

Hardly a murmur is heard from the civic body on any steps to be taken to stop these encroachers, the petition says.

It said the "connivance between MCD officials, builders, politicians and bureaucrats" were writ large in the manner in which these constructions progressed". Sharma alleged hat his letters to Deputy Commissioners of the respective zones has not been replied to so far.

"Massive unauthorised construction which is evident from different photographs (produced in court) clearly shows almost entire staff, right from junior engineer to deputy commissioner of the zone, including the nodal steering committee is answerable to court," Sharma alleged.

The court has directed MCD to reply by December 18, the next date of hearing.

Heading: More power for Gurgaon - Indian Express
Content:
In a freak accident, a property dealer shot himself by accident in Welcome area of East Delhi. Police said the 40-year-old had pointed the gun to his head without the magazine and pulled the trigger in jest before his wife and children. A bullet, which was in the chamber fired and pierced his head.

According to the police, Pulbhusan Tyagi was at home on Wednesday night when his two children said they felt like having food from outside. He agreed and asked them to get ready. "He told his wife, Sangeeta to get his pistol for him. When his wife asked him why he needed his pistol he told her he wanted to clean it. Sangeeta got it for him and he removed the magazine from the gun," a relative said.

His son, Hemant (12) and Shivani (15) went into his room after dressing to go out. He poked fun at his wife for being scared of firearms. He pointed the gun at Hemant and then Shivani, followed by Sangeeta and finally to his temple.

Assuring them there was nothing to be scared he said, "See..." before pulling the trigger. Unknown to him, there was a bullet in the chamber, which was already loaded. It fired and lodged itself on the right side of his head. He fell on the ground, with blood oozing out of his head.

"Seeing the blood, Sangeeta started crying and fell unconscious. Shivani ran to her uncle's house and informed him. He arrived and rushed Tyagi to the nearby Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital, where he was declared dead on arrival.

Police were called in then," a senior police officer. Police registered a case of death due to negligence against the deceased in Welcome Police Station.

Heading: One dies, five injured as truck loses control - Indian Express
Content:
The residents of Gurgaon have reason to cheer. The infrastructure in sectors under the Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) will be upgraded soon. Of this, 75 per cent of the total expenditure will be borne by HUDA and the rest 25 per cent by Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN).

According to a HUDA spokesperson, sector-wise schemes are being prepared for upgrading power infrastructure in all sectors developed by HUDA. He added the DHBVN has also decided to give power supply for streetlights through exclusive electricity lines by installing independent transformers so as to have better control and give reliable supply for street lighting. DHBVN has been asked to prepare estimates for the plan immediately which is to be completed at the cost of the municipalities and HUDA. The DHBVN is also mooting a plan to revamp power distribution system in 17 towns in its area under Accelerated Power Development and Reforms Programme –II (APDRP-II) of the Centre. The plan will soon be sent to the Centre for approval.

The HUDA official added that a special plan has been prepared to strengthen power supply infrastructure for industries at a cost of Rs. 31.56 crores in Gurgaon, Faridabad, Dharuhera, Bawal and Rewari. Under this plan domestic and industrial load would be segregated to give supply to industries through exclusive feeders, overloaded feeders would be bifurcated and old conductor would be replaced to renovate the distribution system. The Nigam has decided in principal to bifurcate all the feeders, in urban as well as rural areas, having over 150 ampere load.

In the pipeline
To tackle the increasing demand of power in Gurgaon, a 400/220 KV gas isulated substation (GIS) will be operational from June next year.
Present demand: 800 MW
By 2010-11 expected demand: 1,200 MW
Land: Underground station which saves upto 25% of land compared to conventional sub-stations
Area: 9.5 acre
Estimated cost: Rs 170-cr
The sub-station would be connected to Bhiwadi at one end and Ballabhgarh at the other.

Heading: Men on bike rob Rs 7.5 lakh in CP - Indian Express
Content:
A 40-year-old man died, while five others suffered minor injuries after a speeding truck hit them in Jehangirpuri area of Northwest Delhi on Thursday. Police said that a woman and an ITI student were among the injured. The incident took place at 9 am on Thursday at the bus stop in Outer Ring Road in Jehangirpuri.

Six persons were waiting for a bus at the stop, when the speeding truck went out of control and crushed them, police said.

"The six victims, identified as Dinesh (40), Dado (45), Apsari (35), Arti (30), Aslam (18) and Yatender (18) were hit by the truck. Dinesh suffered severe head injuries. A bystander called the police, who rushed the victims to Babu Jagjivan Ram Memorial Hospital where Dinesh was declared dead on arrival," a senior police official said.

Police Arti's relatives arrived at the hospital and transferred her to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital. Her condition is said to be critical. The condition of other five are stable at BJRM.

The driver of the truck, identified as Harender, has been arrested. When questioned, Harender said that the brakes of the truck were not working properly and he could not stop it on time.

Dinesh is survived by three children. He worked as an electrician. Yatender who suffered injuries is a student of ITI and was on his way there when the accident took place. Aslam works in a factory in Badli.

Heading: Bisht has upper hand in the battle of equals - Indian Express
Content:
ROADSIDE ROMEO (Animation)
Voices of Saif Ali Khan, Kareena Kapoor, Jaaved Jaaferi
DIRECTOR: Jugal Hansraj
Indian animation has finally come of age. Roadside Romeo, the first Walt Disney-Yashraj rollout is a barrel of fun: "Bole toh, ekdum jhakaas, baap".

It combines the best aspects of both studios — Disney's expertise in creating animated figures which live and breathe, and Yashraj's forte in frothy romance: what better than getting Romeo and Laila voiced by real-life lovers Saif and Kareena?

Romeo is a one-time pampered pooch, now abandoned on the mean streets of Mumbai. Laila is a saucy, red-scarf-around-her-dainty-neck dancer, who only has to bat her impossibly large eyelashes for Romeo to start panting. Trouble looms in the shape of the pug-ugly Charlie Anna (Jaaved), who rules with a ruthless paw and a bunch of louts. He fancies Laila, and woe to any Tom, Dick, or Romeo who dares come in between.

The alacrity with which the characters break into song-and-dance shows that Disney or no Disney, Bollywood rules. Whether style-bhai Romeo is kicking up his heels with his canine pals, or looking for a likely spot to pee ("Yahaan koi toilet nahin hai kya? Man, what a dump!") you can actually see Saif, who does cool like none else. And when sexy Laila shakes her charming rump, breathily coming on to her besotted beau, you know that's Kareena. Both sizzle up the screen.

Where debutant director Jugal Hansraj falters is with the villainous Chaaaarrrlie Anna: Jaaved Jaaferi is made to growl incomprehensibly and break wind more often than getting a chance at being a riot. He does make you guffaw, but only once in a while, and for someone of Jaaferi's goofy brilliance, that's not enough.

But we can live with this Charlie. In his words, he's our chappie, so he makes us happy. We can also handle the strong resemblance our Mumbai curs have to Disney-style American doggie-doos, because we know that given a chance, they will open their mouths to utter a desi "bhow bhow" rather than the westernised "bow wow". Roadside Romeo is Hindi cinema's first stylish, slick animated feature, which pulls off the toughest feat — appealing to both adults and children.

That's, like, cool, dude.

HEROES
CAST: Salman Khan, Sunny Deol, Sohail Khan, Vatsal Seth, Bobby Deol, Preity Zinta, Mithun Chakraborty, Dino Morea, Amrita Arora, Riya Sen
DIRECTOR: Samir Karnik
Two city slickers set out to deliver letters from dead servicemen to their far-flung families, and in the process, discover themselves.

The premise of Heroes is interesting. And in parts Samir Karnik's film does manage to say what it set out to: that pride (the Hindi 'garv' is a better word) keeps the families of the deceased soldiers going, that we civilians sleep peacefully only because someone has given up his life for us, and that we have a country only because we have a brave 'fauji' guarding our borders. But the director falls for the easiest trick in the book: he wrings tears out of so many situations that everything — even the supreme sacrifice that the soldiers make — turns trite.

Heroes needed a radical change in treatment, but it falls through halfway between keeping things low-key and going full-tilt at melodrama. What can you do if pretty Preity is a war-widow, speaking flawless Punjabi, keeping it together for her old in-laws and a young son? And Salman her bluff Jat hearthrob who says : "Teri liye lakh jawani, par yeh jawani desh ke naam", or words to that effect. Sunny plays a rum-swilling disabled airman who loses younger brother Bobby, who carried a torch for the Army. Mithun is an embittered father who hasn't forgiven son Dino for dying. And the two boys-who-turn-into-men on their road journey, armed with a camera and alarming naivete, are Sohail and Vatsal.

The subject deserved a better film.

shubhra.gupta@gmail.com

DAYS OF GLORY
CAST: Jamel Debbouze, Samy Bouajila, Roschdy Zem, Bernard Blancan
DIRECTOR: Rachid Bouchareb
Liberte, Egalite, Fraternite. This film examines the three pillars on which the French Republic stands through the eyes of soldiers summoned from its colonies to fight a war for liberalising a people, while enjoying few of those rights themselves.

Put into the worst of battles towards the end of World War II, with the least compensation in terms of money, promotion, leave or even rationed tomatoes, soldiers from France's colonies in North Africa — particularly Algeria — fight a cold, brutal war and die an unknown death. The government they are fighting for feels no need to understand their religion, needs or culture.

In a great scene, after one hard-fought battle, the tired African soldiers are offered a "treat": ballet in a torn tent. Uncomprehending and disgusted, they walk out.

Nominated for the Best Foreign Language Film at the 2007 Oscars and the Golden Palm at Cannes, Days of Glory has some exceptional performances by its lead actors, who have all enlisted in the war for their own reasons. There is the scholarly and brave Corporal Abdelkadar (Bouajila), who clings to the belief till the very end that the fight against Hitler is his fight; Said (Debbouze), who aims to find reason and hope in his life, led till then in utter poverty, in a place he realises has none of it; Messaoud (Zem), who discovers love in the unlikeliest of places; and Sergeant Martinez (Blancan), a Frenchman in Algeria who is part African, a secret he takes to his grave, constantly torn between the men he knows are being mistreated and his bosses who couldn't care less.

After defeating the Axis powers in Italy, when the Algerian infantry marches into France, it is the first time they set foot on what they have been told is their "motherland". The message is reinforced through martial songs, in speeches, and exhortations to march to yet another battle.

From a small dusty village in Algeria, illiterate and swept up in all that's happening around him, Said has figured it out for himself more clearly. Describing a battle scene, he says: "I threw a bomb at Germany, I beat Germany, all of Germany— I free a country, it is my country. Even if I haven't seen it before."

At the time, he is staring into the eyes of a woman hanging on to his every word, willing to believe anything the soldier of a winning army has to say. The words, you realise, are not for her. Before he marches to a certain death, it's Said's prayer, for himself.

P.S.: The film ends with a note that as its colonies gained independence, France froze the pensions for all its former soldiers at the pre-1959 level despite court orders. That has since changed, thanks to Days of Glory. After then French president Jacques Chirac saw this film, he fully restored the pensions.

Heading: Wild card Batra a step away from glory - Indian Express
Content:
Nitish Arora and Harshvardhan Bisht are popular faces in Delhi's under-16 badminton circuit. As if taking a cue from their chief coach Malvinder Dhillon's observation a couple of weeks ago that their lot (u-16 players) is a step ahead of their age, they squared off against each other in the u-19 category pre quarter-final of the Pramod Mahajan Memorial Badminton tournament at the AIIMS badminton courts on Friday.

The 21-15, 21-9 outcome in Robby's (Harshvardhan's) favour spoke a lot for the winner, but belied the competition.

One of those upcoming faces, according to Dhillon, Harshvardhan battled past his opponent in the first game after being 7-9 down and then in the second, after a jittery start, eased to a 21-9 victory.

"I paid for being too defensive," said Nitish after the match.

"I wanted to push him back in the second game, but couldn't as he came out more aggressively. I tried to tire him out rallying; I knew he's always in a hurry. But that didn't work.

"Apart from this, my shoes tore off during the second game. As a result I was taking time to come back to the centre of the court in time," he added.

As Nitish's torn shoes didn't help, Harshvardhan was quick to get a few tips in between points from coach and father Vikram Bisht. "I was trying to go for the points too early. That's why I lost so many points to unforced errors. I spoke to my father in between and he told me to keep the point on until he (Nitish) opens up the larger part of the court," Harshvardhan said.

As a couple of his open-chested half-smashes drew applause, Dhillon's satisfaction seemed overpowering. "Robby, Trinayan (Lahkar), Bhaskar (Chakravarty), Avilash (Sharma), Nitish (Arora) and Jayank Ahuja are among the most promising among the u-16 age group. They will definitely make it big for Delhi. Bhaskar has already won a u-19 title and the rest are on the correct path. Robby needs to mature a bit, but he's a lot of time for that," said Dhillon.

Work is definitely on to calm down Harshvardhan's hurried approach, even if it's natural. "I can't curb his natural instincts of aggression outrightly. But his game is becoming more and more predictable. Here the standard is such that he's escaping, but whenever he goes abroad, the mistakes become prominent. Even players like Bhaskar are getting ousted in the quarters when they are playing in Chandigarh. For Harshvardhan, I'm making him concentrate on long rallies during practice. He also needs to mature as a player," said Bisht.

At the threshold of making it to the last four now for the first time though, Harshvardhan looked concerned about a jinx that has haunted him during the last three tournaments. "Whenever I've played in the u-19 category, I have been ousted in the quarter-finals. I lost in the Delhi State Championship, JD Tytler and at Punjabi Bag," said Harshvardhan.

And in Kaustav Das the third seed of the u-19 category, he has the last opponent he would've wanted, especially for his jinx to break. "Kaustav certainly stands better chances of winning as he's more experienced. He's a steady player from whom you would not get too many free points. Moreover, he knows my game as we practice together," added the 15-year old.

Later in the evening, Harshvardhan beat Sumit Rawat 21-15, 21-19 in the first round of the men's category.

Heading: Sound Impact - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi's Ratnika Batra upset statemate Shalini Sahoo 6-2, 6-1 in the semi-final of the women's National tennis championship to ensure host representation in the title clash of the tournament. But more impressive than her win over the top seed was the way it came about -- she came into the event as a wild card entry.

Batra's progress in the tournament is more fantastic than believable. Having turned 14 recently, she became eligible to participate in women's tournaments only now and this is her maiden women's tournament. But the girl who feels no pressure when she walks on to the court feels it is no big achievement. "It feels good to reach the final but I don't think it is a great achievement. To win the final would be bigger," she says nonchalantly.

Batra has been part of the Indian squad for the junior Fed Cup and the junior World Cup and had played only in age-group meets -- under-14, 16 and 18 -- so far. Every player she defeated on her way to the final is older to her and more experienced. "Shalini has played in $25000 meets before, she is ranked in the top-10 in India and much more experienced. I have never played against her before this, so it feels good to have played well against her," Batra says. Not just that, she even practices hard with Shalini at the Siri Fort Academy, besides working out at the Rohini Sports Complex.

Batra's performance is indicative of the growing popularity of tennis in Delhi. Ten of the 32 players in the fray were from the capital, while three of them made it to the quarter-finals. If not for facing each other in the semis, it could well have been an all-Delhi final. "I think it's just that there are so many girls playing tennis in Delhi that they end up making up the huge numbers," says Batra.

However, despite her dream run so far, she is not taking things for granted. She knows that her opponent in the final -- Shweta Rana, who has come through the qualifying stages and is herself on a roll here, having accounted for three seeded players en route to the final -- will not be easy. Rana overcame a late challenge from seventh seed Geeta Manohar, winning 6-1, 7-6 (4). But if she wins, it will be the perfect end to an ideal week.

Meanwhile, Shalini Sahoo had the consolation of winning the doubles title along with Treta Bhattacharya, as the fourth seeded duo beat the unseeded pair of Arantxa Andrady and Sayali Bhilare 6-1, 6-3 in the final.

Results: Ratnika Batra beat Shalini Sahoo 6-2, 6-1; Shweta Rana beat Geeta Manohar 6-1, 7-6 (4); Treya Bhattacharya/Shalini Sahoo beat Arantxa Andrady/ Sayali Bhilare 6-1, 6-3

Heading: ’Cause It Matters - Indian Express
Content:
The buzz of Indian rock 'n' roll has British producer John Leckie checking in and choosing his fab four bands

Why would John Leckie, one of the most high-profile record producers of Britain who has worked with popular bands like Radiohead, The Verve and Kula Shaker, fly down to India? Well, to choose his own fab four from the country.

When the British Council began the project Soundpad in November last year, the intention — to showcase the best of Indian rock 'n' roll — must have caused a chuckle in some quarters. But that was precisely what got Leckie and producer Dan Austin interested and to begin the talent hunt. "I decided to be a part of this only because it involved bands from India. I was curious to get to know the local talent that has been creating some buzz around the world," says Leckie, who has been spending all his time at the Yash Raj Studios, staying up until late night, recording with his new finds: Delhi bands Advaita and Indigo Children (previously The Superfuzz), Mumbai's Medusa and Bangalore's Swarathma.

Leckie, who started his career at Abbey Road and worked with Pink Floyd (Meddle and Wish You Were Here) and the Beatles John Lennon (Plastic Ono Band) and George Harrison (All Things Must Pass), has seen and heard the best of Brit rock scene. Now, he has fast-forwarded through Indian rock as well, listening to over 40 bands from across the country. While he was inspired by his chosen four, he brutally says that several others were nothing short of pomposity "It is essential for a producer to be inspired by the music of the artist he is going to work with and these four bands did give me something that I wanted to delve deeper into," says Leckie.

While the barefaced rock of Indigo Children and the electronica of Medusa reminded Leckie of the artists in the UK, he was impressed by Swarathma's theatrical display of Indian folk weaved into Kannada and Hindi lyrics and the serious fusion of Advaita.

Each band has recorded two tracks with Leckie, and an album and a tour are well on the way. The album, British Council's Soundpad, which will be released early next year, will have tracks such as Advaita's Colourful and Just enough, Indigo Children's Sing to me and Swarathma's Jamba and Yeshu Allah aur Krishna.

The bands agree that the journey with the Brit has been one exrordinary experience. Advaita's keyboardist Anindo Bose says, "Though he is a league apart, John was not keen on changing the sound of a band. He just tweaked the notes to make it sound richer." After the hustle and bustle of studio sessions and the album release, the bands will tour India and the UK, starting with The Great Escape festival in Brighton in May. Meanwhile Leckie will be back home to try some new sounds — with some Mexican guitarists and an American band. But he sure will be still thumping Indian rock.

Heading: Stage Effects - Indian Express
Content:
Elizabeth Hurley on issues close to her heart

When Elizabeth Hurley walks into a room, people stop and stare. In Mumbai for the Estee Lauder Companies' Breast Cancer Awareness Campaign on Thursday, Hurley looked resplendent in pink as she strode towards the crowd that thronged to see her, if not to support the cause. Hurley has been the face and now the spokes-model for the perfume megabrand, and clearly takes her role seriously — she got her family to pitch in, with husband Arun Nayyar wearing a pink tie and her six-year-old son Damien a pink turban.

"It's a cause that has affected me personally," the model explained, "I lost an aunt to breast cancer and three of my friends were diagnosed with it. Luckily for them, it was detected in the early stages, so they survived."

Every year a historic landmark is illuminated in pink glow by the Estee Lauder Foundation to raise awareness about breast cancer and, this year, the Taj Mahal Palace and Tower was chosen. "I go around the world doing fundraisers every October and since India feels like home, it is really special for me to be part of this event here," she said. "And the Taj is where I spent my honeymoon."

Demurely draped in a pink sari with silver rosettes, she said her Diwali plans were fixed. "We will be in India during that time, so there are definitely plans to celebrate it, but I haven't been invited to any Diwali parties yet," she laughed.

The actor of Bedazzled and Austin Powers has already declared her love for Bollywood and her desire to act in a movie here. But what about Indian fashion? Has she attended the Lakme Fashion Week that is currently going on? "We just got into town, so let's see what happens," she said. "But I generally do make it a point to attend such events." Well, a showstopper on the front row is not a bad thing.

Heading: Dollar crosses Rs 50 mark, but exporters not happy - Indian Express
Content:
While Delhiites were admiring Vivan Sundaram's faux cityscape made with garbage at Photoink Gallery last month, at Delhi Art Gallery Roobina Karode was sifting through the artist's early works. She carefully went through Sundaram's canvases from his pre-installation era to choose one that would be representative of his present works and decided on a 1981 oil, The Passage. It is a painting within a painting: beside a brush-holding Sudhir Patwardhan is his canvas The Train, while a woman slides through a crimson road. "It foretells Vivan's future direction in oblique ways," says Karode. Sundaram's canvas and 21 others are part of an exhibition at Delhi Art Gallery and a companion book titled Frame. Figure. Field.

At a time when experimentation with multiple mediums is gaining prominence, the exhibition celebrates easel painting and traces its progress in India. There are FN Souza's Nude and MF Husain's untitled canvas with its faceless woman — the human figures looming large, as Karode says, "in its iconic, emblematic presence". In the younger generation, Sovan Kumar has been attributed with radicalising the easel format as a form of social critique. His canvases like Niamgiri depicts flat hills in Keonjhar district where local tribes have tried to resist bauxite mining by industries. This is the return to the origins, to the romance of the easel.

The exhibition is on at Delhi Art Gallery till November 20. The book is priced at Rs 2,500.

Heading: 2 murders reported in a day in city - Indian Express
Content:
The realisation of the US dollar in Indian rupee reached Rs 50.15 on Friday, but it failed to make exporters happy. They complain of low export orders due to the global recession.

Ranjodh Singh, MD, GS Radiators, says: "It appears to be good news, suggesting that exporters will reap big profits. On the contrary, it is not a happy time as the American market faces recession and hence orders are either being cancelled or postponed. We are not really encouraged, despite the historic rise of the dollar."

Regional Chairman of Engineering Export Promotion Council (EEPC) S C Ralhan says: "We had good export orders when the rupee was down but when the time has come to generate more profits, some importers are asking for discounts up to 20 per cent while others are even cancelling the orders."

Industrialists, however, believe that they are still better placed as compared to their Chinese counterparts, as theirs is a major export market.

Ralhan added, "This is the time we have an edge over China and though we are facing a crisis now, it may help us in the long run."

While the realisation of the US dollar in Indian rupee has increased, Euro's realisation has decreased by nearly 6 to 7 per cent.

For the exporters, therefore, it is like a no-win situation as they are forced to compromise at lesser prices in European markets while in the American market too, they cannot reap the expected profits.

A number of exporters are, meanwhile, offering heavy discounts to attract substantial export orders. Importers, meanwhile, have their own share of problems as import has become dearer with the latest development.

RBI credit policy disappoints industrialists

The Industry sector had pinned hopes on the credit policy that was to be announced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday afternoon. They were, however, left disappointed as no major change appeared, forcing some to even opine that a "gloomy time" is around the corner for the domestic industry.

Heading: Powercuts continue unabated even with reduced electricity consumption - Indian Express
Content:
Official figure for murders this year rises to 59

Two cases of murder reported in the city on Thursday have taken the official count to 59 for the current year.

In the first incident, the body of a 55-year-old man was found near the New Vegetable Market in the Salem Tabri locality.

Identified as Vijay Kumar, the victim was a resident of Hira Nagar on the Noorwala Road. His body bore marks of injuries inflicted by sharp-edged weapons on the stomach, chest and legs, said police sources, adding that Kumar was an eyewitness to a clash between two gangs.

The groups — led by Ajay and Jindi — had reportedly clashed on August 9 this year to which Kumar was a witness, sources said.

On the complaint of the victim's brother, Ashok Kumar, the Salem Tabri police have registered a murder case against four local residents — Babloo, Jasbir alias Baba, Indri and Kechhi. No arrest has yet been made.

In the other case, the body of a youth was found on Thursday from the Old Jail premises under the Division Number 2 police station.

The victim, in his mid 20s, had injuries on the body apparently inflicted by some sharp-edged weapons. While the identity of the deceased is yet to be established, the Division Number 2 police have registered a case of murder against unidentified persons and initiated investigations.

Heading: Homeland Punjab brought alive on stage - Indian Express
Content:
Officials promise uninterrupted power supply on Diwali

Even as the temperatures have come down in the city and the usage of electrical appliances like air-conditioners have reduced to the bare minimum, the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) continues to impose two-hour powercuts in urban areas. For the shopkeepers, the frustration is at its peak as they are facing inconvenience during the festival season of Diwali.

PSEB officials justify the powercuts, saying they purchase power as per the old agreements and are not in a position to buy more power, which is available at Rs 11 per unit.

The officials, however, assure that on Diwali, the city will receive 24 hours' uninterrupted power supply, for which a special arrangement has been made. According to sources in the board, there will be no powercuts once the temperatures dip further.

The PSEB is said to be still providing nearly five hours of power supply to the farm sector even though the latter apparently does not need any extra power at this point of time.

The industry sector is also, meanwhile, facing a compulsory weekly off and three-hour peak load restrictions. Industrialists rue the biased attitude of the board, which, they say, purchases power at even Rs 7 per unit during the paddy season, but when it comes to the industry, the board turns into the money-saving mode.

Heading: Say no to coloured sweets, plead scientists - Indian Express
Content:
Sacred Heart Convent School Sarabha Nagar, released a school magazine, 'Sacred Heart Times," on the occasion of Bethany Educational Society Diamond Jubilee Year. The students displayed talent and exuded confidence on the third day of the annual festival. The little children were all geared up to showcase their radiance and vibrancy to their parents.

The Chief Guest, Col. K.J. Singh, commander, NCC Group, Ludhiana, appreciated the participants. He said, "Children are fragile but engender great hopes for tomorrow. Give your support and love. They are the assets of the nation". The performances included a 'Swagtam song', and an English play 'Kingdom of Mathematica' depicting how calculations ruled our daily life. A unique dance number 'Rippling effects' created ripples and set the audience to tap their feet. The Punjabi skit and the 'Giddhe and Bhangra' performance complimented the programme and made the morning memorable.

Dr Varinder Kaur Thind, Principal, Khalsa College for Women, Ludhiana graced the evening function. She released a special issue of Sacred Heart Times, dedicated to BES Diamond Jubilee year in the presence of Chantal, Principal, Veena Vice -principal, Oliva, the K G Head Mistress.

The students of class VII expressed their feelings for their homeland Punjab and its rich culture through a dance drama. The performance was so lively that one could experience the fragrance of the soil of Punjab. The beautiful Punjabi attires of the students were a treat for the eyes. The chief guest said, 'Today's evening is indeed a Punjabi extravaganza. It feels good to see Punjab culture in its full form on stage."

Heading: Tiny tots celebrate Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
According to food scientists, about seven per cent of milk produced in India is used for for manufacturing khoa. It has been estimated and that khoa constitutes one of the two main bases (other being Chhana) for the preparation of indigenous sweets. The local demand for khoa is indigenously met during the winter and normal routine days whereas the demand increases tremendously during festive season and is met through imports from UP and other neighboring states.

Dr H.P.S. Nagi, Head, Department of Food Science and Technology said that for the purpose of bulk transportation, khoa is loosely wrapped in paper, muslin cloth, jute bags, bamboo baskets or any other less expensive and unhygienic packaging material. He expressed that such packed khoa is often susceptible to deterioration through microbial contamination. Moreover, it is highly prone to adulteration during handling and transportation, said Dr Nagi, adding that several incidences are reported in newspapers every year, whereby khoa is found adulterated with low cost-material e.g. maida, blotting/filter paper, mashed potatoes and sweet potatoes.

Dr Negi said that besides low quality and adulterated khoa, halwaiis and sweet manufacturers also use different colourants to improve the appearance of sweets, informed Dr Nagi, saying that in India addition of only eight food colourants viz Erythrosine, Carmoisine, Ponceau HR, Tartrazine, Sunset -yellow, FCF, Indigo carmine, Bulliant blue FCF and fast green FCF were permitted in quantities specified depending upon the food item. According to some reports, non-permitted colours/dyes including Metanil yellow, Malachite green, Rhodamine, Auramine etc., are being used in the preparation of sweets, confectionery, bakery, ice-creams and other food items at local level, especially in rural areas, he said.

He said use of non-permitted colours and excess of permitted colours can have adverse effects on human health. Some of the common after-effects of prolonged use of synthetic colours were allergy, hyper-acidity, asthma, kidney and liver damage, development of tumor and cancer. Therefore, public should prefer sweets manufactured from genuine/ pure khoa and safe use of edible colours only. Generally, consumption of coloured sweets should be discouraged.

Heading: Kids apprised of need to save power - Indian Express
Content:
Diwali was celebrated with enthusiasm at Maple Bear Canadian Playway and Nursery School, Udham Singh Nagar, on Friday. Children decorated the candles with their little hands and lit up the earthen lamps.

Teachers also made rangolis and decorated the school with a massage "Welcome to the gods." Children came in fancy dresses like Lord Rama, Sita, Hanuman, Bharat, Lakshman, Shatrughan etc. Pre-nursery children decorated candles with glitters, ribbons and stars.

Nursery children painted diyas even as tiny-tots danced to the tunes of Diwali related songs. Veena Aggarwal, principal of the school, told kids the importance of the festival.

Heading: UNO Day celebrated - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) on Friday organised a paper-reading contest, "Why and how to save electricity" in the premises of Sanatan Vidya Mandir Senior Secondary School, Deep Nagar.

Chief guests and judges included Manmohan Singh, Deputy Director SLSC (System Losses Study Cell) and Ramesh Kumar Khanna, Assistant Director, SLSC, PSEB.

All participants presented their views on conservation of electrical energy. They explained about the increasing demand of electricity, its misconsumption and shortage of its supply. They elaborated on different methods to save electricity.

The chief guest, Manmohan Singh, in his speech made the audience aware of the programmes organised by PSEB to save electricity. He urged the audience to make judicious use of this energy because its consumption was more than supply. He laid stress on using CFL bulbs, solar inverters and best quality appliances.

Content:
Khalsa Senior Secondary School, Civil Lines, celebrated UNO Day here on Friday. Prof Jagpal Singh, Member Senate, Punjab University, and head of the Department Political Science, SCD Government College for Boys, was the chief guest on the occasion.

Heading: BVM score 2-1 win over Indo Canadian - Indian Express
Content:
The Stroke Unit of Department of Neurology, CMC Hospital, will be observing the World Stroke Day on October 30. For the past two years, the World Stroke Organization has been celebrating World Stroke Day with specific themes. The theme for this year is "Small strokes: big trouble".

This theme emphasizes on 'silent strokes' which are the most common types of strokes. Silent strokes affects thinking, mood and personality of a person. If not treated early it can lead to a major stroke and cognitive impairment.

An education programme is being organised by the Stroke Unit, College of Nursing, College of Physiotherapy and Department of Dietetics for the patients and their relatives. There will be posters, short talks, skits and demonstrations focussing on the theme of the World Stroke Day. A free medical check up and advice will be given for individuals with high risk for stroke. Dr Jeyaraj D Pandian, board of director from South-East Asia for World Stroke Organization, said "Stroke is a preventable and a treatable catastrophe".

Heading: Betting on... Betiyan - Indian Express
Content:
Hotel by the Bay

Discovery Travel and Living,

Sunday, 8:30 pm

Rating**1/2

Ques* What's it about?

Discovery Travel and Living has a new show on offer and its touting it as the first exclusive hotel show. Hotel by the Bay, a 10-part series on the channel will showcase a series of luxurious hotels from around the world. The show that launches this Sunday begins with a look at the Taj Mahal Palace & Tower, Mumbai. HBTB promises to be a sneak-peek into the inner workings of seemingly prefect hotels that work on clock-work precision and satisfy their customers' every need. Hotels plan meticulously for days and arrangements are made well before hand to keep up that reputation that rests precariously in a competitive tourism and hospitality industry.

Ques* Who's in it?

The interesting feature of the show is the lack of a host. Unlike other shows on the channel that made hosts like Ian Wright and Anthony Bourdain household names, this show follows more of a fly on the wall approach, taking us behind the scenes, watching housekeeping staff, chefs, butlers and managers prepare for their daily parade of serving and pleasing an array of guests - from foreign dignitaries and bureaucrats to royalty - hotel staff has to be prepared for any demand from the customer king. While the missing host puts the spotlight on the people who really matter and make the hotel machinery work, the format can get a bit dull with the constant drone of an old-school voice-over.

Ques* What's hot?

The feel of the show is very real and sometimes even intimate. Hotel staff is not the stiff, perfect soldiers one encounters at one of these hotels, but nervous people following orders and trying to impress their bosses and customers. And there is none of the contrived, 'on the frying pan' yelling and screaming one sees in shows like Hell's Kitchen that show demonic chefs making life hell for their juniors. Most of the time, the real faces behind the exquisite multiple-course meals and delicate deserts are benevolent, plump head chefs who encourage their protégés and their gastronomical experiments.

Ques* What's not?

And still, there is the slight attempt to ape the ruthless, reality hotel shows that run their course before Hotel by the Bay. The head chef at the Taj hams it up a bit, playing the 'difficult to please' boss. But that's not the heart of the problem with this show. The entire episode is made with a half-hearted lack of energy. In patches, the camera is shoddy enough to pass of as a home-video. There is also very less about the heritage of the hotel that is being showcased. The Taj Mahal Palace & Tower is part of Mumbai's architectural heritage and has played host to many a star and scion. But they only see a passing mention in the show with bad photographic memorabilia. If this first episode is to set the tone for the show, then it certainly won't be the best kind. Discovery Travel and Living had higher production standards.

Should you be watching it? Lifestyle and luxury travel have been the flavour for some seasons now, and this show adds on to the bandwagon. But it's certainly delightful to get acquainted with the real people who run the show at the luxury havens. And for that, do watch.

Heading: Farmers protest dumping ground near village - Indian Express
Content:
Over 150 residents of Naubasta village on the city's outskirts staged a demonstration at the office of the divisional commissioner on Friday, protesting against the Lucknow Development Authority's (LDA) plan to develop a dumping ground near their village on Devan Road.

The villagers submitted a memorandum at the office, stating that if the LDA did not shift the site of the dumping ground, they will launch an agitation from November 15. The LDA had earmarked 38 hectares of land near Naubasta for the proposed dumping ground.

The villagers staged the protest under the banner of Bharatiya Gramin Dal (UP). Its president Chandra Bhan Singh Patel said, "Over 500 families live in Naubasta. It is only 100 m away from the proposed dumping ground. Two schools, a nursing home and a residential colony are located there. It will pollute the environment."

He added that a pond located in the area has also been included in the earmarked space. "The LDA is going to dump garbage in a pond when there is a High Court ruling against damage to any natural water body," Patel said.

Villages including Dhavaan, Chinhat, Amrai, Matiyari, Hardasikhera, Fatehapurva, Takrohi, Kanchanpur, Matiyari, Ganeshpur, Rehmanpur and other colonies developed by the government are also located near the site. Moreover, the land was fertile and agriculture was the only source of livelihood for the villagers, he said.

LDA Joint Director of Land Acquisition and Development, S B Mishra, said: "The LDA has already surveyed the area. After acquisition, we will hand it over to the Lucknow Municipal Corporation. The land acquisition process has already been initiated."

Asked about the protest by the villagers, Mishra said: "I am not aware of any protest. But as the dumping ground is required for the city, it has to be developed somewhere." Regarding the presence of a pond within the earmarked area, he said in case there is a pond, it will not be used for dumping garbage.
