Heading: Archers decide not to bow before state association - Indian Express
Content:
Forensic experts rule out use of RDX or ammonium nitrate

Forensic science experts have ruled out the use of RDX or ammonium nitrate in the Modasa blast that killed one person and injured several others on September 29.

Experts in the Chemistry department of the Directorate of Forensic Sciences (DFS) in Gandhinagar told Newsline on Saturday that the explosive used in the blast was gunpowder.

"We found no trace of RDX or ammonium nitrate in the samples given to us for examination," said a senior expert, adding, "The main explosive in the sample mixture contained residue of gunpowder."

An Integrated Circuit (IC) that the police had recovered from the blast site is currently being tested at the Physics department of the DFS. The department is likely to handover its final report to the Sabarkantha police, who are investigating the case, by next week.

Unlike the bombs that exploded in Ahmedabad on July 26 and those found unexploded in Surat, the Modasa bomb, according to DFS experts, was a simple Improvised Explosion Devise (IED).

"Gunpowder, packed tightly inside a cast-iron container, was the main explosive material in the bomb. While a simple detonator was used as the primer that initiated ignition, the IC used as timer was non-programmable and fixed time. A motorcycle battery was used to complete this circuit," said a senior scientist, who is supervising the forensic examination.

Meanwhile, an officer associated with the probe said the registration number on the fake number plate of Hero Honda Passion, which was used in the blast, had been traced to a Bajaj Boxer motorcycle in Himmatnagar.

"The motorcycle is registered in the name of a State Transport Corporation employee. There is, however, no connection between the two vehicles," he said.

Superintendent of Police R B Brahmbhatt, who is supervising the investigations, said he was not aware of the reported arrest of some persons from Modasa in connection with the Malegaon blasts by the Mumbai Police. "We will soon get in touch with the Mumbai Police," he said.

Heading: ‘Discovery of terror elements in Hindu outfits not surprising’ - Indian Express
Content:
Over 55 of them boycott Rajkot open meet for anti-tribal stance of the archery association

As many as 55 students from Gujarat's sole archery academy, Eklavya Archery Academy, boycotted the Open Gujarat Archery Competition held at Rajkot on Saturday. They took this step to bring to light how the indigenous sport stands marginalised due to the lack of sponsors and politicking.

Dinesh Bhil, the founder of the academy and three-time national gold winner, said: "The event should have been held at Naswadi, Vadodara or one of the tribal districts. This is an anti-tribal move, therefore the students decided to boycott the event."

He added the organisers should realise that the poor tribal students cannot handle the expenses of going to Rajkot. "They have been holding this event in Rajkot for the last four years. It takes Rs 500-1000 to go to Rajkot. Also, the organisers charge money for registration. How can a poor tribal archer afford all this?" said Bhil.

The organisers, however, have a completely different take on the whole story. "We have 51 participants from all over the state, including Panchmahals, Dahod, Narmada, Surat and Vadodara. We have provided conveyance to all the participants by giving them Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation (GSRTC) bus tickets, along with free boarding and lodging facilities," said Ketan Trivedi, organising secretary of the competition and member, Archery Association of Gujarat.

Trivedi added that the annual competition was held in Rajkot, as there is more media publicity and coverage of the event. "When the event was held in tribal areas, no one came to see these archers. We organised the event in Naswadi five years ago, but there were no sponsors or coverage," said Trivedi.

He added that the event was organised in Rajkot in order to promote the sport in Saurashtra, which had just two students participating from the district.

Interestingly, Trivedi also said that there is a sheer lack of infrastructure and availability of sponsorship in Saurashtra.

"We get around Rs 3,000 a year from the District Sports Authority (DSA), which is a very small amount to organise a sports event of this kind. Some of the equipment like the imported recovery bows, cost around Rs 2-3 lakh," he said.

On the other hand, he said that the Eklavya Archery Academy has 12 recovery bows. "They wanted us to provide them with a special bus to take their students. They have 12 recovery bows. How do you say that they do not have money?" asked Trivedi.

The Archery Association of Gujarat provides recovery bows to the students with 25 per cent discount. "The association also has to pay Rs 25,000 as subscription fee to the Archery Association of India, for which our players get representation in the national level games," said Trivedi.

While Trivedi and the other organisers were trying to market the sport to get sponsors, they were told that only cricket can get them sponsorships in Rajkot and other places.

"There is no scope left for any other sport. If we move the competition to the tribal areas, we will lose whatever sponsorships we get as no one is ready to come and sponsor an event in these areas," said Trivedi.

While Bhil claims that every year the AAG assures them that the event will happen in Bodeli or Vadodara, Trivedi said that the event would be held in Ahmedabad next year.

"It was the Rajkot Archer's Association that agreed to host the event in the city. We had approached Vadodara and Surat, but there was no response," he said.

Heading: Cong dares BJP to snap ties with ABVP, HJM - Indian Express
Content:
Ahmedabad most communal city; hatred against Muslims brewing since 2002, says former DGP

The recent revelations about the possibility of Hindu extremist organisations behind the Malegaon and Modasa blasts is 'not surprising', feels R B Sreekumar, former Director General of Police (DGP), Gujarat. He said this is the result of their concerted plan of mass action against Muslims.

Sreekumar said: "The situation has been ripe since the 2002 riots. Even then Hindu radical outfits like the Bajrang Dal and the Vishwa Hindu Parishad were involved in large scale rioting and violence. A lot of hate literature was being distributed and there is every possibility of more militant elements being born out of all this."

Sreekumar, who was the ADGP (Intelligence) during and after the riots, has in his various confidential reports flagged down the possibility of more targeted violence in the future. All the confidential reports prepared by him during that period are a part of the affidavits he submitted before the Justice Nanavati-headed riot inquiry commission.

In a confidential note titled 'Current Communal Scenario in Ahmedabad City' sent on April 24, 2002 to the Additional Chief Secretary (Home), Sreekumar had profiled the city in the aftermath of the riots.

'Discovery of terror elements in Hindu outfits not surprising' At one place the report says: "Reports indicate that extremist sections of the VHP and the Bajrang Dal are planning mass actions against Muslims in certain strongholds of the minorities…clashes between Hindu and Muslim ghettos by using sophisticated weapons may become a routine affair."

In his many intelligence reports of the period, Sreekumar had also pointed out the large scale procurement of arms by radical elements in both communities.

A 1971 batch IPS officer, Sreekumar, was superceded to the post of the DGP in February 2005, allegedly for his strong anti-government deposition and affidavits filed by him before the Nanavati Commission. He was later given the rank retrospectively by an order of the Gujarat High Court in May this year.

Sreekumar, who was the ADGP (Intelligence) till September 2002, said: "While the organisations involved in the Modasa and Malegaon may not be known names so far, there is every likelihood that they are connected to the Sangh Parivar. It is like some members starting their own militant factions based on the same larger ideology."

Identifying radical Hindu hotspots in the state, Sreekumar said: "Ahmedabad is the most communal place you can find. Also, certain areas around Chota Udepur, near the Madhya Pradesh border, are areas that can be used for training camps and other militant purposes."

According to him, both Hindu and Muslim extremist organisations are feeding 'ideological ammunition' to convert people of the two communities into 'pre-programmed human robots who can be deployed for mass rampage and wanton killings.'

Heading: Escape route: Diversify to escape the downslide - Indian Express
Content:
Saffron party must condemn terror acts of its sister outfits: Modhwadia

Gujarat Congress spokesperson Arjun Modhwadia said on Saturday that the BJP must snap its ties with the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and the Hindu Jagran Manch (HJM) if it really wants to promote peace and harmony in the country.

Modhwadia told the media at the state party headquarters that if the BJP believed in non-violence, it should come out with a strong condemnation of the reported involvement of members of these saffron outfits in the Malegaon and Modasa blasts.

The chief spokesperson said that as a mainstream political party, the BJP should not practice double standards of condemning violence by Muslim outfits and looking the other way when their own sister organisations are found indulging in such acts.

Cautioning the BJP and the RSS against supporting activities aimed at disintegration of the country for political gains, he pointed out that it was internal strife that had resulted in the partition of several countries.

He said the people of the country would never forgive the Sangh Parivar and the BJP for supporting activities inimical to the unity and integrity of India.

Giving examples of the involvement of the sister organisations of the RSS and the BJP in the violent and "anti-national" incidents in the last two years, Modhawadia said that saffron groups were involved in the attack on a Marathi drama in Navi Mumbai on February 20, 2008 and the subsequent blasts at Vashi and Thane in Maharashtra.

Earlier, RSS activists were found assembling bombs in a PWD Colony at Nanded in Maharashtra, he said.

Two Bajrang Dal activists were also killed in blasts while when they were assembling bombs at a house in Kanpur recently, he added.

Modhwadia further said that former Godhra BJP legislator and Bajrang Dal leader Haresh Bhatt had in a sting operation by Tehelka revealed how large quantities of arms and ammunition were assembled by the Bajrang Dal members for the 2002 riots for political gains.

He alleged that in 2000, HJM was indulged in a large-scale violence against Christians in the Dangs district.

Afterwards, saffron forces systematically attacked Christians in Orissa and Karnataka, and now, they are following the footsteps of the SIMI by conducting blasts at different places across the country, he said.

The Congress leader demanded a CBI probe into the Sabarmati Express carnage incident, the Akshardham Temple attack and the murder of former state Home Minister Haren Pandya.

Heading: Tata Motors to put Ahmedabad Stock Exchange into overdrive - Indian Express
Content:
Don't put all eggs in one basket; choose varied investment options, say experts

Gujaratis are known for their acumen in equity and commodity markets not only in the country but the world over. But they, too, have been caught in the web of the prevailing global financial crisis. The result: the Festival of Lights is not as bright this year.

According to commodity market experts, the factors that drive equities and commodities are quite different, as the presence of investors are more in the equity market. However, a concerted campaign launched by the Forward Markets Commission, the regulator of the commodities markets, and two other national commodity exchanges — the Muti-Commodity Exchange of India Ltd (MCX) and the National Commodities and Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX) — has created awareness among the retail investors not to put all eggs in one basket. Further, the advent of spot exchanges will come to the rescue of cotton-growers and farmers to choose the right commodities for sowing and reaping rich harvest of benefits.

Those who turned to commodities as an alternative form of investment have realised the fact that this is a stand-alone asset class. Their returns are not linked to the performance of other asset classes such as equities, debt and realty. Since it is impossible for an investor to predict market trends, the best way is to diversify his assets across investment categories, feel market experts.

V Segar (50), a schoolteacher and savvy investor in Bapunagar, liquidated some of his stock holdings and started diversification of his investment portfolios into gold exchange-traded funds and commodities when the equities market was in bull's phase in the beginning of this year. His permutations and combinations paid him rich dividends in the form of good returns.

A public sector bank staffer and investor in Maninagar, who wished to remain anonymous, said: "In the world of investment, never rely on the so-called investment advisers. Do your own homework by constantly monitoring the market sentiments and act swiftly when an opportunity comes. For getting good returns on any commodity, one has to keenly observe the demand and supply position of that commodity during its sowing and harvest seasons."

According to figures provided by the Forward Markets Commission, the fortnightly trading volumes on commodity exchanges have increased by more than 100 percent to Rs 3,01,000 crore in July 2008 which was Rs 1,45,000 crore in August last year. This proves that more and more investors are turning towards commodities.

Commodities have delivered decent returns even in the long term. In the last three years, gold and silver have generated a return of 20-30 per cent per year, while commodities like pulses and oil seeds have earned annualised returns of 15-20 per cent.

Commenting on the impact of market mayhem on commodities, Pravinbhai D Thakkar, president of the Ahmedabad Commodity Exchange, said: "The prices of castor and guar seeds were hit hard in the global market turmoil. This has dampened the spirit of all stakeholders--growers as well as commodity traders. But this is only a passing phase."

"Friday's great downfall is the cascading effect of the global meltdown and negative sentiment of market triggered by unfavourable credit policy decision of the Reserve Bank of India. The Centre might be right at its end, as the RBI has to control the overall market. Earlier, decision of decrease in CRR and Repo Rate was to increase liquidity in the market, but the RBI has to control everything after all. I felt this is not a bottom of market and further corrections in the equity market is expected,"' said the general manager of Saurashtra-Kutch Stock Exchange of Rajkot.

According to Raju Pobaru, president of Rajkot Commodity Market, the "global rout" has affected the entire local markets, including equity and commodity markets. "Down circuit in the equity market has affected the commodity markets badly. To me this down fall will continue for some more days. Instability in the global markets, especially in the US and the UK markets, will not allow our markets to stabilise," he said.

Pobaru added: "The global price of crude oil has plummeted to 61 dollars but our government is yet to slash the petrol and diesel prices. If the government really wanted to arrest the downslide of markets, it ought to cut the fuel price by Rs 10. On Friday, caster and gaur seeds prices fell deeply. We do not expect any support for the commodity market. Thus, we are expecting this trend to continue further."

(With input from Parish Joshi)

Heading: Kalam delves on lunar mission, market lunacy - Indian Express
Content:
After Nano makes inroads, auto giant may get itself listed on ASE

Tata Motors, which is coming up with the Nano car plant in Ahmedabad district, also holds the key to turning around the fortunes of the Ahmedabad Stock Exchange (ASE). The company may soon get listed on the ASE.

Shareholders here always have a sentimental attachment to the companies which have manufacturing facility in the state. Both Arvind Mills and Reliance Industries have earned a lot of goodwill from the local investors. If Tata Motors decides to get listed at the ASE, it may ensue listing of other companies as well, which is likely to take the ASE to a path of revival.

As of now, there are barely any listings on the ASE as business has shifted to Mumbai. ASE members are sub-brokers of the BSE through the ASE Capital Markets Ltd (ACML), which is a member of the BSE. The business on the ASE went down because companies did not list their scrips after the Harshad Mehta securities scam.

The possibility of the revival of the ASE is not as remote as it seems if one goes by the recent SEBI announcement of allowing to raise individual cap on raising of personal holdings in the paid up equity capital of bourses from five to 15 per cent. Banks, insurance companies and stock exchanges fall in the categories that can have investment in stock exchanges.

ASE executive director K K Mishra is of the opinion that the SEBI move is a good omen for the ASE.

"It will not only give an exit route to the present shareholders, but also open up new vistas for fresh investors to give fillip to this historic bourse. It is also a good chance for the NSE and BSE to ponder over investment here and thus revive this exchange," he said.

SEBI has been receiving requests that the present limit of 5 per cent is acting as a deterrent for attracting long-term anchor/strategic investors in stock exchanges.

Now that the market regulator has agreed to jack up the limit, this should prove a boon to exchanges like the ASE in their second coming – enough for fresh listings from the region.

Heading: Brothers booked for not furnishing details of servants - Indian Express
Content:
Message to budding managers at IIM-A: Think out of the box and turn this challenge into an opportunity

Former President APJ Abdul Kalam delivered a public lecture on the nation, challenges and leadership at IIM-Ahmedabad on Saturday.

He was in the city to take the second session of 'Globalising and Resurgent India through Innovative Transformation' (GRIT) course, jointly designed by him and Prof Anil K Gupta, a senior professor of IIM-A, which commenced on September 12.

On the occasion, Kalam underlined the need for "creative leadership" for attaining the vision enumerated in

'Vision 2020.' Contextually, he also pointed out that the success story of ISRO lies on the fact that the organisation constantly drives on self-motivation with self-designed ideas maintaining the supremacy of the country's space mission.

ISRO has learnt that "partnership with the industry and the education sector is the only way to run," Kalam said, adding that in the process, the organisation has created 'creative leaders.'

Answering a question on the Chandrayaan mission, Kalam said he had always maintained that the moon does not belong to a few developed nations, but to the entire humanity. India's mission to the moon would open up the celestial body to the rest of humanity, he added.

"There is a probability of finding H3, a material having important role in thermodynamics application, on the moon's surface," Kalam said, adding that in case this is confirmed, there would be a race among the nations to get the same from there.

He further dealt with the mission and Vision 2020 and pointed out various developmental works being carried out by the government to achieve the same.

On the current economic slump, Kalam said it is the time for economists and thinkers at IIMs with all their intellectual support system to devise and come up with an out-of-the- box solution to turn this challenge into an opportunity.

Heading: ‘C K Patel sent his resignation letter after Cong expelled him’ - Indian Express
Content:
In a stern warning to the people who employ domestic helps without informing police about their credentials, the Vastrapur police on Saturday booked two brothers — Raman Patel and Ramesh Patel — for violating the city police commissioner's order. Inspector R B Joshi is the complaint in the case.

The complaint, the police said, is a fallout of the murder of one Nanu Katara (19) in the servant's quarter of bungalow number 11 in Sarthi Bungalows last week. While Katara worked as a domestic help in bungalow no 10, owned by Raman, the accused, Prakash Kalasa, was a domestic help in the bungalow no 11, which is owned by Ramesh.

"Neither Raman nor Ramesh had informed the police before employing their domestic helps. Not only this, they did not even check their credentials before appointing them. Also, they did not have photographs of their domestic helps," Joshi said.

Days after the murder, Prakash was arrested from his native village in Rajasthan. "Tracing Prakash took us nearly a week, just because his employer could not give us his photograph," he added.

The businessman brothers have been booked under Section 188 of the Indian Penal Code and are likely to face arrest, sources said.

This is the first complaint of its kind in the city and is expected to come as a clear message for those who employ domestic helps and keep tenants without informing the concerned police station.

Heading: Saffron forces dump terror-tainted sadhvi - Indian Express
Content: Congress spokesperson Jayantilal parmar said here on Saturday that party leader C K Patel, an NRI, was suspended and expelled from the party following which he sent a resignation letter. Responding to a question, he said that after losing the December 2007 assembly elections, Patel was demanding that he should be accommodated in some board or corporation of the Central government.  As the state Congress leaders did not oblige him in fulfilling his demand, he indulged in anti-party activities following which he was expelled. Parmar said Patel's removal would not have any impact on the party as he did not have any mass following.

Heading: Infocity project  in a limbo; GIL now serves public notice on developers - Indian Express
Content:
We have nothing to do with her; she never campaigned for the BJP, says state Bajrang Dal chief

Once in the police net, sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur may now find herself entirely disowned by the saffron quarter altogether.

Bajrang Dal Gujarat Chief Ranchhod Bharwad toed the Sangh line already spelt out by the RSS Sangh Chalak (North), Bajranglal Gupta, on Friday. Bharwad told Newsline that the arrest of the sadhvi is an attempt to malign the Hindu forces. "They are asking for a ban on the RSS, the ABVP and the Bajrang Dal, when the fact is that no Hindu can ever be an extremist," Bharwad said. He also denied that Pragya had ever campaigned for the BJP in Gujarat. Hum ne kabhi suna nahi (We have never heard of it), was all he said.

It may be mentioned here that Bajranglal Gupta had categorically denied the involvement of either the ABVP or the Rashtriya Jagaran Manch in the violence. "The security agencies have named only individuals and linking the organisation with terror is a political move to divert attention from the SIMI and the Indian Mujahidheen," he had said in a press conference in Ahmedabad on Thursday, washing his hands clearly off the Sadvhi. "The law should take its own course," he had said.

Interestingly, sources in the Sangh admit that the sadhvi did have an RSS background and had campaigned for the BJP in Gujarat during the Assembly elections in 2002 and 2007. Gujarat BJP President Parshottam Rupala, however, mixed no words in saying that he doesn't even know her.

Similar sentiments came from former BJP Parliamentarian from Surat, Kasiram Rana, who too refused to acknowledge the sadhvi.

The politicians apart, even Gujarat Vishwa Hindu Parishad president Dilip Trivedi refused to have known the sadhvi. On being asked as to how the Parishad is looking at a sadhvi being linked to terror, he said he is "unaware of the entire matter."

Interestingly, with the terror tag attached to her, Pragya seems to have become a hot potato for BJP rebel Dhiru Gajera, who had joined the Congress in the wake of the last Assembly elections. "I have not heard of this lady and have no clue as to who she is," Gajera told Newsline.

President of the Mahagujrat Janata Party and rebel leader, Gordhan Zadaphia, however, maintained that the process of linking the sadhvi is a political onslaught on Hindu sentiments.

Chaitanyashambhu Maharaj, the sadhu, who had thrown his hat in the electoral ring against a BJP candidate in Ahmedabad in the 2007 elections, too echoed similar sentiments.

"While she might have been active in MP, she was rather unheard of in Gujarat," Chaitanyashambhu said.

He added: "The entire country's focus had come upon SIMI and the Indian Mujahideen as the faces of terror. The arrest of this sadvhi, and linking her to religious bodies, is now being done as a tactic to divert attention."

Heading: Madhu Srivastava takes to Gandhigiri, sends peace message to Raj Thackeray - Indian Express
Content:
The matter is already in court, they can't do it, says CIL

It seems that the Gujarat Informatics Limited (GIL), a nodal agency of the Government of Gujarat, and the Creative Infocity Limited (CIL), the developers of the Infocity project near Gandhinagar, are once again heading towards the confrontation path in the wake of a fresh public notice issued by GIL that all project assets stand transferred to it.

The public notice, issued by the GIL Managing Director, and published in an Ahmedabad-based vernacular daily on Friday, says that "pursuant to the termination of the Agreements with effect from September 4, 2008, all project assets and sub-leases entered into by CIL stand transferred to GIL, and that CIL has no further rights whatsoever to the (Infocity) project, and also that CIL is no longer entitled to collect any payments, rental fees or other money from the sub-leases…."

The notice further says that "any person having any right, interest, claim or demand to the project assets by way of sale, exchange, mortgage, lease, license, tenancy or otherwise howsoever, is required to lodge the same in writing with documentary proof to GIL at its Gandhinagar office within 14 days from the date of this notice….."

It may be noted that GIL had with effect from September 4, terminated the master lease and concession agreements it had inked with CIL for the development of Infocity project. It had claimed that the developers had violated certain terms and conditions of the two agreements. In the termination notice, GIL had asked CIL to handover the project assets to the former within 14 days of the notice date.

CIL had then challenged this in the Gujarat High Court, which directed the Infocity developers to approach the lower court in Gandhinagar. The case is still pending with the Gandhinagar court, and the next hearing is scheduled for November 5.

"How can GIL issue yet another notice (on Friday) claiming that all project assets stand transferred, when the case is still pending with the Gandhinagar court?" said CIL Director Hiten Barot.

Barot added: "After consulting our lawyer, we will challenge this in the court of law. The notice issued by GIL is illegal. The government's undertaking has no legal and moral rights to do this, for it is a minority stake holder, while the developers have a majority stake in the Infocity project."

He accused the government of attempting to take over the Infocity project by using "muscle power," and challenged GIL to take its possession through a legal battle.

"We have already invested over Rs 100 crore in the project, which is coming up on the 150-acre of land allotted to us on a 32-year lease. We have set up four IT towers in the complex. Around 58 IT-software companies have set up their shops there, generating an annual revenue of about Rs 800 crore and providing direct employment to over 13,000 people," Barot said, dismissing GIL charges that CIL had violated terms and conditions of the two agreements.

When contacted, GIL's company secretary N D Panchal said the notice issued was in keeping with relevant laws.

He added: "We are prepared to face any legal battle on the issue involving the transfer of all project assets to GIL."

Heading: Woman allegedly gang raped in Devgadh Baria - Indian Express
Content:
BJP legislator Madhu Srivastava, who recently hit the headlines for brandishing his rifle in the public, was seen in a new incarnation on Saturday. He sent a message of peace to Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) leader Raj Thackeray through the passengers of the Mumbai-bound Jammu Tawi Express.

At 12.30 pm, the Vadodara railway station was abuzz with Srivastava and his supporters rolling out banners with a message: "Shubh Dipawali Varshabinandan. Maharashtra vasiyon ke liye Gujarat vasiyon ki oar se ekta ka sandesh. Hum sab Bharatiya hain (Happy Diwali! A message of unity for the people of Maharashtra from the people of Gujarat. We are all Indians."

Passengers aboard the Jammu Tavi Express were welcomed with red roses on platform number 1. Srivastava told the media: "This is in for the MNS leaders who are indulged in violence against outsiders. I just intend to pass on the message to Raj Thackeray that irrespective of the fact that we belong to different states, castes, or religions, we all are Indian."

Srivastava, who won the assembly elections for the fourth consecutive time in 2007, has been in the news generally for wrong reasons.

He first made news by allegedly threatening Zahira Sheikh, a witness in the Best Bakery case, and then when he was booked for publicly firing in the air.

Heading: BJP MLA accused of forgery - Indian Express
Content:
After waiting for a judgment of the community court for almost 12 days, a 34-year-married tribal woman from Kalidungri village near Devgadh Baria filed a police complaint on October 23, accusing at least seven persons of gangraping her.

However, a senior police officer investigating the case said that the complaint could be fake, as the incident occurred on October 10.

Sub Inspector G N Thakore from Devgadh Baria police station said that seven persons allegedly raped and looted the woman on October 10, following which she complained about the matter to the village Panchayat.

"In the complaint, she had stated that she was raped by seven persons. They are Raisinh Dala, Manga Soma, Kahar Sabu, Bhudar Soma, Mohan Soma, Babu Shakra and Ranjit Shakra. She also alleged that the accused looted her ornaments, worth Rs 12,000," said Thakore.

He added that the police took up the matter after the woman filed a case in the Devgadh Baria court.

Dahod Superintendent of Police Vipul Aggarwal, however, said the matter could be fake, as it was first heard in the local adivasi panchayat.

"There was a fight between the woman's husband and the accused, in which the former was not paid compensation. There is a possibility that the woman filed a rape complaint against the accused in order to teach them a lesson," said Aggarwal.He added that the medical examination of the woman is awaited.

Heading: VMC gets richer by Rs 3 crore - Indian Express
Content: Daskoi BJP legislator Babu Jamna Patel, along with his son Chitrang and two others, has been accused of forgery by a resident of the same village. The other two accused are Chitrang Shah, a city-based builder and the Talati of Ambli village. In his complaint with Sarkhej police on Friday, Prahlad Thakur has alleged that the quartet allegedly forged documents to grab a 3,440 square metre plot in Ambli. According to Sarkhej Inspector G D Trivedi, the complaint was filed following a recent order by the Gujarat High Court.

Heading: DCB gets twenty-seventh accused in its custody - Indian Express
Content:
The Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) has got richer by Rs 3 crore after its first phase of revenue collection. Primarily targeting the advertising hoardings across the city, the VMC had not only scrutinised 780 hoardings, but had also sent notices to major mobile service providers warning them against putting up hoardings on public properties.

After the collection, VMC is now in the process of pulling down the illegally constructed hoarding structures from across the city.

"We have identified structures that were put up without permission and those which have not yet paid the tax. These structures will be pulled down. Most advertisers have not paid the tax for the hoardings for the last two years," said VMC Deputy Municipal Commissioner C M Makwana.

Besides, the mobile phone service providers have been sent legal notices.

In the revenue collection drive, VMC collected unpaid taxes of the last two years. In addition to the tax retrieval, the rates of the hoarding space will also be increased from the initial prices. After the completion of the first phase of revenue collection from defaulters, VMC will go on to other domains of unpaid taxes in the city.

Heading: Septuagenarian stabbed to death over land dispute - Indian Express
Content:
The designated Metropolitan Court hearing the July 26 blasts case, on Saturday, sent accused Abdul Razik Mansuri to police custody till November 6. Mansuri, a resident of Gomtipur, was arrested by the Madhya Pradesh Police on Thursday and handed over to the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB).

Seeking the remand of Mansuri, the DCB said he was suspected to be the one who had procured the gas cylinders used in the blast at the Civil Hospital. He is also suspected to have been involved in other bombs planted in the city. The DCB now has the custody of 27 accused of the serial blasts.

Heading: Helping hand - Indian Express
Content:
With the Lok Sabha polls around the corner, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee has geared up to hit the road with Nandigram and Singur.

She announced a statewide protest against the CPM and the state government on Saturday.

Alleging that the CPM has unleashed a reign of terror in various districts ahead of the general elections, she announced several programmes to combat it on the ground level. The TMC will hold a rally in Singur on November 2 and in Nandigram on November 10.

Banerjee said: "Hundreds of people died in Nandigram, when the CPM recaptured it. Many people of the area are still missing. We will also organise a mamoth rally in Singur demanding the return of land to dispossessed farmers."

She alleged that with Lok Sabha polls approaching, the state government, along with a section of police, is committing atrocities on people in different parts of the state. "Be it Ayushgram in Burdwan, Suri in Birbhum or Dinhata in Cooch Behar — the CPM is conducting Nandigram-style operations, burning down villages and killing people. The victims are mostly minorities."

Banerjee said her party will conduct "SP Abhiyan" against superintendents of police in various districts, including Burdwan, Birbhum, Nadia, West Midnapore, North 24 Parganas and Cooch Behar from October 31. Trinamool leaders are being sent to different districts to gauge the local situation, she added.

Slamming the state government for not allowing the newly-elected Trinamool Zilla Parishads in East Midnapore and North 24 Parganas to operate, she said: "The state government is not letting us set up district planning committees in these districts. Therefore, Central schemes like NREGA and Indira Vikas Yojana are not reaching the villagers."

Heading: Twenty-three and still counting... - Indian Express
Content:
He joined as a student to ultimately end up as its teacher. Srabani Majumder finds out how Gopal Haldar serves his mentor's school with dedication and hard work

It's been a long but wonderful journey for both Supratip Chakrabarty and Gopal Haldar. They met when Haldar, then a student of Class III, approached Chakrabarty seeking help in his studies. Now they are much more than just teacher and student. It is Haldar who, with ample support from other committee members, runs the social welfare organisation established by Chakrabarty more than 20 years ago.

It all began in 1984 when Chakrabarty, then in his early 20s, began teaching the rickshaw-pullers and slum-dwellers in his locality. Not really expecting a good response, but surprised when he got one, Chakrabarty realised soon that he wanted to do more than just teach them. Besides, experience had taught him that there were too many drop-outs and that he would have to provide them with vocational training or some means to earn some money if he wanted to hold on to their attention. With this goal in mind, Chakrabarty established the Vivekananda Adarsha Milan Mandir. The organisation was registered in 1987.

"I have always been inspired by the teachings of Swami Vivekananda. Therefore, I decided to include his name in the name of my organisation," says Chakrabarty. "There were around 40 children at the time of registration. Now, the number has swelled to 120. I cannot admit more students as we do not have a permanent place of our own," he added.

"When we started, classes used to be held either in the verandah of Lake Stadium or on the premises of a temple on Lake Temple Road. Today, classes are held at three places — in a local club near Tollygunge overbridge; at Sahanagar and at Kamarmath (also in Tollygunge). He says that the organisation functions the way any educational institution does. The difference is that it also provides vocational training to students.

At the centre near Tollygunge overbridge, the classes for nursery to Class III are held from 6 pm to 7:30 pm. From 7:30 pm to 9:30 pm classes are held for Classes IV to X. From Class V onwards only girls are admitted at this centre.

The community centre at Sahanagar is larger that the one near Tollygunge overbridge. It also has a library. Between 5 pm and 7 pm classes are held for those studying in kindergarten to Class III. From 7 pm to 10 pm, classes are held for students studying in Classes IV to X. From Class V onwards only boys are admitted.

Haldar, who was listening quietly while this correspondent spoke to Chakrabarty, said: "Once a month there are separate yoga and meditation classes for the students. Also, depending upon their interests, they can learn tabla, tailoring, typing, screen printing and can even opt for a beautician's course. Students are given a school uniform in April-May when the session starts and new clothes before the Pujas. They are also taken on an educational tour and camping once a year.

Chakrabarty added: "Every year we organise an annual programme and a yuva sammelan. We also celebrate Rabindra Jayanti, Independence Day, Republic Day and so on."

As in a school, there are quarterly, half-yearly and annual examinations.

There are around 30 teachers at present. Ninety per cent of them are ex-students. Any person who wants to join the organisation is first encouraged to teach for at least five years. The organisation is run by a 20-member executive committee which takes all the decisions.

Funds are a major problem, says Haldar. "We have to depend on donations and more often than not end up paying from our own pocket." Chakrabarty is all praise for Haldar who he believes is very dedicated. "It is Gopal who organises everything. He takes his job as president of the organisation very seriously."

Chakrabarty still recalls the day when eight-year-old Gopal and his mother first approached him. "I did not realise then that he would spend so many years with us — first as a student and then as a teacher."

Haldar, on his part, acknowledges that Chakrabarty has been a friend, philosopher and guide. He says it is because of the guidance that he got at Vivekananda Adarsha Milan Mandir that he stood first in school every year.

"It is now my turn to give back. Teaching these kids three or four days a week gives me immense satisfaction."

Heading: Mamata to hit Nandigram, Singur, again - Indian Express
Content:
He is arguably Kolkata Maidan's most unsung hero.Nadim Sirajfocuses on Utpal Chatterjee's last big challenge in a career that seldom got the recognition it deserves

He is among Kolkata Maidan's most accomplished sports personalities. Yet, you don't see shutterbugs scurrying after him. In a career in Bengal cricket spanning 23 long years and still counting, he has had almost everything a player-turned-coach can ask for when it comes to performance. Yet, he gets no more than a passing mention when you talk about the who's who of Bengal's sports fraternity. That's why, when legendary spinner Utpal Chatterjee took the mighty plunge and took up the reins of a beleaguered Bengal cricket team as its coach this summer, it was like destiny choosing the right man for the right job.

Repeatedly ignored by world cricket's highest stage because appeasement wasn't in his armoury and all his life refusing to play ball with a fickle media that only chose to pamper the more presentable and demonstrative Souravs and Leanders, cricketer-turned-coach Chatterjee is facing the challenge of his life — a challenge most typical of a man who never yearned for recognition despite years of jaw-dropping performances; a challenge which most others in contention dared not take up simply because it will fetch only brickbats, no kudos, and there's very little to make in terms of money.

Today, Bengal cricket is down in the dumps — its senior team was sent hurling out of the prestigious national Ranji Trophy elite circuit last season. This is the worst phase ever for Bengal cricket. The scenario is so bleak that even Kolkata's darling Sourav Ganguly doesn't have the confidence to put his hand up and lead a resurrection.

But Davidda, as the 44-year-old Chatterjee is popularly known in the Maidan, doesn't mind sticking his neck out — expectedly, the most likely man to volunteer to clear away the filth and restore Bengal cricket to its place of pride knowing fully well that it's a frustratingly thankless job.

"Bengal cricket has given me so much. I made my bones in the Maidan. After all these years and the loads of experience, I thought I should reciprocate," says the humble man oozing confidence over a challenge laden with pitfalls.

"I have taken up this new challenge, yes, and I won't compromise on the effort that I will put in. Just no compromise, that's my style of going about my job, and I believe this team should get the same message."

Words typical of a hard taskmaster, and why not. One look at his career graph will tell you what Chatterjee means by a no-nonsense approach. Having made his first-class debut way back in 1985, the wiry and ever-so-unassuming left-arm spinner was almost like a machine, becoming one of the biggest bowlers in India's domestic circuit with his mind-blowing 504-wicket career haul.

Add to that Chatterjee's powerful contribution in Bengal's famous Ranji Trophy victory in 1990, and you will be left puzzled why such a big-time achiever did not get to take-off at the international level. He did make it to the Indian team in the early 90s but was unceremoniously discarded despite undeniable, sound performances in the few chances that came his way. Why? Simply because the Kolkata-born player didn't have enough backing in the power corridors of cricket administration offices. And, of course, in an era in which exhibitionism is a pre-requisite for sports personalities to get the nod of approval, the shy and reticent Chatterjee just didn't fit the bill to jump on the showbiz bandwagon.

"I am a man of few words," he says, with a matter-of-factness. "I believe in speaking where it matters most, not outside it. This Bengal team knows me well. They have known me for years. So, they know my nature. I believe we communicate with each other well because of the years of association. And my only message to them is: this team doesn't belong to this relegated status. That should be inspiration enough for them to come back hard in the coming season."

So, if this Bengal team miraculously happens to fight back and get back to where it belonged, don't be surprised if you find the team's coach sitting away quietly in one snug little corner — far away from the glare of flashbulbs and celebrations, melting away into the backburner like he has always done after a magical effort.

Not really expecting a good response, but surprised when he got one, Chakrabarty realised soon that he wanted to do more than just teach them. Besides, experience had taught him that there were too many drop-outs and that he would have to provide them with vocational training or some means to earn some money if he wanted to hold on to their attention. With this goal in mind, Chakrabarty established the Vivekananda Adarsha Milan Mandir. The organisation was registered in 1987.

"I have always been inspired by the teachings of Swami Vivekananda. Therefore, I decided to include his name in the name of my organisation," says Chakrabarty. "There were around 40 children at the time of registration. Now, the number has swelled to 120. I cannot admit more students as we do not have a permanent place of our own," he added.

"When we started, classes used to be held either in the verandah of Lake Stadium or on the premises of a temple on Lake Temple Road. Today, classes are held at three places — in a local club near Tollygunge overbridge; at Sahanagar and at Kamarmath (also in Tollygunge). He says that the organisation functions the way any educational institution does. The difference is that it also provides vocational training to students.

At the centre near Tollygunge overbridge, the classes for nursery to Class III are held from 6 pm to 7:30 pm. From 7:30 pm to 9:30 pm classes are held for Classes IV to X. From Class V onwards only girls are admitted at this centre.

The community centre at Sahanagar is larger that the one near Tollygunge overbridge. It also has a library. Between 5 pm and 7 pm classes are held for those studying in kindergarten to Class III. From 7 pm to 10 pm, classes are held for students studying in Classes IV to X. From Class V onwards only boys are admitted.

Haldar, who was listening quietly while this correspondent spoke to Chakrabarty, said: "Once a month there are separate yoga and meditation classes for the students. Also, depending upon their interests, they can learn tabla, tailoring, typing, screen printing and can even opt for a beautician's course. Students are given a school uniform in April-May when the session starts and new clothes before the Pujas. They are also taken on an educational tour and camping once a year.

Chakrabarty added: "Every year we organise an annual programme and a yuva sammelan. We also celebrate Rabindra Jayanti, Independence Day, Republic Day and so on."

As in a school, there are quarterly, half-yearly and annual examinations.

There are around 30 teachers at present. Ninety per cent of them are ex-students. Any person who wants to join the organisation is first encouraged to teach for at least five years. The organisation is run by a 20-member executive committee which takes all the decisions.

Funds are a major problem, says Haldar. "We have to depend on donations and more often than not end up paying from our own pocket." Chakrabarty is all praise for Haldar who he believes is very dedicated. "It is Gopal who organises everything. He takes his job as president of the organisation very seriously."

Chakrabarty still recalls the day when eight-year-old Gopal and his mother first approached him. "I did not realise then that he would spend so many years with us — first as a student and then as a teacher."

Haldar, on his part, acknowledges that Chakrabarty has been a friend, philosopher and guide. He says it is because of the guidance that he got at Vivekananda Adarsha Milan Mandir that he stood first in school every year.

"It is now my turn to give back. Teaching these kids three or four days a week gives me immense satisfaction."

Heading: Unknown fever claims life in Behala - Indian Express
Content:
Tension prevailed in Burdwan's Ayushgram following clashes between the CPM and the Trinamool Congress supporters during the last three days.

During the 12-hour bandh called by the CPM on Saturday, shops, business establishments and schools remained closed.

Amal Halder, CPM district secretary, said: "Trinamool Congress is creating a reign of terror in the area and murdering our supporters and leaders. Our bandh was successful."

On Friday night, about 10 shops were set on fire and dozens of people injured following armed clashes between the supporters of the two parties. "We have posted a contingent of policemen in the area. A few have been arrested in connection with the violence," said R Rajskharan, Burdwan Superintendent of Police.

The violence had begun two days ago, when local CPM leaders led an agitation to the Ramnagar gram panchayat office in Ayushgramand alleging lack of development work in the area. In the recent panchayat elections, Trinamool has ousted CPM from Ramnagar gram panchayat.

While returning from the agitation, Debi Prasad Singh, member of Gushkara Zonal Committee and a resident of Goswami Khanda in Ramnagar, was hacked to death allegedly by members of the Trinamool Congress. Later, clashes broke out between the supporters of the two parties leaving dozens injured. On Friday, the police arrested a local Trinamool leader, Irfan Sheikh, in Singh's murder case.

Trinamool leader Susanta Ghosh, however, said: "The CPM is standing in the way of the area's development. It is also indulging in violence, since we have done well here during the panchayat polls."

Heading: WBUT ponders over adopting e-tools for evaluation - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when deaths of people suffering from vector-borne diseases like malaria, dengue and Japanese Encephalitis have made headlines, an unknown fever claimed the life of a 40-year-old woman on Saturday.

Sujata Ghosh, a resident of ward number 121 in Behala, had been suffering from very high fever for the last two days. She was brought to the Vidyasagar Hospital this morning, but she was declared dead on arrival. "She was running some unknown fever for the last few days ," said Councillor of ward 121, Kishore Ghosh.

A case of chikungunia, meanwhile, was reported in Salt Lake on Saturday. Biren Singh (60), a shanty-dweller, who lives near FB market, tested positive for chikungunia virus. He has been admitted to the Bidhannagar sub-divisional hospital. Singh and eight other shanty-dwellers were suffering from high fever but only he tested positive.

Though there have been no reported case of malaria and encephalitis in the area, eleven cases of dengue have been reported so far. "There is no need for panic. We are taking all possible precautionary measures to prevent outbreak of any mosquito-borne disease," said Nandagopal Bhattacharya, chairman-in-council (health) of Bidhannagar Municipality.

Heading: GJM asks Tamang to leave Darjeeling by November 7 - Indian Express
Content:
E-assessment, which uses information communication technology tools to assess skills of a candidate, is fast gaining popularity among the educational institutions of the state and is also challenging the age-old written examinations to test students.

The West Bengal University of Technology (WBUT) is considering the possibility of adopting this mechanism in its examination system. "Since the university conducts so many examinations, e-assessment can reduce the workload," said Sabyasachi Sengupta, the WBUT Vice-Chancellor. The university conducts examination for nearly 100 papers for around 90,000 students in each semester.

The university authorities, however, are skeptical whether this technique can cover all types of exams or not. "We can start with subjects opted by less number of students and subjects, whose marks do not reflect much on report cards," said Sengupta. Officials feel that colleges can also introduce e-assessment for their internal examinations. A few private colleges have already adopted this method. The NSHM College of Management and Technology, for instance, has adopted the technique for assessing more than 5,000 students in its various courses.

E-assessment brings down the examination cost and ensures declaration of results in record less time. "Several engineering colleges in the state have shown interest in e-assessment. We are working closely with Nasscom and West Bengal Electronics Industry Development Corporation, " said Joy Chowdhury, a representative of Assessment Tomorrow, a UK-based a-assessment company.

Heading: Mill staff block rail tracks - Indian Express
Content:
The Gorkha Janmukti Morcha (GJM) has issued an ultimatum to All-India Gorkha League chief Madan Tamang asking him to quit politics and leave Darjeeling by November 7.

The Morcha is reportedly annoyed at a remark made by Tamang that party chief Bimal Gurung had met state Home Secretary Ashok Mohan Chakrabarti before calling off the recent agitation in the Hills.

Hundreds of GJM supporters gheraoed Tamang's residence in Batsai and raised slogans against him on Saturday. The police had to intervene to disperse the mob. The supporters also gheraoed Tamang's office on Ring Road. They claimed that Tamang has defamed their party chief and should either prove his allegiance to the people of the Hills or move out.

Heading: SP rules out alliance with Cong over Agra, Kaiserganj LS seats - Indian Express
Content:
Train services on the Sealdah mainline were severely affected after employees of Nadia Jute Mill in Naihati blocked tracks for over three hours during the busy office hours on Saturday to protest against the closure of the mill. Nearly 4,000 people blocked roads and squatted on the tracks after they found a lock-out notice outside the mill. They were to receive their weekly salary on Saturday, but the mill administration put up a notice of suspension of work.

42-year-old kills self

A 42-year-old man committed suicide by jumping before a Tollygunge-bound train at MG Road station. The deceased, Kanailal Bhattacharjee, was a resident of Uttarpara in Hooghly. According to Metro officials, following the incident, two trains had to be cancelled, while three others ran late. An identity card revealing his identity was recovered from the victim's possession.

Trains run late in Howrah

The 12-hour bandh in Bihar adversely affected the schedule of trains from Howrah on Saturday morning. Two long-distance trains —Amritsar Express and Toofan Express — had to be cancelled due to the late arrival of their corresponding down trains. Rajdhani Express was four hours late. According to the authorities in the Eastern Railways, except two, all trains departed from Howrah.

Heading: UP Police probes security lapses during Rahul visit - Indian Express
Content:
It will be a wrong move on the Congress' part if they field Raj Babbar as their candidate from Agra. SP had won both these seats in the last elections. In case of an alliance with the Congress, we should be given the two seats Mulayam Singh Yadav Samajwadi Party chief

Samajwadi Party chief Mulayam Singh Yadav ruled out an alliance with the Congress over the Lok Sabha seats of Kaiserganj and Agra from where Beni Prasad Verma and Raj Babbar had won the last elections respectively under its banner.

Yadav said this while addressing mediapersons on Saturday. "It will be a wrong move on the Congress' part if they field Raj Babbar as their candidate from Agra. Samajwadi Party had won both these seats in the last elections. In case of an alliance with the Congress, we should be given the two seats," Yadav said.

Discussions are still on with the Congress leaders on a possible pre-poll alliance, he added. He also demanded a ban on the Barjang Dal. "The Malegaon arrests have further ascertained the involvement of the members of the saffron brigade in anti-national activities," he said. Demanding a judicial inquiry in the Batla House encounter, he said: "We are not against the police or any individual but only want a fair inquiry into the incident."

Earlier, Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee released a book on SP Rajya Sabha member Choudhary Har Mohan Singh Yadav at the Shiv Lok Mahila Vidyalaya. The Samajwadi Party chief was also present at the function.

Comparing the present political scenario with the past era, Chatterjee said: "These days, Parliament is without proper discussions and healthy debate. Rather than holding healthy debates, political parties are more inclined towards staging protests in Parliament."

Chatterjee told the media that the country has taken several positive steps on issues like education, finance, employment and poverty eradication, but there is still a lot of scope for improvement. "With a united approach, all political parties should work on aforesaid issues, as it is extremely important for the development of the country," he added.

Chatterjee said that the time has come for the youth to come to fore and participate in active politics.

"We need energetic youngsters who have the determination and the will power to guide the country in the right direction,"

he said.

Heading: Man shoots daughter dead in Lucknow - Indian Express
Content:
The Special Protection Group (SPG) has dashed off a note to the security wing of the state police regarding the lapses during Rahul Gandhi's Friday visit to Kanpur.

Sources at the wing said a team led by a Deputy Superintendent of Police was sent to Kanpur to collect the exact details related to Rahul's visit. The team will go through the papers containing minutes of the rehearsal of the security drill before the arrival of the VIP. It will also collect letter of the district magistrate sent to the SPG officials containing details of the route finalised for Rahul's fleet and security deployed along the way, sources said.

It is learnt that the SPG has submitted a brief report referring the route chart given by the DM and lapses on the part of Kanpur police. Meanwhile, state DGP Vikram Singh said that ADG (Security) has been asked to probe the alleged security lapses during the visit.

Ruling out any deliberate attempt behind the lapse, the DGP said some confusion was created due to the sudden change in Rahul's route but erring policemen would be taken to task if found guilty.

UP Congress Committee president, Rita Bahuguna Joshi, however, said: "We have sent a complaint to the Ministry of Home Affairs regarding the breach in Rahul Gandhi's security during his Kanpur visit. The DM and the SSP violated the norms for the SPG-protected persons."

"The alibi being given by the senior officials that a sheer confusion led the pilot car of Rahul's fleet to take another route is wrong. The final route chart sent by the DM to the SPG included Rahul's visit to Chandrashekhar Azad University. The pilot car went straight to the circuit house leaving Rahul's fleet despite the fact that it was a part of the security rehearsal conducted only a day before," she added. Joshi alleged that Rahul's security was withdrawn deliberately on the directives of Chief Minister Mayawati.

Kanput SSP Hari Ram Sharma said: "We had summoned additional police force from other districts to ensure foolproof security during the VIP visit. The driver of the pilot car had not left the fleet deliberately. It was a human error."

Heading: Rs 21 lakh heist at drug godown - Indian Express
Content:
Annoyed over her love affair, a man from Gesupur village in Bulandshahar shot dead his daughter on Saturday morning and then buried the body to hide the crime. At noon, the police got the body exhumed and arrested the accused.

Senior Superintendent of Police Bulandshahar, Raj Kumar said locals had spotted Babu burying his daughter's body surreptiously.

The village watchman later informed the police, which procured an order from the city magistrate to exhume the body. The gunshot in her head was clearly visible. Babu confessed to having shot his daughter —Nargis (17)— with a country-made pistol.

He said Nargis had an affair with a youth in the village and had eloped with him a few months ago. She was brought back home later. Babu said he took the extreme step when he came to know that she had a plan to run away with the youth at night.

Heading: Now, special classes for primary students - Indian Express
Content:
Unidentified dacoits barged into a godown in Transport Nagar on Saturday morning and took away medicines worth Rs 21 lakh. 

The miscreants tied the hands and legs of a security guard of the godown, Devendra Kumar, before escaping.

An FIR against unidentified assailants has been lodged by the godown owner Somnath Chadda, a clearing and forwarding ( C & F) agent of Glaxo Smithkline.

Additional Superintendent of Police ( East ) Harish Kumar said, "It is not clear how the miscreants entered the godown, as Kumar had locked the main gate from the inside." The police said Kumar told them that he was arranging medicines inside the godown when he heard a sound on the first floor. When he was moving towards the stairs, two unidentified persons attacked him from the behind and covered his face with a blanket.

"Kumar told us that after tying his hands and legs, the miscreants snatched the keys of the main gate from him and opened the gate. Subsequently, nearly 10 people entered the godown and loaded medicines on to a truck, " said Sadhu Ram, Station Officer, Sarojini Nagar police station. The security guard said: "Before leaving, the miscreants did not close the gate of the godown." The Chief manager of the C & F, J P Yadav said: "When a consignment of medicine reached the store in morning, the vehicle driver found Kumar lying inside the godown with his hand and legs tied." The guard has been sent to the hospital for medical checkup.

Heading: Bedi lends a helping hand to Australian spinners - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to strengthen the knowledge base of students in primary schools, the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyaan (SSA) initiated a special campaign last month for 65 lakh students of Class II and III across the state.

As part of the campaign, the SSA has introduced remedial classes with specially designed curriculum for the students. Focusing on only two subjects for now — Hindi and mathematics — the authorities are planning to extend it to other subjects from the next year.

In this, a class is divided into four groups. Supervised by the teacher, the groups are formed with an academically strong student appointed as the peer leader, who helps the teacher. "The campaign will continue for 30 working days in Lucknow. These classes will provide an opportunity to even weak students to cover the syllabus," said a senior SSA official.

Additional Director, Basic (Lucknow) Mahendra Singh Rana said: "At present, officials are inspecting various schools to ascertain if the curriculum is being followed. The problem arises when a student does not attend the class. In that case, the student misses the syllabus assigned for the day. We then have to take measures to cover the missed syllabus."

Another problem faced is the number of working days assigned to cover the course. "If a teacher is absent on a particular day, the syllabus for the day is missed and the 30 working day period has to be extended," said Rana.

An NGO, Pratham Education Foundation, is helping the SSA in executing the campaign. "We presented a recent survey report in this connection to the SSA on Saturday. While surveying the projects, lots of issues have come to the fore. Among others, the teaching and learning material received by several schools were not as per requirement," said Ashish Kumar Sharma, Uttar Pradesh Rural Programme co-ordinator from the NGO.

The survey was conducted in the districts of Jhansi, Sonbhadra, Mahoba, Kannauj, Allahabad, Kaushambi, Azamgarh and Mau.

Heading: Zaheer deserves to be fined: Hayden - Indian Express
Content:
Australia may have failed in their bid to rope in Manoj Prabhakar to help their pacers master reverse swing but they managed to get spin legend Bishan Singh Bedi share a few tricks of the trade with their rookie tweakers ahead of the third Test against India.

Bedi, in a pink T-shirt and shorts, appeared in the nets this morning and interacted with both Jason Krejza and Cameron White.

"We discussed cricketing things only. Australian manager (Steve Bernard) requested me to come and have a chat with them and that's why I'm here," Bedi said after the net session.

Bedi admitted Shane Warne's retirement has created a huge void in Australian cricket even though he refused to underestimate either White or Krejza.

"Definitely Warne has left a huge void behind him. Let's see how Australia copes up with that. But to be honest, you can never underestimate any Australian player," Bedi said.

Asked about his assessment of both Krejza and White, the former India captain said, "Krejza is a good off-spinner and so is White. But I guess White is too quick for a leggie," said the former left-arm spinner.

"I didn't teach them anything today, in fact it's not possible to teach something in 40 minutes. We only discussed spin, flight and guiles," said Bedi, who spent most of his time with Krejza, telling the rookie turned how to grip the ball and release it.

Since they landed here, the Australian team have been extended whatever facilities they wanted, starting right from their pre-series stay in Jaipur where all sorts of tracks were rolled out to help them prepare.

Trailing the series 0-1 and set to face the Indian tweakers at the traditionally spinner-friendly Ferozeshah Kotla in the third Test, Bedi's inputs would prove handy for the visitors.

Asked if India were being too generous as a host, Bedi said, "Let's not make an issue out of it."

On India's dilemma on whether to accommodate regular skipper Anil Kumble or continue with in-form rookie Amit Mishra, Bedi said, "I must say it's a good dilemma to have."

The former player didn't have much to say about Mishra and said Kumble was his favourite.

The Australian camp, meanwhile, praised Bedi for agreeing to help out the visitors and team manager Steve Bernard said the Indian never shied away from lending a helping hand.

"It's always helpful when someone like him shares his experience. Whenever I'm the manager of the side, I request him to come and help out and he has always volunteered," Bernard said.

Opener Matthew Hayden also acknowledged Bedi's contribution and said he personally learnt a great deal from the Indian, whom he dubbed "a good friend to the Australian cricket team".

"Bishan and I go a long time back at the MRF cricket academy where I gained a lot of knowledge from him, who has incredible knowledge of the game and spin bowling and he is asset to me really to teach me about how field placings were done in the middle," Hayden gushed.

"He has been a great role model for me over the years and a good friend to the Australian cricket team and a good friend to international cricket community," Hayden added.

Heading: ‘My son was an anti-national, he deserved to die’ - Indian Express
Content:
Australian opener Matthew Hayden was happy that the ongoing Test series between his side and the Indians was being played in good spirit on and off the field but said he would have been disappointed had Zaheer Khan not been punished for sending him off during the Mohali Test.

Zaheer was fined 80 per cent of his match fee for circling Hayden and shouting at him as the burly Australian strode off after his second-innings dismissal by Harbhajan Singh, and Hayden said the Indian pacer deserved it.

"I just think there is a certain way that cricket is expected to be played. I think we would have been disappointed if something hadn't happened to Zaheer," Hayden said.

"Put the shoe on the other foot -- if that is Ricky Ponting running from deep extra cover to fine leg to offer Sachin Tendulkar a word of advice on the way off, what's going to happen?" he was quoted as saying by the 'Herald Sun'.

Hayden said match referee Chris Broad had handled the two teams well in the wake of tensions during India's tour of Australia early this year.

"There has only been a few instances really of challenges to the spirit of cricket and they have been dealt pretty well by 'Broady'," Hayden said.

"We were saying this last year as well -- it's not tiddly winks. It's India playing Australia and it should mean a lot to you. There should be passion, it should be evident there is friction and tension on the field. It's not park cricket.

"The expectations of us is that it has got to be done in a way that is within the laws and spirit of the game." The left-handed batsman credited the Indian Premier League for breaking down the barriers between two two sides.

"There has been good spirit on the field and a good spirit off the field, and I reckon IPL has definitely contributed to that," he said.

Heading: Minorities differed on bill for communal harmony: PM - Indian Express
Content:
Parents of two Keralite youths killed in recent encounters in Jammu and Kashmir have virtually denounced their sons for their alleged extremist links and anti-national activities.

While the mother of one of them came out with strong words against the anti-national activities in which his son was allegedly involved, the father of the other told the police that his family did not want to claim the body of his son killed in Kupwara area earlier this month.

"If my son was involved in anti-national activities, he deserved the fate he met with...My prayers are that no woman should face the fate of being called the mother of an extremist," said Safia, the mother of Mohammad Fayas from Kannur, who was killed in the encounter.

Voicing similar sentiments, Syed, whose son Abdul Raheem was also killed in the Kupwara encounter, did not want the body of his son to be brought home for last rites and burial.

In a written request to police in Malappuram, Syed wanted his son's body to be buried in a graveyard attached to a mosque in Kashmir. Police said it would be faxed to authorities in J-K.

According to Safia, her son was lured to the extremist cause by a friend of him called Faisal, who was arrested on Sunday. He had told Safia that her son was being sent to Bangalore where arrangements would be made for his religious studies. Later on, Faisal told her that Fayas was in Ahmedabad and his studies were progressing.

Heading: Solve German rape case, its affecting tourism: Minister - Indian Express
Content:
The Government planned to introduce a Bill to promote communal harmony but the move has not succeeded because some minority communities have reservations over it, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh said on Sunday.

"We prepared a Bill on communal harmony. The Bill was submitted to Parliament but several minority groups came back and said this is not a legislation that is to our liking," he said, adding that due to lack of consensus, the government had to halt the move.

"This was a legislation meant to apply some balm on the communal situation, but if the minority communities say they are not satisfied, if NGOs said they were not very happy, so there is this delay and we have not been able to resolve these tensions," Singh told reporters travelling with him to Japan and China.

Commenting on the Armed Forces Special Powers, Singh said it is true that in the wake of the Manipur agitation, the government had appointed a group to study the situation.

"But quite honestly, the situation in the North East, the situation in Manipur, even the government of Manipur which has withdrawn the Armed Forces Special Powers Act being applied to Imphal is also of the view that this cannot be done away with until the situation improves.

"We have problems in Jammu and Kashmir, we have problems in North East, therefore, I cannot take these risks with the security of our country," he added.

Heading: Malegaon blasts: ATS picks another suspect from Bhopal - Indian Express
Content:
Goa's Tourism Minister Fransisco Pacheco on Sunday asked State Home Minister Ravi Naik to take the alleged German girl rape case to its logical conclusion as the case is affecting state's tourism industry.

"There is utter confusion in the minds of the citizens as well as the tourists who are desirous of visiting the state as to how safe one could be in Goa," Pacheco said in a letter to Naik on Sunday.

"Please issue strict orders to your department to bring these cases to its logical conclusion. Let the message be loud and clear that in Goa nobody is above the law, however, mighty and influential he may be," the minister said.

The Tourism Minister referred to the charges of rape against state education Minister Atanasio Monserratte's son Rohit and Public Works Department Minister's nephew Warren by a German mother accusing them of raping her minor daughter.

Incidentally, Pacheco was the first minister to raise his voice of dissident after British teenager Scarlett Eden Keeling's death case was brought to light.

"There is utter confusion. I have been receiving several calls from both domestic as well as international tourists inquiring about the safety aspect in Goa," the letter reads.

The letter adds: despite my best efforts to convince them that Goa is safe and will continue to be a safe place and that these are incidents in isolation, people somehow do not seem to believe us.

The minister has said the state got bad publicity for last season after British teenager was murdered. "Frequent occurrence of such incidents badly affect the name and the image of Goa," he said.

Pacheco said the ministry as well as stake holders of the industry are trying hard to put their strategies in place to ensure that the flow of tourists in Goa is not on the decline.

"Goa is fast getting insecure tag due to the adverse publicity as a result of frequent occurrence of such crimes," he said.

Heading: Malegaon blast: Uma says BJP disowning Sadvi after arrest - Indian Express
Content:
The Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) of Maharashtra Police has picked up a person from Bhopal for his suspected involvement in the Malegaon blasts and taken him to Mumbai, sources said on Sunday.

However, senior police officials including Inspector General (IG), Special Task Force (STF), Sanjeev Singh denied having any information in this regard but confirmed that the ATS team is in the state for taking into its custody suspected persons specially after the arrest of three persons from MP.

The ATS had earlier arrested three persons from Madhya Pradesh and detained another from Dewas town in the state for their suspected role in Malegaon and Modasa blasts.

A team of ATS officials have arrived in the state a few days and conducted raids at several places including Bhopal, Indore, Dewas, Jabalpur and Gwalior in search of the suspected persons, the sources said.

Madhya Pradesh Police remained tight-lipped on the issue and is not revealing any information in this regard.

However, the ATS team is acting in the state by informing about their actions to the state police, the sources added.

Heading: Dalai Lama 'gives up' on China, hints at retirement - Indian Express
Content:
The arrest of a sadhvi in connection with the Malegaon blasts on Sunday triggered political charges and counter-charges in the Sangh Parivar with BJP accused of disowning her.

Attacking the BJP, Bhartiya Janshakti Party chief Uma Bharti expressed 'shock' that the party and its affiliated organisations were 'disowning' 38-year-old Pragya Singh Thakur, the sadhvi, who is suspected to have links with right-wing Hindu Jagaran Manch.

"I am shocked and it is shameful that the BJP is disowning her and all their organisations are disowning her. When they wanted, they used her," she said, asking BJP President Rajnath Singh to be 'courageous enough'.

Bharti recalled having met Pragya in the late 90s during elections in Bhopal. "At that time, she was working for ABVP," she said, adding after that she had heard Pragya had become a sanyasin.

Countering Bharti, BJP spokesperson Ravishankar Prasad said, "There is no question of owning or disowning her. She left ABVP in 1995-96".

BJP, he said, "has made it clear that anyone who is responsible, the law must take its course, provide evidence, let the action be taken. Even her father has said that if she is responsible, the action should be taken".

Referring to the Batla House encounter in Jamia Nagar in New Delhi, Prasad said, "We don't talk about any probe about the Jamia (incident) during which a courageous police officer died. We always say take tough action against terrorism. Terrorism has no religion".

He further said, "The way media is painting 'Hindu terror' is something we take offence to. Because I see double standards of media evident there".

Heading: Engineering aspirants beware, unrecognised institutes rising - Indian Express
Content:
Hinting that he was planning to retire, the Dalai Lama has said he has 'given up' on efforts to convince China to allow greater autonomy for Tibet after having led the Tibetans' struggle for half a century.

"I have been sincerely pursuing the middle way approach in dealing with China for a long time now but there hasn't been any positive response from the Chinese side," the Tibetan temporal head said at a function in Dharamsala on Sunday ahead of the third round of talks between his envoys and Beijing.

"As far as I'm concerned I have given up," said the 73-year-old noble laureate, according to excerpts of the speech of the Tibetan monk provided by the office of Karma Cheophel, Speaker of Tibetan Parliament in-exile.

The Dalai Lama said he would now ask the Tibetan people to decide on how to take the dialogue forward.

Cheophel, who translated the speech of the Dalai Lama at the function, said, "Earlier he (the Dalai Lama) used to say that he is semi retired but now he says he is almost completely retired."

The Dalai Lama recently underwent a gall bladder surgery in Delhi.

The spiritual leader's spokesman Tenzin Takhla said on Sunday that the Dalai Lama has called a six-day special meeting of Tibetans at Macleodganj starting November 17 to discuss other options for resolving the vexed Tibetan issue.

The meeting is being attached great importance as this is for the third occasion after 1951 and 1959 that such a conclave has been organised.

After a failed uprising against Chinese, rule the Dalai Lama had fled to India in 1959.

The special meeting would be attended by officials of the Tibetan government in-exile here, intellectuals, social workers and people from different walks of life, Takhla said.

During the deliberations, alternate options would be discussed to take forward Tibetans struggle for solution of the vexed issue in view of the fact that China was not showing any 'positive' inclination to the Dalai Lama's middle way approach.

Takhla said the next round of talks between the special envoys of the Dalai Lama and Chinese authorities is expected by the end of October. He did not specify the dates.
