Insurance companies with affiliated thrift institutions regulated by the federal Office of Thrift Supervision include State Farm Mutual, Principal Financial Group, Prudential, Nationwide, Allstate and the American International Group. Insurers with financial holding companies under Federal Reserve supervision include Allianz, Hancock and MetLife.

Heading: India not in recessionary mode, says Subbarao - Indian Express
Content:
Reeling under pressure due to high aviation fuel costs and low occupancy rate, Jet Airways posted a net loss of Rs 384.5 crore in the second quarter of this financial year. The private carrier had posted a net profit of of Rs 28.3 crore in the corresponding period last year. The company's total income in July-September quarter has, however, increased to Rs 3,258.04 crore from Rs 2,254.22 crore in the year-ago period.

After the fiasco this month of retrenching employees and then calling them back, the airline is now considering steps toward cutting costs and route rationalisation. The move to rationalise routes is expected to generate better seat occupancy which should improve the operational efficiency and profitability of the airline.

Jet Airways carried 2.83 million passengers in the last quarter, 7.6 per cent more than a year earlier. The airline filled 66.3 per cent of available seats compared with 66.8 per cent a year earlier.

Jet Airways said that its subsidiary, JetLite (formerly Sahara Airlines), has accumulated losses more than its net worth (equity plus reserves), but it plans to support the growth plans of the budget carrier that would eventually boost its revenue, net worth and profitability.

Noting that Jet Airways has equity and preference investment aggregating to Rs 1,645 crore in JetLite and an amount of Rs 424.72 crore advanced on account of interest-free loans as on September 30, the company said equity investment in the latter is far in excess of the dues to the wholly-owned subsidiary.

Meanwhile, Jet Airways said on Saturday that it was deferring delivery of aircraft by at least a year but has not cancelled any aircraft order as yet. "We have deferred our expansion plan and are postponing our aircraft deliveries by at least a year," the company said in its outlook for the coming financial quarters.

(With PTI)

Heading: Obama’s greatest supporter - Indian Express
Content:
India's growth story will continue despite a slight deceleration, but there will be no recession as in some advanced economies, Reserve Bank Governor D Subbarao said today.

"India's growth will continue and even if there is some moderation, it will only be a modest moderation. But it will not be a recession... there will only be a slight deceleration," Subbarao told reporters here.

Pegging GDP growth for FY'09 at 7.5-8 per cent, he said, this was "our best growth estimate", even though there were other estimates ranging from 7.2-8.7 per cent.

As India's growth is mainly driven by domestic demand and consumption, the country would be less affected by the global financial turmoil but it would not go completely unscathed, Subbarao said.

Justifying RBI's cautious credit policy announced yesterday, Subbarao said that as a central bank, it had to balance price and financial stability.

Heading: Early voting trends show slant toward Democrats - Indian Express
Content:
Barack Obama slowly walked up the steps of his campaign plane here on Friday evening, his suit coat slung over his shoulder, as he concluded his one-day visit home to Hawaii.

From touch-down on Thursday to take off on Friday, Obama spent nearly 22 hours on the ground in Honolulu visiting his ailing grandmother, Madelyn Dunham. He did not say how Mrs Dunham was feeling and campaign aides did not disclose her condition, but he believes this could be his last time seeing her. He had expressed worry in interviews that she may not live until Election Day, and explained that he suspended his campaign schedule to see her, and recalled how he had not been able to get to his mother's bedside before she died. His grandmother's 86th birthday is on Sunday.

During his brief visit here, he spent about seven hours with his grandmother during three separate trips to the apartment where she has lived for about four decades. A small group of reporters accompanied Obama to the Punahou Circle Apartments, but they waited outside as he visited his grandmother.

He did not speak to reporters on his trip and was filmed by camera crews only once, as he took a solitary walk along Young Street in his old neighbourhood. His visit dominated Hawaii television news and newspapers.

After an overnight flight, he is scheduled to appear at three rallies on Saturday, the first of which is in Reno, Nevada, followed by one in Las Vegas and an evening event in Albuquerque.

For the last 21 months, Mrs Dunham has followed the odyssey of Obama's presidential campaign like a spectator on a faraway balcony. She underwent a corneal transplant to see him on television. She reluctantly agreed to film a political advertisement when he urgently needed to reassure voters about his distinctive American roots. She told him during one of their frequent telephone conversations that it might not hurt if he smiled a bit more.

But on Friday, at the Punahou Circle Apartments, a place of Obama's childhood, she lay gravely ill. For weeks, Obama has tracked her condition. When she was released from the hospital last week after surgery to repair a broken hip, he received word that he should not wait until after the election to make what he believes a final visit.

Obama has reached the closing days of his run for the White House without embarking on a formal biographical tour. In a candidacy built on biography, his advisers believed that substance, as well as an overseas trip in July, was a wiser course. But a biographical tour of sorts has unfolded around him here on the one-day visit to see the woman who was a guiding force in his life and who played a supporting role in his candidacy, from the Iowa caucuses to his marquee speech on race in Philadelphia to his general-election effort to win over voters in red states.

"One of the things I wanted to make sure of is that I had a chance to sit down with her and talk to her," Obama said on the ABC News. "She's still alert and she's still got all her faculties, and I want to make sure that — that I don't miss that opportunity right now."

Heading: Kayani: terrorism a national threat, needs immediate action - Indian Express
Content:
Record numbers of voters across the nation are casting ballots before election day, including high proportions of Democrats and African Americans in some of the battleground states in what appears to be a promising sign for Barack Obama.

In North Carolina, which hasn't gone for a Democrat for President since Jimmy Carter in 1976, almost a million people have voted, and Democrats outnumber Republicans by 2 to 1.

"We're going to bust every record we've ever had," Gary Bartlett, executive director of the State Board of Elections, said of the state's early-voting participation.

In past campaign seasons, Republicans have used early voting to their advantage, mobilising a slice of the electorate that typically skews their way. Yet a look at voters in crucial states suggests that Obama is turning out his base in numbers that surpass those of Republican John McCain.

"Historically, we've seen that early voters are older, they tend to be white, have higher incomes and are better educated," said Paul Gronke, director of the Early Voting Information Center in Portland, Ore.

Early voting continues in many states, so the numbers can change. But Obama seems well-positioned in several Republican-leaning states that have the potential to broaden his path to the magic number of 270 electoral votes.

Heading: Nucleus of atom is world’s smallest storage device - Indian Express
Content:
Describing the spate of terror strikes in Pakistan as an "internal threat," Pakistan army chief General Ashfaq Parvez Kayani has said the issue "warranted immediate action".

Endorsing the Government's efforts to forge a consensus national policy to combat terrorism, Kayani said there was an emerging agreement in the country and domestic terrorism has to be addressed with the help of the people.

The entire nation is united against extremists and the 14-point resolution passed by a joint session of both houses of Parliament is testimony to this, he said addressing a passing out parade at the Pakistan Military Academy in Kakul.

Measures would have to be taken in collaboration with the people for wiping out terrorism, which is an "internal threat that warrants immediate action", the army chief added.

These were Kayani's first public remarks on the campaign against terrorism since the special session of Parliament unanimously passed a resolution on Wednesday that said militancy and extremism would be countered through dialogue.

The resolution also called for a review of the methods adopted to fight terrorism in order to restore peace in the country.

It said dialogue would be encouraged with all "elements willing to abide by the Constitution of Pakistan and rule of law" and "must now be the highest priority as a principal instrument of conflict management and resolution".

Kayani also said the Pakistan Army is "fully committed to safeguarding the territorial integrity" of the country and ensuring the writ of the Government. Pakistan would not join the race for weapons though the minimum deterrent would be retained, he said.

Heading: Pakistan army captures Taliban stronghold in Bajaur region - Indian Express
Content:
Someday, you might take business data off a disk drive and move it into the nucleus of an atom. Scientists have demonstrated what is being called the "ultimate miniaturisation of computer memory," storing data for nearly 2 seconds in the nucleus of an atom. This is a key step in the development of quantum computers, according to the National Science Foundation (NSF).

Using a new technique, an international team of scientists "demonstrated that information stored in the nucleus has a lifetime of a few seconds," the NSF says in a press release describing a new study in the journal Nature. "This is significant because before this technique was developed, the longest researchers could preserve quantum information in silicon was less than one-tenth of a second. Other researchers studying quantum computing recently calculated that if a quantum system could store information for at least 1 second, error correction techniques could then protect that data for an indefinite period of time."

The scientists, from Princeton University, Oxford University and the US Department of Energy, broke the 1-second barrier with a system that uses the electron and nucleus of a phosphorous atom embedded in a silicon crystal. The electron and nucleus each behaved like tiny "quantum magnets" that could store quantum information, but the instability of the electron made it unsuitable for storing information. "To overcome the problem, researchers moved the information into the nucleus where it survived much longer," the NSF states. Data in the electron cloud, which is a million times bigger than the nucleus, can be manipulated, thus serving as a "middle-man" between the nucleus and the outside world, researchers say.

"Nobody really knew how long a nucleus might hold quantum information in this system," Princeton researcher Steve Lyon says in the press release. "With crystals painstakingly grown... and very careful measurements, we were delighted to see memory times exceeding the 1-second threshold."

Under the theory of quantum mechanics, atoms and other objects can exist in multiple states, literally being in two places at once. In quantum computing, each individual piece of information could thus have more than one value simultaneously.

Heading: Most docs prescribe placebos, finds study - Indian Express
Content: Pakistan army on Saturday captured a key Taliban stronghold in the Bajaur region bordering Afghanistan as security official said over 1,500 militants had been killed in operations over the past two months. Loisam, the Taliban's main stronghold in the Bajaur fell to Government troops after weeks of fighting as fresh violence in the region claimed 20 lives in the adjoining Swat valley. Military officials said Taliban fighters had offered stiff resistance before the  town was overrun.

Heading: Robin’s Blue shines bright - Indian Express
Content:
Half of all American doctors responding to a nationwide survey say they regularly prescribe placebos to patients. The results trouble medical ethicists, who say more research is needed to determine whether doctors must deceive patients in order for placebos to work.

The study involved 679 internists and rheumatologists chosen from a national list of such doctors. In response to three questions, about half reported recommending placebos regularly. Surveys in Denmark, Israel, Britain, Sweden and New Zealand have found similar results.

The most common placebos the American doctors reported using were headache pills and vitamins, but a significant number also reported prescribing antibiotics and sedatives. Although these drugs are not inert, doctors reported using them for their effect on patients' psyches, not their bodies.

Heading: Slap in the face for Bhutia and Bagan - Indian Express
Content:
Robin Uthappa scored a 76 on a damp wicket as India Blue defeated India Green by 19 runs on Saturday and set up a title clash with Red at the NKP Salve Challenger Trophy here.

Uthappa's 88-ball knock, which had five boundaries and three massive sixes, assumes significance after RP Singh made the most of the new ball on a seaming Barabati wicket aided by a steady drizzle to reduce India Blue to 19 for 2 in just six overs.

The left-arm pacer's first victim was Virat Kohli, who was caught napping off a sharp inswinging delivery from and saw the ball crash onto his stumps. Yuvraj was next — the left-hander paying the price for going for a pull that was never there, eventually dragging the ball onto the stumps again.

It was then that Uthappa took charge; he initially saw the pace bowlers off, waited for the lateral movement to die down, and then pounded the rest of the India Green bowling. He was particularly harsh on Pragyan Ojha, who went for 60 runs off his eight overs.

Uthappa needed support from the other end, and stumper Yogesh Takawale (34 off 50 balls) rose to the occasion. The duo forged a 56-run stand for the fifth wicket that came off just nine overs, and it carried enough weight to see India Blue through to a modest, yet competitive target.

Pujara knock in vain

Chasing 219 in 45 overs, Cheteshwar Pujara slammed 65 (95 balls) but the Green batsmen were all out for 199 in 44 overs. The Saurashtra batsman hung around long enough during the chase but, despite his impressive technique, Pujara didn't have the array of shots to see the team home.

Pujara stitched a quickfire 59-run, sixth-wicket stand with Yusuf Pathan (34 off 32), but eventually perished off a wild slog. The experienced Irfan Pathan (2 for 30), Ashok Dinda and in-form off-spinner R Ashwin (2 for 31) didn't let any of the Green batsmen to settle down, and ensured that wickets fell at regular intervals.

Heading: In the middle of a selection dilemma - Indian Express
Content:
A slap on the face for skipper Bhaichung Bhutia and numerical superiority throughout the second half were not enough to propel Mohun Bagan to a victory in their I-League match against the arch-rivals East Bengal.

Bagan, yet to win a match in the tournament, were held to a 1-1 draw at the Yuba Bharati Krirangan on Saturday. The ugly incident took place in the 46th minute after East Bengal's Surkumar Singh was fouled by Rakesh Masih, and the former retaliated by slapping Bhutia and being red-carded.

Bhutia put Bagan ahead in the second minute, latching on to an Ishfaq Ahmed pass. But Rahim Nabi ensured the equaliser for East Bengal in the 39th minute after being put through by an unmarked Yusif Yakubu.

In the other match in Margao, Odafe Okolie scored a hat-trick and Felix Chimaokwu scored once as Churchill Brothers beat Vasco SC 4-1. Substitute Agnelo Colaco pulled one back for the losers.

Heading: Genie Watson comes out of the bottle - Indian Express
Content:
Between a quick glance at what was left behind in Sri Lanka and a peep into the forthcoming six-match ODI series against England, the situation demands a close look at the NKP Salve Challenger Trophy here.

With players like Virender Sehwag and Sachin Tendulkar, who missed the Sri Lanka series owing to injuries, expected to return, the Kris Srikkanth-led selection committee will have a problem of plenty finalising the Team India middle-order, as six candidates have already lined up as contenders.

Yuvraj Singh, S Badrinath, Rohit Sharma, Suresh Raina, Virat Kohli — all of whom played in Sri Lanka with varied success — will be looking to cement their places in the ODI side against England; joining the race as rank outsider will be Robin Uthappa, who has been off the radar for a few months now.

Uthappa has scores of 94 and 76 in the Challenger here; Raina and Kohli have the luxury of good outings in Sri Lanka to fall back on, and that brings the focus onto the remaining three.

Two matches into the tournament, only Rohit Sharma stands out with a dazzling show — the India Red batsman smashed a match-turning 117-run knock against India Green on Friday on a difficult Barabati Stadium wicket.

In contrast, Badrinath and Yuvraj, who failed to shine with the bat in the Lanka series, have flopped here as well, thus giving Sharma the edge. While the Mumbaikar also had a forgettable outing in the island, he appears to have made amends just when it matters the most. "Well, this century is the best knock of my career so far. It's special, because it helped my team win from a difficult situation," said Sharma. Badrinath looked out of sorts with knocks of 10 and 25 balls while Yuvraj scored just six in one match.

Badri, however, maintains things aren't that bad. "I got starts in both the matches. In the second match, I would have carried on any other day and finished the chase," he asserts.

Heading: Lukewarm response to Red Cross Diwali mela in Panchkula - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Cops unleash fury on teachers - Indian Express
Content:
The Diwali mela organised by the District Red Cross in Sector 5, that concluded today received a lukewarm response. While residents attributed this to the less number of stalls put up this year, officials of the Red Cross, said they were satisfied with the response.

"We did go to the mela but did not find anything attractive or worth purchasing. Efforts should be made to put up stalls which have both quality and variety," said Monika Verma, a resident of Sector 4. Similar sentiments were echoed by another visitor, Rohit Kaushik, a resident of Sector 21. He said that he had come to the mela thinking it would be good in comparison to the last year, but did not find anything special.

Officials of the Red Cross, meanwhile, were satisfied with the response. Talking to Newsline, an official of Red Cross said: "Though the response was less than what was expected, but it was better than the previous years."

Heading: ... torture granthi in case of mistaken identity in Tarn Taran - Indian Express
Content:
Teachers claim they were targeted for blackening posters of CM, Sukhbir in Bathinda

The Muktsar police today reportedly went on a rampage to give a severe thrashing to agitating computer teachers, who were heading towards Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal's house in Badal village from Lambi.

Though the exact information about the number of injured and quantum of injuries could not be ascertained till the filing of this report, many were believed to have sustained injuries ranging from minor to fractures. To escape the onslaught of the police, the agitators ran for cover in all possible directions. While some managed to hop on to public transport, others took the field route to escape.

The police chased the agitators for as long as over five kilometres and even smashed the windowpanes of buses and vehicles in which the agitators tried to escape to avoid the police fury.

Agitators alleged that even as women police personnel had been deployed, it were the male cops who targeted the women teachers. Those spearheading the agitation alleged that they were targeted because they had blackened posters bearing photographs of Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal and SAD chief Sukhbir Badal while registering their protest in Bathinda a few days back.

"I suspect it was a deliberate move to target the protesters in such a fashion," alleged Computer Teacher Union president Gurvinder Singh.

"We had planned a peaceful protest. We were told by officials that the CM would visit his native village on October 31 and we had planned to continue with our peaceful protest till then. But, suddenly one of the police officers deployed at the protest site received a phone call, after which we were told to move away in a harsh tone. The protesters then tried to breach the barrier put up at Kheowali. At this, the police unleashed its fury, launching a mix of lathicharge, water cannons, teargas shells and stone pelting," alleged Gurvinder, who also sustained injuries due to the lathicharge.

"I was being taken for a treatment in a vehicle when a stone hit me on my nose. The chasing cops even hit moving vehicles with canes, even as women sitting inside pleaded with them to stop," alleged Tejinder Kaur, a computer teacher.

"One of the cops hit me on the back with a cane, while we were taking fellow colleagues for first aid," claimed Harpreet Kaur, a computer teacher from Tarn Taran.

"It was all barbaric. The police used every inhuman technique in the book to target peacefully agitating teachers," lamented Gurpinder Singh, the Gurdaspur district president of the union.

As per reports pouring in, a number of the injured agitators returned home after receiving first aid from different private hospitals. "Everyone ran for cover. Now, they are converging at their respective districts," claimed Ferozepur district union chief Harjit Singh.

When contacted, Muktsar SSP Gurpreet Singh Gill said, "Why had they (computer teachers) come here in the first place when they were clearly told that it was the private residence of the CM and if they wanted to register a protest, they should go to the official residence of the CM at Chandigarh." He added that it were the protesters who "crossed the limits". "They were totally adamant and created a nuisance. They even went to the extent of pulling the belts of the women police personnel deployed there," said Gill, denying that any of the women teachers were beaten up by the male cops.

"Rather, they have injured our police force. A gunman sustained a head injury, an SP received an ankle injury and a DSP's right shoulder got injured," claimed Gill.

Heading: Deregulate public buses, Khangura urges Badal - Indian Express
Content:
Guilty SHO, ASI suspended

In yet another case of high-handedness by men in khaki, the Tarn Taran police tortured an innocent Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) granthi, Balwinder Singh, last night in police custody. Apparently mistaking Balwinder Singh for a drug smuggler, the cops picked up the granthi of Baba Budha Sahib Gurdwara from his residence at Madi Udoke village and tortured him.

Admitted to the primary health centre at Sur Singh, Balwinder said he was taken by surprise when a police party arrived at his residence late in the evening and took him to Khalra police station, where he was tortured in the presence of SHO Kamaljit Singh and ASI Kuljit Singh. "They beat me up. They pulled my hair and asked me to strip. They then also used a roller on my legs," alleged Balwinder.

Sarwan Singh, Balwinder's brother, condemned the police for torturing a baptised Sikh. "We have brought the matter to the notice of higher SGPC authorities. They would take up the matter

with senior police officials," he said.

When contacted, SP (HQ) Rachhpal Singh Ghuman said both SHO Kamaljit Singh and ASI Kuljit Singh had been suspended. "They had got a tip-off that some person identified as Balwinder Singh was involved in smuggling of drugs. Without verifying the facts, they took the granthi to the police station and used force on him," said Ghuman, adding that he had visited the police station on getting information of

the incident.

SSP H.S. Chahal, when contacted, said the matter had been brought to his notice and they had suspended both the guilty cops for beating up an innocent citizen. He said a further probe was on and they would take suitable action against the police personnel after a detailed inquiry by a SP-level officer.

Heading: Guruta Gaddi: Date imbroglio forgotten, Makkar, Badal headed for Nanded - Indian Express
Content:
Jasbir Singh Khangura, Congress MLA from Qila Raipur, has shot off a letter to Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, asking him to deregulate public bus service as a Diwali gift to Punjab.

The letter states, "Punjabis have suffered far longer than necessary due to deficient public transport. It appears that till date public transport policy has largely been set to protect the interests of operators and not the travelling public.''

"The stench of corruption permeates the entire system — from the grant of route permits to the draconian regulations applied arbitrarily on some operators by the department, whilst concurrently allowing other operators to go scot free. Politicians and bureaucrats have consequently prospered immeasurably. In response to my Vidhan Sabha question querying the consolidation of the bus industry in Punjab since the formation of your government, your Transport Minister replied that no such consolidation had taken place,'' the letter states.

It is further alleged in the letter, "Yet this answer is fully refuted by most Punjabis, especially in Malwa, where select operators dominate in a manner designed to maximally hurt PRTC and Punjab Roadways. Not that I wish to cast any aspersions on you or your family, but the common man would welcome a full disclosure by you on this issue that your family's bus transport interests have not grown at all during this administration, individually or in cooperation with other private operators and also that the actions of private bus operators in Punjab have not harmed the financial interests of Punjab Roadways or PRTC.''

"You can also settle all doubts once and for all by delicensing all public transport so that buses and mini-buses can ply on any route within Punjab without a permit. There can be no better Diwali gift for the people of Punjab,'' it adds.

Heading: Young farmer taps the sap from floriculture - Indian Express
Content:
Makkar already at Hazur Sahib, says SGPC 'contributing to event's success'

With just a few days to go for the Guru-ta-Gaddi Diwas celebrations planned at Hazur Sahib at Nanded in Maharashtra on October 30, there is a huge rush of devotees headed for Hazur Sahib. Community members from all over the world are set to assemble for the mega event, marking the 300th anniversary of Gurudom to Guru Granth Sahib in 1708.

With the magnitude of celebrations in Nanded promising to be bigger and better that the one organised by the SGPC on October 20, the Sikh body has come under criticism from certain quarters for not organising any prominent function to mark the event. The SGPC was content with just one small function at Talwandi Sabo in Bathinda, where the participation of the devotees was minimal and pandals were seen half empty. "I am amazed that the SGPC has not organised any function in Amritsar to mark the celebrations," said Dal Khalsa general secretary Kanwarpal Singh.

This controversy stems from the fact that the Sikh community has been divided over the date of the celebrations. The SGPC, Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee headed by Paramjit Singh Sarna, Damdami Taksal and American Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee are already done with their functions to mark the occasion as per the Nanakshahi Calendar on October 20, but as per the Bikrami calendar, the celebrations are being planned on October 30.

Interestingly, despite differing on the dates, Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) chief Avtar Singh Makkar reached Nanded today. He told ENS on phone that he was overwhelmed by the response of the devotees. "The religious fervour is appreciable. People from all over the globe are assembling at Hazur Sahib, which is wearing a festive look," he said, adding that the SGPC, along with various kar sewa babas, has been contributing to make the event a success. Even Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal would be taking his team of party leaders and ministers to Nanded to participate in the religious functions.

Meanwhile, a caravan of buses with hundreds of NRIs left for Nanded from here last week. "I am waiting for the flight booking that is being arranged by Indian Airlines, promising a direct Amritsar-Delhi-Nanded flight on October 29," said Harpal Singh, a devotee.

However, such is the rush that most of the 385-member Sikh jatha from Pakistan that arrived in India through the Attari border on Saturday could not leave for Nanded today due to non-availability of seats in the Sachkhand Express. The train is fully booked for the next fortnight and devotees are relying on flight bookings.

There was also some resentment in SGPC circles when members were not allotted the number of rooms earlier promised to them by Sachkhand Hazur Sahib Management Committee, responsible for the arrangements. "The SGPC had to cancel the booking of some trains due to this," said a top SGPC functionary, though confessing that this has not dampened the spirits of devotees to the Sikh shrine.

Heading: Himachal confidential - Indian Express
Content:
While agriculture diversification in Punjab may not have been very successful on a larger scale, it is bearing great fruit at individual level.

Ravi Inder Singh (23), who graduated in electric engineering last year, chose farming as a profession rather than sweating it out in some office. While a major part of his 100 acres are under paddy-wheat rotation, this young farmer is also into floriculture. "Last year we had grown flowers for a leading flower grower of the state. While I learned a lot, the financial returns were not very good. But this year, I have decided to go solo," says Ravi Inder.

After an initial struggle to locate flower importers, he has finally struck gold and is now exporting flower seeds to a firm based in Holland. The variety of seeds include calendula, antrium, poppy and allysum rose, to name a few. Ravi Inder is also flooded with orders for sunflower seeds. "For this I have roped in my uncle and a few local farmers. I have orders for more than six tonnes of sunflowers for this year," he says.

Confident about his returns, he says, "We earn around Rs 20,000 per acre from rice and wheat. In case of flower seeds, my returns will be around Rs 50,000-Rs 2 lakh per acre, while from sunflowers I can earn Rs 1 lakh per acre."

The enthusiastic farmer is quick to add, "The best part is that we do not need much area for this enterprise. For the first year I am shifting just about eight to 10 acres under flowers, which I will later increase."

His argument in favour of floriculture makes sense. "In present times, even the assured crop is becoming a headache to sell. We have been sowing basmati varieties RH 10, PUSA 1121, Muchaal and others. The rates for these paddy varieties were very good till almost two years back, but this year rates for RH 10 have dipped to Rs 880 per quintal. I did not sell a single sack and have it all stacked up in my godowns."

Balwinder Singh Sidhu, Director, Agriculture, agrees that floriculture is one sector where Punjab farmers can explore. "It is a high-risk enterprise, but farmers who can afford to take risks should try and grow flowers," says Sidhu, adding, "The state government is also considering ironing out hurdles like release of export subsidy in time or reducing freight costs."

Heading: State’s CFL scheme finally sees light - Indian Express
Content:
Vigilance Bureau and health care

It seems the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau in Himachal is having problems in handling cases involving persons from senior administrative services and the politicians. After burning its fingers in the Singhi Ram's case —who remained in the hospital during his arrest, things did not work out in the case of Subhash Ahluwalia. The Vigilance Chief I D Bhandari had to face an exit from the post. A senior IPS officer was heard telling a fellow officer, " I think the government should setup pecialised hospitals for all those who require urgent health care after their arrests by the Vigilance Bureau."

Jungle boys

Himachal's forest department, unable to check illegal fellings, was exploring the idea of setting-up forest thanas. The department also wanted forest conservators to be given powers of commissioners to remove forest encroachments. However, they were in for a surprise before the proposal could be put in back and white. An IAS officer, posted as secretary (forests) was given additional charge of commissioner, Kangra division, leaving the forest officers lobby red faced.

CM makes Vajpayee happy

Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal has earned appreciation of former PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Few days back Vajpayee wrote a letter to Dhumal expressing his happiness over the BJP government's performance chart. What actually moved Vajpayee was Dhumal's proposal on strategic Manali-Leh railway line. " The Himachal CM deserves my appreciations as he thought of an issue which is of national significance," Vajpayee wrote.

Duty comes first

Himachal may not be in the election mode this November but IAS officers are going to have gruelling days ahead. Nearly two dozen bureaucrats from the state have been picked up by the EC for their duties as poll observers in different states, including J&K, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan and MP. Those going to militancy hit parts of Kashmir or naxal-affected Chattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh are particularly a worried lot . "It is the call of duty and not an issue of absolute choice," said one.

Heading: Better facilities for farmers - Indian Express
Content:
Himachal Pradesh's ambitious energy saving scheme—- Atal Bijli Bachat Yojana, designed to provide 72 lakh CFL bulbs to all domestic consumers free of cost, is set to roll from next month.

Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board (HPSEB) has decided to place its first order for 40 lakh CFL bulbs of 0.85 Power Factor (PF).

R K Jain, Chairman of HPSEB told The Indian Express that offers have been sent to the lowest bidders for supply of the bulbs. "If the company responds to the rates approved by the Board, orders will be placed," he said, speaking over phone from Delhi.

According to sources, HPL Socomec will get the first contract of 10 lakh bulbs, which the company will be required to supply in a pack of four blubs each. The company had quoted a rate of Rs 396 for pack of four but after negotiations the rate was brought down to Rs 387.

This is also the rate which the company had quoted against earlier tenders. HPL Socomec had raised objections against the rival companies earlier chosen for the supply orders.

Since state's Chief Secretary Asha Swaroop was entrusted with the job to make sure that no new controversy was created, HPSEB even extended the dates for tenders twice to ensure participation of HPL-Socomec, which was given Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) certification few days before finalisation of the tenders.

The company does not have the capacity to supply 72 lakh CFL bulbs of 0.85 PF by December 25, therefore, HPSEB has decided to send offers for nearly 6.3 lakh bulbs to Phoenix Lamps, which quoted the next lowest rates. "A senior HPSEB official informed me about the offer over the phone yesterday but I am not aware of the details yet," said Pawan Sharma, General Manager of Phoenix Lamps.

Sharma regretted losing the bid to a company which had submitted BIS certificate at the fag end and only after date for tenders was extended. " We really wonder how all this happened," he said.

The HPSEB officials said, "By extending the tender dates we managed to break the cartel formed by some companies. It helped the board to get HPL- Socomec at the lowest rates."

Five companies, instead of four earlier selected, had qualified for the supply orders this time.

The surprise being the HPL Socomec, which was earlier disqualified as it did not have the BIS certificate. Other companies in the race include Asian, Surya bulbs, Phoenix Lamps and Havells.

Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal, who had launched the scheme, said, " The government has tried to ensure full transparency in the matter. This an innovative scheme and no other state government has done this."

Heading: Steel processing unit for Nahan - Indian Express
Content:
The state government is committed to ensure better marketing facilities for the farmers and fruit growers in the state, said Govind Singh Thakur, BJP MLA. He was addressing the agriculture awareness training camp organised by Agriculture Produce Marketing Committee (APMC), Kullu and Lahaul and Spiti, at Chounri Bihal, four kilometers from here today. He said Rs 2.03 crore would be spent on the construction of marketing yards, kisan bhawan, grading hall and auction platform in Kullu District. At Chounri Bihal a sum of Rs 1.28 crore would be spent for the construction of auction platform and kisan bhawan, while a grading hall would be built at Patlikuhal at a costof Rs 15 lakh.

Rs 18.9 lakh would be spent on the construction of shops and office at Patlikuhal. A sum of Rs 16.5 lakh would be spent on the construction of office complex at Kullu besides the construction of staff quarters at a cost of Rs 25.50 lakh. Thakur said that the proposed infrastructure would ensure the smooth and expeditious marketing of fruits and vegetables in the Kullu valley.

Heading: ‘Spilt reward money in two parts to ensure total sanitation’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Board of Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL) in a meeting held at Delhi accorded approval for the installation of Steel

Processing Unit (SPU) at Nahan at a cost of Rs 100 crore which would provide employment to more than 2,000 people.

In a statement issued today, with the original copy of approval of SPU, the state Lok Janshakati Party (LJP) Chairman and former MLA Sada Nand Chauhan said the land has been purchased by SAIL at Shambhuwala, about 10 kilometers from here, on Nahan-Paonta road.

He said that if state government extended its support, the foundation stone could be laid by Union Steel Minister and National LJP Chairman Ram Vilas Paswan in the first week of November.

The establishment of SPU at Nahan would provide employment opportunities to the locals, similar to what private industries at Kala-Amb and Paonta sahib did for youths of adjoining states. The locals said though the state government imposed many conditions for providing 70 per cent jobs to Himachalis but they did not implement them strictly.

Heading: Hooda rejects Sukhbir’s claim on Chandigarh - Indian Express
Content:
Encouraged by the response of the local community and panchayats in implementation of the community-led rural sanitation (CLTS) campaign, the Centre is considering a proposal to stagger the reward money under Nirmal Gram Puraskar in two equal installments.

Currently, a reward of Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 lakh is given to panchayats which achieve the status of total sanitation and are open defecation free (ODF). The last ceremony was held at Hisar, where 3,209 village sarpanchs were given rewarded by President Pratibha Patil.

World Bank's fund Water and Sanitation Programme (WSP) has been providing active support in implementing the

CLTS programme. The Centre has proposed strict norms to ensure that all villages, which have already achieved Nirmal Gram status, do not relapse.

One of the step proposed, a senior official at the department of drinking water supply (Ministry of Rural Development) said, is to stagger the reward money in two equal instalments. The first instalment will be released immediately but the panchayat will remain under close watch. The second instalment will be handed over only if the panchayat sustains its status for at least one year.

"If the panchayat falls back, or is unable to carry forward the drive, it will lose the status and may also be asked to return the money. This would help in motivating the villagers and sustaining the drive," said the official.

At a regional sanitation conclave, held in Delhi last week, as a prelude to Third South Asian Conference on Sanitation (SACOSAN), officials from Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Orissa and Uttar Pradesh focused on steps for the sustainability of the total sanitation drive.

R N Batta, Director of Rural Development in Himachal Pradesh, who held the two-day conclave, said efforts are afoot to integrate the drive with other programmes implemented by the government. "We are working to co-relate the rural sanitation with development and social change," he added.

Captain Jindu Ram, pradhan of Khanror-an award winning panchayat, was also invited by the WSP at Delhi conclave to give his first hand experience about the achievement. In Himachal, 267 panchayats have already achieved the status of total sanitation.

Besides the Nirmal Gram Puraskar, which Himachal panchayats have received recently, the state government has also introduced three awards of Rs 10 lakh, Rs five lakh and two lakh.

Heading: Haryana seeks Rs 600 cr to boost agriculture - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana CM Bhupinder Singh Hooda today rejected Sukhbir Badal's claim on Chandigarh, which the Shiromani Akali Dal president had recently made. Talking to mediapersons on the sidelines of the 48th Founders Day celebrations of the Punjab Public School, Nabha, Hooda said Chandigarh is the capital of both Punjab and Haryana and one state cannot stake its claim on the city.

Hooda's reaction follows Sukhbir Badal' recent claim to Chandigarh, who had said that if the NDA comes to power at the Centre, the SAD would help Punjab get back its "complete rights" over the capital city.

Asked about the demand for separate Sikh Gurdwara management committee for Haryana, he said the government has formed a committee headed by State Agriculture Minister A S Chatha, following the demand of Haryana Sikhs. "Let the committee submit its report," he said. He reiterated that a separate management committee will be formed if the Chatha committee recommends.

Punjab government and the SGPC had raised a hue and cry over the issue recently and had sought intervention by the PM, after which the committee was formed. Clearing doubts, Hooda also said Haryana will give its share for the construction of international airport at Chandigarh. He, refused to comment on the Hansi-Butana canal, as the matter is sub-judice.

A grant of Rs 11 lakh was announced by Hooda for the school. Lt Gen T K Saproo GoC-in-C, Western Command, an alumnus of the school, gave away prizes to the students.

Heading: Draft plan ready to make Gurgaon jam-free - Indian Express
Content:
Looking to pump more money into the agriculture sector, Haryana government has asked for allocation of Rs 800 crore to the state from the Planning Commission. Sources in the state government said they are hopeful of getting the amount asked for under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY).

The demand was put forth by Haryana Chief Secretary Dharam Vir at a meeting of the chief secretaries of all states held in Delhi, where the deputy chairman of Planning Commission, Montek Singh Ahluwalia, was also present. Earlier, the Centre had made a tentative allocation of Rs 74 crore to Haryana for integrated development of food crops, agriculture mechanisation, improving soil health & productivity and development of rain-fed farming systems.

The government has also sought increase in the subsidy on the sprinkler irrigation systems from the current 50 per cent to 75 per cent. Incidentally, the quality of underground water in Haryana has gone from bad to worse. According to a study, as much as 54 per cent of the undergound water in the state is brackish.

Fresh water too is depleting fast and not much has been done to replenish ground water. The depletion of ground water table is the main reason why the state government is looking to encourage diversification in the crop pattern. Funds for reclamation of saline soil have also been sought.

The state government also brought to the notice of the Planning Commission the expenditure incurred on power subsidy and irrigation. It made a request for inclusion of the expenditure on power subsidy and expenditure in the criteria for eligibility to get funds under the scheme.

A 50 per cent subsidy is being provided to farmers in the state on the price of hybrid seeds of various vegetables under the National Agriculture Development Scheme. The seeds are available on the sale counters of district cooperative societies and HAFED.

Heading: ‘Integrated agriculture is the way ahead’ - Indian Express
Content:
In a move that could provide relief to the people of Gurgaon from the frequent traffic jams in the region, the state government has mooted a plan for smooth movement of traffic and a engaged a consultant - Urban Mass Transit Company- for the purpose.

The company has conducted a survey and presented the draft of 'Integrated mobility plan for Gurgaon-Manesar urban complex' on Saturday. Director, Town and Country Planning, S S Dhillon, also saw the powerpoint presentation of the draft. Suggestions for improvement in the mobility plan have been invited from local officers, which are to be submitted by November 10. A similar plan is being prepared by the same company for Faridabad too.

The company has prepared short, medium and long-term mobility plans for Gurgaon, divided into three phases. As per the proposed draft plan, the first phase is from 2008 to 2011, the second from 2011 to 2017 and the third phase is from 2017 to 2021.

Dhillon said the population of Gurgaon was expected to go up to 43 lakh by 2021 and by 2031, 59 lakh people were estimated to be employed in the city. He said these factors had been taken into account while preparing the plan.

In the plan, ongoing projects, including laying of metro corridor upto Sushant Lok and construction of three peripheral roads, besides the KMP Expressway, were also highlighted. The government also has a proposal to ply 100 buses exclusively for Gurgaon.

Heading: ‘Efficient tubewells can save 25 pc energy’ - Indian Express
Content:
In View of the numerous challenges facing agriculture production in the country, Haryana Agricultural University Vice-Chancellor, Dr J C Katyal, called upon farm scientists to do action research based on the feedback given by farmers and provide them real-time advisory and technologies.

They should try and ensure that farming becomes productive, profitable and sustainable, Dr Katyal said, after distributing certificates to the participants of the refresher course on integrated farming system, organised by the Academy of Agricultural Research and Education Management (AAREM), HAU.

He also emphasised that farmers must integrate livestock, horticulture and vegetable production with crop production as this practice would provide them get relief from economic losses caused by natural calamities and insect attacks. He appealed to agricultural universities to set up model farms to exhibit this integrated form of agriculture.

A course compendium and a CD were also launched on the occasion. Former director of extension education at HAU and course director, Dr R K Malik, also said that crop production is risky and farmers need alternatives to avoid the risk of crop failure due to natural calamities.

Heading: Caught in the festive rush, city grapples with traffic woes - Indian Express
Content: Haryana has the potential to save 25 to 30 per cent of the energy used in the agriculture sector by making the existing tubewell system energy efficient. This was said on Sunday by Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam MD Vijayendra Kumar, who added that 170 lakh units of electricity can be saved on daily basis by making the tubewells energy efficient by upto 20 per cent. "Setting up a new generating unit to produce the number of units that we can save this way requires a an expenditure of Rs 600 crore," he said.He emphasised upon the need to use electrical gadgets star-rated by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) and equipment approved by the Bureau of Indian Standard (BIS).

Heading: It is not rhetoric, elders’ supervision is a must to prevent mishaps, say doctors - Indian Express
Content:
The perennial problem of inadequate parking space has only intensified with the festive season.

With vehicles parked haphazardly at all junctures, the traffic police have their job cut out in maintaining a smooth flow of traffic.

"The parking lots are full. They are catering to vehicles beyond their capacities. The vehicles keep coming. Where do we accommodate them?" said a traffic policeman deployed at the Sector-19 market.

He added, "People surely cannot park their vehicles two kilometres away from the marketplace."

For the authorities, meanwhile, it is the vehicles parked on roadsides that are causing the chaos. The problem is at its peak during the evening hours in Sectors 34, 35, 17, 18, 19, 22 and 15.

"We are towing away vehicles parked on roadsides in the strictly prohibited areas. At some places, policemen are even allowing parking of vehicles in the no-parking zones to avoid chaos," said DSP (Traffic) J S Cheema.

There are various points along the Madhya Marg where traffic moves at snail's pace.

These points include: Government Press lightpoint, bus stand roundabout, traffic area lightpoints, Grain Market roundabout, Kissan Bhawan roundabout and Piccadily lightpoint.

Superintendent of Police (Traffic) H S Doon maintained they are trying their best to manage the traffic.

"It is courtesy the efforts of the traffic police that traffic does not come to a standstill. The city has more vehicles than the space available in the parking lots," said Doon.

He further added, "We advise people not to park their vehicles at wrong places and listen to the traffic policemen posted at the parking areas."

Advisory by Traffic Police

* People should prefer public mode of transport to go out.

* Avoid taking vehicles to market places near residences.

* Go for shopping, preferably during the day.

* Obey traffic officials on duty.

Heading: Consumer courts in city see a sharp rise in miscellaneous complaints - Indian Express
Content:
Eleven-year-old Ajay and 50-year-old Naresh Kumar unknowingly share something common — they had spent last Diwali not with their loved ones but in the hospital with bandaged eye after being hit by a firecracker.

While Ajay was hurt while trying to light a cracker, Naresh was an unsuspecting victim — standing in his balcony and enjoying the Diwali verve when a rocket hit his eye.

Ajay's parents, residents of Gharaunda, say they first took him to a local doctor, who then referred the case to the PGI. "We spent the whole Diwali night in the hospital. It was traumatic," the family says.

With the Festival of Lights round the corner, celebrations at homes like theirs would come with an optimum amount of caution.

That parent's supervision is not mere a rhetoric spelled by the doctors before every season but a thought worth paying attention to was aptly learnt by Gurmeet Singh last year. A resident of Ropar, Singh's eye was damaged after it was hit by a cracker burst by his own children at their home.

"Last year, four patients lost the vision in one of their eyes. That is the extent of damage that careless playing with crackers can do to anyone. We keep people informed and provide them timely care, but the awareness regarding perils of reckless celebrations has to be very high," said a doctor at PGI.

Dr Rajan Chugh, an ophthalmologist with Fortis Hospital, says playing without a proper supervision can spell doom.

"What's sad is the fact that every year the same number of people become the victims regardless of the awareness drives. Chandigarh still is fairly aware about the need of parental supervision and the safety norms required for a safe Diwali but a large number of patients arrive in the city from the surrounding areas. In most of the cases, we find that the children became the victims because no elder was supervising them while they were bursting crackers."

Heading: After decades of isolation, India can now carry out nuclear trade - Indian Express
Content:
A revolution of a different kind has swept the city's consumer courts. Amongst all the basic category cases defined by the forums, there is an unprecedented rise in the miscellaneous category — a group that covers a varied strata of consumer complaints clearly set apart from the basics.

This directly points to the fact that apart from the basic categories i.e. banking, medical, telephone, insurance, housing, electricity, airlines and railways, a large number of consumers are coming to courts with complaints against educational institutes, courier companies, post offices, defective mobiles or electronic providers, food contamination, travel agency, pest control companies and even against a plumber for not completing the work properly.

The two UT district forums have jointly witnessed 34,738 cases being filed since its inception. Of this, a total of 30,316 are under the miscellaneous category. The UT State Commission, which caters to appeals and direct complaints claiming compensation of over Rs 20 lakh, has witnessed 9,147 cases since inception. Here also, the others category has witnessed a total of 5,707 cases, the maximum of all.

In the well-defined categories, cases of insurance rule the roost at 1,664. Time and again, the consumer forum has been issuing instructions to insurance companies not to repudiate righteous claims on flimsy grounds. They have also been recently applying for punitive damages if the insurance company prepares a false ground or document to justify themselves.

Next in line are the complaints related to the banking sector. The consumer forum received 865 such complaints. Complaints against telecom companies are at 514 while cases of medical negligence have mounted to 166.

Officials at the consumer court say that contrary to the last decade, when the forum merely witnessed cases related to banks and insurance, more and more complaints against unfair trade practices, pest control companies, courier companies, biscuit companies and against coaching institutes are being witnessed.

In September this year, a resident of Sector 49, Harjinder Pal Singh, was awarded a compensation of Rs 25,000 after he moved the forum alleging a packet of Bector biscuits was 100 grams underweight.

The dealers of a water filter in Sector 45, New Milan Associates, were also directed to refund the amount of a defective water filter while it was in the warranty period. A courier company, Deep Seed Express, was also directed to pay Rs 90,000 compensation after they failed to deliver a consignment to the NRI son of a complainant.

A Mohali resident, Gurmeet Singh, was also awarded a compensation of Rs 25,000 after he was dissatisfied with the services of a plumber. "All this is attributed to the increased consumer awareness, now people from all quarters and different walks of life approach the forum. Consumer is the king in today's era and it's a different revolution of a kind," says advocate Deepak Aggarwal.

Heading: PU list of nominated Senate members out - Indian Express
Content:
In view of political uncertainty, intransigent Leftists, an unfavourable opposition and strident criticism from certain international quarters, not many people gave the Indo-US nuclear deal much of a chance.

But a display of resolute approach by the Prime Minister during the confidence vote at Lok Sabha and his astute diplomacy at Vienna ensured that India's ostracism from the international nuclear club and a concomitant failure to harness nuclear energy for civilian use (due to sanctions imposed after 1974) came to an end.

There have been strong reactions after the signing of the deal. In terming this agreement as a 'sell out' of the country's interest, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is only living up to the image of a 'typical opposition'. Their criticism doesn't cut much ice, because the ground work on this deal was done during the time of the NDA government.

As for the Left, one need not be highly discerning to guess that their 'dagger-drawn' approach stems from their inveterate dislike of the United States, rather

than any cogent reservations about the deal itself.

The true endorsement has come from India's top scientists, technologists, economists and diplomats who have given their unequivocal approval to this agreement. Their enthusiasm stems from the anticipation that the deal will facilitate the full use of the latent potential of high-tech sunrise industries, like IT pharma and biotech, as well as strategically important sectors like defence, space and power.

Considering that the scope for gains is immense, the discomfort of traditional rivals like China and Pakistan over this deal is understandable.

Whether the nuclear deal will snowball into a vital issue in the forthcoming state assembly and Lok Sabha elections remains to be seen, but it is imperative that the ruling UPA government explains in clear terms as to what extent the accord has the potential of changing the lives of the Indians. The people of the country need to be told that after decades of isolation, India is now permitted to carry out nuclear trade and commerce in the global arena.

The bogeys of the NPT and the CTBT have been dropped. India has abided by the 'no first-use principle' and has all along emphasised that the use of nuclear power will be purely for civil and economic purposes.

Apprehensions that the country's security concerns have been compromised with are unsubstantiated. The deal clearly specifies that if the geo-political situation worsens to such an extent, that it is strategically important for India to conduct a test, it is entitled to do so.

There would be no sanctions in that case. Even if sanctions are imposed, there is nothing to be paranoid about. India had, anyways, faced sanctions after the 1974 and 1998 nuclear tests.

There is no reason why, in the compelling interest of national security, we cannot bear it again. That, however, is a remote situation and it is not appropriate that irrelevant fears about a hypothetical situation should deprive us of the immense gains that India stands to make at present.

Heading: ‘There is a growing discontent in the CRPF’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Panjab University, on Sunday, released the list of the nominated fellows of the Senate for the term November 1, 2008, to October 31, 2012.

While a total of 36 members will constitute the senate, for the first time a non-teaching employee has also been included in the list.

The prominent names include: V K Sibal, senior advocate, Punjab and Haryana High Court, Satya Pal Jain, Professor Shelley Walia, Pawan Kumar Bansal, Dr K K Talwar, Dr Ravi Kumar Gupta, Peter D'Souza, Professor Ram Rajput, Professor R P Bambah, Professor Radha Kumar, Dr Ishwar Dayal Guar, H S Lucky, Dr K S Aulakh and Professor M Shakeel Ahmed among others.

Professor R C Sobti, vice-chancellor of the University, said, "We have a non-teaching member in the Senate for the first time. Dharam Pal's name was recommended by nine non-teaching unions to be included in the list. Both Professor Ronki Ram, President, Panjab University Teachers' Union and Dharam Pal are ex-officio members who will have a term of one year."

Talking about the visit by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), Sobti said, "The NAAC members have assessed the university. While the positive points of the university are worth highlighting, the authorities will try to bring in changes as suggested by the committee."

He further added, "I will try to execute the recommendations that are within my capacity. I do not completely agree or disagree with the committee's observations. The university's welfare has to be kept in mind before implementing any decision."

Heading: Panchkula braces up for Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
'The CRPF is deployed without the concept of 'Peace Posting' and 'Hard Posting', as is followed in the Army. The officers here are moved from one area to another without being given any break, unlike their counterparts in the Army'

Like the Army, the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has also done a commendable job in curtailing terrorism in various parts of the country. Unfortunately, very few of us are aware of the sacrifices made by them while safeguarding the integrity of the nation. The role and achievements of the force are not projected in the manner it should be done.

The CRPF has been deployed in the terrorist and naxalite affected areas. Now, most parts of Jammu and Kashmir are with the CRPF for counter insurgency operations (CI Ops).

The CRPF has almost replaced the Indian Army in the valley and has been launching successful counter insurgency operations. They are, however, being denied various allowances — Highly Active Field Areas, CI Ops in Forward Areas and High Altitude Allowances — which the Armed Forces were entitled to while serving in the Valley

There is growing discontent in the CRPF as their services, which are nothing less than the ones rendered by the Armed Forces, are being ignored.

The CRPF are deployed without the concepts of 'Peace Posting' and 'Hard Posting', which is followed in the Army.

The officers here are moved from one operation area to another without being given any break, unlike their counterparts in the Army.

Due to adverse conditions, most of the CRPF personnel suffer from job stress, frustration and depression. Figures reveal that the cases of physical and mental stress, suicide and fratricides are on the rise because these personnel serve in the 'Hard Areas' without any respite or peace tenure.

The troops are always deployed in far-flung areas and mostly live in subhuman conditions. Their salaries do not commensurate with the work they do. Their family problems, therefore, gets aggravated due to the financial crunch.

We are unable to understand the recommendation that there is no need of Suraksha Sahayaks (bodyguards) with the paramilitary force officials.

There is a constant threat to the life of these officers. Both the police and the Army officials, operating in naxalite areas, have been allowed to keep bodyguards but CRPF officials are denied the same. What kind of justice is this?

Even after the force has lost several lives in dealing with militancy, they are not treated with due respect.

No doubt, the Army has brought the situation under control in the Valley. Now, the CRPF has been entrusted with the task of ensuring peace and it is as difficult a role as the one the Army had played.

We should pay homage to all the CRPF personnel who have laid their lives for the country and should not forget their sacrifices.

Heading: Negligent doctors to pay Rs 2 lakh for loss of life - Indian Express
Content:
As the festival of lights draws near, authorities in Panchkula have geared up to ensure a safe Diwali.

While the Health department is ready with its staff to meet any eventuality, the police department too has geared up with its force to prevent any untoward incident.

"We are all set for the D-day and will have doctors available throughout night in case of any emergency.

Special arrangements have also been made for surgery, eye and burn cases, which are at a high on that day, so that we are able to handle every eventuality," said a doctor at the General Hospital.

The police department, meanwhile, will set up special checkposts throughout the night along with independent patrolling.

A senior police officer said that they have also called the force from other towns to ensure a safe Diwali for residents.

Heading: Tricity has nothing ‘to-let’ to single, working women - Indian Express
Content:
Holding a charitable hospital responsible for depriving a four-day infant of his mother after the woman died following a caesarean operation, the Punjab State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed Guru Nanak Mission Hospital, Urapar, Nawanshahar to pay Rs 2 lakh as compensation to the child. Two doctors — Dr Munish Kansal of Kansal Hospital and Maternity Home in Nawanshahar and Dr Parminder Kaur of Guru Nanak Mission Hospital in Nawanshahar — have been directed to pay the compensation jointly.

Justice S N Aggarwal said, "No amount is sufficient to compensate the loss of human life. Grant of compensation is a small consolation, a little financial help to a family which is thrown abruptly in different circumstances."

The complainant, Harbhajanjit Singh, a resident of Thammanwal village in Jalandhar, said in his complaint that he married Sunita Rani, a resident of Urapar village. She went to stay with her parents after getting pregnant.

She was medically examined by Dr Parminder Kaur, who told her that she would need a caesarean for the delivery. She had an arrangement with Dr Munish Kansal of Kansal Hospital and Maternity Home and was told that it would cost Rs 15,000.

Sunita Rani was admitted in the hospital on August 8, 2002. The caesarean was conducted and a male child was born.

It was further pleaded that on August 11, 2002, the condition of Sunita Rani worsened while she was still in the hospital. The doctors told her husband that she would need a second surgery. It was alleged that Dr Parminder Kaur and Dr Munish Kansal tried to stop her bleeding by applying additional stitches in a callous manner without anesthesia. The stitches were also given in the most unhygienic conditions. The request of the complainant to refer Sunita Rani to some other hospital also fell on deaf ears. She was then sent to the maternity home of Dr Munish Kansal but there too, the blood flow could not be controlled, after which, Sunita breathed her last.

In his reply, Dr Parminder Kaur pleaded that the patient was handled by a midwife prior to being treated by them.

The Commission ruled that instead of taking the patient lightly, the doctors should have given some serious thought to her deteriorating condition. "Normal treatment was given in a situation which called for radical treatment urgently. It is clear that the patient was not rendered proper post-operation care," said Justice S N Aggarwal.

The commission also held that it is the son who is the real sufferer as he lost his mother while the father has remarried. Of the Rs 2 lakh to be paid as compensation, 75 per cent will be deposited by the father in the name of the minor, Harshpreet Singh, which can be withdrawn after he turns a major," the Commission added.

Heading: Cn & heard - Indian Express
Content:
After initiating an IT boom in the region and bringing about a radical transformation in the lifestyle — Chandigarh — the city that registered the highest per capita income for the fifth time in a row this year, is still biased when it comes to renting house to single working women. The adjoining cities of Mohali and Panchkula too fall in the same league.

Such is the condition that the search for a place to live, leaves the working unmarried women who come from other neighbouring areas, disappointed.

"Even after searching for nearly two months, I could not find an accommodation for myself. I even took the help of property dealers, but that served no purpose. Finally, I had to move in with a colleague," says Parmeet Kaur, an employee of Dell International Services in Mohali.

Although the Rajiv Gandhi Chandigarh Technology Park has drawn various Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) units in both Chandigarh and Mohali, when it comes to renting homes to an unmarried woman, there is a strong denial.

"Not only in Chandigarh, but in Panchkula and Mohali too, the residents are very apprehensive about renting homes to single women, especially those who are working. I was recently approached by two women employed in an IT company. They wanted a two-room house. When I took them to a house in the Mansa Devi Complex in Panchkula, the owner said he would not rent out to single working women," says Vikas Sharma, a property consultant.

Meanwhile, the trend of keeping paying guests is now gaining ground in Mohali and Panchkula.

"I have been keeping girl students as paying guests since the last six years. I do not rent my house to working women intentionally as the sense of responsibility and accountability is more towards them," says Meenakshi Khurana, a resident of Sector 20.

"The situation is very bad when it comes to finding a decent place to live in the tricity. The residents are ready to rent out their house to men, whether working or not, but are biased when it comes to females," laments Banita Thakur, a college lecturer in Chandigarh.

Heading: The lawyer’s less glamourous - Indian Express
Content:
Grapevine is abuzz with reports that Punjab state Vigilance is keeping an eye on who is receiving gifts from whom this Diwali. The state's bureaucracy is, therefore, vigilant and jittery about receiving these greetings in kind from their well wishers. In fact, gifts are slightly out of favour this festive season. The overall gloom in the economy isn't making people very happy and at a time when companies are struggling to pay salaries, shelving out money for expensive gifts is a tall order. The gift exchange custom received a further jolt when two ministers of the state cabinet, Manpreet Badal and Laxmi Kanta Chawla 'appealed' to their officers, to not to accept gifts. 

Popular politicians

Sardonic wit of former Punjab DGP KPS Gill was at display again at a recent press interaction. When asked as to why has he given such a difficult Persian (Tehrek-e-Watan- Parastan) name to his new found organisation, he replied that these days, the mere mention of Persian names conjures up images of terrorist organisations, so he wanted something positive to be associated with it. Similarly, while contrasting the famous politicians of the past with those of the present, he said, "Men like Nehru were illustrious and enjoyed a lot of popularity. Today's politicians are also popular albeit in a different manner. They are so popular that the mere mention of their names provokes spontaneous laughter from us." 

Not bygone yet...

Garrulous commentator Ravi Shastri committed a faux pas during the presentation ceremony which followed Indian team's victory over the Australians in the recently concluded test match at Mohali. While welcoming General SF Rodrigues (Retd), Shastri described him as ex-Governor of Punjab. The realisation dawned upon him soon enough and Shastri apologised at the end of the ceremony by admitting to his inadvertent error. 

Christmas in buses 

On the face of it, there are hardly any similarities between a bus conductor and a Santa Claus. But these days, bus conductors are distributing toffees just like Saint Nicholas. But this disbursement isn't goaded by some festive spirit. It has to do with the same privation that till now afflicted the corner kirana shop i.e. paucity of coins. Either the low denomination coins are in abysmally short supply or our transport corporations have entered into some synergy with confectionery companies, passengers inevitably get toffees. The time is certainly ripe for an elaborate freakonomic research- Affect of sales on confectionery companies in India due to low circulation of coins by the RBI. 

Ageless wonder 

They say a woman is as old as she looks and a man is as old as he feels. But what about the age of a client who is being represented by a geriatric but unprepared advocate in front of a stern judge? Sample this — During the recent proceedings in one of the cases, where an old advocate was seeking acquittal for an accused charged with murder, the judge asked him about his age. The confused advocated mumbled a reply, "30, 35, 40, 50, 55...My Lord". A visibly irritated judge snapped, " I did not ask the age of his entire family". The mortified advocate came up with another gem, "I meant he must be between 30 to 55 years old My Lord." To which, the judge replied, " Your client seems to have taken a rebirth after this murder".

Festivals forever 

Government employees in the tricity are having a blast with the month of October filled with festivals which essentially means a long spell of holidays. While there are some who haven't returned to office since Karva Chauth, there are others who are planning to enjoy a week-long Diwali. Some unlisted holidays have added to the festivity. Meanwhile, those visiting the offices for getting work done receive a standard reply — ab toh diwali ke baad hi saab milenge. Let the festive spirit thrive!

Heading: Party Pack! - Indian Express
Content:
"Many look up to the black coat as a sign of glamour and prestige. Yes, the prestige is there, but glamour? I wouldn't say that," says Advocate Gagan Aggarwal as he takes us through his daily routine.

An early morning riser, he reaches his office in Sector 15 at 8 am. The time-constraint means a quick breakfast and some quick reading of the day's newspapers.

Before we ask him about his family, he shoots: "I hardly get to spend even five minutes with them in the morning. I feel really sad about it but then, work is work. We do have the satisfaction that I am not working in another city."

Once in office, he studies the court cases, does the necessary paperwork and attends his clients

"This is one time when I am available to them as they come with their problems, seeking advice and telling me about the development," explains Gagan.

A practitioner at both the District Court and the High Court, the lawyer heads for the court around 9.30 am.

Here, his time is usually spent "rushing from one court to another. We (lawyers) are always climbing stairs or getting off them. Work apart, it is a good exercise and keeps us fit," remarks Gagan.

Some clients follow him even to the courts. "People come with different cases. Some have family disputes while others may be involved in accidents."

He adds, "A lawyer shares a personal relationship with his clients because they generally meet him at a critical point in their lives. As a result, they are not merely clients, because we build a very humane rapport with them. One has to be patient."

Gagan is also the general secretary, Lawyers for Human Rights, an NGO.

At 2 pm, it is time for lunch with a group of friends, who rarely get to spend time other than the brief encounters during court hours.

Between 4 and 5 pm, Gagan is busy with his paperwork again, updating the diary. At 6 in the evening, he is back to office attending clients till 9 pm.
