India is a stakeholder in improving Afghanistan's socio-economic growth prospects and in the stabilisation of its security situation. This for reasons of both India's own security requirements and the responsibility to assist meaningfully in its neighbourhood. For its people who conduct themselves in difficult conditions, care and compensation are long overdue.

Heading: No new districts in Himachal - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: 2 dead, 1 critical as truck overturns on NH-73 - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has no immediate plans for creating new districts in Himachal Pradesh, a move that remained a hot issue in the earlier Congress government and now Bhartiya Janata Party.

Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal said he was in favour of rationalisation of some tehsils, development blocks and sub-divisions. The move will be restricted to strike a uniformity with assembly constituencies and local administrative units. Dhumal's remarks holds significance in view of the reports that Dhumal was considering the move on reorganisation of districts.

The CM said he had observed that some of the assembly constituencies are spilt in one or two sub-divisions or teshils, while few constituencies do not have even one tehsil . "Now after delimitation of the constituencies, there is a need to reorganise and rationalise some of the local administrative units," he said, putting an end to speculations about new districts.

During his earlier tenure as chief minister, Dhumal had initiated a move to upgrade the status of some of the key sub-divisions. But the move did not pay much results to the BJP. Rather, it created serious heartburn among some of the left-out areas.

Heading: Man accused of raping minor escapes police custody - Indian Express
Content:
Two persons died and one was seriously injured after a truck (HP-12-A7999) lost control and overturned on Ramgarh road (NH-73) late on Monday evening.

The deceased were identified as Mukesh Kumar and Lalit, both aged 27. Lalit's father Kamlesh, 50, was seriously injured in the accident. They were the residents of village Madanpur in Sector 26.

While Lalit was declared brought dead, Mukesh died at General Hospital in Panchkula.

"My husband ran a meat shop in Sector 26 on the highway. Eyewitnesses told me that a truck coming from the side of Ramgarh road lost control, overturned and hit the shop," Mukesh's wife Anita said. Eyewitnesses said the front tyre of the truck burst, causing it to lose control.

A local resident told Newsline that Kamlesh and Lalit had come from their native town in Uttar Pradesh on Sunday.

The truck driver fled from the spot after the incident. Police have impounded the vehicle and registered a case.

Heading: HC rejects Sood’s plea to quash FIR on land grab - Indian Express
Content:
Three Mohali cops, including SHO, suspended, face departmental inquiry

A man, accused of raping his 16-year-old niece, escaped from the custody of the Mohali police on Sunday, following which three policemen were suspended on Monday evening. Gurwinder Singh is in his early 20's and his wife, Balwinder Kaur, is a Home Guard volunteer posted at Sector 36 police station in Chandigarh.

Station House Officer (SHO) Tarlochan Singh, Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Manjit Singh and a sentry at Mataur police station in Mohali faced action for not only keeping Gurwinder, a resident of Phase 3-A here, in 'illegal custody' but 'letting him escape' from the police station.

Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Jatinder Singh Aulakh, who issued the suspension orders with immediate effect, told Newsline that departmental inquiry will be initiated against the suspended policemen while the order to post a new SHO at Mataur police station would be issued later.

The suspended SHO claimed that Gurwinder had come to the police station on his own on Sunday. The police were waiting for the medical examination report of the victim before formally arresting him, the time gap within which he disappeared.

Since Mataur police station, which is temporarily housed at the community centre in Sector 70, lacks lock-ups to keep criminals, Gurwinder, as was the case with others, was asked to sit on the bench. After sitting for 20-25 minutes, he told the policemen that he wanted to go to the toilet and escaped.

Gurwinder is a taxi driver and was later booked for allegedly raping the daughter of his wife's sister.

Mataur SHO, who was the investigation officer before being suspended, told Newsline that the victim is a Class X student at a private school in Chandigarh. She, along with her younger sister and brother, was left in an orphanage in Sector 16, Panchkula, years ago following the death of their parents.

Around three years ago, Balwinder, in her mid-30s, had married Gurwinder and adopted the victim from the orphanage. This was her second marriage.

In her statement, the minor girl told the police that the incident occurred on Friday evening. After her uncle returned home, she served him dinner and went to the bedroom with their 2-year-old son. Soon after, Gurwinder followed her, bolted the bedroom's door from inside and made sexual advances towards her. When she resisted, he allegedly thrashed her before raping her and fled from the spot. He allegedly threatened her with dire consequences if she told anyone about the incident.

A case under Sections 376 and 506 of the IPC was lodged against Gurwinder on Saturday and the victim was medically examined.

Second time guilty

This is the second time in past nine months when Gurwinder was booked on same charges and on the complaint of same victim. In January, the victim had accused Gurwinder of rape but both the parties had reached a mutual compromise during the trial, following which Gurwinder was absolved of the charges.

Heading: You are in safe hands today - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another blow to the alleged efforts of the accused to hush up the Kansal village land deal, a single bench of the Punjab and Haryana High Court headed by Justice Sham Sunder dismissed a petition seeking quashing of an FIR filed in 1999.

Puran Singh, a resident of village Kansal, had filed a complaint in 1998 with the then Punjab financial commissioner Shamma Maan alleging grabbing of his land through forged signatures.

After an inquiry by the Joint Collector (Majri), FIR No. 168 was registered at the police station in Mohali on October 13, 1999, on charges of forgery and cheating against Randhir Sood, a property dealer and Darshan Singh, the then Naib Tehsildar (Majri) and one Sonam Kumar.

Incidentally, Sonam's address in Ferozepur was the same address which, at the time of offence, belonged to former Punjab governor general BKN Chhibber's parents-in-law. General Chhibber's son Sonum Chhibber has also been questioned in this regard by Mohali Deputy Commissioner.

The Mohali police have, till date, not done anything substantial in the entire case despite being pulled up by the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

In 2007, when the then Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court, while hearing a Public Interest Litigation pertaining to grabbing of village common land (shamlat land), summoned the status report on the said FIR, Sood filed a petition seeking quashing of the said FIR stating he had reached a compromise with the complainant.

The fact that the status report on the said FIR has already been summoned by another bench in the court was concealed while filing the quashing petition.

As the accused named in the FIR are considered high-profile and well-connected, the Punjab police allegedly did not initiate any action for more than six years. When the Punjab and Haryana High Court directed it in 2004 to file the status report on the said FIR before the court at Kharar, the Punjab Police instead opted to file a cancellation report. However, the Kharar court refused to accept it and ordered re-investigation.

The Punjab police still remain in a deep slumber.

In December 2007, Justice VK Jain, the then Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court, took a strong note of 'pseudo' names used by Chhibber allegedly with the objective of securing a piece of land in village Kansal registered in his name.

Justice Jain (now retired) had also asked the state of Punjab as to what action they have taken against Sonum Chhibber.

In January this year, the Mohali Deputy Commissioner summoned Chhibber to explain his alleged involvement in the entire case, to which he feigned ignorance and denied having any involvement in the case.

The forged land-deals, which are also the basis of the FIR, bear his pictures as one of the buyers and his maternal grandparents' address.

Heading: Mohali court complex will house offices only - Indian Express
Content:
'Another residential site in the vicinity of the complex will be shortlisted shortly'

The District Administrative and Court Complex (DACC) in Mohali will come up without residential complex, if the latest development turns practical. A 13-acre site in Sector 76 has been found "suitable" for housing the official complex of the district civil, police and judicial officers. The decision was taken at the High Court Building Committee meeting held recently, Deputy Commissioner Rahul Bhandari said on Monday.

Bhandari said that according to the preliminary sketch prepared by the Punjab Chief Architect, at least 13 acres was required for setting up the administrative and court complex. "For making provisions of residential accommodation, some other site in the vicinity of the official complex will be selected," said Bhandari.

The selected site owned by the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) is part of the 34 acre chunk of prime land recently vacated by the Radha Soami Satsang Beas (RSSB) from its allotted chunk of 200 acres on the southern side in exchange of regularisation of its encroachment on 34 acres on northern side of Sector 76.

While almost 10 acres of the vacated 34 acres were to be allotted by the GMADA to six cooperative house building societies, which were awaiting land allotted to them in 2004 for construction of multi-storeyed flats in Mohali, almost 13 acres was expected to be left vacant after making provisions of roads and other public utilities.

The GMADA was still awaiting any proposal or request to consider allotment of land for the DACC. "If any of our sites suits our requirements, let the competent authority moves us with a proposal," said GMADA Chief Administrator Vivek Partap Singh.

On this, Bhandari said: "After receiving High Court Building Committee meeting proceedings, the Home department and Administration will move the GMADA for land allotment."

After abandoning four sites earlier earmarked and recommended for the DACC, four new sites were recently shortlisted for the "much delayed" project. In the absence of the DACC, the district civil, police and judicial officials lack permanent official and residential accommodation.

While the district civil and police wings are temporarily working from the old building of the Punjab School Education Board in Phase I, the district judicial courts are working from a community centre in Phase 3B1. Also, some community centres are occupied to house Police Lines and a police station.

Even the deadline fixed by former Punjab and Haryana High Court Chief Justice Vijender Jain to earmark the site has expired but the state government was yet to take the call. A 22-acre site in Saneta village and another 3.83 acres in Sector 62 were earlier earmarked for the DACC but due to certain reasons, both these sites were rejected. Later, two another sites in Barmajra and Balongi villages were recommended but they were also not approved by the state government.

Former Chief Minister Captain Amarinder Singh had laid foundation stone of the complex in Sector 62 while inaugurating the Mohali district on April 14, 2006. Ironically, even the foundation stone has gone missing from the site. The 3.83 acres in Sector 62 site was abandoned as it was "insufficient" in view of the High Court Building Committee norms, which requires at least 16 acres exclusively for the court complex.

The decision was taken at the High Court Building Committee meeting held recently, Deputy Commissioner Rahul Bhandari said on Monday.

Bhandari said that according to the preliminary sketch prepared by the Punjab Chief Architect, at least 13 acres was required for setting up the administrative and court complex. "For making provisions of residential accommodation, some other site in the vicinity of the official complex will be selected," said Bhandari.

The selected site owned by the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) is part of the 34 acre chunk of prime land recently vacated by the Radha Soami Satsang Beas (RSSB) from its allotted chunk of 200 acres on the southern side in exchange of regularisation of its encroachment on 34 acres on northern side of Sector 76.

While almost 10 acres of the vacated 34 acres were to be allotted by the GMADA to six cooperative house building societies, which were awaiting land allotted to them in 2004 for construction of multi-storeyed flats in Mohali, almost 13 acres was expected to be left vacant after making provisions of roads and other public utilities.

The GMADA was still awaiting any proposal or request to consider allotment of land for the DACC. "If any of our sites suits our requirements, let the competent authority moves us with a proposal," said GMADA Chief Administrator Vivek Partap Singh.

On this, Bhandari said: "After receiving High Court Building Committee meeting proceedings, the Home department and Administration will move the GMADA for land allotment."

After abandoning four sites earlier earmarked and recommended for the DACC, four new sites were recently shortlisted for the "much delayed" project. In the absence of the DACC, the district civil, police and judicial officials lack permanent official and residential accommodation.

While the district civil and police wings are temporarily working from the old building of the Punjab School Education Board in Phase I, the district judicial courts are working from a community centre in Phase 3B1. Also, some community centres are occupied to house Police Lines and a police station.

Even the deadline fixed by former Punjab and Haryana High Court Chief Justice Vijender Jain to earmark the site has expired but the state government was yet to take the call. A 22-acre site in Saneta village and another 3.83 acres in Sector 62 were earlier earmarked for the DACC but due to certain reasons, both these sites were rejected. Later, two another sites in Barmajra and Balongi villages were recommended but they were also not approved by the state government.

Former Chief Minister Captain Amarinder Singh had laid foundation stone of the complex in Sector 62 while inaugurating the Mohali district on April 14, 2006. Ironically, even the foundation stone has gone missing from the site. The 3.83 acres in Sector 62 site was abandoned as it was "insufficient" in view of the High Court Building Committee norms, which requires at least 16 acres exclusively for the court complex.

Heading: It’s official, Mohali is number 2 in state on the dengue radar - Indian Express
Content:
Professor Prati Pal Singh of the National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER) in Mohali has been awarded the Indo-European Union (Indo-EU) FP7 research project.

The research project, New Approaches to Target Tuberculosis (TB), primarily aims at the discovery of new anti-tuberculosis drugs, especially for those patients causing bugs, which are resistant to commonly used anti-TB drugs, says Professor Singh, the investigator incharge of the project.

The project has been funded in collaboration with five European laboratories after a stiff competition, stated a press release issued today.

NIPER has identified TB new drug discovery research as a thrust area and has discovered and patented several new anti-TB molecules. Some basic innate immune mechanisms have also been studied and published which will go a long way in treating the most complicated latent stages of TB bacilli.

Additionally, an entirely different class of drugs, an opiate, has been found to treat TB in animals. With the massive funding from the project, TB researches will get a major boost at NIPER, and very exciting findings, novel drugs and specifically trained scientists and students are expected out this project.

Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the bacteria that causes TB, has been reported in 9,000 year old skeletons. Nearly one-third of the world's population carries TB bacilli, and one in ten of these people will develop TB.

TB kills 1.6 million people per year, 4, 400 people per day and every twenty seconds one person dies of TB. The problem of drug resistance in TB is compounded with the emergence of extensively drug-resistant TB that is virtually untreatable.

In India, an estimated two million new cases and half-a-million TB deaths occur annually, which translates into approximately 1,000 deaths per day.

India's estimated TB burden stands at well above US $ 3 billion per year. TB is curable; however, the lengthy treatment is very difficult and at times not available. Almost all the anti-TB drugs were discovered more than 50 years ago and no new drug has become available in Past 30 years.

Without any new discovery of faster-reacting, safe, simpler and affordable drugs, the TB situation may turn from bad to worse, and if immediate actions are not taken, science may even fail society, expert opine.

Heading: Youth stabbed after tiff - Indian Express
Content:
The high number of dengue cases recently recorded in Mohali has taken the city to the second place in the list of the most dengue-hit city in Punjab, just behind Ludhiana, said Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare, Vijay Kain in Mohali, at a meeting on Monday.

Chairing a special meeting to take stock of the alarming situation, Kain pulled up the local civic and health officials for their failure to control the spread of dengue fever, which he confirmed, has claimed 3 lives and left 171 suffering in the city so far.

Kain called for an explanation as to why the spread of dengue has not been checked despite the tall claims of the local officials of taking the necessary preventive steps.

He directed the civic and health officials to step up cleanliness and fogging operations in the area and clear such places, which have turned into mosquito hotbeds, leading to the spread of dengue.

Mohali Civil Surgeon Avtar Singh intimated Kain that as many as 13,824 houses have been surveyed in the district and mosquito hotbeds, in most of the places, have been cleared.

Heading: Shop, gorge, indulge yourself: It’s Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
A 22-year-old youth was stabbed on Monday with a bottle outside a liquor vend in Manimajra. The victim has been identified as Tasleen Ahmed of Manimajra. Doctors attending to him stated his condition to be serious.

Police said Tasleen alongwith his two friends had gone to a tavern in Manimajra. Deepak Kumar (40), a property dealer, was consuming liquor there. "Suddenly both of them started quarrelling over some issue. The owner of the tavern asked them to leave the place immediately. Tasleen came out of the tavern. Deepak followed him with a bottle and smashed it on his head before stabbing him on his stomach," police said.

Eyewitnesses said Kumar attempted to escape from the spot but was caught by some truck drivers sitting nearby. The police immediately reached the spot and rushed the victim to the PGIMER. Police have registered a case of attempt to murder under Section 307 of the IPC against Deepak Kumar and arrested him. Tasleen is a painter in the motor market in Manimajra.

The accused was medically tested and found to be under the influence of liquor.

The owner of the liquor vend also allegedly tried to destroy evidence by pouring water on the floor outside the vend where the incident took place. Police said they will take action against the owner after investigating the matter.

Heading: Police step up patrolling in city, highways ahead of festival - Indian Express
Content:
Visitor makes Diwali brighter for many

In a gesture reflecting the warmth and affection of the festive season, Rashida Raza from Lahore donated blood at the Rotary & Blood bank Society Resource Centre in Sector 37 on Saturday. Rashida was in the city with her husband to attend the Sangeet Sammelan, Indian National Theatre's annual festival of music. She returned to Pakistan on Sunday. "Rashida is a housewife and made an impromptu decision to donate blood when she heard of the shortage of blood for dengue patients in the tricity," said Kanta

Saroop Krishen, president of the Blood Bank Society. "All of us were overwhelmed by the spirit of compassion she displayed."

"Both Rashida and her husband, Kasim Raza, are fond of classical music. As his wife donated blood, Kasim went around proudly, filming the entire event on his handycam," she said.

Police launch special search operation ahead of Diwali

Keeping in view the festive season, the Chandigarh police launched a special search operation in Burail village to trace and nab miscreants and anti-social elements for three hours, starting at 5 am. About 100 police personnel were deployed in the cordon and search operation, which was upervised by the Deputy Superintendent of Police (Operations) and training.

CRPF personnel and Punjab police commandos cordoned off the entire area. 17 search parties of south division each consisting of one NGO officer and two other ranks were constituted for the operation.

The police rounded up 12 suspects and issued stranger rolls for 12 other persons.

All were let off later in the day after verification.

To maintain the law and order situation in the city, the police have set up 40 nakas in various parts of the city. Each exit point in the city was sealed and the personnel checked vehicles entering the city.

Special teams have been constituted to keep vigil on crowded places like markets and cinema halls.

A special joint checking with PCR staff, traffic police and paramilitary personnel was carried out ate in the night.

Heading: Fire for crackers tame as sales plummet despite rampant illegal business in city, suburbs - Indian Express
Content:
As part of the heightened security measures on the eve of Diwali, the Mohali district police have launched a special anti-sabotage drive to check the activities of anti-social elements in the entire district.

A special vigil is being maintained at all the bus stands, railway stations, dhabas and restaurants across the district, said Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Jatinder Singh Aulakh.

"We have tied up with the Chandigarh Police to ensure security on entry and exit points, sharing boundaries with Mohali and Chandigarh," disclosed the SSP.

Aulakh added that the police patrolling has been stepped up on all the State and National Highways passing through the district and the suspected terrorist hideouts are also being constantly monitored.

PCR vehicles, equipped with wireless sets and sophisticated weapons, have been deputed on round-the-clock duty, revealed the SSP.

The border checkpoints in the district have been strengthened and all the outgoing and incoming vehicles are being screened. A co-ordination is being maintained with the state and central intelligence agencies, added the SSP.

The district police have urged residents to follow the guidelines and precautions on fire safety norms to avert any untoward incident during the bursting and display of fireworks.

"Light your home with joy, not with flames of sorrow," concluded Aulakh.

Heading: Shoppers beat inflation, pack city markets - Indian Express
Content:
The sale of crackers in Mohali, Kharar and Kurali has hit a low on the eve of Diwali. Lack of interest among public, mainly children, and strict guidelines issued by the district administration are being seen as the main reasons behind the present situation.

"With the continuous decrease in sale and profit over the past few years, this time we decided not to sell crackers at our shop," said Amit Kumar, a merchant in Kharar.

Poonam, a resident of Mohali and a wholesale dealer, said that strict specifications framed by the authorities have prompted her not to keep crackers on sale in her shop. While the number of retailers has gone down by nearly 50 per cent this time, the situation for wholesalers also generates little optimism, if any.

"Besides the decrease in the commission given by manufacturing companies, the low sales have severely affected our business," says a Kurali-based wholesale firecracker dealer Harish Kumar while adding that for the first time, they had offered discounts on their cash sales.

Earlier, only a few shopkeepers were allowed to sell crackers from permanent shops after obtaining permission from the district Administration. For the past few years, however, small vendors have joined the business selling the potentially dangerous crackers in each and every corner of the district without any requisite permission.

Despite the low sales of fire crackers and stern orders issued by the District Administration, the illegal sale and storage of firecrackers continues unabated. This comes as a threat to the densely-populated areas, where the business continues unabated.

While the district Administration had specified the sites for selling permitted crackers, no one had put up any stalls courtesy the authorities concerned, who allegedly turned a blind eye to the blatant violation of rules prescribed under the Explosives Act.

A wholesale cracker merchant, carrying out his business illegally, said he is not afraid of any "trouble" as such business dealings were being carried out only with regular customers.

Interestingly, the wholesale and retail cracker sellers, who were issued with licences, mandatory for the purpose of carrying out business at the specified places, have put up stalls in the narrow and busy markets. Also, none of them have taken any precautionary arrangements, as prescribed by the district Administration. Apart from a fire service in Mohali, the district has no other arrangements to control the situation incase of a fire breakout. Most markets, in which the majority of the cracker sellers operate, are too narrow to allow fire tenders to move in case of emergency.

DC SPEAKS

"I have asked the SSP to ensure strict compliance of the prohibitory orders so that no untoward incident takes place. The SSP has assured me to press into action his SPs and DSPs to check the illegal sale of crackers," said Deputy Commissioner Rahul Bhandari.

Heading: ‘The sky should be the limit for such imaginative designs’ - Indian Express
Content:
The district markets were thronged with city residents on the eve of Diwali on Monday as customers were lured with heavy discounts and incentives.

Packed in impressive gift wraps, the bandwidth of sought after items was huge: clothes, crackers, dry fruits, chocolates, jelly candles and sweets among others.

On the 'sweets' front, laddoos, kaju barfis and mixed mithai boxes were the runaway winners. However, the overall sales of sweets recorded a decline compared to previous years.

While most temples and gurdwaras were lit up since Sunday night, one could still find electronic lights being installed till Monday evening.

The maximum rush was witnessed at shops selling electronic goods, greeting cards, gift items, utensils and toys.

While cracker sales failed to register a seasonal boom, alcohol sales rose by over 50 per cent, with premium brands leading the sales chart.

Heading: Industrial area will get good roads, streetlights soon, says home secretary - Indian Express
Content:
There was a time when the growth rate of Chandigarh was slow. The time has, however, come for that growth rate to be accelerated. The reason could be any: the people, the Administration, overall growth rate of the country, growth at the international level or the recognition the city has gained in the international arena.

We are all aware that Chandigarh was perceived as a human body by Le Corbusier — Capitol complex in Sector 1 being the head, City Centre in Sector 17 being the heart and Panjab University and Industrial Area as the left and right limbs with the network of roads serving as the arteries.

If any part of the growing body starts to decay, remedial measures need to be taken.

The Industrial Area of Chandigarh is beginning to decay. Consequentially, the Administration decided on a Conversion Policy for the industrial plots. While one mall has come up in the area, it has been subjected to severe criticism for lack of proper parking among other things.

There is no doubt the malls have created parking problems but such issues need to be tackled. Compare the number of citizens going to the area then and now?

The Industrial Area has started to vibrate.

The Conversion Policy is primarily going to benefit the Administration and the proprietors of the malls. These malls, however, should not be mere money making propositions.

Let the malls organise for fully computerised, air-conditioned hi-tech public transport to ferry people from various sectors to the malls. The malls could charge extra money for the facility.

The Administration can develop the area as a recreational zone by developing parks, water sports and opening good eating joints.

The entire area needs a preplanned, preconceived and comprehensive plan that has to be monitored at the level of the Administration. The sky should be the limit for such imaginative designs.

Money should be invested for the development of public transport and recreational facilities. Travelling in such hi-tech public transport and a visit to this area shall, in the times to come, become a status symbol.

Let the Administration make significant publicity in this connection. Not using personal transport will save on fuel, pollution, congestion on the roads and also help us, in a humble way, to contribute towards the slogan "Go green".

Heading: Over 156 CCTVs at 20 crossings, three markets by January 31 - Indian Express
Content:
Civic amenities in Industrial Area will be improved by providing better roads and streetlights for the convenience of traders. The assurance was given by Home Secretary Ram Niwas during a meeting regarding the development of infrastructure in the industrial areas today.

Members of the committee included Finance Secretary, Chandigarh Housing Board chairman, Municipal Corporation commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Chief Engineer (UT),

Chief Engineer Housing Board, Chief Engineer

Municipal Corporation, Chief Architect and Director of Industries.

The prominent industrial associations of the city were also invited to present their viewpoints.

The presidents of the industrial associations put forth various issues of erratic power supply, subway connectivity of Industrial Area Phase-I with Phase II, changes in the building bylaws, parking space and removal of encroachments.

After discussion with officers of the concerned departments, the home secretary issued directions to take immediate steps on all the pending issues.

He laid special emphasis on the repair of internal roads of Industrial Area and development of civic infrastructures such as widening and maintenance of internal roads and streetlights.

Heading: Bharat Electronics Limited to develop aircraft gadget on behalf of CSIO - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Administration has finally invited tenders for the installation of close-circuit television cameras (CCTVs), which will be installed at 20 roundabouts and intersections, besides three busiest marketplace of the city by January 31. The final date of closing the tenders is fixed as November 3.

In all there would be 156 CCTV cameras installed at various locations, including 28 cameras at different places in Sector 17 market and 14 cameras each in Sector 22 and 35 markets, respectively.

In addition to these locations, five cameras each will be installed at 20 roundabouts and intersections identified by the police and the Chandigarh Administration. The total project cost is about Rs 5 crore. The funds, which were initially lying unused with the Chandigarh Police, were transferred to the account of the Chandigarh Administration's Engineering Wing in January this year.

Confirming the development, UT Chief Engineer Kishanjeet Singh said: "The CCTVs will be installed at all the locations by January 31, which is the deadline for completion of the project."

According to the officials of the Engineering department, the CCTV cameras will not only be used for monitoring the traffic flow on particular junctions, but will also play a vital role in preventing and detecting crime in the busy marketplace.

The cameras will also be utilised for the purpose of catching violators on the road, tracing the vehicles, which are involved in accidents and manage to escape from the spot, due to absence of policemen at certain points during odd-hours.

"The cameras at strategic locations in marketplace shall help us identifying the suspicious elements and would definitely lead to better monitoring," added a senior UT Police Official.

The Chandigarh Police, which initiated the project, before transferring the project to Administration's lap owing to lack of technical expertise, had already invited expression of interest from various multinational companies.

Certain companies had come forward expressing their interest to take up the project.

A team of the Chandigarh Administration's Engineering Wing had already discussed the concept with their counterparts in Delhi, before finally launching the tenders last week.

The entire concept plan with technical intricacies was also referred to the Chandigarh Police a few months back for their final scrutiny, to which the police had given a go-ahead in July this year.

Roundabouts, where the CCTVs will be installed

* Madhya Marg (Matka chowk; Press lightpoint; Transport lightpoint; Railway lightpoint; Sector 26 Grain market roundabout; Sector 7-8 roundabout)

* Dakshin Marg (Industrial Area Phase-I-II roundabout; Sector 20 gurudwara roundabout; Kisan Bhawan roundabout; Indian Express roundabout)

* 3BRD lightpoint; Aroma hotel lightpoint; Centra Mall lightpoint

* Jan Marg (Sector 22-23 lightpoint; Sector 16-17 lightpoint)

* Marketplace and parking areas of Sector 17, 22, 35

Heading: Woman dies of burns - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Scientific Instruments Organisation (CSIO) will transfer the complete technology of indigenously developed Head-Up Display (HUD) for the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) to Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) for production on Thursday. Union Minister of Science and Technology Kapil Sibal will be present on the occasion.

Dr Pawan Kapoor Director, CSIO, Chandigarh, while confirming the details on their 49th Foundation Day, said: "We have already conducted around 1,000 successful test flights of HUD with the LCA Tejas.

The HUD developed for LCA is quite perfect and on a par with imported HUDs. This promises to make the country self-reliant in HUD technology as one of the Line Relay Unit (LRU) of the aircraft, which as of now is being imported from countries like USA, Israel, UK costing more than Rs one crore each. The indigenously produced HUD would cost around Rs 50 lakh each."

The HUD system comprises a pilot display unit, processor and multi-functional upfront control panel. The HUD fitted in the cockpit of the aircraft displays primary flight and weapon aiming information on several modes in collimated form.

"This is projected with good quality of images in front of the pilot's eyes enabling him to view the information superimposed on his outside world view without having to change his line of sight through the bean combiner," director added.

Defence authorities have recently successfully test fired a missile fitted with the CSIO-developed HUD. Recently, HUD technology has been upgraded for night flying also as required by the Air Force. The Air Force has already given their acceptance to the CSIO-developed HUD.

CSIO officials engaged in the process said HUD forms an important part of the cockpit of the fighter pilot and its overall development is considered a challenging task.

"The design and development of the HUD involves multi disciplinary activities like optics, mechanical and electronics as well as high-end software implementation. The indigenous HUD is at par with the best HUDs available in the world," they added.

Heading: Babus enjoy an extended festive holiday - Indian Express
Content:
Asha Dandyan, 43, a resident of Sector 6 in Panchkula, died of 80 per cent burns under mysterious circumstances in the wee hours of Monday. Dandyan is wife of a city-based hotelier, Balbir Pal Dandyan, who owns Indian Palace Hotel in Manimajra and Maheshpur. Neighbours said there was a big fight last night after which the screams of the woman were heard.

"It was late at night around 10.30 pm that the woman was rushed to the General Hospital. She was then referred to PGI, where she died. According to the statement of Balbir Pal, his wife was cleaning the pooja ghar when she accidentally caught fire late last night," said a police official on condition of anonymity. Sources said Asha was Balbir's second wife and all the three children —- Sapna, Manu and Anu —- were her step children.

Sources said there were continuous conflicts in the family. "There was hardly any day when there were no fights in the family and it was only the daughter Sapna who was close to the woman. On Sunday night, a lot of noises were heard from the house and like every day there were fights over something. It was within few minutes that Sapna came running shouting for help for her mother. It was after that that the woman was rushed to the hospital in Sector 6. It was strange to notice that Balbir Pal did not go to the hospital," said a resident of the area on condition of anonymity.

The forensic team reached the spot. The police have registered a case on the statement of the family members. However, other angles are also being investigated.

Heading: PU Senate members nominated - Indian Express
Content:
While the Punjab Government offices wore a deserted look today, officials' strength in the Chandigarh Administration and Municipal Corporation offices was quite satisfactory. Despite being the first working day of the week, not many officers were present in their offices — thanks to the weekend, which will be followed by Diwali and Vishwakarma Day on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Many officegoers opted for a leave on Monday and managed a comfortable five-day vacation including the weekend (Saturday and Sunday) and two gazetted holidays (Tuesday and Wednesday).

Sources at the Punjab Civil Secretariat said that there were not many officials present in their cabins today. Even a visit to the Secretariat wore a deserted look, as even the parking lots, which is generally full of vehicles with red beacons, was almost empty.

The CISF guards posted on security duty at the gate of the Punjab Civil Secretariat said, "Since morning, merely a handful of officials have entered the Civil Secretariat. However, on any other normal day, even our schedule remains quite hectic as we have to open the barricades after every two or three minutes for giving way to the officials' vehicles."

A few of the officers, who chose to work today include Punjab Chief Secretary Ramesh Inder Singh, Principal Secretary (Home) Punjab Dr B C Gupta and Secretary Personnel Jasbir Singh Bir. The only officer working at the Punjab Chief Minister's office was OSD to CM, D S Mangat.

While Dr Gupta reached his office at 9.30 am and was busy clearing the files, the chief secretary was busy in some meeting at the Chief Minister's residence forenoon and came to his office in the afternoon.

On the other hand, the attendance was better at the Punjab Police Headquarters. In the Crime Wing only ADGP (Crime) J P Birdi was present as the IG (Crime) Parmod Kumar, DIG (Crime) B K Uppal were on leave and AIG (Crime) Gautam Cheema was out of station as he had to give witness in a case.

At the Municipal Corporation, Chandigarh, most of the officials including Municipal Commissioner as well as the Mayor were present in their offices. A large number of officials and other staff have been assigned duties for inspecting various markets in the city. The teams were on duty till the markets closed for the day. While the Mayor visited various wards for inspection, the Commissioner toured markets to check anomalies. Both were accompanied by officials.

At UT Secretariat, senior officials though remained busy in the official function of Administrator at Maloya, but were present in their offices later half of the day.

Heading: ‘Tech savvy’ municipal councillors fail to update official website - Indian Express
Content:
Members of the Panjab University Non-Teaching Employees Federation welcomed the nomination of the federation president in the university Senate.

This is the first time that a member of the federation has been nominated for the Senate.

The list of the nominated members was released on Sunday.

The members would be ordinary fellows of the Senate from November 1, 2008 to October 31, 2012.
