Heading: Coucillors, sarpanches to raise awareness about job schemes - Indian Express
Content:
The Municipal Corporation councillors might have raised a demand for laptops time and again or announced the decision to facilitate residents by accepting their complaints online. But the civic body has failed to upgrade its website.

Sample this — Mayor Pardeep Chhabra's term will be complete by the end of the year, but the list of sub-committees constituted by him has not been upgraded.

The committees that had been constituted by former Mayor Harjinder Kaur is what one gets to see while surfing through the official website of MC.

The website is looked after by the IT Department of the MC. The list of anomalies is quite long.

Further, the mobile number being used by Harjinder Kaur is listed as Chhabra's number. Meanwhile, the number being used by Chhabra is listed in front of Union Minister of State for Finance Pawan Kumar Bansal's name.

The officials had announced a decision of having the agenda of the House Meet and Finance and Contract Committee meeting as well as the minutes on the website. The aim was that the public has access to details of the work that the MC is undertaking and its progress. However, the home page of the website has not been upgraded since the 132 nd meeting of the House which was in August. The agenda or the minutes have not been updated since then.

The former Medical Officer of Health Dr G C Bansal was repatriated more than two months back. However, his name still figures in the list of officials. The website also needs to be upgraded where the details of the work done by MC are present. The new projects undertaken by the Municipal Corporation find no mention. An official of the corporation said that the website would be upgraded soon and the anomalies will be removed.

Heading: A Swish Set - Indian Express
Content:
The Municipal Corporation councillors and the sarpanches of different villages have been asked to spread awareness about the benefits available under the Swaran Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojna (SJSRY). This will be done in the nine villages around the city.

It was felt that the targeted beneficiaries of the scheme were not well informed about the provisions for them. The scheme is essentially forBPL families. The Municipal Corporation is running around 35 courses for the BPL families under SJSRY scheme with an aim of making them competent for self-employment.

These include computer applications, refrigeration, electric work, textile designing, tailoring, making soft toys, training programme for medical attendants. The task of starting the courses is taken up by the NGOs. Each batch lasts for six months. In the last financial year, more than 4,000 people were trained.

However, it was felt that the people were not aware about the facilities being provided. The issue was also discussed in the MC House. The councillors stated that the members of BPL families were not aware of the various schemes for them. They also found it difficult to avail the loans which they can get.

The villages that are being included are — Hallomajra, Burail, Attawa, Badheri, Butrela, Dhanas, Maloya, Dadumajra and Kajheri.

Heading: Lighten Up - Indian Express
Content:
Diwali brings a bright & sparkling make-over 'at home' for many in the city

All dolled up

Preetica Gill, Designer

It's a place she spends the most time in. It's Sector 35 based designer Preetica Gill's seven-year-old studio that sees her settle with clients, mostly prospective brides and churn out dazzling trousseaux wear for them. This year, Gill decided to do a makeover for her pad. "And I made sure it was well in time for Diwali," smiles the pretty Preetica who worked out a cheerful look for the space. So in came bright wall paints, some interesting cushions and a sparkling range of candles. "I heard everyone saying Diwali this year would be low-key because of the economic crisis, but I decided to add cheer by going all out with my studio," laughs Gill. That's the spirit!

Shower of light!

Dr Rajan Chugh, Laser Specialist

Diwali is the time my creative juices overflow and I get almost paranoid about flushing out the junk, clutter, dust and along with it the negative forces. But when it comes to a new look for the festival, it's experimenting with crazy lighting systems that get me started. This year, I have in place three types of light systems which are simply dramatic. Hidden lighting that throws light from all around and you can't see the source, fine neon lights and also dressy ones for the trees. It's a sparkling and cheerful effect, after all, the festival is all about light.

Spick & Span

Guneet Singh, Event Manager

What's Diwali without hectic spring cleaning, a fresh coat of paint, de-clutter days and a traditional look. So every Diwali, I follow all this like a ritual. Ganeshas and festive motifs are must-haves for me.

Homing in

Rashi Adlakha

My new home is our dream come true and we worked at a hectic pace to move in before Diwali, for we wanted to have the puja here and start a brand-new life on an auspicious note. It's been really hectic, and I had to take off from work to set it up, but we wanted everyone to wish us on Diwali in our new home and share our joy. Diyas, fresh flowers, rangolis, it's going to be a dressy and traditional affair.

Festive Flavour

Anshu Anand, Interior Designer

Diwali is all about colour, so be it a traditional home or contemporary ambience, a splash of it will bring out the festive flavour. For me, bright coloured cushions, ascent features like pedestal lamps, lots of floral arrangements work wonderfully. Basically anything to do with nature, for it makes one happy and the festival is all about joy. To bring in a novel look, I suggest we go in for beaten copper pieces, crystal bowls with floating candles and petals, vases with flower decorations and silver candle stands. Diwali marks the financial year too, so it will not be complete without Goddess Laxmi and Ganesha statue or mural. Finally, it's the look of the house from the exterior that catches the attention, so one can have a colourful rangoli in the driveway or entrance, hanging terracotta stuff and lotus ponds.

Heading: Warmth from the Valley - Indian Express
Content: The Lakme Fashion Week drew to a close on Friday. On a day when bad designs reigned supreme, Anuj Sharma emerged a winner with his "Knot for You" collection. The collection revolved around strategically placed knots that bound, shaped, draped and constructed his carefully tailored outfits. Effortlessly chic, he only made use of crepe and georgette. For a Grecian effect, the designer knotted the fabric to create versions of flowers or a butterfly-like effect and held the garments at the shoulders with the help of slim black ribbons. Meanwhile, the ensemble of the day went to Aneeth and Chinar of Gaba, who created some rustic magic with their khadi and handloom line. What we loved the most was a pair of loose pedal pushers in white teamed with a two-layered, smock, flowing green tunic with a white embroidered gamcha thrown around the bag. Nice. But thank god, the fashion weak is over.

Heading: AIE centres a boon for the children of migratory labour - Indian Express
Content:
This one is well-timed. With October on its way out and November stepping in, it's also time to bid goodbye to the summer sizzle. With winters not too far, the exhibition by the Jammu and Kashmir State Women Development Association has arrived in the city with a truckload of winter warmth. Leading the lineup are woollen shawls, stoles and suits. What's unmistakable all through is the fine handmade embroidery, also known as the crewel stitch that runs right through the work. With the workmanship coming in straight from the artisans, the prices are equally down to earth. You can bag yourself a pretty warm stole for as little as Rs 1,200 or a fully worked upon Pashmina for as much as Rs 7,000. Also finding their way in are unstitched embroidered suits and kurtis in a variety of fabrics - the woolen ones for peak winter to comfy cotton for summer. These are priced as low as Rs 550. At the exhibition you can also lay your hands on dry fruits such as almonds and walnuts brought in fresh from the Valley.

The exhibition is on at Bal Bhavan grounds, Sector 23 till November 3.

Heading: MOU signed for 775-MW Luhri hydel power project - Indian Express
Content:
Kangra district administration has opened an Alternate Innovative Education (AIE) centre on the premises of the Jwalamukhi temple at Jwalamukhi, for educating the children of migratory labour. This centre is proved to be a boon for these children, as they now get study instead of resorting to begging.

The district administration has decided to open two more such centres at Baijnath and Sansarpur Terrace near Pong Dam, under the centrally-sponsored Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) scheme. In the Jwalamukhi AIE centre, about 60 children of the labourers have been admitted and are getting education, said Mamta Chaudhary, Additional Deputy Commissioner, Kangra district. Among these, 50 are girls.

Some of these children use to beg outside the temple premises or loiter here and there, she said. The ADC said she visited the temple in March and found that some of children of migratory labour also resort to begging.

"I enquired about them from the Temple Officer and found that there are many such children who are not studying at all,'' said Chaudhary. She then asked the temple authorities and the District Project Officer of SSA to conduct a survey of such children.

The temple and the SSA officials met the parents at their work site and motivated them to send their children to the AIE centre being opened near the temple. "The parents of these children finally agreed to send their children to the centre," said Chaudhary. The 60 children studying here are in the age group of six to 14 years.

These children are being given free uniform, books and other reading and writing material, apart from meals. A permanent teacher has been appointed at the AIE centre, which was opened in June. The children are provided food from the community kitchen of the temple, and it is ensured that every child get proper food, Chaudhry said. It is also ensured that they attend school daily.

The ADC said one such AIE centre will be opened at Sansarpur Terrace near Pong Dam, where industrial units are situated. "Children of migratory labour working in these factories at Sansarpur are not getting an education. We will open a centre at Baijnath too," she added.

Heading: Infantry day celebrated - Indian Express
Content:
At Least four years after Satluj Jal Vidyut Nigam (SJVN) was allotted the 775 MW Luhri project, a downstream project on Satluj river, Himachal Pradesh government today signed the MOU for the execution of the project. The cost of the project is estimated at Rs 5,700 crore.

Along with Luhri, the Nigam also signed an MOU for the 40 MW Dhaulasidh project, the first hydel project to come up on Beas river, in chief minister Prem Kumar Dhumal's home district Hamirpur.

The MOUs were signed by HK Sharma, Chairman-Cum-Managing Director of the Nigam, with the state's Principal Secretary (Power) Ajay Mittal, in presence of the chief minister.

Himachal government will have 49 percent equity share in the project and will get 12 per free power, beside 49 percent on the generation cost. An additional one percent free power will be available to the state under local areas development grants, said Mittal.

Sharma said the project will be completed in a time-bound manner, using the latest technology. The company, which is already executing the 412 MW Rampur project on Satluj, will commission the project in seven years. The cost of power will be Rs 3.40 per unit, he added.

The Dhaulasidh project is likely to be completed in four years. The power will cost Rs 3 per unit. Sharma hinted that the project capacity may be doubled to to 80 MW.

A unique feature of the agreement provides for allocation of one hundred (100) units of electricity per month to each project-affected family for ten years, from the commissioning of the project. The company shall run community development schemes for the villages in the vicinity.

Before signing the MOU, Dhumal held a meeting with the Nigam's CMD. He urged that locals should be provided maximum jobs at all levels in these projects. He added that at the level of workmen (technical and ministerial), 100 percent recruitment should be done from the land outsees as first preference, and followed by those from Himachal Pradesh.

Sharma said that in the 636 MW Khab project, there had been no headway for some time because of local resistance. He claimed that the project will give a big boost to the local economy, beside containing heavy silt inflow in Satluj river.

Heading: BJP in a fix over selection of candidates - Indian Express
Content:
The 61th infantry day was celebrated here at Shimla's Annadale ground to commemorate the day when the first Indian army contingent was air-lifted to Srinagar on October 27,1947.

The ceremony was organised by 14 Jammu and Kashmir rifles. The army officers and jawans, who had assembled, said, Pakistan had attacked with the help of raiders who had advanced along Uri-Baramula-Srinagar road. Maharaja Hari Singh had signed instrument of accession to India, a day before the army reached here.The soldiers fought reversing the tide of battle and saving Kashmir as part of Indian Union.

Major general R K Arora of the Army Training Command laid wreaths on behalf of GOC-In-C Training Command. Others present included Brigadier Khushal Thakur, Station Commander, Shimla, and Col K S Kalsi, Commanding Officer, 14 Battalion J&K Rifles.

Heading: Fire official injured in mishap - Indian Express
Content:
The ruling BJP is in a fix over the issue of selecting its candidates for the upcoming Lok Sabha elections.

While Congress has started gearing up for the polls, BJP's delay in selecting the candidates might harm its prospects in the elections.

The party had declared its candidate for the Hamirpur parliamentary seat about four months ago. But it has still undecided about selecting candidates for the remaining three seats, including the politically important Kangra parliamentary constituency.

The party bigwigs say candidates for Shimla and Mandi have been shortlisted, but options are open for Kangra district. Till now, after four months , no names have been declared by the party, even after several meetings among the and deliberated upon the issue.

Kangra parliamentary seat is important for both the BJP and the Congress. The Congress has decided to field sitting MP Chaudhary Chander Kumar, but the BJP is in a bind over the issue. The decision of Rajya Sabha member Shanta Kumar not to contest the elections has made things more difficult for BJP.

The name of Rajiv Bhardwaj, a party worker from Nurpur in Kangra district, has been suggested by Shanta Kumar. But another faction led by those close to the CM is trying to push their candidate.

The party is keeping in mind the caste equations of the segment. The names of former MP Kirpal Parmar, Ravinder Singh Ravi and Sarveen Chaudhary, Cabinet rank ministers in the Dhumal government, have been discussed. Ravi and Parmar belong to Rajput community and Sarveen Chaudhary is from other backward classes. Both castes are dominant in this segment.

Other names which are doing rounds in the party circles are that of Transport Minister Kishan Kapoor and former revenue minister and sitting MLA from Jwali, Rajan Shushant.

Heading: Red Ribbon Express chugs in Bathinda - Indian Express
Content:
D S Verma, the Incharge of the Fire Brigade Office here, sustained serious injuries yesterday when he was going with his team in a fire-fighting vehicle, to control the fire at Bohlion. On the way, the front door of the vehicle opened, and Verma fell down. Despite his injuries, he helped the firemen in controlling the fire.

At Bohlion, a tractor had overturned and caught fire. The driver, Tapinder Singh, was stuck under the tractor. The firemen controlled the fire and also saved the driver's life. Tapinder was brought to Nahan Hospital along with Verma, where both were admitted in a serious condition. The driver is stated to have suffered a serious financial loss too. The residents of area praised Verma for his bravery.

'Cong appointed unqualified teachers'

Nahan: General secretary Himachal Employees Confederation, Vinod Kumar Thakur, today alleged that the Congress government had brought down the quality of education in government schools by appointing unqualified teachers through the PTA. He said that no proper criteria was adopted for the appointment of these teachers. He urged the government to take suitable steps against such 'wrong appointments'.

Thakur urged the government to consider the pending cases of 'employment on compassionate ground'. The confederation has thanked for CM for sanctioning 5 per cent dearness allowance.

Heading: Searching body of teenager, CBI stops water of Bhakra - Indian Express
Content:
Spreading AIDS awareness across the country, Red Ribbon Express reached Bathinda today, and would remain here till October 29.

The project is a joint venture of National AIDS Control Organisation and Rajiv Gandhi Foundation. The bogies of the train contain explicit information about the disease, including the causes and preventive measures. Seminars are also being held inside it, while a bogey has been dedicated to counselling.

A number of people, most of them youth and students, visited the counselling centre on the first day of the train's arrival, said Bhupinder Singh, one of the counsellors.

Among others who welcomed the train included Bathinda Member of Parliament Paramjit Kaur Gulshan, Punjab State AIDS Control Society Additional Project Director Dr NM Sharma, Bathinda Deputy Commissioner Rahul Tewari, Civil Surgeon Dr Neelam Bajaj and SSP Ashish Chaudhary.

Heading: Crackers being sold - Indian Express
Content:
The CBI went an extra mile to fulfill the wish of an anguished mother and got the water in Bhakra-Beas canal stopped in the hope of tracing the body of her young daughter murdered four years ago.

The case relates to the mysterious death of 17-year-old Amandeep Kaur, who was murdered in January 2004 allegedly by Jagtar Singh, against whom the CBI has secured an Interpol red corner notice. The accused is believed to be in Germany.

The CBI had last week brought together four different agencies — Bhakra-Beas Management Board (Nangal), Irrigation Department, Punjab State Electricity Board and civil administration — to stop the water flow after one of the accused arrested in the case said that they had killed Amandeep and dumped her in the canal. The distraught mother pleaded with the CBI if it could do something to recover her daughter's body for performing last rites, a senior CBI official said.

The CBI, with the help of divers from Bhakra Beas Board, searched a 30-km stretch after the water was stopped from 8 am to 2 pm last week. But no body was found. The CBI has arrested Jarnail Singh alias Jony, who is alleged to be involved in the murder conspiracy.

The victim, whose father is an NRI and at present in Italy, is believed to have had an affair with Jagtar Singh, but broke off after the accused forced her to marry him, the CBI said in its chargesheet. The family of the victim had filed a complaint about Amandeep's missing with the local police, who registered a case only after five days.

CBI investigations showed that Jagtar surrendered before a court in Punjab on April 16, 2005, after the court had issued non-bailable warrants against him. On May 28, 2005, the local police moved an application before the Judicial Magistrate for discharging Jagtar, who was finally set free on May 31, 2005, the CBI said.

The case was transferred to the CBI on May 25, 2007, on orders from the Punjab and Haryana High Court. In its chargesheet, the CBI claimed that Jagtar and Jarnail had murdered the girl and put the body in a gunny bag and later dumped it in Mukerian Hydel Channel. The water flow at the point at which the body was thrown is high and the officials of Bhakra Dam and PSEB had said that the body could have flown to river Beas, it said.

Heading: Guards’ no to extra shift halts trains - Indian Express
Content:
The lower-level administration employees have failed to implement the orders of the Deputy Commissioner (DC) of prohibiting the sale of crackers in congested areas of the city. The DC had issued orders under Section 144 of the CrPC, which the shopkeepers are flouting right under the nose of the administration.

A visit to the congested markets of the city, including Imamnasar, Attari Bazaar, Shikhan Bazaar, Rainak Bazaar, revealed that the streets in these markets were so narrow that even a small fire tender could not enter.

"We cannot send our children to the narrow streets of the city," said residents of Attari Bazaar.

DC AS Pannu could not be contacted for comments.

Heading: New medical college for St George, GT and Cama hospitals - Indian Express
Content:
Central Railway (CR) suburban services, on both the harbour and the main lines, were brought to a standstill for hours on Monday by railway guards refusing to work "overtime" to make up for 20 guards who did not turn up.

According to J N Lal, Divisional Railway Manager (Mumbai Division) of the CR, some 20 guards did not turn up on Monday as per the roster. In the afternoon, when the administration asked guards on duty to work an extra shift, they did not comply.

This led to clogging of trains one behind another, called "bunching" in the Railway parlance, as guards refused to board trains occupying platform slots at Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST).

There are 576 guards working with the suburban railway of the CR, against the sanctioned 594. "The standard duty hours for a guard is 10 hours, but in suburban railway they work for around six hours," added Lal.

"We had finished our duty when we were told to do "overtime", but simply couldn't due to work overload. Also, most of us wanted to go home due to Diwali," said a guard on morning duty who refused to work extra time.

"But we were not agitating," he clarified.

Commuters had to face the heat. They either had to alight and take the road route or wait till train services were normal again. It was particularly hard on women and senior citizens. It took 2 to 3 hours for the train to cover the Parel-CST stretch, which otherwise takes 20-odd minutes.

"As the trains were stranded on one side (the slow track towards CST), there were few on the other track," said Punit Karnik, a commuter.

Though motormen run the trains, guards play a pivotal role. "The guard is in charge of the train and alerts motormen in case of any emergency, especially from the rear side. He gives motormen the signal for departure after ensuring all commuters are safely on board," said an Indian Rail and Traffic Service (IRTS) officer. "In case of any accident, he, along with the railway cops, ensures the track is cleared for the next train."

Meanwhile, the railway administration said they had taken steps to avert such a situation in future. The guards and the railway administration (additional DRM) held a meeting to sort out the problem. "We have issued them a warning so that such things do not happen in future," added Lal.

Heading: Royer Byrne delivers lecture on F1 car designing in IITB Techfest - Indian Express
Content:
With work for AIIMS-level makeover of the state-run JJ Group of Hospitals in the city already on, the state government is mulling creating another college within the JJ Group.

The JJ Group of Hospitals run by the state Medical Education Department has four hospitals — JJ Hospital, St George Hospital, GT Hospital and Albless and Cama Hospital—- and a medical college, the Grant Medical College, under one umbrella.

The government is now looking at creating a separate medical college outside JJ Hospital.

"We are considering a separate college for the three hospitals, apart from the one in JJ hospital. This medical college will be attached to the three other hospitals of the JJ Group of Hospitals," said Secretary (Medical Education) Bhushan Gagrani.

Under the Central government project for upgrading medical colleges across the country to the level of its premier medical education centres, AIIMS, the largest medical college in Mumbai — Grant Medical College — was selected for the makeover in the first phase.

Under the plan, the Centre approved a grant of Rs 100 crore with Rs 20 crore from the state government for the makeover. In the second phase, the government medical college in Nagpur has been selected for a similar makeover.

The government is planning to shift the staff from JJ hospital to the new college once it is set up and is getting more staff if they require.

Heading: Prosecution in POTA case says accused using Al-Qaeda manual to delay case - Indian Express
Content:
Ability to work in a team is the key to be a F1 designer, Byrne tells students

For students of the IITB, it was once in a lifetime opportunity as the man behind Michael Schumacher's 88 Formula One — currently the design and development consultant for Scuderia Ferrari (the racing arm of Ferrari)— Royer Byrne mentored them on designing models at a lecture in the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IITB) as part of the Techfest's pre-festival lecture series on Monday. Byrne and Schumacher had topped the chart winning the highest number of both drivers' and constructors' titles in Formula One history. Byrne interacted with students of various colleges across the country, including IITB, Thapar University-Patiala, KJ Somaiya College of Engineering and RV college of Engineering, Bangalore. Byrne, who was 'never born an engineer and had to pick it up along the way' shared experiences of his journey towards becoming one of the greatest designers in Formula One, with the students. While answering a question posed by a student on the qualifications required to be a F1 designer, he said that grades and other credentials would be the primary criteria, but another overriding qualification would be the ability to work in a team. He said that cars designed by individuals were history and all the future car designs would belong to a team.

While delivering lecture on the greener cars, he said, "The challenge is to reduce costs and to turn green." He also said that it would be necessary to decrease the fuel consumption of cars by 20-30 per cent by 2011 and by 50 per cent by 2015. The cars of the future will show far more aerodynamic efficiency as compared to the present ones, he said. He also said that the kind of dominance that Ferrari has had over the past decades would be difficult in the future and the competition would be 'far more closer'.

Nazir Hussain of the Motor Sports Association of India (MAI) who was also present in the function emphasized on the need to improve infrastructure. He said, "If we have the infrastructure, the drivers will come through. Our circuits are not up to the Formula One standards."

Heading: October heat relaxes, Mumbai settles at 33 degree Celsius - Indian Express
Content:
The special public prosecutor Suresh Gholkar has wrote to the state government's law and judiciary department that an accused in the 2003 Mulund-Vile Parle and Mumbai Central Railway Station blasts is following the Al-Qaeda manual to make sure that the trial will not begin.

Gholkar has recently wrote a four page reply to the department explaining his stand on the false allegations made by a former National Defence Academy (NDA) professor Anwar Ali Khan, who was arrested for serious charges under the Prevention of Terrorist Activities Act (POTA). Khan has been in custody since his arrest. Khan used to teach Urdu in NDA.

Khan had written to the Law and Judiciary department alleging "professional misconduct" on Gholkar's part by deliberately taking dates and "fattening his professional fees." The public prosecutors appointed by the Law and Judiciary get fees for each appearance they make in the court for a case. Their appearances are proven by the roznama recorded by the court.

Gholkar in his reply to the department said that Khan had made allegations "out of sheer frustration and with malafide intention to harass him mentally." Explaining that 50 per cent of the accused in this case, including Khan belong to the banned Students Islamic Moverment of India (SIMI), Ghokar stated that they were "found to follow the instructions in the Al-Qaeda manual". As per chapter 12 of the Al-Quaeda manual, the accused should behave in such a way that the trial in which they are charged should not commence at all, Gholkar pointed out.

"To achieve this object", the accused are trying to stall the progress of the trial by making allegations against the judge or the public prosecutors, he said. Earlier, the accused had sought transfer of the case from the then Special Judge A P Bhangale. They had also made allegations against the investigating officers in the case. Thus, the accused are following the Al-Qaeda manual and Khan's complaint is a "glaring example," Gholkar stated.

In 2003, three bomb explosions — in Karjat-bound train at Mulund Railway Station, blasts at a food stall at Mumbai Central and a crowded Vile Parle market— took place within a few days. The blasts claimed lives of at least a dozen of people and injured over 100 persons. There are a total of 16 accused in the case, including alleged SIMI chief Saquib Nachan.

Appearing for most of the accused in the case, defence lawyer Mubin Solkar said that Khan had made such an allegation. "Most of the accused have been in custody since their arrest and lodged at Thane jail. Many of them have filed bail applications which are pending in court. This is the first case where educated youths were allegedly involved in conspiring, planning and executing blast in Mumbai," he added.

Heading: Mumbaikars to bear the brunt of BMC’s move to cut water supply by half, say developers - Indian Express
Content:
After a week of immense humidity — with mercury soaring as high as 35 degree Celsius — the city temperature on Monday settled at the standard normal for the month ie; 33 degrees Celsius, the IMD said. On Monday, Colaba recorded a maximum temperature of 32.1 degree and Santa Cruz, 33.1 degree Celsius though the humidity hovered at a high 93 per cent. Night temperatures were also settled at 22.8 degree Celsius and 20.9 degree Celsius in Colaba and Santa Cruz respectively, just one degree over the standard normal. The normal minimum temperature for October is 22 degrees Celsius, sources said.

When contacted, K Sathi Devi, director of IMD, Mumbai, said, "Usually, humid, hot weather is typical in October due to the high moisture content in air after the monsoon. In fact, humidity is so high in Mumbai after monsoon that we consider the months of October, November and December as post-monsoon months. Mumbai, officially, has only two months of winter — January and February." The highest October temperaturs recorded in the past 10 years were in 2001 and 2002, when the mercury had risen as high as 37 degrees.

"The trend we've observed in the past years is that after the initial heat tempered down, the weather settles at normal. We are expecting the temperatures to settle at around 33 deg Celsius." The IMD noted that winds were also shifting from landwards north-easterly to north-westerly. Officially, winter will set in the city only in January, an IMD official said.

Heading: No more entertainment tax than levied: HC - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbaiikars who are planning to buy a fancy flat in upscale housing complexes in the coming years will have to look for getting water from borewells and tankers.

As a solution to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's (BMC) proposal for reducing water supply to newly constructed buildings by half - from the present 90 litres per person a day to 45 litres per person a day for buildings whose demand is less than 2 lakh litres a day— developers have said that digging borewells, rainwater harvesting and purchasing water from outside city at higher costs will be the options they will explore. However, they said the civic body's decision was unfair as residents would have to pay a heavy price for purchasing these flats and yet will not get any respite in water taxes.

"If the BMC is not in a position to provide water connections or supply less water than prescribed, we will dig borewells and go in for rainwater harvesting," said Niranjan Hiranandani, a developer. "We will also be proposing the mayor and corporators to give us concession in taxes for providing adequate water," he said.

However, the civic water department also proposed that those whose demand exceeds that figure will simply have to wait as the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's water supply sources are significantly augmented. The 90-litres per capita a day is an existing national norm for water supply and existing buildings that already have water connections will continue to get this supply. Quizzed on the issue, Hydraullic Engineer M M Kamble said that developers would have to dig borewells and go in for rainwater harvesting to cope with the water shortage.

Rustomjee constructions, who have projects coming up in Bandra and D N Nagar at Andheri in the coming months, said that it already has properties with borewells and rainwater harvesting. "Digging borewells is not the best option for the builders, but if there are no other options left, we will have to do it. We will explore other options of purchasing water from outside the city and bringing water tankers," said C J Mathews, head, marketing.

Mohan Deshmukh, president, Maharashtra Chamber of Housing Industries, said that providing water supply to buildings is responsibility of the BMC. "The BMC has not been able to cope with the increasing demand and upgrade its infrastructure. They should provide better options instead of suggesting digging borewells to builders," he said. He said that many builders would opt for purchasing water from irrigation department, MIDC, or parts of Thane and Vasai-Virar.

Heading: City to represent India at World Cyber Games in Germany - Indian Express
Content:
In a significant relief for Swanston Multiplex Cinemas Private Limited, which runs the popular FAME ADLABS at Andheri, the Bombay High Court recently quashed notices issued by the state government for levying entertainment duty.

The multiplex operators can now heave a sigh of relief as they would have had to shell out lakhs if the notice had been upheld by the court.

"The state was not entitled to claim more than what could be levied as entertainment duty during the two-year period, irrespective of the fact that the exhibitors have shown on admission tickets issued to patrons 45 per cent of the duty though they were liable to pay only 25 per cent during the incentive period," the court held while quashing the notices issued against the multiplex.

It is the Company's contention that on the basis of the objects of the Ordinance and on the basis of Section 3 13(a) of the Bombay Entertainment (Amendment) Act, 2001, the petitioner applied for exemption to set up a multiplex for which they invested huge capital, time and efforts.

The petitioner contended that it was solely based on the assurance of the state government they went ahead and set up the multiplex "on the clear understanding that the nature of exemption was retention benefit whereby the petitioner was entitled to collect the entertainment duty from the patrons and not to pay the same to the state during the exemption period."

Under the exemption, the multiplex does not have to pay any duty for the first three years from the date of commencement of the Multiplex Theatre. For the subsequent two years, a 25 per cent rate is levied and from the sixth year, full amount of duty has to be paid.

The petitioner, however, received a notice from the Collector seeking a payment of Rs.1,16,95,846 as tax including interest during the fourth year since the commencement of the multiplex.

The petitioner contended that it was unclear how the authorities arrived at the figure along with an interest of 24 per cent. The petitioner further contended that the authorities had levied the full entertainment duty at the rate of 45 per cent without considering the exemption. It was argued by the petitioner that they were paying the statutory duty as contemplated under the exemption.

The state government's argument centered on the fact that this is a clear cut case of unjust enrichment and the state was justified in claiming the amount of entertainment duty collected by the petitioner from the patrons as shown in the admission ticket to be paid to the Government with interest.

The state pointed out that the petitioner in the admission ticket showed entertainment duty as 45 per cent and the petitioner has no right to retain the duty collected from the patrons. It is the case of the petitioner that there are no guidelines for pricing of the cinema ticket rates.

A division bench of Justice J N Patel and Justice K K Tated, however, concluded that "merely because the proprietors printed full entertainment tax duty on the tickets though they were only liable to pay 25 per cent of tax duty" does not mean they are liable to pay 100 per cent entertainment tax.

"On other hand, it would deprive them of the incentive which has been specifically offered under the scheme for which the Act came to be amended and would be in total conflict with the object and reasons" of the amendment of the Act, the court observed.

Heading: Of registration, documents and legal rights - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai has another reason to hold its head high, as some of its citizens are all set to represent India at the internationally awaited World Cyber Games '08 (WCG), at Cologne in Germany between November 5 and 9.

The preliminary rounds in India were held in New Delhi on October 17 and 18, and in Mumbai on October 23 and 24. Following the preliminary rounds, the regional winners from Mumbai and Delhi competed on October 25 to see who would represent India at Cologne for the grand finale of the WCG. Mumbai emerged winner by beating Delhi.

"There are around ten games, and each has a different set of rules. The games will help you meet people from totally different cultures and backgrounds. My team members are from Netherlands, Denmark and Belgium," said Reuben Pereira, 18, who will represent India in FIFA Soccer 2008.

"The best part is that you get to meet people with whom you usually chat online. India has a long way to go, but we have improved a lot," he added. Pereira is not new to the WCG, or the cyber-games arena, since he has been winning tournaments since 2006 and practices for 10 hours a day.

"It is a good experience, though in India it used to be a nine-city thing earlier. It is a much bigger scene abroad, though we're getting there," said Arun Singh Ravi, who is the representative for the game Need For Speed, and is looking to rank somewhere in the Top-8 this year. "This is the third time we are taking part. We have been winning straight through all three years. We are pretty much the same team except for a few players here and there. The WCG is a fun, exciting learning platform for us," said Mikhei Mehra, part of the Counterstrike team, adding that since the international team had much more professional backing, they were in a different league.

Designed to encourage healthy gaming, the World Cyber Games allow the best gamers around the world to gather in various cities and share their experience of the cyber-games that are modelled along the lines of the International Olympic tournament. This year, 70 countries will participate in the WCG.

Heading: History revealed through coins - Indian Express
Content:
Sometimes, the law is an ass. In this case, the State is an ass, hell bent on making an ass of anyone who has a house to sell, a testament to register, or any mandatory job to do in the Registry. You are prohibited from walking into the Registry, taking your turn, handing over the document at a desk, and going home, receipt in pocket. For decades, registration of a document was as simple as drinking tea. Now, first of all, you must take an appointment. Plain sailing you may think. You think wrong. You walk in, encounter milling crowds. You now have the ass's tail -- step one.

"May I have an appointment, please?" as polite as can be.

"You can only get it on the phone," you are firmly told.

You try to comply, being a law abiding senior citizen -- very senior -- very civic-minded.

The phone appears to be off the hook. You try repeatedly. By hook but not by crook, you get through.

"All appointments are taken" is the deadly response. You are not easily fobbed off. "Never mind," you say, "give me a time 2 to 20 days from now, I will accept whatever time is free."

The third day is Monday. Lucky girl! I get the Monday afternoon.

On Monday, I acquire the ass's ears -- step two.

An officer looks at the document, "Very well. Call the executant of the document.""But he has left India. If he is expected to be in India, why would he appoint me his constituted attorney?" I ask bewildered. "That is the Rule," I am firmly told.

I am a law abiding citizen. But I am a law abiding citizen, full of curiosity to know the source of the Rules, purported to be made under a law, full of eagerness to know the rationale of a provision of or under the law. And you know what? All efforts to identify any relevant law under the extant Registration Act (a central Act), have failed. Neither could a Secretary in the Law Department of the State of Maharashtra show me any relevant section of the Act, when I pointedly requested it. Nor could the DGI, whose job is to see that everything done at the Registry is fair and square. Nor could a competent lawyer making a diligent search. Nor could the Chief Minister, who kindly gave me audience. Nor could anyone else show me any law that allows the Maharashtra state government to refuse a citizen the legal right, the safety and the comfort of registering a valid document, such as my Power of Attorney. No Maharashtra amendment could be located, purporting to permit the making of rules, that would say that a representative of a person executing a valid document can not register it in the absence of the latter. And indeed, if any amendment were made, or purported to be made, on first principles it would be repugnant to the provisions of the Act. Parliament has clearly evinced an intention that representatives can produce documents for registration. Any state legislature would be acting contrary to the law, in introducing or purporting to introduce any amendment entirely contrary to the intention of Parliament.

The Registry, where the thriving side business of agents is extremely evident, has made asses of us all. I am the ass par excellence because I would not pay anyone a paisa.

This has rendered null my Power of Attorney, and the consequent return from England to India, of my son-in-law to sign his own document, which I was empowered to do, by means of his Power of Attorney.

The coins are of particular interest because the first depictions of Buddha in human form happened during this period

With the Dinesh Mody Numismatics Museum at Santacruz launching the Dinesh Mody Numismatics Society last week, its inaugural function gave interested numismatists in the city an insight into the age of the Kushanas. For, kicking off the inaugural function was Robert Bracey, curator of the Kushana Coins Project at the British Museum , who delivered a lecture on coins of the Kushana Dynasty, unraveling various mysteries of that period through an analysis of the coins.

Titled 'Kushana Coins: The Structure and Chronology of their Issue - What We Know Now' -the Bracey lecture helped throw light on how the study of coins helped in the reconstruction of the history of the Kushanas, an empire that extended from Afghanistan through India and Burma. Bracey, who is the Assistant Editor, Journal of the Oriental Numismatic Society in the UK , specializes in the history of the Kushana period. "The coins are especially important because the first depictions of Buddha in a human form were in this period. Till then the depictions were symbols- a lotus, or an elephant," said Dilip Rajgor, General Secretary, Dinesh Mody Museum Society. "Bracey is an expert on Kushana coins, and has come here especially come to deliver a lecture," he adds. The Dinesh Mody Numismatics Museum is located within the University Campus at Kalina in Santacruz, and the Dinesh Mody Museum Society is looking at organizing lectures and talks by various scholars in the coming months.

The society will also hold regular meetings for coin collectors and dealers in order to exchange numismatic discoveries and will have coin exhibitions, quizzes on coins along with excursions to various historical sites, monuments and museums.

Heading: Silver worth Rs 1 crore seized by Octroi Dept - Indian Express
Content:
A security guard working for D-Mart, a departmental store in Bangur Nagar at Goregaon intended to celebrate an early Diwali by swindling money worth Rs 20, 05,430 on Saturday night. He left the city with the huge amount. A case was immediately filed and the Bangur Nagar police managed to track and arrest the accused Sanjay Vaghchure (30) and his accomplice Yogesh Gholap (21) within 48 hours from a village near Sinnar, in Nashik, where they were hiding. Vaghchure has been charged with cheating and criminal breach of trust. The police have recovered cash worth Rs 19,99,000 from the accused.

Vaghchure had been working with D Mart for the last two months and was known to the manager of the mall. Securitrans India Pvt Limited, an Oshiwara based company that handled the daily transfer of the store's earnings to the bank, posted him there. The money was transferred daily by security vans to the bank after the responsible security guard took the money from the cashier and punched a card with the mall security. Since the last month Tushar Parab, Vaghchure's colleague, was made in charge of depositing the malls daily earnings, but on Saturday he went on leave. The security agency was arranging to send someone for this job, but Vaghchure took this opportunity and told the cashier that he was in charge for the day. Later, he fooled the mall security by telling them that the mall security card was with Parab.

When the police reached his residence in Borivili his house was locked as he had left with his wife and two children. A team was immediately sent to Sinnar, Nashik where he had relatives.

There they were told that he was living with his uncle in a farm in a nearby village. The police immediately zeroed in on him and arrested him.

The police also arrested Gholap who was with him and immediately confessed to aiding him in committing the crime.

Heading: Read My Mind proves too good for Mighty Hearts in feature - Indian Express
Content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's Octroi Department has seized 560 kg silver worth Rs 1 crore which was brought into the city from Gujarat evading octroi duty. A penalty of Rs 2 lakh was collected from the importer.

Vigilance officer on special duty, Babaji Lakhan, had led the squad of civic officials at Mumbai Central railway station early morning last Thursday and seized the silver consignment.

Civic officials allege that importers do not declare the silver consignment and hide it alongwith other goods.

"Only if the consignment is opened to verify the goods that the hidden and expensive items are revealed. We had received tip-off about the silver consignment and acted accordingly," said an official.

Last month also 350 kg silver and other silver items worth Rs 70 lakh was seized.

Officials said that on an average 4,000 parcels are brought out from Mumbai Central railway station, however there is a huge difference between actual payment of octroi at the railway premises of these goods. A flying squad of vigilance department too has been formed at the Mumbai Central Railway station octroi posts to keep an eye on the evasion of octroi.

Heading: LAST BITE  with Sudharshan Shetty - Indian Express
Content:
Chef Francesco Apreda of the Hassler Roma promises to introduce real Italian food to Mumbai, come November

The three most famous things from Italy are the Church, Sophia Loren and the Hassler Hotel. Since we know enough about the first two, it's time we get some know-how about the best hotel in all of Italy. This is why Chef Francesco Apreda from the hotel's Imago restaurant will step into the kitchen at Vetro, The Oberoi, Nariman Point, in November.

Apreda says that the Hassler Roma had always been foremost on his list of ideal work locations. Located at the top of the Spanish Steps, the hotel is historic in the true sense of the word. "The magic of cooking from such a height and with such an exceptional view is indescribable, as well as the fulfillment of any chef's greatest dream," he says.

Now, he runs Imàgo, the Italian restaurant at the hotel. Apreda does a very good job of selling Italian food to Italians in Italy—a task by no means easy. "I started working when I was 13. The hallmark of my cooking is constant research for the best and most prized products, always fresh and seasonal, transformed into my own creative interpretation of Italian food," he says, explaining how he manages to re-invent himself.

"We are taking to Vetro what we prepare and offer guests in Rome at Imàgo," he says about the food he's going to prepare in Mumbai. Some delightful dishes include Fusilloni pasta with quail ragout carbonara style, a delightful Pear and asparagus parmigiana timbale with mushrooms and artichoke sauce, Roasted fillet of sea bass with shallots and Cannellini beans, eggplant and ginger sauce, Semolina and Taleggio cheese pudding with Belgian endives and red onion sauce and Glazed breast of duck with dried fruit, amongst other things.

Apreda is from the region of Campania, a place synonymous with the truest mozzarella cheese. Besides that, it's a region where Mediterranean food with lots of fish and pasta dishes are very famous. Comfort food for him is Italy's most famous export to the world —good old spaghetti. "Spaghetti with a fresh seafood sauce—it reminds me of home. As a Neapolitan, therefore from the homeland of pizza, it would be banal to say pizza," he says.

Italian food is served extensively in Mumbai, second only to Chinese food. The reason for this, Apreda says, is that people are very aware thanks to travelling widely. Besides, Italian food is easy to make and healthy to eat. "Fresh and seasonal ingredients, and an expert hand that knows the tradition is all it takes. If you know how to innovate using new techniques, there's nothing like it," he says.

As for his time in our city, he says, "I want to have the time to research for spices and products that I can incorporate into my Italian dishes. Upon returning to Rome, I will immediately create a menu with the theme of Indian spices, because my cooking also includes influences from other parts of the world—since I have travelled far and wide."

Heading: TURNING OVER - Indian Express
Content:
The last meal that I still reminisce was the one I had last month in London. I went with a friend and gallery owner called Fabio Rossi to lunch at an Italian restaurant called Assaggi in Nottingham. It's a very special place and rather exclusive with only 11 tables and personalised service. We had pasta with pork and truffles, fresh crab lightly drizzled with lemon juice and olive oil, and a bottle of Soave Monte Fiorentine, a white wine that went well with the dishes we ordered. It was a lazy lunch since the restaurant reserved the table for the whole day and the lunch time went upto 7 pm.

We were dilly-dallying over lunch and Rossi said it that this was closest to his mother's cooking. The fare is so fresh and simple yet it's really delicious. And since we were on the main street we could watch people walk by. The meal was marvelous and the restaurant had a great laidback vibe. The next time I'm in London, I will go there again for sure.

Heading: MEAL TICKET - Indian Express
Content:
Bibimbap
(Pronounced bee-bim-bop)
Don't hesitate to ask for it: Bibimbap is one of Korea's best-known dishes this side of Seoul. Nutritious and delicious, bibimbap is a simple-to-make dish. It just takes steaming hot sticky rice and ladles of vegetable stew or meat to get it right. In Korean, it means 'mixed meal'.

The first mention of bibimbap has been found in a 19 century anonymous cookbook called Siuijeonseo. In the book it's called Buibuimbap.

A raw or fried egg and pieces of beef are the usual additions to a dish of bibimbap. These ingredients are mixed into the dish just before eating. In most Korean households, it's a common everyday food. In Mumbai, ask for bibimbap at Pan Asian, ITC Grand Maratha and India Jones, Trident.

Heading: Arrest warrant issued against the Todis in Rizwanur case - Indian Express
Content:
Bus conductor Mahendra Hule (27), who had joined BEST just a year ago, still shudders when he recalls how Rahul Raj had held him at gunpoint.

His colleague Shivaji Borade (51), on the other hand, shudders at what might have been; it was he who informed the police and he realises his action might have meant death for Hule. Borade, however, feels the police should have tried to contain the gunman instead of shooting him down.

It was around 9 am when BEST bus No 322 inched past the crowded Bailbazar stop in Kurla. The dozen passengers on the upper deck of the double-decker were shocked when a young man rose from one of the seats, went to the back of the bus, held a chain around Hule's neck and then whipped out a gun.

"I'm still in shock. I was so terrified because I knew if even one man refused to obey him he would have shot me then and there... I'm still trembling."

Moments earlier, Hule, who was on the upper deck, had asked Raj if he had bought a ticket. "When I asked him for the ticket, he waved. I thought he possibly had a monthly pass. Eight or ten minutes later he attacked me from behind. He put a chain around my neck and pointed the gun on my head," Hule recalls.

The gunman kept yelling that he did not want to harm anyone, but had come to take on Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray.

Borade, who has worked with BEST for 26 years, was on duty on the lower deck. He managed to inform the nearby police chowky, possibly averting a disaster.

For Borade what was imperative was to ensure his young colleague's safety. However, he admits that when he considered approaching the police, the thought crossed his mind that the man could kill Hule for this.

"I heard people shouting and yelling and therefore I tried running on to the upper deck. The man (Rahul Raj) was holding a gun to Hule's forehead. He was yelling, "Don't come up or I will kill him'. Then I ran to the nearest police chowky and brought the police along with me," Borade says.

While he was running to the police chowky, Hule's ordeal was constantly running through his mind. "He has joined only about a year ago and to face such a situation," he says.

Hule says he doesn't know if he'll be able to put the incident out of his mind. "I was staring at death. I don't know if I can get back into that bus," he says.

BEST committee chairman Pravin Chheda also announced a reward for the duo. "We will also reward the bus driver and other conductors for the presence of mind that they showed during the incident and helped save many lives by ensuring police intervention at a crucial time," said Chheda.

Heading: CBI raids Todi house, finds it empty - Indian Express
Content:
The CBI court on Monday issued an arrest warrant against Ashok Todi, Pradip Todi and Anil Sarogi in the Rizwanur Rehman case.

Delivering the order, judge Bibhash Chatterjee directed the CBI to produce all three of them before the court on November 3 and remanded Mainuddin alias Pappu, a close friend of Rizwanur's family, in judicial custody till November 10.

The CBI had filed a chargesheet in the case on September 22 and had accused Ashok Todi, Pradip Todi, Anil Sarogi, Pappu and three police officers of abetment of suicide. Subsequently, the court had issued summons asking them to appear on Monday.

But instead of personal appearance, the Todis and Sarogi filed a petition to be 'kept in abeyance' of the criminal proceedings.

Their lawyers argued that the CBI court should not initiate the trials now, in compliance with a Supreme Court order of October 13.

Ashok Todi, father-in-law of Rizwanur, had moved a petition in the Supreme Court on October 13, seeking a stay on the CBI probe, which was rejected by the apex court.

Moving the petition, the counsel of Todis said the Supreme Court had stayed the commencement of trial in the case till the disposal of the appeal filed by Todis, which was pending before a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court.

The Supreme Court had asked the High Court to complete the hearing within six months. But the CBI court rejected the argument and issued an arrest warrant against the three who had not appeared before court.

On the other hand, on Monday, Pappu appeared before the magistrate of the CBI court. Rejecting the bail petition of Pappu, the magistrate said the CBI had framed criminal charges against Pappu and hence the proceedings could be jeopardised if the court granted him bail. Pappu was remanded in judicial custody and would be again produced on November 10.

The CBI court had asked three officers of Kolkata police — Ajay Kumar, Sukanti Chakraborty and Krishnendu Das — to appear on November 3. The three police officers had surrendered on September 30 before the CBI court.

Heading: TMC-Cong link puts a question mark on PSDF’s survival - Indian Express
Content:
Officials from the Central Bureau of Investigation raided the residence of the Todis on Monday, soon after an arrest warrant for them was issued by a special court. They, however, had to return empty-handed.

On Monday, all seven accused in the Rizwanur Rehman case were to appear before the designated CBI court. But the two Todi brothers, Ashok and Pradip, and their relative, Anil Saraogi, failed to turn up.

The court issued an arrest warrant against the brothers. The CBI has been asked to ensure that the Todis are produced in court on November 3.

The CBI officers in court immediately got in touch with their seniors in Delhi. The major part of the investigations into the Rizwanur Rehman case has been done by a special CBI team from Delhi. After getting the green signal and a copy of the court order, a team from Kolkata went to the residence of the Todis in the evening, but could not find them.

The family of Rizwanur Rehman was happy about the order. Expressing satisfaction over the arrest warrant, Rizwanur's brother Rukbanur said: "It seems finally justice will prevail and the soul of Rizwan will find peace."

He hoped the other accused will also be brought to justice.

The gates of the Todi residence were closed throughout the day on Monday even as a large contingent of mediapersons waited outside.

A source said the Todis were in hiding out in Kolkata, while another CBI source said they had probably gone out of town to avoid arrest.

"Why the Todis did not appear in court today is a mystery," said a CBI lawyer. "They had probably got the hint that the court order might not be in their favour, so they decided against appearing in court," said a CBI source.

Pappu alias Moinuddin, also an accused in the case, was sent to jail for 14 days by the same court.

"We will move the High Court against the lower court's order," said the Todis' lawyer. He, however, did not comment on why the Todis failed to appear in court.

Heading: Vector-borne diseases spread to districts - Indian Express
Content:
The growing proximity between the Trinamool Congress and the Congress has put a question mark on the future of Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee's Progressive Secular Democratic Front (PSDF), formed when the agitation in Singur and Nandigram was at a peak.

During her recent visit to Delhi, Banerjee not only met Congress chief Sonia Gandhi, but was also seen hobnobbing with Samajwadi Party leader Amar Singh. A leader of CPI-ML (New Democracy), Pradip Banerjee, whose party was a Front ally during the Singur and Nandigram movements, said: "It is not clear with whom she will form an alliance. If it's the Congress, we will not be able to continue in the Front. If there is an alliance with the Samajwadi Party, we have no objections. But there should be no direct alliance with the Congress."

The leaders of SUCI echoed similar views. 'When we entered into an alliance with the Trinamool, we had an understanding that the party will maintain equidistance from both the BJP and the Congress. Till now, it is not clear what she (Banerjee) will do. If she does not keep equidistance from the two parties, we will have to think otherwise," said Pravash Ghosh, SUCI state secretary.

According to Trinamool sources, however, several party leaders are of the opinion that it is necessary to tie up with a national party for the upcoming Lok Sabha polls. "The recent panchayat and civic elections were all local body polls, where we tied-up with small state-level parties. But the Lok Sabha elections are a different ball game altogether," said a senior leader. A source close to Banerjee, however, said: "As of now, the Trinamool does not want to annoy its SUCI and the Naxal partners, who have played an important part in Trinamool's success in the recent polls." Leader of the Opposition and Trinamool MLA Partha Chatterjee said: "She did not discuss the issue with me. But whatever decision she takes I will accept it." Rumours are doing rounds that Banerjee is looking for a different poll formula — she wants to enter into a loose alliance with the Congress and keep her Front intact.

Heading: Governor Gandhi gives father-daughter duo a lift to airport - Indian Express
Content:
While the state government has been busy containing the outbreak of vector-borne diseases in Kolkata, the diseases have assumed alarming proportions in the districts. Malaria, dengue, chikungunya and Japanese Encephelitis have spread across Hooghly, Howrah, North and South 24-Parganas. Since health infrastructure is comparatively weak in the districts, experts fear that the menace will spread unchecked.

Eleven people have died in the state capital, and now the state health department has sounded an alert in some districts. "We are sending medical teams to the affected areas and are trying our best despite limitations. The infrastructure for detecting and treating such outbreaks is better in the city compared to villages," said Sanchita Bakshi, Director, Health. The district health officials, in collaboration with local panchayat authorities, are organising awareness camps at villages affected by chikungunya. But little else has being done.

According to reports, 104 residents of Chanditala, 187 from Singur and 133 from Khanakul have been suffering from high fever. Thirty blood samples have been sent for test. The results confirmed that 11 people from the three blocks have been affected with chikungunya. "We have sounded an alert after talks with the health department officers," said Bhusan Chakraborty, Hooghly's Chief Medical Officer.

Those afflicted with chikungunya are being treated at their homes. "We have sent medical teams to all such villages. All block medical health officials have been asked to keep a close watch in their respective areas, Chakraborty said.

In Kolkata the latest victim succumbed to cerebral malaria in Chetla on Sunday. Already, four people have died of malaria, three of dengue, one of Japanese Encephelitis and two of an "unknown" fever. The "unknown" fever, in fact, has gripped several areas of North 24-Parganas, including Budge Budge and Falta. In Salt Lake, 25 slum dwellers are suffering from it. Another was found to have contracted chikungunya.

Heading: Dasmunsi indisposed, Cong puts two on hotseat - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi gave a lift to an elderly man and his daughter to the Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Airport in his car early on Monday morning.

The taxi, in which the father-daughter duo was travelling had developed a snag on the A J C Bose Road and the two suddenly found themselves stranded as a replacement was hard to come by at that hour, said an member of the Governor's staff. Gandhi was on his way to the airport to catch a 6 am flight to Chennai. He saw them and asked them what was the problem. He then said that since he was also going to the airport, he could easily drop them. The elderly man and his daughter hopped into one of the cars in the convoy still unaware who their benefactor was.

"Who is the kind gentleman?" the father asked the driver of the car. Pat came the reply: "He is the Governor of West Bengal, Gopalkrishna Gandhi."

Heading: Clouds gone, city gears up for Kali Puja, Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
With the condition of its state unit chief Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi being critical, the Congress is now looking at an alternate leadership in view of the upcoming elections.

On Monday, Subrata Mukherjee and Pradip Bhattacharjee were named joint working presidents. This was decided at a meeting held at the home of veteran party leader and Union external affairs minister Pranab Mukherjee.

"The high command has decided that we have to take on the responsibility in the absence of Priyada," Subrata Mukherjee told The Indian Express. According to party sources, the move is also meant to keep the various lobbies happy. Subrata Mukherjee is known to be close to Dasmunsi while Bhattacharjee is said to be close to Pranab Mukherjee.

Senior leaders of the party also discussed the party's strategy for the coming Lok Sabha polls. The leaders also deliberated on the by-elections in three constituencies, said Subrata Mukherjee.

The by-elections in Nandigram (East Midnapore), Para (Purulia) and Sujapur (Malda) are scheduled for December.

The seat in Nandigram fell vacant after sitting CPI legislator Mohammed Illiyas resigned after bribery charges were levelled against him. The Sujapur seat fell vacant as sitting Congress legislator Rubi Noor died recently. The seat in Para fell vacant after sitting legislator Bilasi Bala Sahis of the CPM was nominated the zilla parishad sabhadhipati.

According to sources, the leaders also discussed the possibility of a tie-up with Trinamool Congress for the by-elections.

"Though an official tie-up will not take place, there may be some understanding at the ground level. Where we are strong, like in Malda, we will ask them to support us and where they are strong, like in Nandigram, we will try and support them," said a senior Congress leader.

Heading: Fire Department, police make special arrangements - Indian Express
Content:
According to Met Department, cyclonic storm Rashmi that was moving towards the state has changed its course towards Bangladesh coast

Incessant rains have finally given way to sunshine, providing a much-needed relief to the city residents on the occasions of Kali Puja and Diwali.

As the sky cleared, many residents were seen flocking Baaji Bazar, which wore a deserted look on Sunday after weather played a spoilsport.

According to Met Department, the cyclonic storm, Rashmi, which was moving towards the state has changed its course and has crossed the Bangladesh coast now.

"We predict a clear sky on Tuesday with no treat from thundershowers. However, the sky may remain cloudy in some places," said Alipore Meteorological Department deputy director-general L R Meena.

With the storm moving towards Bangladesh, traders at Baaji Bazar are now calculating their losses.

"So far business has been very poor. On Sunday, we received very few customers because of heavy showers. We had stocked diyas, candles and other items worth Rs 3 lakh, most of which have not been sold yet," said M Sazar, a shopkeeper at Bazi Bazar.

Meanwhile, as youngsters poured in with their parents to make the most of last-minute shopping for firecrackers, stall owners at Baaji Bazar chipped in to pay Rs 60,000 to provide 500 wooden planks to ensure a smooth passage for customers through muddy fields.

"Today is the last day and we have to make the most of it. Since the field is full of small puddles, some of the stall owners have put together money to get wooden planks for customers," said M Shamshi of Raju Stores.

Unlike the grim picture at Baaji Bazar that one saw on Sunday, firecracker business started catching up on Monday. "We expected most of the customers to visit the market on Sunday, but due to the thundershowers 75 per cent of our sales got hampered. Yesterday, we expected a sale of Rs 3 lakh, but could manage to sell goods worth Rs 80,000 only," said Sanjeev K Montu of Babunand Stores.

"I was supposed to take my children to the market on Sunday, but unfortunately the weather played a spoilsport. So, I have come here today to buy firecrackers and candles," said Sarbani Saha, a resident of Dhakuria.

Heading: Coal India to go for new ventures, aims for global status: Chairman - Indian Express
Content:
With 2,242 Kali Puja pandals across the city, the Kolkata police and the Fire Service Department are on high alert to make sure that there are no mishaps during the festival.

Apart from Kolkata, surrounding areas like Barasat and Dum Dum have some of the biggest puja pandals.

Till Monday afternoon, the Fire Department had permitted 4,843 puja committees to erect pandals all over the state.

"We usually divide the city and its neighbouring areas into three zones — A, B and C. Our method of dividing the city is very different from that of the Kolkata police. Since Monday is the last day for getting the permission for erecting puja pandals, we expect the number of pandals in and around Kolkata may increase, as many committees are still approaching us for the permission," Gopal Bhattacharya, Director of Fire Services, said.

This year, Bhattacharya said, puja committee members were given special training on following the fire safety norms in pandals. According to the director, the puja committee members were trained at the Institute of Fire Safety at Mohammed Ali Park.

"This year, we have asked puja committees to use tin sheets, instead of tarpaulin sheets that are normally used for the roofs of pandals. Tin is safer against firecrackers." Bhattacharya said.

Besides these, the Fire Department will also be stationing fire tenders in eight police stations in the city to take care of any emergency situation arising during the festival.

The department is working with the Kolkata police to ensure that people do not burst banned crackers. Both the Kolkata police and the Fire Department will keep strict vigil on multistoried buildings. The police have built watch towers to keep tabs on these buildings.

Heading: Pollution board ultimatum to 31 industries to bring down emissions - Indian Express
Content:
After becoming the 18th public sector undertaking to have achieved the 'Navratana' status on October 24, the Coal India Limited (CIL) wants to go for new ventures in foreign countries as part of its investment plan.

"We want to become a global company," said CIL chairman Partha Bhattacharya, adding that he is in talks with a few companies in Australia and CIL has plans to acquire coal fields in Europe and Africa.

"While there are some mines which are up for outright sale, there are others which allow equity participation. We are looking at both the options," Bhattacharya said.

The company is also planning to acquire 1 lakh to 75,000 acres of coal mines throughout the country in the 11th Five Year Plan.

The status empowers the largest coal-producing company in the world to have administrative as well as economic autonomy.

Unlike earlier, when all the policy decisions were taken by the Cabinet Committee of Economic Affairs, now this power will be delegated to the board of directors of CIL.

The Navaratana status also allows the coal company to take up projects up to Rs 1,000 crore, including investments in other countries.

The Navratana status also gives the CIL the autonomy to decide on affairs of all its subsidiaries, including Eastern Coalfield Ltd (ECL) and Bharat Coking Coal Ltd, which are under the purview of the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR).

According to the CIL chairman, the company has aggressive plans of reviving these two companies, including the expansion of Chupervita, Hura and Sonpur Bajari coal mines under ECL.

The CIL, with two of its sick sister concerns, has surpassed last year's production in the period April to September 2008.

"Compared to the last year, we have had a growth of more 6.93 per cent. We are also hopeful that the production this year will be higher than the last year," Bhattacharya said.

The company will also put emphasis on more joint ventures for extraction of coal. "We have already asked for the letters of expression of interest from companies to excavate coal from abandoned mines. We will encourage more joint ventures in the future," the CIL chairman said.

With the new status, the CIL has to withdraw its shares on the stock exchange through an initial public offering within the next three years. The company plans to offer its shares to land losers from whom it will acquire the land for coal mining.

Power dept mulls importing coal
The tussle between the state Power Department and Coal India Limited (CIL) continued even as the Power Department was contemplating importing about 1 lakh tonne of coal to provide fuel for its thermal power plants for about a month.

Earlier, the CIL had refused to increase the supply of coal for the thermal power plants of the state. Despite repeated requests by the West Bengal Power Development Corporation Limited (PDCL), the CIL is not sending extra coal. "The coal supply has not improved," said S Mohanty, chairman of PDCL.

There has been a shortage of coal for the thermal power plants in the state. The difference between the supply and demand of coal is about 10,000 tonnes a day, said PDCL sources. This has resulted in eroding the stock of coal at the power plants.

The Power Department has decided to import extra coal from Australia and New Zealand. "We are planning to import about 1 lakh tonne of coal. This should be enough to tide over the next month," Mohanty said.

The imported coal is generally of a better quality with very little ash content and a high calorific value.

The Power Department officials, however, did not give a specific time frame when the coal would reach its plants. CIL authorities refused to comment on the issue.

Heading: Muralitharan likely to play for Bengal in Ranji opener - Indian Express
Content:
The glitterati of Kolkata have chosen to keep things quiet this Diwali

No boisterous parties, no ostentatious display of wealth and very little gambling. Air kissing, social networking and revelries will take a backseat this Diwali as the glitterati of Kolkata settle for a muted Diwali. "How can we celebrate during such dismal times? With Singur and the slump in market, there is very little to celebrate this year," says Arijit Dutta, film distributor and owner of the Priya Cinema. Usually Dutta and his friend are flooded with Diwali party invitations this time of the year but this year things are different. "I have hardly received any invitations. Not many people are in the mood to celebrate it seems," says fashion designer Agnimitra Paul. While many have cancelled their Diwali parties, others have chosen to keep it a small affair.

The celebrations at the Russi Mody household too will be a muted affair. "I will host a few friends for dinner and then we will burst some crackers. No gambling for us this year," says Mody. Recession, the Singur imbroglio and the rains have dimmed this year's celebrations considerably. Gambling, which is an essential part of any Diwali celebration will be little more than a necessary evil at most dos this year. "Generally, people gamble like crazy during Diwali. But I plan to stay away from gambling this season. In fact, my husband and I have decided to spend a night away from the celebrations at the Tollygunge Club this Diwali," says Rita Bhimani, corporate public relations expert, and one of the city's most prominent socialites.

The scene was quite to the contrary last Diwali, when Bhimani rushed from one party to another. "Generally we don't have the time to settle down in one party. Even before we finish a drink in one, it's time to leave for another party. People would party till wee hours of the morning," adds Bhimani. People are most likely to call it a night early this year. "It is almost vulgar to celebrate at a time when so many people have made such huge losses," sums up Dutta.

Heading: High Styles, Low Times - Indian Express
Content:
The Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB) is trying hard to get Muttiah Muralitharan's service from the very first match of the Ranji Trophy. Bengal, being relegated to the Plate Group of the championship, will start their campaign against Assam from November 3. According to the CAB joint-secretary Arun Mitra, the Sri Lankan spin doctor will play from the very first match if he is available. The CAB roped in Muralitharan after the BCCI took a decision to allow overseas players to play in the Ranji Trophy.

International commitments shouldn't be a problem for the offie though. Sri Lanka will embark on Zimbabwe trip in the third week of November and will play their first match on November 21. So, for the Ranji lung opener at least, Muralitharan is likely to be available.

The Bengal selectors today, however, announced a 14-member squad for first two matches sans the Sri Lankan. Laxmi Ratan Shukla will lead the team, and if Murali comes, the squad will be of 15 members.

Squad: Laxmi Ratan Shukla (captain), Rohan Banerjee, Anushtup Mazumdar, Srivatsa Goswami, Manoj Tiwari, Riddhiman Saha, Subham Bose, Sourashish Lahiri, Ritam Kundu, Irish Saxena, Ranadeb Bose, Shibshankar Paul, Ashok Dinda and Aveek Chowdhury.

Heading: Seeds have it easy in sub-junior tennis - Indian Express
Content:
With plummeting stocks, a jittery economy and the fear of a bomb blast in every market, there's little to cheer this Diwali season. Despite the generally bleak scenario, Tod's, the quintessential Italian leather brand, formally launched its first store at the Capitals. Champagne flowed as the 100-odd guests mingled, marvelling at the bags, shoes and belts, mostly priced at over Rs 50,000.

"So far, our expansion plans haven't changed, but, of course, we're anxious about how things will play out," said Sabine Altmann of Tod's. Bipasha Basu, clad in a purple dress and black belt, made a fleeting stopover to light the lamp and quickly survey the products. Other guests included socialites Ameeta Seth and Tanisha Mohan, who walked out with a tussle bag for Rs 78,000. We spotted the ubiquitous Tikka Shatrujit Singh examining some dazzling accessories for men. When rich Indians tighten their belts, it just goes down a notch or two; from ostrich skin to faux leather.
