Heading: Will Vaghela’s apparel park give him a foothold in Gujarat? - Indian Express
Content:
Pranav Chopda, the taller half of India's boys doubles pair at the World Junior Championships here, remembers how he once left the door key inside the latched room at their hotel base in Indonesia. India's junior singles No 2 Aditya Prakash then had to climb a ladder and enter through a window to let them all in.

The tale was to repeat on-court many times, as Prakash and India's stars in singles hauled them back into contention, on way to the hosts' fourth-place finish in the team event of the World Juniors — India's best-ever.

Cheering vociferously for their mates on court, passing on hurried tips, even defending India's bloopers in doubles, this team, like coach P Gopichand commented, stayed together and fought together.

The bonding though wasn't whipped up over a couple of days of competition. It can be traced back to the last seven months — to the ABC Championship in Malaysia, their first international meet together, where the boys and girls would sit separately hardly talking to each other. The bunch then went onto 70-day long camps in two parts to Indonesia, where away from homes and with nothing but badminton training to focus on, team mates turned into friends. And finally, coming here to Pune's Youth Commonwealth Games, the bonding was in full flow, as Indians picked a clutch of medals.

Bonding on tour
Saina Nehwal joined the group only for tournaments, but less as the star of the team, more the senior pro whose focus and preparation methods were to be quietly observed and followed.

But for the other dozen, it's been a year where they spent longer travelling with the camp mates than staying home. "The whole year, I've just been with them. When we wrap up everything and go home after a long time on November 3, I think all of us will be quite sad," says Sikki Reddy.

In that period, they've spent several Sundays in Indonesia, playing pranks on each other, getting to know their team mates in harmless banters, and even improving the Hindi accents of the southern players. "Friendships matter, because you get used to doing things with the team," says Chopda.

Heading: Now, ABVP on police radar - Indian Express
Content:
Union Minister to bring much-hyped project to Godhra, fuels speculation that he will contest LS elections from here

Union Minister Shankersinh Vaghela's announcement on Sunday to set up an apparel park at Godhra in central Gujarat is being interpreted by political analysts as part of his move to contest the next general elections from the Godhra parliamentary constituency.

Analysts feel that Vadodara would have been the best place for an apparel park, and selecting Godhra for one of the eight apparel parks to be set up in the state appears to be an attempt to nurture the area for political gains.

Sources in the Congress say that after losing his parliamentary constituency of Kapadvanj in the delimitation exercise, the best option for Vaghela is Godhra.

They said that Patan and Gandhinagar may also be considered, but Godhra is the safest bet for him keeping in view the strong base of the Congress in the region and Vaghela's rapport with the people at grassroots level there.

Party sources said that both Patan and Gandhinagar will be tough constituencies for Vaghela. The party has a weak presence in Patan and BJP's prime ministerial candidate L K Advani is contesting from Gandhinagar. In the past, both T N Seshan and Rajesh Khanna have lost with big margins from Gandhinagar against Advani.

Under the circumstances, Godhra seems to be the only option left for Vaghela, the only one among the state Congress leaders to match the stature of Chief Minister Narendra Modi and offer him a challenge.

Post-Godhra, when the Congress was in shambles with most of its leaders having withdrawn into their shells and keeping their mouth shut against Modi, it was Vaghela who was handed over the charge of the state unit. He challenged Modi with the support of his Shakti Dal. However, it is a different matter that the Congress lost the 2002 Assembly elections, which was fought amid deep communal polarisation.

The four of the seven assembly seats forming the Godhra parliamentary constituency now with the Congress and the Nationalist Congress Party, and the return of the tribals to the Congress fold, is said to be another reason for Vaghela to move to Godhra.

In fact, a public meeting organised by him in the tribal heartland of Devgadh Baria on the eve of December 2007 elections was reported to be the biggest gathering in the recent political history of the state.

Out of the five parliamentary election victories of Vaghela, he won two — 1977 and 1991— from Godhra. However, in 1996, he lost the seat and his political adversaries, including Keshubhai Pate, within the BJP were blamed for his debacle. When the opportune moment came, Vaghela rebelled against Keshubhai in 1996 and became the Chief Minister for a brief period in 1997 with the support from the Congress and the Janata Dal. Though he joined the Rashtriya Janata Dal subsequently, he later moved to the Congress in 1999.

Heading: Five accused in Delhi blasts now in remand of crime branch - Indian Express
Content:
Some members of saffron party's student body summoned for questioning

After saffron outfits like the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), Bajrang Dal and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), it is now the Akhil Bharthiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) — BJP's student wing — which has come under the scanner of Sabarkantha police, investigating the September 29 Modasa blast.

Deputy Superintendent of Police K K Mysorewala said on Monday: "We have summoned some active ABVP members. This is to record their statements in connection with the probe." He, however, refused to name the persons summoned.

In the near month-long investigation, the police have so far recorded the statements of 500-odd people. "Over 200 of them are Hindu, including people associated with the VHP, the Bajrang Dal and the RSS in Modasa," said Mysorewala.

He added: "But let me clarify that these people were questioned because of their past records and not on the grounds of their association with any organisation. We have also questioned around 300 Muslims here, including those associated with Islamic outfits."

Sources in the Sabarkantha police said the arrest of Sadhavi Pragya Singh Thakur from Surat and claims by the Mumbai police over the involvement of Indore-based Hindu Jagran Manch in the Malegaon and Modasa blasts, might be the reason behind summoning ABVP members.

The 15-member team probing the blast case are counting on two things— finding an eyewitness who might have seen the accused person(s) parking the bomb-laden motorcycle and the success of the forensic experts to decipher and trace the original chassis number of the vehicle to its owner.

"Unfortunately, we could not be lucky in either of the two," said an inspector associated with the probe. About the Mumbai police's claim to have solved both the Malegaon and Modasa blasts, Mysorewala said, "We will contact them soon."

Meanwhile, accusing the police of inaction in a 'politically motivated' blast in Modasa, Sabarkantha Congress MP Madhusudhan Mistry said: "I had forwarded the names of the three suspects to the Sabarkantha police, but they did nothing. If the accused of the Ahmedabad serial blasts can be arrested in no time, why the delay in the Modasa case?"

The blast near a mosque in Sukka Bazaar had claimed the life of a 15-year-old boy and injured several others ahead of Eid.

Heading: Relative shock: Man kidnaps his wife’s brother for ransom - Indian Express
Content:
DCB gets their custody for probing their role in the July 26 blasts in Ahmedabad

The Ahmedabad police on Monday got the remand of five alleged members of the Indian Mujahideen in connection with the July 26 serial blasts. The five were in the custody of the Delhi Police for their alleged role in the September 13 blasts in the National Capital.

An Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) team took their custody at a metropolitan court in Delhi, where the local police produced them in the morning on the completion of their 12-day custody. The accused have been identified as Mohammed Saif, Zia-Ur-Rehman, Mohammed Shakeel, Shaquib Nisar and Zeeshan Ahmed.

Abhay Chudasma, Deputy Commissioner, DCB said, "They will be brought to Ahmedabad and produced before a local court soon."

During their interrogation by the Delhi Police, the accused had reportedly confessed to having been involved in the Ahmedabad blasts also.

Following this, the Gujarat Police moved an application before the Delhi metropolitan court, seeking transit remand of the five. The DCB said their names surfaced during the interrogation of the 27 accused of the Ahmedabad blasts, who are currently in its custody.

While Saif was arrested immediately after the September 19 encounter at Jamia Nagar, Zeeshan was arrested later that day from the Jhandewalan area in central Delhi where he had gone to give an interview to a private TV channel. A day later, Mohammed Shakeel, Zia-Ur-Rehman and Saquib Nissar were arrested from south Delhi.

All five have been booked under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code, the Explosive Substances Act and the Prevention of Unlawful Activities Act.

Heading: King’s family goes astray from pride land - Indian Express
Content:
12-year-old victim rescued by Surat police, accused arrested

A Harinagar residents kidnapped his minor brother-in-law and demanded ransom from his father-in-law for the safe release of the boy. However, the police rescued the boy from Varachha on Sunday and arrested three people in this connection.

The police said that on Friday, 12-year-old Rujal Mistry, a resident of Thakore Deep Society in Udhna Magdalla Road, was on his way to the nearby ice-cream shop with his brother in-law Kailash Kumawat, a resident of Harinagar in Udhna, when two persons, identified as Dinesh Bhargav and Mukesh Parekh, intercepted them. They took them to a room at Ghanshyam Nagar in Varachha on gunpoint .

Dinesh then called Rujal's father Omprakash Mistry, a building contractor by profession, and informed him about the abduction of the two. He demanded a ransom of Rs 2 lakh for their safe release.

Omprakash checked at his house and learnt that Kailash and Rujal had left the home and did not return. He later contacted the police and lodged a complaint of kidnapping.

The police started investigating the phone number on Omprakash's mobile phone and found that the call was made from Udhna. When the kidnapper called Omprakash on his cellphone for the second time and told him to deliver the money at Udhna Darwaja junction to a man on Sunday afternoon, the police located the number to an STD booth in Varachha.

The police maintained a watch at Udhna Darwaja junction in civil clothes along with Omprakash, who was carrying the cash in his hands. When Mukesh appeared before him for the cash, the police caught him. During interrogation, Mukesh disclosed that Kailash was also involved in the crime.

The police asked Mukesh to make a call to Dinesh and inform him that the money has been received. Later, the police conducted raids at Ghanshyamnagar in Varachha with Mukesh and rescued Rujal. They arrested Dinesh and Kailash.

Umra Inspector R S Patel said, "Kailash had taken loans from his family and was unable to pay it back. He had married Sapna, Rujal's elder sister, two years ago."

Heading: Now, apply online for licence to drive - Indian Express
Content:
Villagers near Gondal town spot lion, lioness and two cubs

A pride of lions, including two cubs, has come out of their natural habitat in the Gir Forests and reached the outskirts of Gondal town in Rajkot, some 150 kilometres away. A few years ago, one lion had reached the Kotda Sangani village after crossing several grasslands.

The news of the transit of the big cats from the forests to a human habitation has now raised the eyebrows of environmentalists.

Rajkot Deputy Conservator of Forest G.S.Wadi said the villagers of Panchyavadar informed them that some wild animal had killed cow and a calf at two different places near Gondal town. "First we thought it must be a leopard or a hyena, but when our forest team reached the scene, it was confirmed that this was the handiwork of a lion pride. Some villagers also confirmed that they saw a lioness and two cubs near their fields. From the pugmarks, our team has confirmed a lion, a lioness and two cubs."

Conservator of Forest Bharat Pathak said: "After we were informed by the team of the Rajkot DFO, we sent in two teams, one from Junagadh and one from Dhari, to catch the pride. Till Sunday night, our teams were following the lions. We will catch them soon. We are assuming that this pride must have come from the Dhari-north side forest." "A week earlier, we had received information that this pride was located somewhere near the Bhesan area. Our teams have set two cages near the Gondal town on the Jamkandorna Road. Until now, the animals have not attacked any humans; just made two-three kills in the vicinity of Gondal," Pathak added.

Incidentally, after news spread that a pride of lions has come into the area, people started gathering enthusiastically in a bid to see the big cats, which is now causing inconvenience to the foresters to sight and catch them.

Heading: Saurashtra faces severe shortage of fertiliser - Indian Express
Content:
NIC selects Ahmedabad RTO for launching pilot project

A long wait and serpentine queues at Road Transport Offices (RTOs) across Gujarat will soon be a thing of the past. For, the State Transport authorities have mooted a proposal to introduce online registration of applications for learning licence by vehicle owners/drivers on the lines of passport offices.

The National Informatics Centre (NIC), Hyderabad, which is developing a special web-based module for the registration of learning licences, has selected the Ahmedabad RTO for launching this project on a pilot basis.

"The project will be the first of its kind in the country. The NIC today informed us that the Ahmedabad RTO has been selected for introducing this project on a pilot basis. The NIC team is busy developing a web-based learning licence registration module that is likely to roll out by February next year," State Transport Commissioner S J Haider told Newsline on Monday.

Haider said that if the Ahmedabad experiment succeeds, an online registration of applications using the same software could be introduced in rest of the RTOs in Gujarat. This module is expected to help vehicle owners obtain learning licence quickly and without facing any hassles.

Ahmedabad Regional Transport Officer Atul Gor said that after an online registration is done by vehicle owners, the RTO would give them a specific date and time to pay the registration fees at the office and also appear for the driving test.

The entire exercise will take just 40 minutes or so to issue learning licences, Gor said, adding, "Under the existing system, it takes at least six hours to complete this procedure that involves filling and checking of application forms, registration of documents, the use of biometric machine and conducting driving test."

"Once we succeed in implementing this project, the Ahmedabad office may introduce online registration of applications for issuing 'pucca' driving licence to vehicle owners as part of a pro-people approach our department has adopted," he added. At present, the Ahmedabad office issues nearly 300 learning licenses daily.

Heading: Clean Diwali: Awareness rises, pollution level dips - Indian Express
Content:
Severe shortage of fertilisers in some parts of Saurashtra led to a chakka jam in Visavadar town, while a minor skirmish was reported among the farmers in front of a fertiliser depot at Ambalash village in Talala taluka. No major untoward incident has been reported so far and adequate police force has been deployed at both the places.

According to the police, angry farmers staged a chakka jam on the Visavadar-Kalsari Road for three hours. The police rushed to the spot and brought the situation back to normal.

Elsewhere, fertiliser was sold at the Ambalash village depot under police protection. But due to the huge gap in demand and supply, a minor scuffle ensued, as many farmers were unable to get the fertiliser, and the sale was postponed.

According to the farmers, the demand for fertiliser rise to 400 tonnes during the winter. In the current season though, only 35 to 40 tonnes of stock, hardly 10 per cent of the total demand, reached the depot. Since the last couple of months, fertiliser containing DAP (Di-Ammonium phosphate) and NPK (sodium phosphorus potash) has disappeared from the market.

Due to the short supply of manure, whatever stock has been received in the region is now being sold under police protection. Officials have, however, said that during the next 15 days adequate stock of fertiliser will be arriving, which will be enough to satisfy the demand.

Harshad Ribadiya, Congress leader from Visavadar town, said: "Farmers were queuing up for the last five days for fertiliser. In spite of the long wait, they did not get the required fertiliser."

He alleged that during the BJP rule, farmers could not even get fertilisers on time. The Congress has submitted a memorandum to the mamalatdar in this regard and warned that unless the situation improves, the party will resort to a stern agitation.

Heading: City hospitals ready with healing touch - Indian Express
Content:
Sale of firecrackers drops to an all-time low as people show a preference for smoke-free festival

Come Diwali and what we get along with brilliant lights, firecrackers, sweets and new clothes, is pollution. To cite an example, the level of respirable suspended particulate matter (RSPM), which had dropped to 82 micro-grams per cubic metre in 2008 as compared to 198 micro-grams per cubic metre in 2001, is expected to reach 150 just after Diwali.

This despite claims by the Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) that there has been a decline in pollution levels because of several initiatives taken by it. K C Mistry, Regional Officer, GPCB, Ahmedabad, said: "Pollution levels are definitely going down with increased public awareness and participation. There are reports of firecracker sales reaching an all time low." He said a reason for this drop has been that more and more schools, residential societies, social organisations and environment activists are advocating a pollution-free Diwali.

The most air polluting substances during the festive season are the oxides of nitrogen, sulphur dioxide and the particulate matter. GPCB has said that the permissible levels are 80 microgram per nanometre cube.

Mistry said the 17 Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations spread across the city will continuously monitor the level. The GPCB will also spread awareness about 'firework pooling'.

"People resort to car pools to save fuel and reduce pollution. Similarly people from one residential complexes pooling together for firecrackers and enjoying them at a common place should be encouraged," he added.

Taking note of the Supreme Court norm about the permissible level of sound pollution, the GPCB is all set to ensure the 125 decibel (db) at 4 metres from the point of bursting crackers. Last year, 114 db was recorded and this year the GPCB plans to carry out random checks to in this regard.

Some Dos

* Ensure adult supervision when children burst firecrackers

* Fireworks should be used only on an empty ground with no combustible or inflammable material around

* Use a candle or agarbatti to light firecrackers

* Keep a bucket of water or fire extinguisher nearby to prevent any untoward incident

* Aerial fireworks should be used only on open landing areas

* Only one person should light one firework at a time. Others should watch it from a safe distance

* In case of major burns, after extinguishing the fire, remove all smouldering clothes. Wrap the victim in a clean bed sheet

Some Dont's

* Do not tie electric lights to metal poles

* Do not keep the fireworks in the open. Keep it away from the reach of children, animals and any heat source

* Avoid wearing silk or clothes made of inflammable materials

* Don't play with fireworks

* Don't light aerial fireworks if there is heavy wind

* Don't ignite fireworks in any container

* Don't wear loosely hanging clothes; secure all clothes properly

Heading: Ignore ‘terrorist’ allegations against Sardar Patel, says Guv - Indian Express
Content:
108 emergency service fortifies its fleet of ambulances to tackle any eventuality

Apart from a lot of sparkle and noise, another element associated with Diwali is a surge in the number of medical emergency cases. With less than 24 hours to go for the festival of lights, all the major medical institutions in the city claim to have geared up to tackle burn and firecracker-related accidents.

The 108 emergency service has roped in three extra ambulances to tackle any situation.

Kaushal Patel, district manager of Emergency Management and Research Institute (EMRI), said: "At present, we have 21 ambulances operating in Ahmedabad city. Although last year there wasn't much awareness about the 108 services, this year we are expecting the number of road traffic accidents reported to us to increase by 20 percent along with other emergencies. We are confident of handling the surge in the number of emergency cases during Diwali."

Two of the city's biggest general hospitals, the Civil Hospital and V S Hospital are confident of aptly handling any emergency situation.

Civil Hospital superintendent MM Anchaliya said, "Although there has been no marked increased in the number of emergency cases during Diwali in the last couple of years, the plastic surgery and the Burns Department will remain open 24 hours."

He further said the hospital had successfully managed the emergency situation during the serial blasts in July.

V S Hospital Deputy Superintendent U B Shah said the leave of all resident doctors have been cancelled, while medicines and surgical materials have been stocked up. "Even the professional staff will be available round the clock," he added.

State secretary of the Indian Medical Association Bipin M Patel said that on Diwali, at least 50 per cent doctors in the city would work round the clock.

Heading: ASI may block BRTS elevation - Indian Express
Content:
Governor Naval Kishore Sharma has said that allegations being hurled from certain quarters against Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel that he was a "terrorist" deserves no response.

He was speaking at a function to mark the release of the Hindi version of Sardar Patel– Ek Sinh Purush originally written in Gujarati by Dr Rizwan Qadri.

Sharma said that people like Sardar Patel and Mahatma Gandhi should occupy the centre stage and not the political parties.

He emphasised on the need for a full-fledged syllabus on Patel's life in universities instead of the current practice of dedicating a chapter or two on him.

Assembly Speaker Ashok Bhatt and Union Minister of State for Petroleum Dinsha Patel also spoke on the occasion.

The book, priced at Rs 300, has been published by the Gurjar Granthratna Karyalaya. Nearly 2,500 copies of the Gujarati version had been sold over three years and its third edition is on the cards, said Dr Qadri, a research scholar of history, who teaches at the Swaminarayan Arts College.

Heading: It’s recession time at IIM-A Insight-2008 - Indian Express
Content:
2-km corridor passes through half-a-dozen protected monuments

As the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system heads towards the completion of a part in the first phase, more difficult phases ahead are also closing in on the project, along with its progress.

A major roadblock is likely to be the construction of elevated corridor from the New Cloth Market near Raipur to Dariapur Gate. The two-odd km elevated corridor will pass through as many as half a dozen Centrally-protected monuments. They are the Sarangpur Darwaja, Shaking Minarets of Sidi Bashir Mosque near the railway station, Panchkuva Gate, Shaking Minarets near the old DRM Office, Kalupur Darwaja, Prem Darwaja and Dariapur Darwaja.

Under the existing rules, there is a blanket ban on modern constructions and repairs of old buildings in the 100-metre vicinity of such monuments.

Shivanand Rao, Superintending Archaeologist of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), said he had no knowledge of any AMC plans for the construction of the elevated corridor. "Before starting the work, the AMC authorities will have to seek permission from the ASI Director-General.

The application for necessary permission will have to be routed through the Gujarat office, he said, adding that the permission could not be taken for granted and in the absence of any such authorisation, it would be illegal.

D Thara, the director of JNNURM projects in the city, said the elevated corridor would have to be built to facilitate a smooth traffic in the congested area through which it is proposed to pass. She said the AMC is planning to build just a road, and not a heavy structure.

"We are still studying various options," she said, adding that the necessary permission will be taken from the concerned authorities at an appropriate time. Talks with the railway authorities will also be held to work out the suitable time for the closure of the road for carrying out the construction work, she said.

Heading: Crime Branch busts gangs of auto-lifters; recovers vehicles worth Rs 5.5 lakh - Indian Express
Content:
Drastic dip in footfall leaves organisers a harried lot

'Insight-2008,' the 'Consumer Marker Research Fest' of the Indian Institute of Management –Ahmedabad, witnessed a drastically reduced footfall of 2,000 compared to last year's 8,000. For the students who had organised the fest, it was an unexpected shock.

Partho Pratim Das, in-charge of Corporate Communications, who has been tracking the footfalls at the institute, said: "The number of people visiting the fest has dropped significantly even though we had made full attempts at wide-scale publicity. In fact, the publicity was good in all terms. It is around 1,800 to 2,000 this year; while last year the footfall was around 8,000."

The organisers had a tough time roping in participant companies. Many companies backed out at the last moment, while many others wanted to play it safe. Nevertheless, the organisers were able to secure an almost equal number of projects as last year.

Organisers believe a major reason for such a low response by both participant companies and the public is the market downturn.

"Apart from the very obvious effect of the market downturn, this year the fest had been organised quite close to Diwali, which also seems to have affected the participation as in earlier years the fest was organised at least at a week's gap from Diwali," said Pratik Agarwal, event coordinator. "The fest was on Dhanteras day, but anyways, we definitely did not predict such a response," said Partho.

Heading: Essaying a turnaround: Murder convict shows his literary side - Indian Express
Content:
The Local Crime Branch (LCB) of Banaskantha busted two gangs of auto-lifters during a special patrolling in the area to maintain law and order during Diwali, on Sunday.

In the first incident, the LCB team nabbed a member of a gang that operated in the Mehsana-Patan-Sabarkantha region, and seized vehicles worth Rs 5.5 lakh. In the other incident, they caught three persons with a stolen jeep.

LCB Inspector J G Saiyed said, "The Deputy Superintendent Police had directed us to patrol the area ahead of Diwali. We started patrolling around 12 in the noon, and arrested the four between 3 and 4 pm."

Saiyed said that after preliminary investigation, they came to know that the thieves are three in number. "But we suspect the involvement of many more," he added. "This looks like an organised racket operating in north Gujarat. Two of the gang members used to steal the vehicles, while the one caught (Shantu Thakarda) sold them through touts in other areas. Shantu had no knowledge about the whereabouts of the other two."

Deputy Superintendent of Police, Banaskantha, D N Patel said they suspect the root to be much deeper as none of the stolen vehicles were from Banaskantha.

Shantu was arrested from Dhaniyala Chowkri near Palanpur, while three others — Dilwar Khan Parmar, Lashkar Mir and Mehpatsinh Chauhan — were caught with a jeep. The vehicle was stolen at gunpoint near Harivoi jungle. All the four were later produced before the Danta Civil Court on Sunday, which sent them to police remand till October 30.

A total of eight vehicles, including a Tata 407 tempo and seven motorcycles (two Bajaj Discover, one Hero Honda Passion, one Bajaj Pulsar and three Bajaj Splendor), were recovered from the gang.

Heading: Slack Surat cops pulled up for sloppy probe in murder case - Indian Express
Content:
Manoj Patel, a murder convict serving life sentence in the Vadodara Central Jail since 2002, surprised scholars with his write up in a recent essay competition on the topic of the 'Future of Gujarati language'.

Patel, much to the surprise of the judges, highlighted Mahatma Gandhi and globalisation together in his piece, debunking the stand taken by saffron thinkers on the influence of the western languages on Gujarati. He won Rs 1,000 and a certificate as a consolation prize at the event organised by Bruhattar Gujarati Samaj, Mumbai

Deepak Mehta, a retired professor of Gujarati literature from Bombay University, who was a part of the jury, said Patel could have been a fresh face of the global Gujarati literature.

"He states in his essay, that now, one cannot blame an educated Gujarati for picking up an English novel by saying it is a foreign language. For, it is a globalised world and everyone has the right to learn, understand and speak any language," said Mehta. He further quoted Patel as saying in the essay, "We have come a long way from criticising Lord Macaulay and what the British rule did to the country. It is a passé. But at the same time, one should not forget their mother tongue."

Mehta, who judged his essay at the competition, said he was not aware of Patel's identity. "I just knew that a prisoner from Vadodara Central Jail has written the essay, as Patel himself stated that he is a 'pucca' prisoner. All the pages were checked by the jail superintendent," said Mehta.

He further said that the Bruhattar Gujarati Samaj has sent the copies written at the event for publication as a book.

"We had participants from all over the world writing about the future of the Gujarati language. Therefore, we are publishing the book," said Mehta.

Although jail officials refused an audience with Patel (prisoner no. 76564), they said he is one of the well-behaved prisoners.

"From participating in all kinds of activities, to reading all the newspapers, Patel has shown exemplary behaviour as a prisoner of this jail," said Jail Superintendent LV Kharadia. "His interest in essay writing has had a good

effect on other prisoners as well," he added.

According to the jail authorities, Patel had murdered two persons in Silvassa in 2002 over a drunken brawl. He was working in the family business.

The police, however, did not provide any details about his family upon Patel's request.

Heading: MSU initiates dialogue with Durham University for fellowship - Indian Express
Content:
Senior minister censures senior officials for not making any breakthrough in seven months

Surat Rural police have found themselves on a slippery ground in a murder case which has remained undetected for the last seven months now. During the Chief Minister's Swagat programme, a senior minister has pulled up the top brass for showing lethargy in the investigation. The programme deals with the quick resolution of issues in different parts of the state through video conferencing.

According to the FIR filed with the Bardoli police station this April, Ashish Pareek, a resident of Bajipura, was killed between April 6 and April 8, and his body was found near a canal in Vastan village.

After the family came to know about the incident, the irregularities started surfacing. According to Amit, the younger brother of the deceased, one Shehzad Kapadia killed Ashish because of some financial fallout. Besides, Assistant Sub-Inspector Natu Chaudhari and Constable Mahendra Patil of Bardoli police station conducted the last rites without following the formal procedures, thereby destroying the evidences.

The investigation was later handed over to Dangs Deputy Superintendent R P Barot. But Barot's investigation could not throw much light for a long time and the investigation officer was once again changed on May 22. It was handed over to Deputy Superintendent SC/ST Cell H S Ninama.

Amit Pareek said: "We have been pleading for a proper investigation, but our requests have never been properly heard. One of the well-wishers suggested about the online grievance redressal cell in which we applied. During the video conference, which took place on October 23, the minister asked us to initiate a proper investigation."

The minister also immediately pointed out the discrepancies in the case and asked the police to video graph the place of incident, which is the water canal, he added.

Amit said the investigating officers did not file a chargesheet in the case even after so many months. "They give different reasons and seek extension to file the chargesheet, which ideally has to be filed within 90 days."

Surat Superintendent of Police Kesrisinh Bhati said: "We have already conducted some tests on the two main accused and also got some further clues. We had applied for further tests at the Forensic Science Laboratory in Gandhinagar on October 2, and are awaiting the dates."

Meanwhile, Bhati added, the two police personnel from Bardoli police station are under suspension and are at the Kheda Headquarters as per the formal procedure.

Heading: Encore - Indian Express
Content:
Leadership guru Robin Sharma is in Mumbai to dole out more guidance

Some are born leaders. Some acquire leadership. For the acquired lot, particularly in the corporate world, there is Robin Sharma, the author of The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari. This book of wisdom has been a companion to many unobtrusive beings the world over for a decade now.

In this world of cut-throat competition, Sharma's self-mastery books have many takers. In the 10 years, he has churned out as many guidance books.

"My clients are spread across 60 countries. Nearly 80 per cent of them are big companies," he says.

Yet, Sharma is not keen on creating a generation of leaders. He probably believes in instilling leadership qualities in moderate doses.

"Every leader doesn't have to be a CEO. Leadership can happen at any level. Employees should emerge responsible in their respective groups," he says.

When he talks, Sharma doesn't appear very different from his smiling avatar on his books' cover-with a clean-shaven shining pate and his usual black shirt. He appears at peace too.

But that was not the case a decade ago. "It was my quest to find the real meaning of success and happiness that led to writing my first book The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari," he admits. This successful lawyer published the book himself which has changed many lives since, including his own.

However, his conquering of the world has not been total. There is still a community of readers who staunchly stay away from self-help and guidance books. How does Sharma plan to sell his book to them? His answer is stoic: "My goal is not to convert those who are not open to changes. I don't judge them. They are probably the people living in fear, not ready for growth."

The meltdown has many of Sharma's clients panicking. "Stick to your fundamentals, your game-plans," is what he tells them. Then he goes on to add: "Leadership is not shown in easy times."

This 'life coach' follows it up by saying, "Rough seas make better sailors." Such fire and brimstone sentences keep cropping up in our conversation.

But not as much as they appear in his books, which are very smart repackagings of Oriental wisdom and philosophies. Some are very familiar and pithy theories of good living retold.

Sharma, the propagator of leadership qualities, does admit that all these lines are not original. Some are inspired by the books of philosophy, leadership and autobiographies that this voracious reader has been lapping up for years. The rest can be attributed to his life's experience.

At home, the self-help guru is happy to share leadership with his two children. Sharma, who was divorced 10 years ago, considers children to be the greatest teachers, heroes.

After conducting a leadership seminar, hosted by FICCI FLO, last week, the author of Indian origin also launched his book The Greatness Guide II, a sequel to his The Greatness Guide in Mumbai. Next year, the leadership expert is eager to share more tricks of achieving success with his upcoming The Rockstar and the Butterfly.

Heading: Comic Capers - Indian Express
Content:
With two films — Karzz and EMI — hitting the screens within a fortnight, we might hazard a guess that this is Urmila Matondkar's comeback year. But ask Matondkar and the once-Rangeela girl would shrug: "I was never out of the scene. It was just that the scripts were not appealing enough. I don't do films just because I have to be in the limelight."

In EMI, which will be released on November 7, Matondkar plays a widow who needs a personal loan to make ends meet, after her husband commits suicide. "It is very different from my role of a vamp in Karzz," said Matondkar, dressed in a flowing green dress. The actor might not have had a string of box-office hits but has evidently been spared the need to take a loan in real life.

And if she is to be believed, the film has ensured that she will never take one in future. "I never knew there was a thriving underground business of recovery agents," she rolled her eyes in disbelief. Now with two films down, she is all set to let her hair down and go home to celebrate Diwali.

Heading: Politicians, parties pitch wrestlers from city akharas on election mat - Indian Express
Content:
Boman Irani gives suspense a shot with Maharathi, but agrees, comedy is his forte

Actor Boman Irani, 46, is a very busy man these days. With close to seven films (99, Maharathi, Three Idiots, Banda Yeh Bindaas Hai, Teen Patti, Yuvraaj, Little Zizou) lined up for release in the coming months, he has absolutely no time in between shooting schedules and post-production work.

"I should slow down. After all I am still young to the film industry and I have taken on so much work. But I am happy that I have been trusted with vital roles in movie projects. I call it destiny," he states philosophically.

In between 'walking off the ramp' at fashion designer Anita Dongre's show at Wills India Fashion week recently and filming, Irani has little time for anything else.

But he will soon be seen on screen in a small cameo in Karan Johar's Dostana, alongside John Abraham and Abhishek Bachchan.

"I am not too fond of cameos but sometimes its part of being in this industry," says Irani, who was recently in town for the promotion of his film Sorry Bhai. But ask Irani to choose from his line up of movies and he quickly comes up with Maharathi, the Paresh Rawal and Naseeruddin Shah starrer based on a popular Gujarati play by the same name.

It's a murder mystery revolving around a wife's attempt to kill her husband by hiring a hit man. The shooting of the film is complete. "To be cast opposite Naseeruddin Shah is exciting in itself. I have watched his films when I was younger. And I miss the conversations we would share over lunch on the sets of the film," he reminisces.

This thriller is a one-off, says Irani, declaring that comedy will remain his forte.

"I don't like slap stick comedy. I feel there is much more to a situation that just the gag," he says.

These days Irani is busy winding up shooting for 99, based on the secret world of gambling, in which he plays a recovery agent with Kunal Khemu.

Ask him what he misses most from his pre-acting days and Irani responds, "Photography. I carry my camera every where but hardly find time to use it."

Heading: Cong list of 53 not final: changes in the offing - Indian Express
Content:
Sushil Kumar's Olympic medal-winning effort sure did lift the profile of wrestling and the Delhi man may have had politicians lining up for photo-op, but many wrestlers from different city akharas would begin trailing candidates as the Assembly elections draw closer. Not many politicians admit it openly, but many wrestlers with little chance of making the big league are hired by parties and individual candidates as musclemen.

Sharad Chauhan, the Bahujan Samaj Party's Assembly candidate from Narela, says, understandably, that his party has "never needed" the service of these pehelwans. "But I know other parties have used them," he says. "The people who use such tactics do not always win, though. In Delhi, especially, it doesn't work that well. But, yes, parties and candidates do employ musclemen in some localities."

An activist from one of the main political parties (name withheld on request) says, "Pehelwans can be used to force people to vote for our candidate. They (musclemen) sometimes snatch voters' sheets and press the button themselves."

The more famous akharas, though, say their trainees do not participate in such activities. Ranvir Singh Dheka of Captain Chandrup akhara in Model Town says a wrestler, if serious about the sport, cannot afford to join politics. "Our boys are focused on the goal of getting medals," he says. "They won't be able to practice if they start roaming around in jeeps of politicians."

But he admits that politicians often use pehelwans at election times. "Though our boys are strictly focused on practice (at Chandrup akhara), we know that several pehelwans do work with politicians. The retired often even join political parties because they may not find work otherwise."

Wrestlers say job openings for them are few and far between and only a handful earn through the sport. Therefore the eagerness to join up with parties — to earn some quick cash, he says.

Ramesh Malik, an Asian Games silver medalist wrestler who now runs a security agency, says, "Nature bestows a human being either with brains or brawn. A pehelwan has the muscle power but most of us are uneducated."

Many find work as security guards, or as bouncers at nightclubs or go back to their villages. Some, on the other hand, get involved as strongmen for political parties, another wrestler says.

A party worker says the money on offer depends on the prestige and budget of the election. "In Assembly elections, we spend Rs 1 lakh to Rs 2 lakh on hiring the services of pehelwans but it is less than Rs 1 lakh for MCD elections," he says. "Parliamentary elections are a huge event so we may spend between Rs 3 lakh and Rs 5 lakh per constituency. It also depends on the strength of the group that we hire."

Heading: Speed-check cameras hit road block as police, govt fight over tender - Indian Express
Content:
It may be too early for celebrations for the 53 Congress candidates whose names were shortlisted during the party's central election committee meeting on Saturday. For, senior Congress leaders, including Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit, want several names replaced.

Union minister Kapil Sibal and party MP from Karol Bagh Krishna Tirath are also backing Dikshit's decision. Though in a feat of sorts Dikshit managed to push several names of her choice, it seems she is still not happy with the list.

"The final list will be issued by the All India Congress Committee (AICC). Nothing is official right now," Dikshit told Newsline on Monday.

South, West and Outer Delhi will see major reshuffle in the list of candidates, it was indicated.

The final list is expected to be released by the end of this month. A senior Congress leader said "at least" 25 per cent of the names would be replaced. "There are several candidates backed by Ashok Gehlot, Sajjan Singh and J P Agarwal who are likely to be axed from the list now," the leader said.

Of the 49 sitting MLAs, 34 had managed to get their names in the list declared on Saturday. But changes are expected in Sangam Vihar constituency, where Tek Chand Sharma, in mid-70s now, has been fielded. Senior party leaders, though, are reportedly not very happy with his nomination — he was not given a ticket in 2003 as he was considered too old to stand for elections.

Even MLA Mahabal Mishra, credited to have built a Congress base in Palam and Pappankalan areas, could be axed, party leaders said. Mishra's name is part of the 53-candidate list but senior leaders are reported to be reconsidering the decision. Significantly, Mishra had spoken out openly against Sheila Dikshit's leadership in the past.

Similarly in Chandni Chowk, Prahlad Singh Sawhney's name is likely to be replaced. Saini's name was forwarded by Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee but several senior players feel he is a non-performing candidate.

Dissent brewing
Meanwhile, Delhi Congress is facing a rebellion from candidates who could not manage to get their names in the list of the 53 shortlisted candidates. Aspirants from constituencies such as Mundka, Krishna Nagar, Deoli, Sangam Vihar Badarpur, Rajinder Nagar and Rajouri Garden are openly spewing venom against the party brass. Netaji Ram Singh, the former MLA from Badarpur, is leading the pack along with sitting councillors Hemchand Goyal and Rajni Dagar.

The trio resigned from the party on Sunday and even protested in front of the AICC office at 24, Akbar Road. Former NCP MLA Ramvir Singh Bidhuri, who recently joined the Congress, has been fielded from Badarpur.

Netaji Ram Singh today said: "I have been associated with the Congress for the last 25 years and was still ignored by the party leadership. But Bidhuri, who has always switched parties, has been awarded only because he joined the party recently.

"My people are upset with the development."

In Devli, where Congress opted for Harnam Singh, ticket aspirant Rashmi Gangwal led the protests. Similarly, Brahm Yadav and Manish Chatrata organised protests against Ramakant Goswami, who got the nod for Rajinder Nagar constituency. In Rajouri Garden, the party picked former BJP MLA Dayanand Chandel, and the rebellion has run deep with ticket-seeker Dhule Chand Lohiya leading the protest.

In Mundka, the rebellion is led by former councillor Memwati Barmala, Jagdish Yadav and Baldev Barmala. Shambhu Dayal Sharma has got the ticket from Mundka. Aspirants also protested against Independent councillor Deepika Khullar, who has been given the ticket from Krishna Nagar.

Heading: Denied admission after battle with TB, High Court comes to teen’s aid - Indian Express
Content:
Ahead of the Commonwealth Games, the police's plan to put up hi-tech cameras in 18 of the Capital's intersections has been kept on a tight leash by red tape, with the government now asking questions about the tendering process.

Though tenders were issued eight months ago, the government asked the traffic police to issue fresh tenders as it apprehended litigation from the firm which was initially rejected. Since then this project — to install cameras that would have kept speeding in check — has been in limbo.

Global tenders were first floated on October 5, 2007. Four firms responded — Turbo Consultancy Services, Almighty Techserv, Bharat Electronics Limited and Adtech Systems. A technical inspection of their equipment was carried out by the police on January 14. The inspecting panel included police officials, professor at the Indian Institute of Technology M Jagadesh Kumar, the dean of School of Planning and Architecture Professor A K Sharma, and scientist S Velmurgan from the Central Road Research Institute.

Chennai-based Adtech Systems failed to showcase the equipment and was rejected. Turbo Consultancy Service was also overlooked for the poor quality of their supply.

The Delhi Police's purchase committee then opened the financial bid on February 4 this year, after the technical committee nodded at the other two firms — Bharat Electronics and Turbo. Bharat Electronics Limited bid almost 22 per cent less and was given the job on February 14.

However, the government raised its first objection before the procurement process could begin on February 20. Turbo Consultancy Services had objected to the manner in which the tendering was concluded, it said. The Delhi Police asked the government the exact nature of the objection but was told to furnish a certificate which would say: "The successful bidders has met with the technical specification as mentioned in the tender and due process of tendering has been observed in the instant case."

The police issued the certificate on March 18, but the government decided to go for re-tendering on March 31.

Since April, the file has not moved with the police, only words have been exchanged. Additional Commissioner (General Administration) R S Krishnia wrote to the government in May saying: "We can not go for re-tendering merely on the apprehension of litigation." Police sources said each time a tender is issued, the police spends Rs 80,000 on advertisement alone.

Meanwhile, Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) has also knocked on the doors of Lieutenant Governor Tejendra Khanna. The company now plans to drag the government to court, more so because BEL has taken delivery of the cameras from a German firm, sources said.

Till the matter is resolved, Joint Commissioner (traffic) S N Shrivastava said the police will concentrate on the intelligent traffic system — another savvy network of synchronised traffic lights, cameras etc.

Shoppers stop city
Traffic came down to a crawl on several city roads on Diwali-eve. The Ring Road remained choked between Naraina T-point and Brar Square. In West Delhi, traffic crawled between Meera Bagh and Paschim Vihar; in Pitampura, jams stretched from three to four hours. Even New Delhi area, normally free of traffic jams, was clogged as jams were reported from Aurangzeb Road.

Heading: Month on, Jamia panel gets blast suspects ‘good lawyer’ - Indian Express
Content:
At 15, Shaina appears serious for her age. She has every reason to be so after a two year struggle with tuberculosis, followed by a legal battle in Delhi High Court against her government school, which chose to shut its door on her.

The eagerness to pursue her studies has so impressed Justice Vipin Sanghi that in a recent order he highlighted Shaina's case as an example to remind Delhi government authorities that they are "bound to grant admission to every child who seeks admission in a government school".

A Class VI student at Government Girls Senior Secondary School, Yamuna Vihar, Shaina was in the middle of her school hours on February 21, 2005 when she suddenly started bleeding from the mouth and was rushed home. Even earlier, Shaina had missed out on her annual examinations after falling ill. But the gutsy student had got herself re-admitted and was working towards good grades at the time of the incident.

She was detected with acute tuberculosis and got a clean bill of health two years later: on September 7, 2007.

The teenager, however, was in for a shock when the school refused admission despite repeated requests.  "I was certified as having been cured of tuberculosis. But the school in early July 2008 refused me admission," she submitted before Justice Sanghi.

The school chose to remain adamant about not admitting her despite recommendations from the Deputy Director of Education on July 24, 2008. "The Deputy Director sent Shaina back to her school with a recommendation that her case should be considered for admission as per the rules," I R Naqvi, counsel for the student, told the court.

In court, the school did not even bother to respond to notice issued for a written explanation for their conduct.

"The circumstances in which the petitioner (Shaina) could not continue have been sufficiently explained. There is no reason to deny admission to her," the court observed.

The school was directed to re-admit her in Class VI for the 2008-09 academic session. "I will start class as soon as the school reopens after vacations," the young girl said.

"Denying a child admission because she missed two years to undergo treatment is criminal. The court order will act as a precedent," Ashok Aggarwal, a child rights lawyer who represents cases of several government school children, said.

Heading: Constitution Club restaurant finds new customers in poll season - Indian Express
Content:
A month after Jamia Millia Islamia formed a legal aid committee for its arrested students, the committee says its main achievement till date has been providing moral support to family members of the suspects arrested for the September 13 serial blasts and to "facilitate" the process of providing them with good lawyers.

Biswajit Das, part of the three-member committee and also director of the Centre for Culture, Media and Governance at Jamia, said the committee first contacted family members of the suspects and ensured Zia-Ul-Rehman and Shakeel got the services of a good lawyer. Anwar Khan is fighting the case on behalf of the arrested duo.

Rehman and Shakeel are students of the university.

"It was first important to instil confidence among families of the two as they were in tremendous trauma," Das said. "We also worked to ensure that the family members could meet them. Now, they are meeting each other off and on."

The legal aid committee was formed on September 25, after Rehman and Shakeel were arrested on charges of being involved in the serial blasts. Besides Das, professors Radha Kumar and Azra Razzack constitute the committee.

About the university's move to help the students, Biswajit said the committee was never meant to be run on university fund. "The committee was an autonomous body that worked on the premise that the students were innocent until proven guilty," he said. "We did not take a single penny from the university, nor did the legal advisor of the university have anything to do with it.

"We are completely satisfied with our work."

Heading: Cops: No crackers burst after 10 pm last Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
The blank side of a letter written to Rahul Gandhi by a Congressman from Mumbai, stuck on the glass doors, says it's "lunch hour" at Bharatiyam, the "multi-cuisine restaurant" that opened shop on the renovated premises of the Constitution Club a few months ago.

There is an absence of any discernible promotion and the restaurant has not even put up a board outside the Constitution Club. Not surprisingly, it has not seen many customers since it opened eight months ago.

Business, however, picked up recently, thanks to ticket seekers for state elections in the Hindi heartland.

"We are rather popular now, especially since the Delhi polls are around the corner. A whole lot of bureaucrats and politicians have working lunches here. Dinners are more of a family affair," Anil Mathur, general manager at Bharatiyam, said.

Among the regulars, Mathur said, are former Delhi chief minister Sushma Swaraj and former Union minister Rajiv Pratap Rudy. "They often come with their families for dinner," he said.

When Newsline visited Bharatiyam this week at lunch time, the restaurant was in the middle of lunch hour. It is open to everyone, contrary to the popular belief that only members of the Constitution club can dine there.

Rajiv Pratap Rudy, who spearheaded the renovation efforts at the club, said: "I believe a whole lot of non-members have lunch at the club now. This place was a total shack for almost 55 years before we took up the renovation. The purpose was to create a respectable place for Members of Parliament to meet at. It's open to non-members because attendance was initially dismal."

Not so anymore. On any given day one can find safari suits of all hues occupying the tables at Bharatiyam. While most Members of Parliament may choose the fare at the Parliament over the restaurant, many MLAs, ticket-holders from various parties, bureaucrats and even party workers do patronise Bharatiyam. Quite a contrast from a few months ago, when lunch hour catered only to the staff at the club.

Heading: Malhotra slams Sheila govt on power situation - Indian Express
Content:
Even if the fact that no crackers were burst in the Capital after 10 at night last Diwali might seem unlikely, the Delhi Police have said so on record, in a reply to an RTI query.

In December 2007, Dev Ashish Bhattacharya filed an RTI application, asking the Ministry of Home Affairs about the implementation of a judicial order, which states that no cracker should be burst in the Capital between 10 pm and 6 am. The order was passed on July 18, 2005, keeping in consideration the noise and air pollution caused by crackers on Diwali.

Bhattacharya said: "The Supreme Court clearly stated in its order that fire crackers should not be burst from 10 pm to 6 am on Diwali night. The Apex Court also asked the Delhi government to conduct awareness campaigns for residents to make them understand the bad effects of crackers. I, however, have not seen any such thing even when Diwali is around the corner."

Some questions asked by Bhattacharya include: "In how many districts of Delhi was the order implemented by authorities and is the government proposing to fix any accountability on the authorities concerned for their failure to implement the order of the judiciary?"

The application was forwarded to all deputy commissioners of police for answers after reaching Delhi Police headquarters, and most replied that the orders were implemented properly in their districts.

While the then Central District DCP replied that no violation of the order was reported in his district on Diwali in 2007, the then Northwest District DCP said the instructions were forwarded to all station house officers of the district. Other districts too mentioned that the order was implemented in their jurisdictions on Diwali.

Answering a question about which government agencies are responsible for implementing the order, the then DCP (Licensing) replied: "The district police administration and licensing branch are the responsible agencies for implementing the orders of judiciary related to usage of crackers. Being the nodal agency, the licensing branch has circulated the instructions for follow-up to the district police. In addition to the police department, the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) and explosives department in Faridabad are also responsible."

"The DCPs said in reply to my RTI query the order was implemented properly in their areas. I don't think so. Many would not believe that no crackers were burst after 10 pm in the Capital last Diwali."

In a follow-up to last year's RTI query, the applicant filed another application on October 18, 2008, asking the authorities about who would be responsible if crackers are burst after 10 pm in Delhi on Diwali. He also asked whether the Supreme Court appointed any authority to oversee the implementation of the order.

Heading: Govt draws up plan to check pollution - Indian Express
Content:
While electricity has so far remained a non-issue in the run up to the Delhi polls, BJP chief ministerial candidate V K Malhotra slammed the Sheila Dikshit government on Saturday about the "power crisis in Delhi".

The last six years have seen massive reforms in the power distribution structure in the Capital, with distribution being handed over to private players. However, in a statement Malhotra has said the discoms need to take on more accountability, particularly when it comes to meters. "The discoms, which are the owners of the metres, go scot-free and bear no responsibility for defects that develop in the metres without any fault of the consumers." In line with the recent suggestion made by the Electricity Consumers Advocate Committee (ECAC), Malhotra too has asserted that he will look towards ensuring that metres become the responsibility of the discoms alone.

Quoting figures from the media, Malhotra said, "As per figures available from the press, Delhi is currently facing a shortage of 395 MW." He said such a dismal situation during Diwali shows the current government's indifference towards the people. However, according to figures available with the State Load Despatch Centre (SLDC), Delhi is at present under-drawing power from the Northern Grid. Because of pleasant weather conditions, the power situation is "largely under control", a power official said.

A discom official said: "It's not true that we are carrying out powercuts during the festive season. Whatever cuts are there, they are scheduled due to maintenance reasons and uploaded on our websites much in advance for people to see. Moreover, we will ensure that there is no load shedding on Diwali."

Malhotra also added that mishaps and accidents were occurring because "even streetlights have not been functioning properly". While the concerned land owning and municipal agencies are responsible for installation of streetlights, the maintenance rests solely with the discom that functions in that area. "We ensure that adequate repairs are carried out as and when complaints are forwarded to us. Streetlights are a priority and they always get importance as far as maintenance is concerned," a discom official said. However, the dismal condition of street lighting in many areas confirms Malhotra's complaint.

Other power-related issues that have found mention in Malhotra's campaign are the generation capabilities of old power generating plants, such as the Indraprastha power plant and the Raj Ghat power plant. "These plants have not been repaired and are running at a much depleted capacity," he said.

Heading: Speeding trucks leave trail of blood - Indian Express
Content:
With winter expected to set in and Diwali just round the corner, the Delhi government has drawn an action plan to check air pollution in the coming months. In a meeting with Environment Pollution Control Authority Chairman Bhure Lal and member Sunita Narain, and Transport Commissioner R K Verma, Chief Secretary Rakesh Mehta has decided to ensure strict monitoring of diesel generators, used in homes, by the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) for air and noise pollution.

In an effort to ensure that a better monitoring system is in place, officials said that 599 pollution checking centres across the city will be computerised and connected to the environment department. While the government will keep a check on pollution caused by Delhi's two coal-based power stations, IP Station and Raj Ghat Station, the committee has also decided to start an awareness campaign against the burning of dry leaves and will use dry leaves for making compost.

Bhure Lal has also asked for strict directions to be given to toll operators that non-destined vehicles be stopped from entering the Capital. While the government has appealed to residents to avoid bursting crackers, the CPCB will be monitoring air pollution after Diwali to assess the impact of crackers on air pollution.

Heading: Gujarat Police get transit remand for serial blast suspects - Indian Express
Content:
Journey to aiport proves fatal for family, man killed, father-in-law injured by speeding vehicle

A truck rammed a car and a bike, killing the biker and injuring his father-in-law in the car. Police officials said that the incident took place on Mahipalpur road in Vasant Kunj late on Saturday night.

The deceased, Rajender (35) was going to drop his brother-in-law to the airport. His father-in-law, Rai Singh (55) was driving a Maruti 800 car and his son, daughter and wife were in it.

"Around 2 am, a speeding truck hit the bike from behind and then hit the car. The truck dragged the motorcycle at least a 100 metres before it braked. The driver abandoned the truck and fled," a senior police officer said.

A PCR van rushed the victims to AIIMS Trauma Centre where Rajender was declared dead on arrival, while Rai Singh is still admitted in the hospital. His condition is said to be stable.

All vehicles have been impounded. A case of causing death due to negligence has been registered against the driver, who is yet to be identified and arrested.

Rajender lived in Shiv Vihar with his family.

Trucks mow down four in separate incidents
Four persons, including a minor were killed in two separate road accidents in Narela area of Outer district in the last 24 hours, police said. The first incident was reported around 9.30 pm on Sunday night on the Bhorgarh-Alipur road in Narela area. Police said the victims, Rakesh (30) and Raghunandan (40), were heading towards Bhorgarh from Alipur on their bike, when a speeding truck hit them head on. The driver fled the scene, while the bikers died on the spot.

Police said that Rakesh, a resident of Nawada in Narela, was a contractor while Raghunandan who hails from Gaya in Bihar was a labourer.

In the second incident, two persons including a minor, were mowed down by a speeding truck in Narela around 2 pm on Monday.

The duo was on a bike coming from Narela, when the truck hit them from behind, resulting in their death, police officials said.

The deceased have been identified as Deepak (13) and Praveen (20). Both were residents of Swatantra Nagar.

The accused driver fled with the truck.

Heading: 9 years after sack, Tihar driver wins back job - Indian Express
Content:
A city court on Monday gave its nod to Gujarat Police for taking the five suspected terrorists, arrested in connection with Delhi serial blasts, to various places in Gujarat for probing their alleged role in the synchronised terror attacks in Ahmedabad. Allowing the transit remand of all the suspects - Mohammed Saif, Zeeshan Ahmad, Mohammed Shakeel, Zia-ur-Rehman and Saquib Nissar - the magistrate found substance in the contentions of the Gujarat police prosecutor regarding the necessity of their custodial interrogation for gathering vital links in the blast probe.

The Gujarat police had contended that the accused were required for investigations into the blast in Ahmedabad on the evening of July 26, which had claimed 56 lives and left scores of people injured. The transit remand was given for the case registered with Maninagar Police station there. They further submitted that as many as 27 accused had already been arrested in connection with such cases and the names of these five suspects surfaced during the investigation. Meanwhile, Rajasthan Police, also present in the court, sought custody of Mohd Saif, saying the suspect had revealed significant facts about the terror module and the shops from which the cycles, used in carrying out the blasts in Jaipur, were purchased. The magistrate, asking them to move an appropriate application before the court in Gujarat in this regard, however turned down the plea.

The court's order came after the Special Cell officials of Delhi Police told the court that they did not want further custody of the five accused. During the proceeding, the counsel for the accused opposed plea of Gujarat Police saying that the Delhi Police had earlier secured their custodial interrogation only on the ground that the accused were to be taken to various places in Gujarat and Rajasthan. Saif was arrested following the Batla House encounter in Jamia Nagar in South Delhi on September 19 while Zeeshan was arrested on the same evening from Jhandewalan area in Central Delhi where he had gone to give an interview to a private TV channel.

The other three accused - Shakeel, Zia-ur-Rehman and Saquib - were arrested from Shaheen Bagh here on September 20. All the accused have been booked under various provisions of the IPC, Explosive Substances Act and Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

Heading: Last of Bunty’s gang in police net - Indian Express
Content:
Virender Kumar, fired from his job of a driver on the charges of smuggling tobacco into Tihar Jail, will soon be wearing his uniform once again and get back to work, thanks to a judicial order. With the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) quashing the dismissal order by noting that Kumar's termination was bad in law, Tihar Jail authorities have been directed not only to reinstate him but also pay him full back wages and other job benefits since the date of his termination.

The order has come to the rescue of Kumar, left in the lurch following a series of inquiries against him resulting in different findings, spanning a period of nine years. Kumar was held on May 29,1999, while ferrying loaves of bread from Jail number 2 to Jail number 4 for inmates in the official truck. Though his vehicle was thoroughly checked as he entered the premises, on his way back, security personnel searched the truck again.

To his shock, Kumar was told that 200 tobacco packets, hidden under the driver's seat, were recovered from the vehicle. He was subsequently detained and a departmental inquiry ordered. The first inquiry held him guilty of flouting the jail manual and breach of duty. Kumar was dismissed by an order in July 2002.

His subsequent appeal with the jail authority also failed to yield any positive result. However, the tribunal, through an order in 2004, found the inquiry was conducted in an improper manner, as the official, who was a part of the investigation, should not have been the adjudicating authority for deciding the issue.

A fresh inquiry was ordered but it provided no relief to Kumar, as the subsequent authority held the dismissal warranted and necessary in view of his guilt. "Recovery of such a huge quantity of prohibited items, 200 packets of tobacco, clearly indicates the ulterior motive of the official charged for obtaining illegal gratification by smuggling prohibited items into the jail," the appellate body had held, throwing out Kumar's plea.

Kumar approached the CAT again, contending the order was "arbitrary," for it based its findings only on the report of the previous investigation. Finding substance in his arguments, the tribunal said it was not fair on part of the appellate authority to refrain from passing a reasoned and speaking order and deciding the issue on the basis of previous findings.

"It is strange that a finding of guilt has been recorded against the applicant by the enquiry officer by simply rejecting his defence," said the bench headed by Justice V K Bali, who also criticised the authority for not revealing as the grounds on which Kumar's termination justified.

"While the conclusion drawn on its very face may appear to be wholly arbitrary and capricious, and no reasonable person could ever have arrived at such a conclusion, the courts are duty-bound to interfere," said the tribunal in a recent order.

The CAT then allowed Kumar's petition and asked the Government authorities to reinstate him in the service with back wages and other benefits that would accrue to him under the service rules.

Heading: Abducted trader, driver choked to death - Indian Express
Content:
Two months after Delhi Police killed Om Prakash alias Bunty in an encounter, Special Cell on Sunday arrested a key member of his gang, Om Shiv alias Kallu.

Kallu is reportedly a sharpshooter of the gang and was involved in all the firing and robbery incidents with Bunty in the last few months before his death. With Shiv's arrest, officials said all the dreaded members of this gang have been either killed or arrested. Shiv was on the run for the last four months and officials said he was hiding in several states including Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan.

Shiv, 24, a resident of Badarpur, and a good friend of Bunty's brother Sonu came in touch with Bunty in 2006. "Bunty had actually helped him in getting bail on the condition that he would join his gang after release and commit robberies," said Alok Kumar, DCP (Special Cell). Shiv is a sharpshooter and he used to ride pillion on the bike when Bunty and his gang members committed robberies on two bikes in Delhi. "He never hesitated at firing whenever anyone resisted. He was second only to Bunty when it came to firing at the victims," said a police officer.

Bunty and Rajesh Pinni were killed in encounter by the South Delhi Police on August 25 while another member Israel was arrested from Tamil Nadu a few days after the encounter. Nasir was arrested before the encounter.

"The whole gang is finished now. We are trying to verify if Bunty committed more robberies in other states and who were providing him shelter," said a senior police officer. The gang used to commit daylight robberies and the commissioner had to announce a reward of Rs 50,000 on each of its members.

Crimegraph
The gang came shot to notoriety when they killed a vegetable dealer on Hapur Road in April this year.

First week of July: Bunty gang killed one Gurdeep over personal enmity.

06, July: The gang robbed a Pulsar bike in Defence Colony.

11, July: Riding on bikes, they tried to rob a CBZ bike in Lajpat Nagar. When victims resisted, they were shot. After few minutes, they tried to rob another biker at the Andrews Ganj flyover. When a scooterist tried to help the biker, he was shot dead.

12, July: Shiv and others fired at an shopkeeper in Ambedkar Nagar and robbed him.

13, July: The gang robbed a Pulsar bike in Mayur Vihar. The same day they robbed a petrol pump in Sarita Vihar of Rs 60,000.

In following days on July and August, the gang had killed around five persons and 12 robbery cases were registered against them.

Heading: Seven Tihar lifers to walk free on Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
Asphyxia led to the death of an abducted businessman and his driver, the three persons charged with their abduction have revealed to the police.

The South Delhi Police arrested the three accused on Monday after extensive raids across the city.

According to police, the deceased, Ravi Jain, a businessman based in Vasant Kunj, was lured by the accused who promised to supply him gold at a price lower than the market rate.

Tempted by the offer in the height of the festive season, he had gone to Ghaziabad with his driver, Gajraj on October 12.

A case was registered after the daughter of the deceased, Puja Jain, complained that her father had gone missing after he left on a business deal.

Police tracked his movements and found that he had left his Nissan car with one Pankaj (20). He was taken into custody and on sustained interrogation, he admitted he had kidnapped Jain with the help of Shahnawaz (19) and Javed (23).

"Pankaj took Jain inside the banquet hall for the deal while the driver, Gajraj, was waiting outside in the car. Once inside, Jain was overpowered by the accused and his mouth was gagged with surgical tape. After some time Pankaj called the driver inside, where he was also gagged. Jain and Gajraj died of asphyxia," DCP, South, HGS Dhaliwal said.

Police said the accused disposed the dead bodies by in Gang Nahar near Murad Nagar. Pankaj drove down to Delhi in Jain's Nissan car, where he parked it in the Palika Bazar parking lot and abandoned it.

Heading: Three arrested for forgery, preparing fake I-cards - Indian Express
Content:
On rare occasions, prisoners get a taste not only of festivals, but also freedom.

Seven convicts serving life sentences in Tihar Jail got a Diwali gift they will cherish. Two days ago, Lieutenant Governor, Tejendra Khanna, passed an order allowing them to go home.

The prisoners, who have been lodged in jail for many years, need to furnish Rs 10,000 as surety and they will be free forever. Khanna ordered the release on October 24.

The seven lucky prisoners who are being released are Ram Chander alias Tiger, Lalit Kumar, Satish Khandelwal, Panna Lal, Ata-Ur-Rehman, Sunil Chand Jain and Sanjay Singh. All of them are convicted for murder.

Sunil Chand Jain and Sanjay Singh will not have to furnish any surety as they have been in jail for more than 20 years now.

Jain had reportedly killed a family in 1980s. Officials said that their records and applications were being considered by Lieutenant Governor for a long time.

"After reviewing several factors, including the convict's behaviour in jail and track record, the remissions and releases are usually decided. These seven prisoners have behaved very well. Now they return to their families forever," said a jail official.

Apart from these releases, some 11,000 prisoners in Tihar jail are also celebrating Diwali inside the jail.

A senior jail officer said, "The inmates have prepared sweets which will be distributed among them. They will also light candles but there would be no crackers because of security reasons."

Officers confirmed the relief to life convicts has taken place in Tihar jail after a long time.

Though prisoners are released and remissions in punishment are given on Independence Day and Republic Day, murder convicts are usually not considered.

Heading: Home run with a feather touch - Indian Express
Content:
Three arrested for forgery, preparing fake I-cards

The South Delhi Police have arrested three persons on charges of forging and preparing fake identity cards of various Government departments. Police said the accused, Zia-ur-Rehman (23), Anis-ur-Rehman (23) and Mohd. Qumar UI Zama (21) worked for major mobile networks and forged documents for giving mobile phone connections to customers. Police officials said on October 20, a Cyber Cafe' owner "who was sensitised under the 'Eyes and Ears' " scheme informed Vasant Vihar Police Station about a suspicious person using the café. The café owner copied the information from the suspect's pen-drive. On checking it, it was found that there were various fake ID cards of government departments. — ENS

Police said the suspect was traced to Munirka with the help of technical surveillance. On Sunday, accused Anis-ur-Rehman was arrested and photocopies of six fake identity cards of sensitive government departments alongwith a mobile phone and two SIM cards were recovered from his possession.

Police arrested the other two accused after Rehman's confessions. Police officials said the accused Zia ur Rehman and Mohammed Qumarul Zama were working as sales executives for leading mobile operators. To get maximum connections for their customers, they decided to use the computer expertise of the third accused, Mohd. Qumar ul Zama to procure fake identity cards.

Police said the gang sold over 100 mobile connections on the basis of these forged documents.
